notes: On 2 January 2022, police forces used tear gases to disperse a group of around 80 migrants supported by members of associations before the dismantlement of their camp situated in Coquelles. During the intervention, one activist accused of slapping a policeman was arrested.

On 3 January 2022, around 700 people demonstrated in Dortmund against coronavirus-related measures and vaccination. One man refused to wear a mask and got arrested by police officers. Around 70 people gathered for a counter-demonstration at the call of Die Partei. Counter-demonstrators were against Nazis who they accuse of being within the Querdenken movement.

On 3 January 2022, around 4,000 people, including far-right members, demonstrated in Rostock against coronavirus-related measures and possible compulsory vaccination. Police officers used batons and physically pushed demonstrators who tried to break through barriers. Around 80 people gathered for a counter-demonstration.
On 3 January 2022, people demonstrated in Erfurt against coronavirus-related measures. Police officers used tear gas.

On 5 January 2022, seven protesters, including 6 organized by RRP: Revolutionary Workers Party, gathered for coordinated 'one-person pickets' in front of the embassy of Kazakhstan in Moscow - Central in support of mass protests in Kazakhstan, participants of which were demanding the withdrawal from politics of the influential former president Nursultan Nazarbayev. Police intervened to disperse the event, detaining all of its participants.

On 5 January 2022, around 3,000 people, including Querdenken members, demonstrated in Munchen against coronavirus-related measures. Police officers pushed, used their batons and tear gas against demonstrators. Around 400 people gathered for a counter-demonstration. One person was arrested but it isn't quite clear if it was within the demonstration or the counter-demonstration.

On 6 January 2022, approximately 10 protesters gathered for coordinated 'one-person pickets' in front of a monument to a Kazakh poet on Chistoprudnyy Boulevard in Moscow - Central in support of mass protests in Kazakhstan, participants of which were demanding the withdrawal from politics of the influential former president Nursultan Nazarbayev. Police intervened to disperse the event, detaining all of the protesters, including a journalist.

On 7 January 2022, at least seven protesters gathered for coordinated 'one-person pickets' in front of a monument to a Kazakh poet on Chistoprudnyy Boulevard in Moscow - Central in support of mass protests in Kazakhstan, participants of which were demanding the withdrawal from politics of the influential former president Nursultan Nazarbayev. Police intervened to disperse the event, detaining all of its participants.

On 8 January 2022, over 2,000 persons, including members of the Yellow Vests movement and members of the CGT union, participated in two demonstrations in Lyon. They called for the removal of the bill changing the coronavirus-related 'sanitary pass' into a 'vaccination pass' with the obligation to provide a proof of vaccination to resume social and professional activities. The police intervened using tear gas and a police grenade accidentally landing inside an apartment, but no injuries nor fatalities were reported.

On 8 January 2022, up to 600 people demonstrated in Dijon. They called for the removal of the bill changing the coronavirus-related 'sanitary pass' into a 'vaccination pass' with the obligation to provide a proof of vaccination to resume social and professional activities. They also denounced the declarations of the French president, according to which he would 'hassle unvaccinated people'. The police intervened using tear gas, while no injuries nor fatalities were reported.

On 8 January 2022, between 2 pm and 5 pm, around 4,500 took to the streets in Bregenz (Bregenz, Vorarlberg) to protest against coronavirus-related measures, specifically the introduction of mandatory vaccination against coronavirus by the government. 23 people were fined by police for failing to comply with mask requirements and one participant was temporarily arrested for declining to identify himself.

On 8 January 2022, a 'medium double-digit number of people' took to the streets in Hildesheim (Hildesheim, Niedersachsen) to protest against coronavirus-related measures. 17 misdemeanor proceedings were initiated on the scene by the police due to failures to comply with face-mask obligations. One demonstrator was taken into custody after filming police action in presumed violation of the Art Copyright Act and resisting.
On 8 January 2022, around 250 people staged a protest in Luxembourg against the coronavirus policy of the Luxembourg government. 4 protesters were arrested by police forces.

On 9 January 2022, about 100 residents of Miloslavov gathered for a spontaneous rally. They were protesting against violence and abuse, following a recent case of brutal bullying of a local girl by other youngsters. Law enforcers later dispersed the protest due to coronavirus-related restrictions on public gatherings. They also detained two individuals who could not prove their identity.

On 9 January 2022, in the evening, after the end of a large previous protest, about 20 people gathered by the main train station in Salzburg (Salzburg, Salzburg) to denounce coronavirus-related measures. Police officers intervened due to 'noise disturbance and disorderly conduct', asking participants to identify themselves. Two of them resisted and were taken into custody by the police.

On 9 January 2022, 20 to 30 people affiliated with the 'left scene' staged a protest in a protected area in the center of Innsbruck (Innsbruck, Tirol) to denounce a simultaneous demonstration against coronavirus-related measures in the city. Participants were isolated from the procession of the demonstration they were denouncing, 10 of them temporarily arrested by the police for refusing to disclose their identity and 21 fined for allegedly violating gathering requirements amid coronavirus.

On 10 January 2022, activists gathered for a rally in Warsaw, protesting against a ceremony commemorating the so-called Smolensk tragedy and against its politicization by the current government. Police officers intervened in the protest, chasing some protesters and holding them for a period of time.

On 10 January 2022, in the evening, groups of counter-demonstrators composed mainly of Antifa activists repeatedly tried to block a 'walk' of opponents to coronavirus-related measures in downtown Oldenburg. In order to prevent clashes, the police repeatedly pushed back some counter-demonstrators, using a service dog and pepper spray against one counter-demonstrator.

On 10 January 2022, about 30 people gathered in front of the town hall in Gottingen to protest against coronavirus-related measures. About 240 people took part in a simultaneous counter-demonstration. Police had to resort to force by pushing demonstrators and counter-demonstrators to avoid interactions between both groups.

On 10 January 2022, around 150 people took to the streets in an unauthorized series of 'walks' in Schweinfurt to denounce coronavirus-related measures. 70 participants were fined by the police. A 51-year-old female demonstrator tried to break through a police cordon, attacked an officer and bit him on the leg, before being arrested.

On 10 January 2022, in the evening, around 2,000 people took to the streets in Augsburg to protest against coronavirus-related measures. Police had to intervene several times, notably seizing a demonstrator's knife and telescopic baton. A Hitler salute performed by a demonstrator was being investigated by the police.

On 10 January 2022, up to 1,000 people took to the streets in Fulda, taking part in a series of 'walks' and taking part in a 70-car procession, to protest against coronavirus-related measures. One male demonstrator was temporarily arrested by the police after a scuffle.

On 10 January 2022, in the evening, people took to the streets in Trier to protest against coronavirus-related measures. One demonstrator was taken into custody by the police, who identified several participants after they failed to comply with COVID restrictions.

On 10 January 2022, in the evening, about 100 people took to the streets in Schwabach (Schwabach, Bayern) to protest against coronavirus-related measures. Several participants were arrested by the police, notably a man who insulted law enforcement officers and tried to kick one of them.

On 10 January 2022, in the evening, around 300 people took part in a 'walk' through the streets of Schleswig to protest against coronavirus-related measures. Several arrests were made by the police after some participants refused to comply with COVID face-mask requirements.

On 10 January 2022, in the evening, between 500 (according to the police) and 800 people (organizers), including neo-Nazis, Querdenken supporters, coronavirus deniers and an AFD affiliate, took to the streets in Rostock to oppose coronavirus-related measures. During the procession, some demonstrators tried to force their way through a police roadblock, prompting law enforcement officers to resort to pepper spray.

On 10 January 2022, about 1,000 people, including far-right activists, gathered in downtown Bonn to protest against coronavirus-related measures, specifically compulsory vaccination against the virus. In front of the Academic Museum, police forces pushed a group of counter-protesters after they allegedly refused to observe greater distance from the main demonstration. The counter-demonstration saw the participation of The Greens-affiliated assembly leaders and urged people to get vaccinated against coronavirus.

On 10 January 2022, in the evening, about 350 people took to the streets in Friedrichshafen to denounce coronavirus-related measures. The camera of a journalist covering the event was hit by a participant, who then tried to take the device away. The perpetrator was temporarily arrested by the police.

On 13 January 2022, people, predominantly young people, gathered in Vitoria-Gasteiz against the eviction of an occupied center by the Gasteiz Socialist Council. An activist chained himself in the facilities to prevent the eviction. Police forces intervened to dissolve the protest and evict the people in the building. One person was arrested, and police forces made nine identity checks.

On 13 January 2022, students blocked Francois-Arago high school in Villeneuve-Saint-Georges. The police intervened to disperse them and arrest one of them. They denounced the coronavirus sanitary protocol established in schools by the Ministry of Education.

On 13 January 2022, at the call of eight teacher unions (SNUIPP-FSU, SE-UNSA, FEP-CFDT, SNES-FSU, FO, CGT-Education, SNALC, SUD Education) and three high school student groups (VL, MNL, FIDL), 8,200 people, including Socialist Party, LFI and French Communist Party candidates to the presidential election, including MPs, demonstrated in Paris. The police intervened to disperse students who blocked with garbage cans the entrance of high schools. They denounced the coronavirus sanitary protocol established in schools by the Ministry of Education.

On 13 January 2022, in the morning, three employees of the Bartolo-Misasi nursing home (owned by the Igreco group) supported by the USB union climbed onto the roof of their clinic in Crispi square in Cosenza (Cosenza, Calabria) to protest against the announced dismissal of 51 employees by the entity's owner. The protesters, who brought fuel canisters with them threatened to set themselves on fire. The roof was cleared in the afternoon following the intervention of police forces.

On 13 January 2022, around 140 people gathered outside Ernst Deutsch Theater at Friedrich-Schutter-Platz in the Uhlenhorst area of Hamburg - Hamburg-Nord (Hamburg) to denounce coronavirus-related measures. Two demonstrators hit the camera of a Morgen Post journalist covering the event. Another participant was taken into custody by the police for refusing to wear a face mask.

On 14 January 2022, 15-20 anti-vaccination protesters gathered at a few locations in Chester. They started rallied at Chester Magistrates Court, where one of their members was due to appear in the dock, then blocked entry to the Chester Crown Court, and headed off to the city center. Police arrested two protesters on suspicion of a public order offense outside Chester Magistrates Court.

On 15 January 2022, three protesters gathered for coordinated 'one-person pickets' on Pushkin Square in Moscow - Central to demand free and fair elections, freedom of the press, the release of political prisoners and the dismissal of the Russian president. Another demonstrator at the nearby Red Square also stood in protest in support of political prisoners. Police intervened and detained all 4 participants of the event.

On 15 January 2022, approximately 40 protesters gathered in Yekaterinburg to oppose a possible war against Ukraine, in light of recent geopolitical demands by Moscow towards NATO and authorities in Kyiv. Police intervened in the event, detaining two of its participants.

On 15 January 2022, about 700 counter-demonstrators to a anti-coronavirus measures 'walk' in Kassel was organized by entities including FFF, The Left, Grannies Against the Right, and The Greens. A group of Antifa activists split off from the main counter-demonstration and ignited flares, in the hopes of meeting Querdenken-affiliated demonstrators. The police, who temporarily arrested about 35 participants from the Antifa counter-demonstration to keep both groups separated, also pushed some of the group's participants, injuring one mildly.

On 15 January 2022, two protests took place in Luxembourg against the coronavirus policy of the Luxembourg government, with around 30 and 350 people respectively. Police forces arrested around 30 protesters in the context of the latter action, which was not authorized by the authorities.

On 16 January 2022, around 15,000 people staged a protest march through Amsterdam to denounce the coronavirus policy of the Dutch government. 9 demonstrators were arrested. The march was an initiative of Nederland In Verzet.

On 17 January 2022, people demonstrated in Copenhagen over the official ceremony to begin work on an artificial island named Lynetteholm that is suppose to house 35,000 people and protect the port of Copenhagen from rising sea levels. Demonstrators claimed that the project could harm both the marine and the urban environment. Later, one activist attempted to stop the ceremony and was removed by the police personnel.

On 17 January 2022, four activists arrived to the town hall in St. Petersburg - Tsentralny, moving around in ice skates and using crutches, to protest against local authorities' handling of winter in the city, claiming not enough was done to clean St. Petersburg from snow and ice. Police intervened in the event and detained all of its participants, on the grounds that the protest was not authorized.

On 17 January 2022, in the evening, around 50 people took to the streets for an unregistered 'walk' in Ritterhude to protest against coronavirus-related measures. Two demonstrators were excluded from the gathering by the police as they refused to wear a face mask and a criminal proceeding was initiated against a female demonstrator for insulting law enforcement officers. About 20 people took part in a registered counter-demonstration.

On 17 January 2022, in the evening, an estimated 800 people 'walked' from Alexanderplatz to the Brandenburg Gate in Berlin - Mitte to protest against coronavirus-related measures. Demonstrators stopped for a gathering in front of the ZDF media station headquarters. A group of Antifa counter-demonstrators was pushed by the police to keep them away from the main demonstration.

On 17 January 2022, in the evening, around 50 people took to the streets for a 'walk' in Worpswede to protest against coronavirus-related measures. Criminal proceedings were initiated against six demonstrators who refused to wear a mask, while one was taken into custody by the police for further identification. 30 people took part in a simultaneous counter-demonstration.
On 17 January 2022, around 1,500 people took to the streets for a 'walk' in Cottbus to denounce coronavirus-related measures. Police officers used tear gas after one demonstrator 'resisted' them.

On 17 January 2022, up to 600 people, including far-right activists, took to the streets for an unregistered 'walk' in Magdeburg to denounce coronavirus-related measures. Pepper spray was used and one male demonstrator threw a bottle at police officers. About 350 people simultaneously gathered at the Old Market under the slogan 'Solidarity through the pandemic' to demonstrate in favor of compliance with coronavirus-related measures.

On 17 January 2022, in the evening, several hundred people took part in unregistered 'walks' in downtown Hannover, some blowing whistles, igniting firecrackers and shouting 'resistance,' 'freedom' or 'no dictatorship', to denounce coronavirus-related measures. The police peacefully dispersed several unregistered gatherings, though there were scuffles with one group of demonstrators in the Kropcke area, with one demonstrator sustaining injuries.

On 17 January 2022, 250 people took to the streets for a 'walk' in Oldenburg to protest against coronavirus-related measures. A counter-demonstration was staged simultaneously and gathered 300 people, who then formed a human chain. The police pushed a group of about 50 distinct counter-demonstrators from 'the left scene' away from the 'walkers' to keep all groups separated.

On 17 January 2022, in the evening, about 120 people gathered for an unregistered 'walk' in Deggendorf to protest against coronavirus-related measures. The police prevented the 'walk' from taking place.

On 18 January 2022, about 40 activists physically occupied a road in Krakow, protesting against politicization of the so-called Smolensk tragedy by the government. Law enforcers dispersed them detained some.

On 18 January 2022, the police cleared out the 'Sfascio Occupato', an occupied building in Genova (Genova, Liguria). The building had been occupied by an anarchist group on 2 January 2022. No clashes were reported.

On 18 January 2022, five activists affiliated with the Extinction Rebellion movement chained themselves to a bridge in Prague, effectively blocking the traffic. They were demanding shutdown of coal-based energy production, highlighting climate-related concerns. Law enforcers removed them from the spot.

On 18 January 2022, in the morning, at the call of XR, around a dozen activists staged a sit-in protest in the hallway of the Ministry of Finance in Den Haag (Zuid-Holland) to demand an end to public subsidies for fossil fuel companies. Police forces intervened around midday, removing and arresting the protesters. The action coincided with a parliamentary debate on the government's policy statement.

On 18 January 2022, around 80 people gathered outside the Volksschule school in Voitsberg to protest against coronavirus-related measures, specifically after a picture of a male student taking a test outside his class, by the window, in the absence of a face mask - and after the school questioned the validity of his mask exemption certificate - circulated online. A demonstrator's dog bit a police officer, injuring him slightly. One demonstrator was arrested for refusing to wear a mask.
On 19 January 2022, residents protested in the 5 Maji neighborhood in Tirana against the demolition of the buildings in their area. Police arrested several protesters.

On 19 January 2022, members of Rouvikonas protested inside the headquarters of the Public Power Corporation (DEI) in Athens - Central Athens, where they unfurled a banner and scattered fliers against energy price hikes. There were detentions.

On 19 January 2022, about 1,400 people took to the streets in Linz to denounce coronavirus-related measures, specifically planned mandatory vaccination. A group of demonstrators stopped by a nursery and started shouting at parents and filming them when realizing that children inside were wearing face masks. Some tried to break into the building, but were pushed back by a police cordon formed outside the nursey amid the tension.
On 20 January 2022, residents protested in the 5 Maji neighborhood in Tirana against the demolition of the buildings in their area. Police arrested several protesters.

On 21 January 2022, French police intervened to dislodge 74 environmental activists (Alternatiba, Attac, Extinction Rebellion) who briefly occupied Le Bourget airport tarmac to denounce the use of private jets which is allegedly increasing the global warming side effects. They also denounced alleged the double standards of government's environmental policies. One person was arrested.

On 22 January 2022, four activists gathered for coordinated 'one-person protests' at Pushkin Square in Moscow - Central, demanding the release of political prisoners, including opposition leader Alexey Navalny, an end to political repression, and in support of freedom of the press. Police intervened in the event and detained all of the participants.

On 22 January 2022, members of SYRIZA Youth unfurled a banner from the White Tower landmark of Thessaloniki in solidarity with a young woman who reported that she was raped on New Year's Eve setting in motion an investigation of a sex trafficking ring allegedly implicating wealthy families and businessmen in Greece and Cyprus. About 50 DIAS and DRASI police officers removed the demonstrators from the landmark and detained 3 of them.

On 22 January 2022, detainees in the San Pietro penitentiary in Reggio Calabria (Reggio di Calabria, Calabria) protested in the facility. The protest was promptly stopped by prison police officers. Motivations of the protest are not clear.

On 22 January 2022, 150 to 250 persons demonstrated in Dijon. Police force intervened to prevent some protesters from blocking the road. 5 people were arrested. They called for the removal to the coronavirus 'vaccination pass' with the obligation to provide a proof of vaccination to resume social and professional activities.

On 22 January 2022, anti-vaccine demonstrators marched into the Buchanan Galleries shopping centre in Glasgow in a show of opposition against the government-led coronavirus vaccine roll-out. After reports of families of shoppers being intimidated by the crowd police intervened and arrested two men.

On 22 January 2022, around 500 people demonstrated in Innsbruck against coronavirus-related measures. Some demonstrated 'harassed' (it doesn't seem physical), provoked, and insulted police officers. Two people tried to prevent the ongoing identity check and were arrested for it.
On 22 January 2022, around 1,500 people demonstrated in Erfurt against coronavirus-related measures. Police used tear gas to disperse the demonstration.
On 22 January 2022, around 1,200 people demonstrated in Offenbach am Main against coronavirus-related measures. A man who allegedly did a Nazi salute was temporarily arrested.
On 22 January 2022, around 750 people demonstrated in Cottbus against coronavirus-related measures. 3 people were arrested.

On 22 January 2022, two protests took place in Luxembourg against the coronavirus measures of the Luxembourg government. At the Champ du Glacis, around 200 people staged a protest march to Place de l'Europe. A second action assembled around 50 people at the Schuman roundabout. 1 person was arrested.

On 23 January 2022, protesters gathered in Khimki to oppose plans for a real estate development project in the valley of the nearby Grachevka river. Police intervened in the event and detained its organizer.

On 23 January 2022, around 40 anarchists protested in Trento (Trento, Trentino-Alto Adige) against a drill installed a few days before. Two persons attempted to sabotage the said drill, but the police physically stopped them.

On 23 January 2022, hundreds of students gathered in Pantheon square in Rome - City Center (Roma, Lazio) to protest against the death of a student who died during a high school internship in a factory in Udine province on 21 January 2022. Police officers intervened beating up demonstrators. Three students were injured. A group of students, belonging to OSA, spontaneously marched towards the Ministry of Education, escorted by the police. They denounced the country's work-study program.

On 24 January 2022, police forces dispersed around 50 protesters, including CGT-affiliated former workers at the LSI company, health workers, and members of teaching unions, in Aubusson, prior to the visit of the French President. The workers were denouncing the closure of their factory in 2017, while other protesters were expressing their hostility to the coronavirus vaccination pass.

On 24 January 2022, around 16 environmentalists belonging to Extinction Rebellion staged a blockade protest at the proposed site of the new Velindre Cancer Centre in Whitchurch stopping trucks carrying out construction work from enterring the site. Police dragged protesters away so as to let trucks pass, however there were no reported arrests.

On 24 January 2022, around 40 people, including SPD members, gathered in front of the town hall in Kopenick in Berlin - Treptow-Kopenick (Berlin), to form a solidary human chain and protested against the spread of conspiracy ideologies in the coronavirus pandemic. Around 300 people inlcuding AFD, NPD, and the Third Path staged a counter-demonstration on the Luisenhain against the corona measures. Police dissolved both groups of protesters and arrested 87 of them.

On 24 January 2022, around 20 people demonstrated in Lilienthal against coronavirus-related measures. 30 people gathered for a counter-demonstration. Few people which could have been in both demonstrations were arrested.

On 24 January 2022, 75 people in small groups demonstrated in Ritterhude against coronavirus-related measures. 2 demonstrators who refused to give their personal details were taken into custody as a result.
On 24 January 2022, almost 50 people demonstrated in Schwanewede against coronavirus-related measures. Around 6 people were arrested.
On 24 January 2022, people demonstrated in Gladenbach against coronavirus-related measures. One person was arrested.

On 24 January 2022, 24 climate activists demonstrated and blocked traffic on highway A103 in Berlin - Tempelhof-Schoneberg and on highway A114 in Berlin - Pankow (coded separately) to call on authorities for a law against food waste. Demonstrators also called for policies for more sustainable agriculture as food waste causes carbon dioxide and consequences on the climate. 24 people were temporarily detained. The association calls itself 'Uprising of the Last Generation'.
On 24 January 2022, people demonstrated in Wiesentheid against coronavirus-related measures. Police officers intervened but no details about it were reported.

On 24 January 2022, 70 demonstrators gathered in front of the Lichtenberg town hall in Berlin - Lichtenberg (Berlin), against coronavirus-related measures. Police intervened and arrested 59 demonstrators.

On 24 January 2022, 400 people held a demonstration rally in front of the town hall of Schoneberg in Berlin - Tempelhof-Schoneberg (Berlin), against coronavirus-related measures. Police intervened and arrested 56 of them.

On 24 January 2022, 24 climate activists demonstrated and blocked traffic on highway A103 in Berlin - Tempelhof-Schoneberg (coded separately) and on highway A114 in Berlin - Pankow to call on authorities for a law against food waste. Demonstrators also called for policies for more sustainable agriculture as food waste causes carbon dioxide and consequences on the climate. 24 people were temporarily detained. The association calls itself 'Uprising of the Last Generation'.

On 25 January 2022, climate activists, including Extinction Rebellion members, continued the occupation of the construction area at Amager district of Copenhagen demanding to stop the building of a housing complex in Amager Faelled nature area in Copenhagen, claiming that it would harm native animal species. Police personnel detained and removed several protesters from the venue.

On 25 January 2022, entrepreneurs protested against obligatory cash registers outside the parliament in Kiev. The protesters made an attempt to storm the Parliament. They were restrained by riot police. As a result, some protesters were arrested.

On 25 January 2022, around 350 climate activists camped and demonstrated in Osterholz to call for the preservation of the forest as well as an end to the ongoing evacuation of the camp. Police officers tried to evacuate the camp. Around 1,500 trees are to be felled to make way for a spoil heap of the lime industry.

On 26 January 2022, three protesters gathered at Petrogradskaya metro station in St. Petersburg - Petrogradsky to denounce the handling of coronavirus cases and problems with clearing snow in the city, for which they blamed the governor of St. Petersburg. Police intervened in the event and detained participants.

On 26 January 2022, at dawn, DIGOS police forces cleared a building occupied by anarchists in the Aurora neighborhood of Torino (Torino, Piemonte). Six occupants tried to barricade themselves in the building, but were eventually taken outside.

On 26 January 2022, 9 activists from Bake Bidea and AP blocked the railroad tracks near Tarnos, in a blockade of the Basque Country. Police arrived and arrested the protesters, who were later summoned to a local court.

On 26 January 2022, an unknown number of people took part in a torchlight procession in Spijkenisse (Zuid-Holland) to protest against the coronavirus measures of the Dutch government. One person was arrested for swearing at a police officer.

On 26 January 2022, nearly 300 people demonstrated in Warnemunde against coronavirus-related measures. Demonstrators called for freedom of choice concerning coronavirus vaccination and peace. According to an eyewitness, a pensioner was physically pushed by officers during the demonstration.

On 26 January 2022, climate activists of the 'Osterholz Stays' movement camped in Osterholz to call for the preservation of the forest (1,500 trees are to be felled to make way for a spoil heap of the lime industry). Police officers continued to evacuate the camp for the second day as activists are hiding in trees.

On 27 January 2022, Extinction Rebellion activists staged a protest performance at Trondheim Airport in Stjordal demanding to reduce aviation CO2 emissions. Later, police personnel arrested and removed activists from the venue.

On 28 January 2022, Extinction Rebellion members entered and attempted to occupy the City Hall of Copenhagen in protest against the construction of a housing complex in Amager Faelled nature area of Copenhagen. Police personnel detained and arrested 8 activists.

On 28 January 2022, between 200 and 300 people, including students, self-managed social center activists, and S.I. COBAS affiliates, took to the streets in Milano - Municipio 1 (Milano, Lombardia) to demand more safety and less labor precarity for students. Police forces intervened physically to disperse the demonstrators in front of the Assolombarda headquarters. One demonstrator sustained a head injury. Protesters denounced the country's work-study program following the death, of a work accident, of an 18-year-old student from Udine while doing an internship in Lauzacco on 21 January 2022.

On 28 January 2022, ER activists staged a sit-in on the road near Castello square in Torino (Torino, Piemonte), blocking traffic, to call on the Piemonte Region to honor its commitments in addressing the climate emergency. Activists staging a sit-in were dragged away from the road by the police, while others climbed on the gates of Palazzo Reale where they waved protest banners.

On 29 January 2022, an unknown number of people continued their protest occupation of the Sterrebos forest in Born (Limburg) against its imminent demolition for the car factory Nedcar, while about 50 people were protesting against the municipality's decision to grant a tree-logging permission to make room for the factory nearby. Seven people were arrested upon trying to join the occupants.

On 29 January 2022, at the call of Young Farmers union, farmers blocked with their tractors the entrance of a supermarket in Lamballe. The gendarmerie intervened to disperse them. They called for a revalorization of their product prices acquired by retailers.

On 29 January 2022, around 10,000 people, including QAnon members, demonstrated in several locations across Vienna against coronavirus-related measures. Police officers used tear gas and arrested 3 people for not respecting coronavirus health regulations.

On 29 January 2022, around 100 students and members of self-managed social centers threw red paint on the door of the headquarters of the Union of Industrialists (Confindustria) in piazza dei Martiri in Napoli (Napoli, Campania) to protest against the death of Lorenzo Parelli. The protesters attempted to force the police cordon and the police responded with a charge and hit protesters with batons.

On 30 January 2022, around 1,600 people staged a protest march from Brussels-North (Brussels - Schaerbeek) to the Atomium in Brussels - Ville de Bruxelles to denounce the coronavirus policy of the Belgian government and the resignation of the Federal cabinet. Although no incidents were reported during the march, 3 protesters were arrested. The protest was an initiative of Belgians United For Freedom.

On 30 January 2022, people demonstrated in Schwedt (Oder) against coronavirus-related measures. A demonstrator tried to hit a police officer, who was enforcing coronavirus regulations, with a flagpole in vain. He was arrested.

On 1 February 2022, 4 Insulate Britain defendants, including a Labour borough councilor, glued themselves to the steps of the Royal Courts of Justice in London - Westminster to oppose the court proceedings against them of breaching a High Court injunction by protesting on the M25 in September 2021. Their fellow protesters cheered for them outside the gate; however, they were subsequently removed by police and arrested.

On 1 February 2022, around 230 people demonstrated in Bregenz at the call of FBP against coronavirus-related measures. One woman outside of the demonstration in her car but who felt solidarity with, accelerated towards police officers who wanted to proceed to an identity check. 3 police officers had to jump to the side to avoid being run over but no one was injured. One person was arrested.

On 1 February 2022, about 20 people protested in front of the House of Representatives in Den Haag (Zuid-Holland) against the coronavirus measures of the Dutch government. Police arrested three people who refused to leave.

On 1 February 2022, dozens of climate activists camped and demonstrated in Vienna - Donaustadt to call for the preservation of the forest as well as an end to the ongoing evacuation of the camp. Police officers evacuated the camp. 48 people were arrested. Around 1,500 trees are to be felled to make way for a spoil heap of the lime industry.

On 2 February 2022, around 20 members of an environmental group blocked the access to the construction site of the future Olympic aquatic center in Aubervilliers. The police intervened and made five arrests.

On 2 February 2022, 10 Extinction Rebellion entered the building of the Ministry of the Environment (MITE) in Cristoforo Colombo street in Rome - Ostiense (Roma, Lazio), managing to reach the fifth floor and splashing employees, walls and furniture with red paint, to denounce the lack of actions to mitigate global warming. The activists were arrested on the scene by the police.
On 2 February 2022, Extinction Rebellion activists sat and blocked traffic in Skien to demand a declaration of climate emergency. Later, police personnel removed and arrested two activists.

On 3 February 2022, 17 members of Rouvikonas protested outside a venue in Athens - Central Athens where the mayor of Athens was holding a speech. The protesters scattered fliers, shouted slogans and unfurled a banner before they were detained, but the mayor requested they are not charged.

On 3 February 2022, dozens of students of the Brequigny high school and of the university of Rennes demonstrated in Rennes. They denounced the increase in academic registration fees and called for the defense of a public and free university. The police intervened using bastons and tear gas and made an arrest, while no injuries nor fatalities were reported.
On 3 February 2022, an unknown number of people continued the protest occupation of the Sterrebos forest in Born against its imminent demolition for the car factory Nedcar. 1 protester was arrested.

On 4 February 2022, 5 climate activists demonstrated and blocked traffic on different highways in Munchen to call on authorities for a law against food waste. Police officers had to intervene physically to remove protesters who glued themselves to the road. Demonstrators also called for policies for more sustainable agriculture as food waste causes carbon dioxide and has consequences on the climate. The association calls itself 'Uprising of the Last Generation'.

On 5 February 2022, nine protesters gathered for coordinated 'one-person pickets' at Pushkin Square in Moscow - Central to demand freedom of the press in Russia, the release of political prisoners, an end to political repression and torture in Russian prisons, as well as to oppose a possible war by Russia against Ukraine. The squatters called themselves the London Mahknovists. They hung a Ukrainian flag, declaring that it 'belonged to Ukrainian refugees', and contested Russian President Vladimir Putin. The Police wearing riot gear used a drill to break in and arrested eight people.

Police have made several arrests at the scene.

On 15 March 2022, Extinction Rebellion activists blocked the entrance of the Schlumberger research center in Cambridge, trying to stop staff, visitors and deliveries from entering. They claimed Schlumberger made 'profits from our unhealthy dependence on oil and gas'. They set up a boat, a fake oil rig and metal tripods outside the building. The police arrested some of the protesters and three people were charged.

On 15 March 2022, about 20 students and researchers of the University of Technology and members of the University Rebellion Eindhoven, a split off of Extinction Rebellion, protested in Eindhoven (Noord-Brabant) against the presence of Shell during the two-day Career Expo held on the campus. They disrupted the fair by holding protest signs and playing music in front of the Shell booth. The university security asked them to leave and when they refused, the police was called. Police arrested three people.

On 15 March 2022, in the afternoon, at the call of the No Future For Agrobusiness collective, around 120 people staged a protest action at the entrance of the Forum for the Future of Agriculture event in Brussels - Ville de Bruxelles (Brussels-Capital Region) to denounce agro-business lobbying and greenwashing practices. Protesters blocked access to attendees and sprayed fluorescent liquid to symbolize pesticide toxicity. Police forces intervened with tear gas to disperse the crowd and arrested 11 demonstrators.

On 16 March 2022, protesters against the detention of migrants, who did not have residence papers and were sent to deportation centers during large police operations in central Athens, rallied outside the Attica General Police Directorate in Athens - Central Athens. MAT officers attempted to disperse the crowd and arrested 14 protesters.
On 17 March 2022, around 60 fishers blocked the access to the oil depot in La Rochelle. They denounced the raise in the gas price. The police intervened and made several arrests.

On 17 March 2022, several hundred persons, including students, blocked the access to the Bretigny high school in Rennes. They called for resources for public schools and denounced police violence. The police intervened using tear gas, while no injuries were reported.

The police intervened, pushing demonstrators, while no injuries were reported.

They also called for the University of Cambridge to cut its close ties with the company. Police arrested two protesters on suspicion of criminal damage and aggravated trespass.

On 19 March 2022, three activists protested in Moscow against the destruction of the Bitsevsky Park. Police arrested the protesters and released them later on the same day.

Demonstrators claimed that one of them was dragged behind a bush by DIGOS officers and his body was pushed while he was on the ground, making him choke and causing him mild injuries, which later required first-aid treatment. The police denied the story and said the demonstrator had suffered pain in an arm while on the picket.

On 25 March 2022, interim civil servants protested inside the Cadiz (Andalucia) municipality to complain about their poor labor conditions. Two persons were arrested.

On 28 March 2022, activists gathered near the embassy of Russia in Warsaw and poured artificial blood on its walls, symbolizing their protest against the Russian war in Ukraine. They were detained.

On 8 April 2022, gendarmerie forces intervened to dislodge workers who were occupying a site part of the Network of Electricity Transport in Saumur. They were calling for an increase in their salaries and the recruitment of more personnel.

On 8 April 2022, climate campaigners belonging to Extinction Rebellion and Just Stop Oil Campaign blocked roads on Tower Bridge London - Tower Hamlets to demonstrate against the use of coal, oil and gas. Protesters unfurled a banner reading 'End fossil fuels now' from the side of the bridge in response to the government's plans to shore up its energy security following the Russian invasion of Ukraine. Police ended the demonstration and arrested four protestors.

On 8 April 2022, activists of the Extinction Rebellion movement blocked a central highway in Prague by lying on the ground, demanding protection of the climate and faster phase-out of fossil fuels, also related to the current war of Russia against Ukraine. Law enforcers removed them from the road.

On 8 April 2022, Extinction Rebellion activists blocked an oil terminal in Sjursoya, Oslo to urge the government to end its reliance on fossil fuels. Later, police personnel detained and removed activists from the venue.

On 9 April 2022, between 5,600 and 35,000 people, including members of the Yellow Vests movement, EELV and LFI, as well as environmental activists, demonstrated in Paris in at the call of Alternatiba, Greenpeace, Nous Toutes and Friends of the Earth. They called for a better future and for measures against the climate emergency. Some participants, including Yellow Vests activists, were tear gassed by the police.

On 9 April 2022, at the call of Extinction Rebellion, some 8,000 people (according to organizers), including a mechanical engineer, took to the streets and staged several sit-ins (in Oxford Street and Regent Street) in London - Westminster (England) to call for an end to the fossil fuel economy. 39 participants were arrested by the police for blocking the road.

On 10 April 2022, at the call of Extinction Rebellion, hundreds of people, including doctors and nurses, scientists and Polish Extinction Rebellion activists, took to the streets and staged sit-downs in the center of London (England), blocking both Lambeth and Vauxhall bridges, to demand an end to the fossil fuel economy, which some of them claimed was funding the war in Ukraine. The police made 38 arrests while clearing the 'occupied' bridges.

On 10 April 2022, in the morning, more than 20 Extinction Rebellion and Just Stop Oil activists blocked access to the Exolum Oil Storage in Grays (Thurrock, Thurrock, England) to call on the British government to stop all new gas and oil projects. Police officers cleared access to the facility by carrying activists away.

Around 10 April 2022 (weekend of), Extinction Rebellion and Just Stop Oil activists blocked access to the Kingsbury Oil Terminal in Kingsbury (North Warwickshire, Warwickshire, England) to call on the British government to stop all new gas and oil projects. 29 arrests were made by the police throughout the weekend.

On 10 April 2022, protesters dug a secret underground tunnel under a key tanker route to the BP Kingsbury Terminal in Kingsbury (North Warwickshire), hidden by a 'modified caravan' surrounded by Just Stop Oil activists. The group said that a number of people were arrested and five activists remained inside the caravan working on the tunnel, while the police stated that the tunnel was cleared.

On 10 April 2022, before dawn, 40 Just Stop Oil activists blocked the gate of the Buncefield Oil Terminal in Hemel Hempstead (Dacorum, Hertfordshire, England) to call on the British government to stop all new gas and oil projects. The police made several arrests on the scene.

On 11 April 2022, around 40 Just Stop Oil demonstrators continued to be locked onto pipework at the Inter Oil Terminal in Grays (Thurrock) following anti-fuel protests. The police arrested 9 protesters. The demonstrators have been chained to the pipes for over 30 hours.
On 11 April 2022, at least 12 members of ALG demonstrated and blocked traffic on a highway (A66) in Frankfurt am Main against investments in fossil energy projects. 12 people were arrested.

On 12 April 2022, people gathered in front of the Dorogomilovskiy court in Moscow to support the former editors of a student magazine DOXA, who are on trial for filming a video in support of student protesters. Police intervened in the event, arresting 8 people.

On 12 April 2022, members of the Droit au logement (DAL) organization demonstrated in front of the Housing Ministry in Paris. They called for housing measures for poorly-housed and 'priority' Dalo families. The police intervened and arrested the spokesperson of the organization. Demonstrators claimed the arrest was made in a forceful way.

On 12 April 2022, at least 50 people demonstrated, glued themselves to a road, and blocked traffic on a highway (A66) in Frankfurt am Main against investments in fossil energy projects and to raise awareness concerning climate change. Around 50 people were arrested.
On 13 April 2022, anti-war protesters organized pickets in Moscow against the Russian military invasion in Ukraine. Police intervened in the event, arresting three protesters.

On 13 April 2022, hundreds of Extinction Rebellion activists marched from Constitution Hill to Buckingham Palace in London - Westminster to demonstrate against the use of fossil fuels. Meanwhile, scientist members of the Extinction Rebellion, wearing lab coats, glued themselves to the Department for Business, Energy and Industrial Strategy building entrance to demand immediate action on climate change. At least 10 people were arrested after spray-painting on the glass facade of the building.

On 13 April 2022, 100 people belonging to the Extinction Rebellion carrying placards protested at Shell's headquarters in London - Lambeth to demonstrate against the fossil fuels industry. Dozens of protesters glued themselves to the reception desk inside the building and the ground outside to express their demands, and the police arrested them.

On 13 April 2022, Just Stop Oil activists glued their hands to roads and climbed on top of oil tankers outside Esso oil refinery in Purfleet-on-Thames, demanding the government stop funding new oil and gas projects. Police removed activists from the road and arrested them.

On 13 April 2022, at least 40 members of ALG demonstrated, glued themselves to a road, and blocked traffic on a highway (A66) in Frankfurt am Main against investments in fossil energy projects and to raise awareness concerning climate change. Around 40 people were arrested.

On 13 April 2022, people demonstrated in Bremen (Burgdamm district) against coronavirus-related measures including possible compulsory vaccination. A man who resisted an identity check injured two police officers and got arrested.

On 13 April 2022, activists defending Troitsk Forest in Moscow attempted to stop the ongoing logging and blocked the exit from the site with their car. Police intervened in the event, arresting a journalist.

On 14 April 2022, the Hard Line (Stram Kurs) activists, including party leader, carried out an anti-Islamic demonstration in Rinkeby, Stockholm, where they were met by a group of around 300 counter-protesters. Later, police personnel stopped the demonstration and removed protesters from the venue due to the high security risks.

On 14 April 2022, in the evening, at the call of UNEF, students gathered at Pantheon square in Paris to support the reception and regularization of student refugees and students form Ukraine. Police used tear gas to disperse them.

On 14 April 2022, 3 people protested outside Walleys Quarry in Newcastle-under-Lyme against the landfill's smells. One of the men glued his hands to the landfill site's gate to express their demands. They were all arrested by the police.

On 14 April 2022, at least 3 members of VGT demonstrated in Klagenfurt to denounce animal cruelty in pig farming. 3 demonstrators were arrested, one of them is said to have been slapped but the police denied the incident.

On 14 April 2022, 10 'Renovate Switzerland' movement activists blocked the Mont Blanc bridge in Geneva to demand the authorities measures in terms of energy renovation of buildings to reduce CO2 emissions. Police forces arrested 3 activists.

On 14 April 2022, members of the Scrap Factory Farming campaign and Animal Rebellion protested outside the Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs headquarters in London - Westminster, demanding the government support farmers in switching to growing crops instead of rearing animals. Protesters demonstrated with barrels of oil props and placards reading, 'Defund Oil. Scrap Factory Farming'. Police arrested four people.

On 14 April 2022, 5 activists belonging to Just Stop Oil stopped a fuel tanker and forced the closure of the Chiswick roundabout in London - Hounslow to demand the government end new licenses of fossil fuels. Four men clambered onto the fuel tanker while a woman sat in front of the vehicle. Around 30 police officers surrounded the tanker and arrested them all.

On 14 April 2022, at least 40 people, including ALG members, demonstrated and blocked traffic in Frankfurt am Main to call for climate protection. Demonstrators sprayed oil on the road, which caused a cyclist to slip and fall. Around 40 people were arrested.
On 15 April 2022, around 40 people gathered in St. Petersburg, protesting against the demolition of the historical building of the bathhouses. Police intervened in the event, arresting 2 protesters.

On 15 April 2022, in the early hours, a dozen of Just Stop Oil activists blocked access to the Kingsbury oil depot in Kingsbury to demonstrate against the fossil fuels industry. Police arrested 12 people.

On 15 April 2022, in the early hours, Just Stop Oil activists blocked access to the Navigator and Grays Oil Terminals in Grays to demonstrate against the fossil fuels industry. A lorry driver affected by the protest yanked one protester to express his frustration with the delay. Police arrested 28 people.

On 15 April 2022, Just Stop Oil activists gathered at the Kingsbury terminal near Tamworth, Staffordshire to call on the Government to stop new oil and gas projects. The police arrested 12 demonstrators.

On 15 April 2022, Just Stop Oil activists climbed ontop of oil tankers at the Grays oil terminal in Grays, Thurrock to call on the Government to stop new oil and gas projects. The police arrested a total of 28 people between the Grays oil terminal and the Navigator depot.

On 15 April 2022, Just Stop Oil activists gathered at the Navigator depot in West Thurrock, Thurrock to call on the Government to stop new oil and gas projects. The police arrested a total of 28 people between the Grays oil terminal and the Navigator depot.

On 15 April 2022, in the early morning, a number of Just Stop Oil activists, among them a doctor, gathered at the Kingsbury Oil Terminal in Kingsbury, North Warwickshire to call on the Government to halt new oil and gas projects in the UK. Seven demonstrators climbed up between the pipes of the loading bay, blocking the terminal. The police charged nine protesters and arrested 12.

On 15 April 2022, around 120 people demonstrated in Berlin - Mitte against the eviction of the Kopi housing project and self-managed social center. People occupied an old building (on Kopenick Street 137), climbed the property's fences, set off fireworks, and firecrackers, and climbed on construction vehicles. Between 13 and 15 people were arrested and police officers cleared the camp.

On 16 April 2022, the Hard Line (Stram Kurs) activists, including the party leader, held an anti-Islamic demonstration in Skanegarden, Malmo, where they were met by a group of counter-protesters. Later, police stopped the demonstration and removed the activists for security reasons. During the demonstration, one man attempted to drive through the police fences to injure the Hard Line leader, but was stopped.

On 16 April 2022, members of the Armenian community of Thessaloniki rallied in Aristotelous square and marched to the Turkish consulate on the anniversary of the 1915 Armenian genocide carrying Armenian flags. The protesters were shouting slogans and holding a banner reading 'the Armenian new generation does not forget the genocide by Turks in 1915'. The protesters attempted to break a police cordon, but they were prevented from entering the consulate to post a protest voting.

On 16 April 2022, at the call of CGT and SUD unions, SOS Racism, Greenpeace, the Human Rights League, the UNEF and political parties, between 9,200 and 40,000 persons demonstrated in Paris against the far-right RN party ahead of next weekend's presidential run-off. At the end of the protest march, police forces used tear gases to disperse protesters from the NPA party who wanted to start a static protest.

On 16 April 2022, thousands of Extinction Rebellion activists took to the streets and reached Marble Arch in London - Westminster to call for an end to the use of fossil fuels, with some participants blocking traffic, two climbing Marble Arch and three onto a Shell oil tanker on Bayswater Road. The Metropolitan Police arrested around 76 protesters.
On 17 April 2022, anti-war activists in Moscow held a series of pickets, protesting against the Russian military invasion in Ukraine. Police intervened in the event, arresting the protesters.
On 17 April 2022, anti-war activists in St. Petersburg held a series of pickets, protesting against the Russian military invasion in Ukraine. Police intervened in the event, arresting the protesters.

On 17 April 2022, around 6 Extinction Rebellion activists staged a protest performance in Skien by interrupting an Easter service in a local church to demand a declaration of climate emergency in the country, draw attention to climate change and to oppose the construction of new cabins in a natural area. The police removed the protesters, presumably without the use of excessive force.

On 18 April 2022, 5 Strategy-18 activists held a series of pickets in Murino, protesting against the repressions carried out by the Russian authorities towards the Crimean Tatars. Police intervened in the event, arresting all participants.

On 18 April 2022, around 800 people, including members of DFG-VK, DKP, MLPD, REBELL, VVN-BdA, demonstrated in Dortmund to call for peace amid the war in Ukraine, denouncing the war and militarization. Some demonstrators fought (one demonstrator was choked) because some demanded the eviction of MLPD from the demonstration before police officers separated demonstrators, with no reported injuries. They had gathered for an Easter March.
On 19 April 2022, 3 activists held a series of pickets in Moscow, protesting against the Russian military invasion in Ukraine. Police intervened in the event, arresting the protesters.

On 19 April 2022, members of Jewish student group UJEF and SOS Racism activists protested by throwing fake ruble money in front of RN party headquarter in Paris. They denounced alleged financial support received by the far-right party from Russia. Police forces intervened to disperse them.

On 19 April 2022, 5 climate activists of Renovate Switzerland blocked a highway at the Wankdorf exit near Bern to denounce government's inaction against global warming. The police force intervened to disperse them.
On 20 April 2022, 3 activists held a series of pickets in Moscow, protesting against the Russian military invasion in Ukraine. Police intervened in the event, arresting the protesters.
On 21 April 2022, 3 activists held a series of pickets in Moscow, protesting against the Russian military invasion in Ukraine. Police intervened in the event, arresting the protesters.

On 21 April 2022, around 20 Extinction Rebellion and Greenpeace activists continued to protest for the tenth day in Lappohja, Hanko, demanding an end to Russian fossil fuel freight traffic through Finland. Police dispersed the protest and five protesters were detained for moving from the protest camp to the train tracks.

On 23 April 2022, activists from the Stop Islamisation of Norway movement (SIAN) staged an anti-Islamic demonstration in Sandefjord and were met by a group of counter-protesters. Later, the police had to stop the demonstration for security reasons.

On 23 April 2022, 7 protesters in Moscow participated in a series of pickets at different locations, protesting against the Russian military invasion in Ukraine. Police intervened in the event, arresting all protesters.

On 24 April 2022, 3 protesters in Moscow participated in a series of pickets at different locations, protesting against the Russian military invasion in Ukraine. Police intervened in the event, arresting all protesters.

On 24 April 2022, between 400 and 500 people took to the streets in Nantes to denounce the reelection of the French President and the presence of the far-right RN candidate in the runoff. Police forces used tear gases to disperse them.

On 24 April 2022, around 100 Kurdish people and campaigners belonging to the South Yorkshire Migrant and Asylum Action Group (SYMAAG) and Sheffield Trades Union Council gathered outside the Sheffield Town Hall to protest the Turkish government's decision to launch military strikes against Kurdish fighters in Iraq and Syria. Police arrested one man under anti-terror laws for displaying a flag supporting the Kurdistan Workers' Party (PKK), pushing and using pepper spray against other protesters.
On 25 April 2022, Delivery Club couriers gathered in Moscow, protesting against wage cuts. Police intervened in the event, arresting 12 protesters, including one journalist covering the protest.

On 25 April 2022, 18 members of VGT occupied the office of an OEVP member in Klagenfurt against the full slatted floor husbandry of pigs and demanded a discussion with the Minister of Agriculture. Police officers intervened and arrested the participants.

On 25 April 2022, environmental activists from Extinction Rebellion and Greenpeace blocked and chained themselves to a vessel carrying Russian oil in Norwegian waters near Tonsberg. Later, police removed and temporarily detained 20 activists.

On 26 April 2022, three climate activists belonging to Insulate Britain were arrested after gluing themselves to the furniture inside Stratford Magistrates' Court in London - Newham. They denounced charges against them following their involvement in protests at the Poyle Interchange at junction 14 of the M25 near Heathrow Airport on 27 September 2021. Police removed the protesters.

On 26 April 2022, Just Stop Oil activists gathered outside the Kingsbury Oil Terminal in Kingsbury to call for an end to the production and use of fossil fuels. Police arrived at the scene and made 16 arrests on suspicion of obstructing the highway.

On 26 April 2022, around 200 environmental activists from Extinction Rebellion stood and blocked traffic in Stockholm demanding to abolish government subsidies to fossil fuel related companies, to stop importing fossil fuels from Russia and to declare climate emergency in the country. Later, police forces removed activists from the venue.

On 27 April 2022, anarchists and students rallied for a 5th day against MAT riot police presence on the Aristotle University of Thessaloniki campus. Student demonstrators reported that riot police pushed them away using their shields. Police were called in to protect work to transform a section of the Biology department, which was an unauthorized anarchist hangout for 34 years, into a library. The hangout had been evacuated in December.

On 27 April 2022, climate activists belonging to the campaign group Just Stop Oil gathered outside the Kingsbury Oil Terminal in Kingsbury for the second protest in two days, calling for an end to the production and use of fossil fuels. Police arrived at the scene and made 10 arrests.

On 29 April 2022, 5 protesters, including a former member of the Council of the Human Rights Center 'Memorial', participated in a series of pickets at different locations in Moscow, protesting against the Russian military invasion in Ukraine. Police intervened in the event, arresting all protesters.

On 29 April 2022, four Extinction Rebellion activists blocked a street in Padua (Padova, Veneto) by displaying banners against climate change. DIGOS police forces intervened and arrested the protesters.

On 30 April 2022, 4 protesters in Moscow participated in a series of pickets at different locations, protesting against the Russian military invasion of Ukraine. Police intervened in the event, arresting all protesters.

On 30 April 2022, animal rights campaigners blocked access to a livestock market in Norwich to protest against the industry. Police arrested two protesters after confrontations between protesters and those trying to access the site. This event was organized by Norwich Livestock Market Animal Vigils.

On 30 April 2022, vegan activists protested outside the livestock market in Norwich by blocking the road to farmers. Two people, one farmer and one protester, were arrested following angry confrontations between cattle farmers and vegan protesters. No one was reported injured.

On 1 May 2022, left activists organized a demonstration in Novosibirsk, commemorating Labour Day. Police intervened in the event, arresting 6 protesters, including several activists from the Russian Communist Workers' Party, who were holding a banner with an appeal to workers of different countries and signs for freedom of assembly.

On 1 May 2022, members of Rouvikonas rallied outside the main offices of ruling party New Democracy in Moschato, Athens - South Athens. The demonstrators scattered fliers, shouted slogans and unfurled a banner. DIAS police arrived at the scene and detained 48 people.

On 1 May 2022, protesters in Moscow participated in a series of pickets at different locations, protesting against the Russian military invasion of Ukraine. Police intervened in the event, arresting at least 7 protesters.

On 1 May 2022, on May Day, around 150 members of a far-left group demonstrated in Rennes. They denounced capitalism and fascism. The police intervened using tear gas and water cannons, while no injuries nor fatalities were reported.

On 1 May 2022, around 2,000 people demonstrated in Hamburg - Hamburg-Mitte (Hamburg), in HafenCity, on the occasion of Labor Day for more equality between rich and poor. Demonstrators apparently 'harassed' the police and the latter used batons to push the people back. Police officers arrested some demonstrators.

On 2 May 2022, environmental activists continued to block a wind power plant construction site near Solleftea calling to stop construction works. Later, police intervened and removed activists from the venue. Two people were arrested.

On 2 May 2022, 3 protesters in Moscow participated in a series of pickets at different locations, protesting against the Russian military invasion in Ukraine. Police intervened in the event, arresting all protesters.

On 2 May 2022, 3 protesters in St. Petersburg participated in a series of pickets at different locations, protesting against the Russian military invasion in Ukraine. Police intervened in the event, arresting all protesters.

On 2 May 2022, around 15 people demonstrated in Paris. They denounced police violence after a police officer shot dead two men who were trying to escape a police control on the Pont-Neuf Bridge on 24 April 2022. Some demonstrators were forcibly taken away by the police and fined on the grounds that their gathering had not been authorized.

On 3 May 2022, at 4 am, Just Stop Oil activists blocked access to the Nustar facility in Clydebank (West Dunbartonshire) by climbing on top of tankers and locking on to the entrance. Twelve protesters sat on pipes and three were on the silos to halt operations. They demanded that the UK Government end new oil and gas projects in the UK. The protest lasted 60 hours [coded as three events] and the police arrested 31 demonstrators overall.

On 4 May 2022, environmental activists from the Nature and Youth Movement continued the blockade of the construction site near Forde (Vestland) to oppose the ongoing construction works, arguing that it would cause environmental damage. Later, police personnel intervened and removed the activists from the venue. Several people were temperately detained.

On 4 May 2022, Just Stop Oil activists continued to block access to the Nustar facility in Clydebank (West Dunbartonshire) by climbing on top of tankers and locking on to the entrance. They demanded that the UK Government end new oil and gas projects in the UK. The protest started on May 3rd and lasted 60 hours [coded as three events]. Overall, the police arrested 31 demonstrators.

On 5 May 2022, 3 protesters in Moscow participated in a series of pickets at different locations, protesting against the Russian military invasion of Ukraine. Police intervened in the event, arresting all protesters.

On 5 May 2022, around 30 Greenpeace activists broke into the premises of the Naturgy power plant in the Campanillas district of Malaga (Andalucia) to denounce its burning of Russian gas, allegedly financing the country's war on Ukraine. Spanish police detained 23 demonstrators.

On 5 May 2022, PAH activists gathered outside a building on Neptu Street in Lleida to oppose the simultaneous eviction of a family from the building, which they claimed left a family with children and a pregnant woman homeless. Two demonstrators were arrested and one police officer suffered a finger injury after being bitten by a demonstrator.

On 5 May 2022, Just Stop Oil activists continued to block access to the Nustar facility in Clydebank (West Dunbartonshire) by climbing on top of tankers and locking on to the entrance. They demanded that the UK Government end new oil and gas projects in the UK. The protest started on May 3rd and lasted 60 hours [coded as three events]. Overall, the police arrested 31 demonstrators.

On 6 May 2022, over 500 Extinction Rebellion activists launched an 'Overconsumption Rebellion' named protest and blocked a main road in central Helsinki (Mannerheimintie). The police dispersed the protest and 65 people were detained.

On 6 May 2022, about 10 far-left activists gathered for a protest, disturbing a memorial service for the politician Pim Fortuyn, who was murdered in 2002, in Rotterdam. Police arrested two protesters.

On 6 May 2022, environmental activists, including Extinction Rebellion members, blocked several major bridges in Copenhagen to demand the government to end its reliance on fossil fuels, to stop urban development in natural areas and to declare a climate emergency in the country. Total of around 90 activists were detained during the day.

On 7 May 2022, 3 protesters participated in a series of pickets at different locations in Moscow, protesting against the Russian military invasion in Ukraine. Police intervened in the event, arresting all protesters.

On 7 May 2022, around 50 Extinction Rebellion activists staged a protest at a terminal of Helsinki-Vantaa airport in Vantaa, highlighting the impact of flying on the environment. They blocked the entry to the airport security check. Police dispersed the protest and 28 people were detained for not following orders. An additional group of protesters gathered to support the protest outside the airport.

On 7 May 2022, members of the ACPV and Cosa Nostra pro-independence Valencian group gathered in Castello de la Plana (Castellon, Valencia) to celebrate the day of the Valencian Community. Police detained two activists who intended to hang a banner on a building.

On 7 May 2022, at the call of AI and several feminist associations, including Women Inc., hundreds of people staged a protest on Dam Square in Amsterdam to denounce the US Supreme Court's plan to overturn abortion rights in the US. A group of 20 to 30 demonstrators headed towards the US consulate, blocking tramway lines and graffitiing streetcars, and resisted police forces as they attempted to arrest a female demonstrator. Two people were arrested.

On 7 May 2022, activists from Extinction Rebellion and the Danish Association for International Co-operation sat and blocked a road in Copenhagen to oppose the government's refugee policy and to demand declaration of a climate emergency. Later, police removed activists from the venue. Around 10 people were detained.

On 7 May 2022, a large number of people, including coronavirus deniers, members of Free Assange, Querdenken, and MLPD, demonstrated in Koln against the war and arms deliveries to Ukraine. Demonstrators gathered to counter an ongoing political rally by The Greens for the North Rhine-Westphalia elections, in which the country's Foreign Minister was taking part. Three men were arrested. One because he ignited pyrotechnics.

On 8 May 2022, 3 protesters participated in a series of pickets at different locations in Moscow, protesting against the Russian military invasion in Ukraine. Police intervened in the event, arresting all protesters.
On 8 May 2022, in the morning, the police has freed the UGT building in Madrid - Centro (Madrid) occupied by Extinction Rebellion activists to denounce a speculative operation.

On 8 May 2022, environmental activists, including Extinction Rebellion members, demonstrated in Amager district of Copenhagen to oppose the construction of a housing complex in Amager Faelled nature area. Later, several activists blocked the entrance to the construction site and were detained by the police.

On 9 May 2022, 11 protesters participated in a series of pickets at different locations in Moscow, protesting against the Russian military invasion in Ukraine. Police intervened in the event, arresting all protesters.

On 9 May 2022, people participated in the commemorative Immortal Regiment march in Korolev, marking the Soviet Union's victory over Nazi Germany. Among participants were high-ranking government officials, members of the Russian military and veterans. This year, some participants joined the march, carrying Z symbols and photographs of their relatives who had died in Ukraine since the beginning of the Russian military invasion on 24 February 2022. Police arrested one woman for joining the march with an anti-war sign, protesting against the war in Ukraine.

On 9 May 2022, over 1 000 000 people participated in the commemorative Immortal Regiment march in St. Petersburg, marking the Soviet Union's victory over Nazi Germany. Among participants were high-ranking government officials, members of the Russian military and veterans. This year, some participants joined the march, carrying photographs of their relatives who had died in Ukraine since the beginning of the Russian military invasion on 24 February 2022. Police arrested an independent municipal deputy, who joined the march with a portrait of a former prisoner of Nazi concentration camps, who was killed by the Russian forces in Ukraine.

On 9 May 2022, Extinction Rebellion activists demonstrated at Copenhagen Kastrup Airport in Kastrup to oppose the expansion of the airport. Several activists entered the restricted area and attempted to glue themselves to the runaway. Police personnel removed and detained the activists.

On 10 May 2022, around 100 Extinction Rebellion activists protested by roads and tracks near an oil refinery in Kilpilahti, Porvoo, blocking traffic to the site. They protested against the company, Neste, buying fossil fuel from Russia. Police dispersed the protest and 42 people were detained for not following orders.

On 10 May 2022, a bailiff intervened and attempted to put an end to a permanent protest organized by the HS2 Rebellion environmental group at the Bluebell Woods Protection Camp near Swynnerton in Staffordshire. HS2 Rebellion activists were denouncing deforestation brought about by the High Speed Two (HS2) line and climate change, and started a tunnel occupation under the camp as a result. Protesters moved underground after bailiffs arrived to evict the camp.

On 10 May 2022, Animal Rebellion activists demonstrated in various locations of Copenhagen calling to ban animal agriculture, to switch to plant-based diets and to declare climate emergency. Several activists sat and blocked traffic near Tivoli Gardens while others glued themselves to the road. Later, police personnel removed activists from the venue, around 36 people were detained.

On 11 May 2022, an unknown number of Greenpeace activists staged a protest action at the Noordersluis in IJmuiden, blocking a soy ship from entering the Port of Amsterdam. They claimed the ship contributed to widespread deforestation in Brazil. Police forces intervened to arrest 12 activists.

On 11 May 2022, environmental activists, including Extinction Rebellion members, blocked a major road in Copenhagen to demand the government to end its reliance on fossil fuels, to stop urban development in natural areas and to declare a climate emergency in the country. Five activists were detained.

On 12 May 2022, Turkish Cypriot livestock breeders rallied in Northern Nicosia to protest that there is no authority to discuss their problems with amidst a political crisis that has left Northern Cyprus without a government. The protesters attempted to unload manure outside the Presidency building and other locations. Police arrested 6 protesters including the head of the Animal Producers and Breeders Association.

On 12 May 2022, the Hard Line (Stram Kurs) activists carried out an anti-Islamic demonstration in Trollhattan, where they were met by around 200 counter-protesters. Later, one counter-protester was detained after he tried to breach the police fence.

On 12 May 2022, in the morning, a group of housing rights activists ('Home Rights Network' ('Rete Diritti in Casa'), Artlab, 'The Collective' ('La Collettiva'), and 'Political Ecology Parma' ('Ecologia Politica Parma')) picketed the entrance of a building in the Colonne neighborhood of Parma (Parma, Emilia-Romagna), to protest against the impending eviction of an ill woman and her nephew from the premises by law enforcement. Scuffles occurred when a group of police officers and carabinieri tried to remove demonstrators from the entrance of the building.

On 12 May 2022, 4 Climate Strike activists attempted to block a fuel tank by setting up two large bamboo scaffoldings on the access road in Rumlang. They demanded a curb in carbon emissions. Police forces intervened to stop the protest, and arrested them.
On 13 May 2022, several protesters were arrested in Vasteras after they tried to bypass the police fence and to enter a location, where another rally was taking place.

On 13 May 2022, members of the association of couriers (SVEOD) rallied in Athens - North Athens to protest against the dismissal of a colleague following his participation in the 6 April general strike. Police detained tens of protesters.

On 13 May 2022, around 700 metal workers members of the UGT, CCOO and CIG protested in Ferrol (A Coruna, Galicia) in the second day of the ongoing strike. A protester was arrested for resisting authority.

On 13 May 2022, around 100 activists from Extinction Rebellion blocked a major bridge in Copenhagen to demand the government to end its reliance on fossil fuels, to stop urban development in natural areas and to declare a climate emergency in the country. Later, police personnel removed the activists, at least 18 people were temporarily detained.
On 14 May 2022, members of anti-establishment groups marched in Athens - Central Athens. Police detained 13 demonstrators. The cause of the protest was not reported.
On 14 May 2022, people demonstrated in Vannes to call for the abrogation of the coronavirus vaccination pass. Police forces intervened to arrest a protester making too much noise.

On 14 May 2022, Extinction Rebellion activists blocked the traffic in Torino and tried to block the entrance of the PalaAlpitour before the Eurovision Song Contest urging the music artists to declare a climate emergency. The police intervened by removing the activists from the entrance of the PalaAlpitour. They identified around 70 activists and arrested 30.

On 14 May 2022, around 2,550 people, mostly Querdenken members, demonstrated in Hannover against coronavirus-related measures, especially concerning vaccination in the region. One demonstrator claimed on a stage that Nazis were in power in Ukraine, and the police removed him physically without arrest. Querdenken members were part of 'Querdenken-511'.

On 15 May 2022, 13 climate activists belonging to Greenpeace stormed an oil tanker containing Russian diesel near Grays as it attempted to dock to protest against the continuation of Russian oil and gas trade with the UK despite a ban on such trade put in place by the UK government since the Russian invasion of Ukraine. 8 activists were subsequently arrested by the police.

On 16 May 2022, at the call of FELGBT and Crida LGBTI, several dozen LGBT rights activists staged a sit-in in front of the Casa del Llibre on the Rambla de Catalunya in Barcelona (Catalonia) to try to prevent the presentation of a book that demonstrators considered 'transphobic'. Police officers deployed as a cordon in front of the venue charged demonstrators with truncheons, while police forces claimed they were 'hit' by some demonstrators who tried to force their way into the venue before intervening.

On 16 May 2022, at the call of SEPC, around 100 people, including students, rallied outside the Government Delegation in Barcelona - L'Eixample (Catalonia) to denounce the order of the Superior Court of Justice of Catalonia (TSJC) that requires at least 25% of teaching hours to be taught in Spanish. The police removed four participants who had chained themselves and staged a sit-in as part of the demonstration.

On 16 May 2022, environmental activists blocked a wind power plant construction site near Solleftea calling to stop construction works. Later, police intervened and removed the activists from the venue. One person was detained.
