On 16 May 2022, 4 members of ALG demonstrated in Dresden and blocked traffic against fossil fuels, calling for a more decisive policy against the climate crisis. Police officers intervened to remove the protesters who had glued themselves to the road.

On 17 May 2022, 3 protesters took part in a series of pickets at different locations in St. Petersburg, protesting against the Russian military invasion of Ukraine. Police intervened in the event, arresting all protesters.

On 17 May 2022, climate activists belonging to Extinction Rebellion gathered outside an oil industry conference being held at a hotel in the Mayfair area of London - Westminster to protest against the fossil fuel industry's aims to extract further fossil fuels from the African continent. Protesters glued their hands to various objects in their surroundings and displayed banners criticizing the industry. Six people were finally arrested by police.

On 18 May 2022, four environmental activists from Extinction Rebellion entered the Norwegian parliament in Oslo and glued themselves to their seats to demand the government to stop the oil exploration and to declare climate emergency. Later, police personnel removed and temporarily detained the activists.

On 19 May 2022, 3 NOD activists held pickets in Krasnoyarsk, demanding the recognition of the disintegration of the USSR into independent states as illegal. Police intervened in the event, arresting the protesters.

On 20 May 2022, an unknown number of Extinction Rebellion activists staged a protest in Rotterdam, blocking traffic at the Regentesse bridge, to demand a decrease in the use of fossil fuels. Police forces intervened and arrested 13 activists.

On 21 May 2022, Extinction Rebellion activists demonstrated against over consumption in three shopping malls in Helsinki. 13 people were detained (two people in Kamppi, six in Tripla and five in Kamp Galleria mall).

On 21 May 2022, at the call of the 'Basel Free of Nazis' group, around 30 people demonstrated against the organization of a meeting by the UDC in Basel. Police forces used tear gases to disperse them.
On 24 May 2022, activists gathered near Bitsevsky Park in Moscow, trying to stop construction works in the park. Police intervened in the event, arresting two protesters.

On 24 May 2022, an unknown number of Extinction Rebellion activists staged two protest actions in Rotterdam against the continuous governmental support for fossil fuels in the Netherlands. At the headquarters of Shell at the Weena and the Hofplein, activists glued themselves to the streets to block traffic. At the Maasvlaakte, Port of Rotterdam, activists blocked the access to the Onyx oil facility. In total 175 protesters were arrested after they refused to disperse on police order. The protests took place in the context of Extinction Rebellion's action week against fossil fuels in the Netherlands.

On 27 May 2022, about a dozen Algerian people gathered outside Palazzo Chigi in Rome - City Center (Roma, Lazio) to demonstrate against the President of Algeria while he was visiting the Prime Minister of Italy. Demonstrators threw eggs and tomatoes at the Algerian president's motorcade, hitting the windshield of the car where the president was sitting. Police intervened and tackled one of the demonstrators to the ground.

On 28 May 2022, several dozen animal rights activists belonging to the Animal Justice Project climbed onto the roof of the Farmers Market in Darlington to protest against the animal agriculture as the facility hosts the annual National Beef Association Expo. It was reported that a farmer drove a muck spreader towards a protester and one fell causing a dislocated finger. Police are investigating allegations of assault whilst 5 activists were arrested on suspicion of criminal damage.

On 30 May 2022, activists from Restore Wetlands movement blocked motorway traffic in Stockholm to demand the government to restore drained wetlands in the country. Later, police personnel removed activists from the venue. Ten people were arrested.

Around 30 May 2022 (as reported), dozens of household movement activists gathered outside the Centrale Montemartini in Rome - Ostiense (Roma, Lazio) to demonstrate against the housing crisis. Police officers in riot gear charged the demonstrators.

On 30 May 2022, 6 members of ALG demonstrated in Munchen to call for climate protection and against reliance on fossil fuels. They tried to glue themselves but were removed physically quickly by police officers.

On 30 May 2022, several members of ALG blocked traffic and demonstrated in Kempten (Allgau) to call for climate protection and an immediate stop of investments in new fossil infrastructure. Police officers intervened physically to remove the demonstrators from the road.

On 31 May 2022, residents gathered in Moscow to prevent illegal laying of communications on Efremov Street. Police arrested a Moscow Duma deputy from an opposition political party Yabloko, who joined the protesters.

On 31 May 2022, 4 members of Palestine Action staged a blockade of offices used by defense firm Elbit in the Holborn area of London - Camden to protest the company's supply of military hardware to the Israeli government. All 4 protesters were arrested at the scene.

On 1 June 2022, at least 1,000 fishers from all over Italy gathered in front of the Ministry of Agriculture in Rome - City Center (Roma, Lazio) to protest against the increase in the price of diesel fuel. After some demonstrators detonated cherry bombs in XX Settembre Square, they were charged by the police and subsequently asked to proceed in smaller groups.

Around 1 June 2022, workers at Kamila warehouse, which supplies various Coop stores throughout the region, picketed their workplace in Parma (Parma, Emilia-Romagna) to demonstrate against the lack of payment of their overtime working hours and their precarious contractual conditions. The picket, which was organized by ADL COBAS, was cleared by the police and carabinieri in riot gear, who removed demonstrators from the gate and pushed some participants.

On 1 June 2022, hundreds of people gathered for a spontaneous gathering during a vigil organized by Reclaim These Streets in Clapham Common in London - Lambeth, for murdered Sarah Everard. Met Police threatened participants with large fines and subsequently arrested several attendees whom they accuse of having participated in a gathering on March 13 2021 that broke with coronavirus restrictions.
On 2 June 2022, three protesters held pickets at different locations in Moscow, protesting against the Russian military invasion of Ukraine. Police intervened in the event, arresting all protesters.

On 2 June 2022, activists of the ORP movement gathered in Warsaw during the visit of an EU representative, demanding preservation of the EU membership and promotion of the EU-related values in Poland. At least one citizen journalist was detained.

On 2 June 2022, activists from Restore Wetlands movement blocked motorway traffic in Stockholm in connection with the UN conference Stockholm+50 and to demand the government restore drained wetlands in the country. Later, police personnel removed activists from the venue. Ten people were arrested.

On 2 June 2022, the collective 'Truth for Adama' gathered in front of the High Court of Paris to call for the release of an expert witness report that would prove the police's responsibility in the death of Adama Traore. Police forces used tear gas to disperse them.

On 2 June 2022, 25 people associated with the group Animal Rebellion, a pro-vegan animal right group, gathered for a protest, one with a poster reading 'Reclaim Royal Land,' at the Queen's Platinum Jubilee on the Mall in London - Westminster, to disrupt proceedings non-violently before the Trooping the Color ceremony, against the Crown's inaction on the climate emergency and their continued support for meat, fishing, and dairy. Mirror Police subsequently arrested four activists, one wearing a crown, for obstructing the highway and dragged them out after they broke past security and sat down in the path of the parade.

On 2 June 2022, people gathered outside the Queen Elizabeth House in Edinburgh to protest the use of a new gas field. The rally was organized by Just Stop Oil and six people were arrested by the police. Demonstrators also threw red paint over the building and painted 'Blood on your hands' on the building.
On 2 June 2022, members of ALG occupied the University of Hamburg in Hamburg - Eimsbuttel (Hamburg) to call for climate protection. Police officers intervened to evacuate the demonstrators.

On 3 June 2022, about 1000 activists gathered for a rally and a march in Prague, criticizing the government and demanding its resignation. Minor skirmishes with the police occurred and one activist was detained.

On 4 June 2022, 4 protesters participated in pickets at different locations in Moscow, protesting against the Russian military invasion of Ukraine. Police intervened in the event, arresting all protesters.

On 4 June 2022, several persons threw what seemed to be whipped cream at the former Minister of National Education (Renaissance, ex LREM) on the occasion of his visit to Montargis, as part of his campaign as a running candidate for the 2022 legislative elections. Two of the perpetrators were later arrested and identified as teachers who acted to denounce the policy implemented under his mandate as a Minister.

On 4 June 2022, 6 women ran onto the track at the Epsom Derby in Epsom to protest animal abuse and cruelty in the horseracing industry. The police removed the demonstrators from the track. The protest was organized by Animal Rebellion.

On 8 June 2022, during a conference organized by a public-private oil company, eight students and members of Fridays for Future, Legambiente, Extinction Rebellion and Last Generation demonstrated against the company's policies on sustainability, in front of La Sapienza University of Rome, in Rome - Tiburtino (Roma, Lazio). Police forces physically intervened to suppress the demonstration - there were no casualties.

On 8 June 2022, climate activists from Groups Climaximo and Scientist Rebellion staged a protest and interrupted a conference in Lisbon (Lisboa) in which Environment Minister Duarte Cordeiro was speaking to protest about climate change. Police forces phisically pushed protesters outside the room.

On 9 June 2022, 3 protesters participated in pickets at different locations in Moscow, protesting against the Russian military invasion of Ukraine. Police intervened in the event, arresting all protesters.

On 9 June 2022, a group of people gathered outside the Lefroy House building in Dublin (Dublin City) to support the protestors inside the building who were protesting at the manner properties were left unoccupied during a housing crisis. At least two protestors were arrested.

On 10 June 2022, environmental activists took over the highway in Cascina Gobba neighborhood in Milano - Municipio 3 (Milano, Lombardia), and demonstrated against government policies of ecological transition, complaining about delays and imperfections in their implementation. Police forces intervened to suppress the demonstration, and there were no casualties.

On 11 June 2022, about 200 to hundreds of people gathered in the neighborhood of Peckham in London - Southwark to protest an immigration raid that led to the detention of one Nigerian man. Demonstrators blocked traffic with their bodies. According to demonstrators, the police pushed demonstrators to clear roads and attempted to arrest demonstrators, resulting in minor injuries. Members of Stand up to Racism were present. There were no arrests.

On 11 June 2022, a dozen 'Last Renovation' environmental group activists blocked the bridge of Neuilly in Paris to demand a law on the energy renovation of buildings in France. Police forces were deployed to arrest 9 of them.
On 12 June 2022, 3 anti-war protesters staged pickets at different locations in Moscow, due to the military invasion of Ukraine. Police intervened, arresting all protesters.
On 12 June 2022, 3 anti-war protesters staged pickets in the center of Samara, due to the military invasion of Ukraine. Police intervened, arresting all protesters.
On 12 June 2022, 4 anti-war protesters staged pickets at different locations in St. Petersburg, due to the military invasion of Ukraine. Police intervened, arresting all protesters.

On 13 June 2022, around 50 people gathered in Norrebro district of Copenhagen to oppose the demolition works of a local municipal housing complex. Demonstrators attempted to occupy the housing complex but were later removed by the police personnel.

On 13 June 2022, about 20 to 50 people blockaded the entrances to a nuclear weapons base in Coulport to protest the use of nuclear weapons and to call for disarmament. Members of CND Scotland, Faslane Action for the Bomb Ban, Trident Ploughshares, and Extinction Rebellion were present. The police arrested 3 people for blocking the entrance to the base.

On 13 June 2022, members of Palestine Action blocked the entrance and occupied the roof of an Arconic manufacturing plant in Birmingham, causing a 'small amount of damage' to the building while climbing on top of it according to the police, to denounce the use of the company's metal production in the manufacture of military aircrafts sold to Israel. Demonstrators also claimed Arconic metals were responsible for the Grenfell Tower fire on 14 June 2017. The police arrested 5 people for criminal damage to the building.

On 13 June 2022, six environmental activists sat and blocked traffic in Trondheim to demand to stop oil exploration and action on the climate emergency. Later, all the activists were detained by the police.

On 14 June 2022, people, including members of Stop Deportations, gathered and blockaded Colnbrook Immigration Removal Centre in London - Hillingdon to protest a policy that would deport asylum seekers and illegal migrants to Rwanda. The police arrested two to nine people on the scene.

On 14 June 2022, dozens of people, including members of Stop Deportations, gathered and blockaded an immigration center in Manston to protest a policy that would deport asylum seekers and illegal migrants to Rwanda. The police arrested two people.

On 14 June 2022, at the call Extinction Rebellion and the collective 'Stop Cruises', around 20 activists used small boats to block the access to the port of Marseille preventing the arrival of cruises they consider are causing environmental pollution. Gendarmerie naval forces were deployed to disperse them and arrested one activist.

On 14 June 2022, four environmental activists sat and blocked traffic in Nardo, Trondheim to demand to stop oil exploration and action on the climate emergency. Later, all the activists were detained by the police.

On 15 June 2022, environmental activists sat and blocked highway traffic in Trondheim to demand to stop oil exploration and declaration of a climate emergency. Later, all the activists were detained by the police.

On 16 June 2022, Extinction Rebellion activists entered and demonstrated in Gothenburg (Goteborg) Municipality building to demand to reduce use of fossil fuels and to declare climate emergency. Later, police personnel removed and temporarily detained the activists.

On 17 June 2022, Animal Rebellion activists attempted to demonstrate during Prime Minister Mette Frederiksen's speech in Allinge-Sandvig (Bornholm) and were detained by the police. The protesters called to ban animal agriculture, to switch to plant-based diets and to declare climate emergency.

On 17 June 2022, environmental activists sat and blocked highway traffic in Trondheim to demand to stop oil exploration and declaration of a climate emergency. Later, all the activists were detained by the police.

On 17 June 2022, around 100 activists from Extinction Rebellion blocked an entrance to an oil port in Gothenburg (Goteborg) to demand to reduce use of fossil fuels and to declare climate emergency. Concurrently, a group of people in boats and kayaks attempted to block ships at sea. The activists were later detained by the police.

On 18 June 2022, environmental activists took over the highway and demonstrated to raise awareness on issues related to climate change, in Rome (Roma, Lazio). Police forces intervened, dragging the demonstrators to the side of the highway.
On 18 June 2022, several activists sat on a road in Wroclaw and blocked it, demanding protection of the climate. Law enforcers removed them from the road.

On 18 June 2022, Extinction Rebellion activists stood and blocked traffic in Gothenburg (Goteborg) to demand to reduce use of fossil fuels and to declare climate emergency in the country. Later, police personnel removed activists from the venue, several people were detained.

On 18 June 2022, about 150 people demonstrated in Amsterdam (Noord-Holland) against police violence. According to the police, protesters committed vandalism, put stickers on cars, threw cans and sprayed graffiti on walls. When officers called them on their behavior, some of the protesters turned against the police (although the report does not provide further details on what exactly happened). The officers then used their batons but did not arrest anyone.

On 19 June 2022, 23 members of Rouvikonas protested outside the Ministry of Justice in Athens - Central Athens, scattering fliers in support of a jailed anarchist on hunger strike, and they were detained.

On 20 June 2022, 'Last Renovation' environmental activists blocked a road in Boulogne-Billancourt to demand a law on the energy renovation of buildings in France. Police forces were deployed and arrested a number of them.

On 20 June 2022, environmental activists from Last Generation chained themselves and blocked traffic on the GRA beltway (Grande Raccordo Anulare) in Rome (Roma, Lazio) to demonstrate against the continued use of gas and coal as energy sources. The police removed the protesters from the beltway. Several demonstrators were arrested.

On 20 June 2022, four environmental activists sat and blocked highway traffic in Trondheim to demand to stop oil exploration and declare a climate emergency. Later, all the activists were detained by the police.

On 20 June 2022, around 80 people, including ALG members, demonstrated in Berlin to call for more climate protection. Demonstrators called on the government to implement concrete solutions to tackle climate change. 5 people blocked several highway exits in western Berlin. Around 75 people were arrested.

On 21 June 2022, Animal Rebellion activists blocked an entrance to a dairy products company's distribution center in Ishoj to demand to ban animal agriculture, to switch to plant-based diets and to declare climate emergency. Later, police personnel removed the activists from the venue. Eight people were arrested in connection with the incident.

On 21 June 2022, around 50 Extinction Rebellion activists blocked traffic twice in central Helsinki, calling attention to the climate crisis. Police dispersed the protests. 19 people were detained for not following police orders.

On 21 June 2022, environmental activists sat and blocked highway traffic in Oslo to demand to stop oil exploration and declare a climate emergency. Later, all the activists were detained by the police.

On 22 June 2022, residents gathered in St. Petersburg, protesting against the construction of alluvial territories in the northern part of Vasilyevsky Island. Police arrested one protester, who was released on the same day.

On 22 June 2022, five environmental activists took over the highway and demonstrated to raise awareness on issues related to climate change, in Rome (Roma, Lazio). Police forces intervened, dragging the demonstrators to the side of the highway.

On 22 June 2022, Animal Rebellion activists blocked an entrance to a dairy products company's distribution center in Ishoj to demand to ban animal agriculture, to switch to plant-based diets and to declare climate emergency. Later, police personnel removed the activists from the venue.

On 22 June 2022, environmental activists sat and blocked highway traffic in Oslo to demand to stop oil exploration and declare a climate emergency. Later, all the activists were detained by the police.

On 23 June 2022, ten animal rights activists from Animal Rebellion blocked an entrance to a dairy products company's distribution center in Ishoj to demand to ban animal agriculture, to switch to plant-based diets and to declare climate emergency. The activists were later detained by the police.

On 24 June 2022, around 10 Extinction Rebellion activists took over the highway and demonstrated against continued government subsidies for fossil fuels, in Rome (Roma, Lazio). Police forces intervened, dragging the demonstrators to the side of the highway and arresting them.

On 25 June 2022, a dozen members of an environmental group carried out a road blockade in Paris (Ile-de-France). They called for a bill on renewable energy for buildings and used glue to stick their hands on the ground. The BRAV-M intervened, removing the glue from their hands and moving them behind the security barriers, while no injuries nor fatalities were reported.

On 26 June 2022, activists gathered for a rally in Inowroclaw, protesting against a visit of the head of the ruling party to the city. Law enforcers pushed them out of the road and used tear gas against some of them.

On 26 June 2022, between 800 (according to the police) and 2,000 (according to organizers) people, including IB, and MLPD members, demonstrated in Garmisch-Partenkirchen near Elmau Castle against the ongoing G7 Summit and imperialism. Among the central themes of the rally were the climate crisis and fears of an escalation of the Ukraine war. The event was organized by the Alliance 'Stop G7 Elmau'. 4 people were arrested.

On 27 June 2022, 5 environmental activists from Last Generation organization gathered on the GRA beltway (Grande Raccordo Anulare) in Rome (Roma, Lazio) with the intention to block the traffic to demonstrate against the continued use of gas and coal as energy sources. The DIGOS police prevented them from blocking the road and took them to the police station.

On 27 June 2022, around 150 people, including hikers, a Japanese monk, and cyclists demonstrated in Garmisch-Partenkirchen against the ongoing G7 Summit at the Elmau castle. Demonstrators called for climate protection. 6 people were arrested for doing a sit-in.

On 28 June 2022, employees of Kib-Tek, the Turkish Cypriot Electricity Authority, protested in Nicosia during a meeting with the president of EL-SEN, the Turkish Cypriot Electricity Authority Employees' Union. They started shouting slogans and demanded the resignation of the union president. Police removed the protesters who would not leave the premises.

On 29 June 2022, 26 farmers from the farms of the Valhondo de Caceres Foundation, and ASAJA members, entered the Caceres City Council in Caceres (Extremadura) during the plenary session, laid on the ground and blew whistles to protest against the intention to put all the foundation's farms up for auction. Protesters were removed by police forces.

On 29 June 2022, about 30 people gathered for a demonstration organized by members of the Durham People's Assembly, Abolish Detention, No To Hassockfield and Women for Refugee Women, outside Derwentside Immigration Centre in Consett, in order to prevent the removal of women from the UK to Nigeria. 5 protesters were arrested on suspicion of blocking the highway.

On 29 June 2022, 'Last Renovation' environmental activists blocked the A13 highway near the Auteuil entrance in Paris (Ile-de-France) to demand a law on the energy renovation of buildings in France. Police forces, including the BRAV-M, were deployed and evacuated a number of them.

On 29 June 2022, an unknown number of people associated with Just Stop Oil, including some students, gathered for a protest at the Kelvingrove Art Gallery and Museum in Glasgow, to call for art institutions to join the group in 'civil resistance' against climate change. 5 protesters were arrested after they glued their hands to the frame of a painting in the art gallery and spray-painted the group's logo on the walls and floor of the art gallery, causing the museum to close early.

On 29 June 2022, activists affiliated with the 'Last Generation' ('Ultima Generazione') campaign took blocked the GRA highway near Portuense Street near Magliana Vecchia (Roma, Lazio) to raise awareness on issues related to climate change. Police forces intervened, dragging the demonstrators to the side of the highway.

On 29 June 2022, about 25 Extinction Rebellion activists staged a protest in the Tax Service in Den Haag (Zuid-Holland), occupying the building to denounce governmental financial support for fossil fuels. Police forces intervened and arrested 22 activists.

On 30 June 2022, 43 people, members of ALG, demonstrated and blocked traffic on several roads (A111, A100, A113) in Berlin to call for climate protection. Demonstrators said that a demonstrator was kicked to the head by police officers who pushed and shoved them. The victim suffered a broken collarbone and a mild concussion, and the police confirmed that one demonstrator was injured.
On 3 July 2022, 3 anti-war protesters staged pickets at different locations in Moscow, due to the military invasion of Ukraine. Police intervened, arresting all protesters.

On 3 July 2022, activists gathered in Kielce, protesting against the visit of the ruling party representatives to the city. Members of KOD and ORP movements participated. Several of them were detained.

On 3 July 2022, 6 Just Stop Oil activists stormed the track of the Formula 1 British Grand Prix in Silverstone (England) as part of a demonstration calling for the end of fossil fuels. Protesters were dragged away from the track by race marshals and subsequently arrested by the police.

On 3 July 2022, around 50 people, including members of 'Smash Cruiseshit' (SC) demonstrated in Kiel, on the waters of the Kiel Fjord, and blocked 3 cruise ships to denounce the climate-damaging consequences of cruise tourism, neocolonialism, and exploitation at work in cruise ships. Police officers intervened, bringing some activists ashore and seizing some of the ships used during the demonstration.

On 4 July 2022, three protesters - a mother and her two adult children - staged pickets in Elista, protesting against the infringements of the freedom of speech. All were arrested and charged with administrative offenses.

On 4 July 2022, citizens held a protest in Sevilla (Andalucia) to denounce the rise in the price of electricity, as well as the blackouts that many residents are suffering this summer. The National Police arrested one of the protesters for resistance and serious disobedience.

On 4 July 2022, an unknown number of farmers staged a protest action along the A67 highway, blocking traffic in Hapert to denounce the new Dutch nitrogen policy and its impact on their sector. Police forces intervened and arrested one protester.

On 4 July 2022, around 5 vehicles staged a protest action on the A2 highway in Born, blocking traffic to support the farmer protests against the new Dutch nitrogen policy and its impact on their sector. Police forces intervened and arrested 2 people.

On 4 July 2022, an unknown number of farmers staged a protest action in Sneek, blocking access to the supermarket distribution center of Poiesz to denounce the new Dutch nitrogen policy and its impact on their sector. Upon the arrival of police forces, the protesters, whom a lot of non-farmers had joined, refused to leave. During a police intervention to disperse the crowd, 4 people were arrested.

On 4 July 2022, an unknown number of farmers staged two protest actions in Zwolle, blocking access to the distribution centers of Albert Heijn and Jumbo to denounce the new Dutch nitrogen policy and its impact on their sector. Around 200 people assembled at the Albert Heijn distribution center at the Galvaniweg, where 6 people were arrested after police forces intervened to break up the blockade in the evening.

On 4 July 2022, 5 Palestine Action activists chained themselves to the gates of an industrial facility owned by UAV Engines in Shenstone to protest the production of defense hardware, which they claimed was being used by the Israeli military against Palestinian civilians. All five activists were arrested on suspicion of aggravated trespass and criminal damage.

On 4 July 2022, cost of living activists staged a 'go-slow' protest on the M4 road near Caldicot to call on the government to lower fuel costs as the price of petrol increases. Police arrested 12 demonstrators for breaching a legal notice prohibiting prolonged slow driving.

On 4 July 2022, around 30 members of ALG demonstrated in Berlin - Charlottenburg-Wilmersdorf and blocked traffic at the at the Seestrasse/Beusselstrasse exit on highway 100 and at the level of the Goerdelersteg to call for more climate protection. Around 5 demonstrators glued themselves on the highway (A100) and were arrested.

On 5 July 2022, 20 activists concentrated in the Florida neighborhood in Alicante (Valencia) in front of a house to stop an eviction by preventing the access of police agents. Activists showed resistance and threw themselves to the ground to prevent the agents from removing them from the door of the house.

On 5 July 2022, a big group of farmers staged a protest at the Lidl supermarket distribution center in Heerenveen to denounce the new Dutch nitrogen policy, blocking all access to the facility. Later that day, a large police force assembled and forced the protesters to go home. A group of farmers continued towards the A32 in Heerenveen in an attempt to continue the action there. The police forces tried to block the tractors from entering the highway. A police officer fired live ammunition at a tractor, when a 16-year-old farmer tried to pass the police blockade with his vehicle. Three people were arrested.

On 5 July 2022, 4 climate activists belonging to Just Stop Oil staged a demonstration at the Royal Academy art gallery in London - Westminster, gluing their hands to Da Vinci's The Last Supper, in protest against the continued operation of fossil fuel industries. The activists were arrested on suspicion of causing criminal damage.

On 6 July 2022, an unknown number of farmers staged a protest action in Bleiswijk, blocking access to the distribution centers of Albert Heijn and Hoogvliet to denounce the new Dutch nitrogen policy and its impact on their sector. Police forces intervened and arrested up to 19 protesters.

On 6 July 2022, 3 members of Extinction Rebellion demonstrated in Bregenz and glued themselves on the road to draw attention to the climate emergency. Police officers intervened to remove the demonstrators.

On 6 July 2022, an unknown number of Extinction Rebellion activists staged a protest on the A12 road, as well as on the Malieveld, in Den Haag (Zuid-Holland), blocking traffic, to call on the government to stop subsidizing fossil fuels and related projects. Police forces intervened and arrested between 15 and 20 protesters blocking the A12 road.

On 7 July 2022, about 35 health workers, who were suspended from their jobs because they were not vaccinated for the coronavirus, marched to the private home of the Prime Minister in Athens - Central Athens and were detained by police.

On 7 July 2022, 3 teenage anti-war activists staged a protest in front of the local administration in Smolensk, due to the military invasion of Ukraine. Police intervened, arresting one of the protesters, who was holding a sign, and another person who stopped to talk to him.

On 7 July 2022, environmental activists protested in Zagreb against expanding the LNG terminal for liquid. The police intervened, arresting one activist despite not displaying violent behavior during the protests.

On 8 July 2022, about 150 activists gathered for a rally in Prague, declaring their support to Russia during the current war against Ukraine and protesting against the government's support to Kyiv. At least one activist was detained for displaying a tattooed svastika.

On 8 July 2022, an unknown number of farmers blocked a road intersection in Hoogeveen (Drenthe) to protest against the new nitrogen regulations of the Dutch government. As the protesters refused to leave, the police intervened and physically removed the protesters, though no detention or arrest was specified.

On 8 July 2022, in the morning, members of ALG demonstrated and blocked traffic at several highway exits in Berlin - Steglitz-Zehlendorf to call for climate protection. Eight demonstrators were temporarily arrested and checked by the police.

On 8 July 2022, ALG activists demonstrated and blocked traffic at the Sachsendamm highway exit in Berlin - Tempelhof-Schoneberg to call for climate protection. Some demonstrators were temporarily arrested and checked by the police.

On 9 July 2022, five Extinction Rebellion activists protested at an ING branch in Almere city center (Flevoland) as part of a national action against the bank's financing of the fossil fuel industry. Two were arrested for refusing to leave. The protest was part of a broader movement involving actions in 20 cities, including Amsterdam and Nijmegen.

On 9 July 2022, Last Renovation environmental activists blocked a road near Porte de Sevres in Paris to call on authorities to improve the energy efficiency of buildings. Police forces were deployed to disperse them.

On 9 July 2022, people gathered outside the Coca-Cola factory in Nogara (Verona, Veneto) at the call of Rise Up 4 Climate Justice and ADL COBAS to protest against the factory's water consumption considering the period of drought. They also demonstrated against the price paid by Coca-Cola for the use of water, which they regarded as too low. The police charged the demonstrators, who were approaching the factory's gates. No one was reported injured.

On 9 July 2022, an unknown number of Extinction Rebellion activists occupied the ING bank office in Alkmaar to denounce the bank's investments in fossil fuels. Police forces ended the action, arresting at least one activist.

On 9 July 2022, around 100 activists from the environmental movement Climaximo protested outside the Sines Galp refinery in Sines (Setubal) to demand the gradual closure by 2025 of the refinery, responsible for the largest amount of CO2 emissions in Portugal, and the guarantee of employment for all workers. Around a dozen activists were detained by the police forces after jumping the wall and entering the premises.

On 9 July 2022, 7 XR activists occupied an ING bank office in Den Bosch (Noord-Brabant) to denounce the bank's investments in fossil fuels. Five activists who stayed after the bank's closing time were arrested by the police.

On 9 July 2022, 5 XR activists occupied an ING bank office in Den Haag (Zuid-Holland) to denounce the bank's investments in fossil fuels. One activist who refused to leave the premises was arrested by the police.
On 9 July 2022, 4 XR activists occupied an ING bank office in Utrecht (Utrecht) to denounce the bank's investments in fossil fuels. Three activists were arrested by the police for trespass.

On 9 July 2022, around 10 members of ALG demonstrated in front of the German Chancellor's Office in Berlin - Mitte to call for more climate protection and against fossil oil energies. Demonstrators were arrested by police officers after having dumped black paint on a lawn.

On 9 July 2022, an unknown number of Extinction Rebellion activists occupied an ING bank office in Nijmegen to denounce the bank's investments in fossil fuels. Police forces ended the action, arresting 5 activists.
On 10 July 2022, several dozen nationalist activists gathered for a rally in Brno, demanding a removal of a flag of Ukraine from a local statue. Law enforcers detained several of them.

On 11 July 2022, around 50 residents staged a protest in Sagasi-Deibuk, Dagestan, against the plans of the local administration to supply technical water to the new kindergarten. Police tried to arrest several protesters, which resulted in skirmishes.

On 11 July 2022, more than 60 climate activists belonging to Extinction Rebellion continued an occupy-style demonstration at a mine in Glynneath after gaining access to the site office and scaling its roof the previous night. Activists criticized the Welsh Government for its lack of communication with the public over its provision of a license to extract 42 million tonnes of anthracite coal from the mine. The demonstration was brought to an end with 7 arrests being made for trespassing offenses.

On 11 July 2022, around 40 members of ALG blocked traffic, glued themselves to roads in 5 different places, and demonstrated in Berlin - Charlottenburg-Wilmersdorf (around the road A100) for better climate protection and a coal phase-out. 24 people were arrested. One refuse worker affected by one of the roadblocks grabbed a female climate activist from the group and pulled her off the road.

On 12 July 2022, 9 Last Renovation activists blocked the ring road, waving flares, to interrupt the Tour de France race in Cluses. They sought to raise awareness about the dangers of global warming. Gendarmerie forces were deployed and arrested them.

On 13 July 2022, around 2.000 people, including small entrepreneurs and MKKP members, including the vice-mayor of the 9th district of Budapest, Momentum MPs and district council members, and the Budapest vice-mayor, a Momentum MEP, as well as PDSZ and Extinction Rebellion members, marched from Oktogon square to the Karmelita government building and then finished the march by blocking the Elizabeth bridge in Budapest in protest to the change of the fiscal regime for small entrepreneurs, freelancers, and self-employed people. At least 3 people were arrested for a short time, including a man accused of throwing a chain at police and two MKKP leaders.

On 13 July 2022, 10 people demonstrated in front of an airbase in Norvenich, denouncing the alleged storage of nuclear weapons in the area. Some demonstrators attempted to enter the air base grounds by climbing over a fence. Police forces intervened to stop them. The rest of the gathering was reported as peaceful.

On 14 July 2022, 2.000-3.000 people, including small entrepreneurs and MKKP members, including the vice-mayor of the 9th district of Budapest, a 2nd district council member, the independent mayor of Hodmezovasarhely, and the MSZP mayor of the 14th district of Budapest, protested in Budapest - V, by blocking the Elizabeth bridge in protest to the change of the fiscal regime for small entrepreneurs, freelancers, and self-employed people. Police arrested at least 3 people for a short time. One protester threw a bag of garbage at a police car.

On 14 July 2022, members of the Yellow Vests movement participated in a static demonstration in Paris. They called for social and fiscal justice on the occasion of the French national day. Demonstrators were pushed by police forces after they had formed a cordon to prevent demonstrators from taking part in a march.

On 16 July 2022, 'Last Renovation' environmental activists blocked a road in Porte d'Orleans at the entrance of Paris to call on authorities to take measures against global warming. Police forces were deployed to disperse them, arresting 14 people.

On 17 July 2022, 7 detainees in a pre-trial detention center in Volsk (SIZO no. 2) staged a protest against the beatings, to which they were subject on the previous day by the prison guards. At 1 am, the protesters started making loud noises in their cells in a coordinated way, and one of them cut himself. The guards intervened, using force against the detainees.

On 17 July 2022, an unknown number of people staged a protest action at the border crossing with Germany in Bad Nieuweschans, blocking traffic with their cars to support ongoing farmers' protests. The protesters carried reversed Dutch flags and farmers' handkerchiefs. Later on, the group moved on to Winschoten, where a roundabout was blocked. Police forces arrested one person there.

On 17 July 2022, climate activists belonging to Extinction Rebellion marched through central Plymouth to the Valero Fuel Depot in the Cattedown area of the city to protest against the continued use of fossil fuels. Police stopped protesters from entering the depot, enforcing an injunction against such protests on the site.

On 17 July 2022, 6 healthcare workers belonging to Extinction Rebellion gathered outside JP Morgan offices in London - Tower Hamlets to protest against JP Morgan's role in financing fossil fuel industries. All six activists were arrested by police.

On 18 July 2022, around 500 people protested in Budapest - V, with the leading by Momentum MPs, a Momentum Budapest vice-mayor, MKKP, a Parbeszed MP, and an independent MP, against the tax regime imposed for small entrepreneurs. Food delivery workers and Extinction Rebellion activists joined the rally. The police used an electric shocker against 2 protesters, while trying to unblock the Margaret bridge. Five people were arrested for a short time.

On 18 July 2022, several hundreds of residents staged a protest against frequent power outages in Makhachkala, blocking a road. Police tried to disperse protesters with tear gas. 11 protesters were arrested and charged with minor hooliganism.

On 19 July 2022, Varos a Mindenkie activists protested outside a district-owned house in Budapest - XV, holding a live chain to oppose the evacuation of a family. The police used an electric shocker against one of the protesters.

On 19 July 2022, 7 climate activists staged a protest action in Den Haag (Zuid-Holland), jumping into the Hofvijver pond, to denounce the lack of governmental action against climate change in the context of record-high temperatures recorded in Western Europe that day. Police forces picked up some activists who refused to swim to the shore with boats and fined them. The activists were members of XR, Fossil Free Netherlands, and International Socialists.

On 20 July 2022, 5 people associated with Just Stop Oil gathered for a protest and scaled motorway signs on the M25 [coded as Longford] in response to the extreme temperatures in the UK and the Government's 'inadequate preparations' for climate change. They climbed signs at junction 10 eastbound near Cobham, Surrey, the Poyle interchange at Heathrow between junctions 14 and 15, and in Dartford between the Queen Elizabeth Bridge northbound and junction 30. Police were forced to close the roads, causing traffic delays, and arrested all 5 protesters.

On 22 July 2022, 6 Last Renovation activists briefly interrupted the 19th stage of the Tour de France cycling race on a road in Lasseube-Propre to demand more climate action and building renovation measures from the government. One activist lit a flare to warn cyclists of an upcoming road blockade, which was staged by five activists sitting in the middle of the road, chained by their ankles to each other. The race resumed after 10 minutes, after gendarmes dragged activists away from the road.

On 22 July 2022, 6 environmental activists gathered for a demonstration in Fleurance, during the Tour de France, in support of the environment. The activists linked themselves by chain and sat down on the roadway to prevent the bikers from passing. Police arrested the 6 individuals.

On 22 July 2022, three Ultima Generazione activists glued themselves to a Botticelli painting in the Uffizi museum in Florence (Firenze, Toscana), to demand more climate action. They were taken away for identification by Carabinieri officers.

On 23 July 2022, activists of the Calea Neamului group protested during a speech of the Hungarian PM Viktor Orban in Baile Tusnad, shouting slogans against Hungarian revisionism towards Transylvania. The protesters were shortly removed by the police.

On 23 July 2022, 6 people demonstrated on the airplane runaways of the airport in Biarritz at the call of the AP and Bake Bidea organizations. They called for the release of two elderly ETA Basque political prisoners and denounced their detention conditions for the last 32 years. The police arrested them.

On 23 July 2022, 9 people chained themselves to train tracks in Bayonne with the aim to stop the traffic at the call of the AP and Bake Bidea organizations. They called for the release of two elderly ETA Basque political prisoners and denounced their detention conditions for the last 32 years. The police arrested them.

On 24 July 2022, residents staged a protest in Noginsk against the head of the Noginskiy district, because, according to the protesters, he beat up a local veteran. Police intervened, arresting 4 protesters.
On 24 July 2022, activists gathered for a flowers-laying ceremony in Moscow to commemorate the victims of the Russian military invasion of Ukraine. Police intervened, arresting 8 activists.

On 24 July 2022, several SOR party supporters and members, including MPs and a district council president, as well as a PCRM MP, protested outside the Prosecutor General's Office in Chisinau - Centru, condemning the actions of the prosecutors regarding SOR officials. The police arrested several participants who tried to install tents in front of the building.

On 25 July 2022, underage refugees in the refugee camp for minors in Pafos, who were demanding a daily allowance for transport costs among other issues, attempted to resist when they were prevented from protesting on the road blocking traffic, but withdrew soon after.

On 28 July 2022, around 30 farmers threw up a roadblock on the A18 highway in Westendorp, parking their tractors on the road and dumping garbage on the tarmac, to denounce the new nitrogen policy of the Dutch government. One person was arrested by intervening police forces.

On 28 July 2022, police forces cleared the former Omero high school, an occupied building in the Bruzzano neighborhood of Milano - Municipio 9 (Milano, Lombardia). The building had been occupied by the Ri-Make collective. Around 10 people were taken away. There were no clashes.

On 30 July 2022, around 80 people, mostly Antifa members, demonstrated in Kampen (Sylt) against far-right movements and an announced (but ultimately canceled) rally of far-right members. Some demonstrators who were occupying private property were evacuated by the police. The occupiers call themselves 'Black-Red 1st May'.

On 30 July 2022, around 50 residents gathered in Nizhnekamsk, protesting against cutting down local forests to build a highway. The protest was co-organized by a member of the Communist Party. The event was interrupted by a local deputy, after which police demanded the protesters leave the area and arrested several of them.

On 1 August 2022, in the late evening, a dozen people, including at least two farmers, staged a protest action on a bridge over the A7 highway in Marum against the Dutch government and its coronavirus and agricultural policy. Two people were arrested after insulting surveilling police forces.

On 1 August 2022, an unknown number of people staged a protest at the city hall of Almelo against the municipal decision to remove a graffiti in the city center displaying a reversed Dutch flag, a symbol of the recent farmer protests in the Netherlands. During the demonstration, the leader of the Viruswaarheid action group was present. When the protesters refused to go home at the agreed-upon time, the atmosphere turned tense, resulting in 4 arrests.

On 1 August 2022, between 1,200 (according to the police) and 5,700 (according to organizers) people, including Querdenken members, students and alleged pro-Russian demonstrators opposed to Germany's military support of Ukraine amid the ongoing war, demonstrated in Berlin - Mitte from the Reichstag building through several districts of City East back to the seat of the Bundestag, against coronavirus-related measures and for the release of the founder of the 'Querdenken' movement, calling for more democracy, self-determination, and freedom, and chanting slogans such as 'Lying Press'. One person was temporarily arrested for denigrating deceased people. They gathered on the occasion of the 2nd anniversary of the 1st nationwide Querdenken demonstration, on 1 August 2020.

On 2 August 2022, activists gathered for a rally in Borovany, protesting against a visit of a controversial politician to the city. Minor skirmishes with the bystanding supporters of the politician were reported and one person was detained by police.

On 2 August 2022, a demonstrator was arrested by the police while taking part in a multi-day picket over unfair wages and working conditions organized by GMB outside Amey depot in Frimley. The reasons for the arrest were not specified.

On 2 August 2022, climate activists from the Fast Action Response Team protested by occupying ExxonMobil pipelines under the M25 highway near Wisley to denounce the project, citing environmental concerns. Protesters occupied a number of tunnels related to the project and police forces intervened to stop the occupation.

On 3 August 2022, activists gathered for a rally in Cesky Krumlov, protesting against a visit of a controversial politician to the city. Minor skirmishes with the bystanding supporters of the politician were reported and one person was detained by police.

On 4 August 2022, people protested outside of a library in Hove ahead of the Drag Queen Story Hour event for children and called for canceling the event. An unknown number of people also gathered in support of the LGBTQ+ community and the event. Police forces arrested two citizens who were protesting in favor of the event after they got 'into an altercation' with anti-drag protesters.

On 5 August 2022, a group of six individuals disturbed an event organized by environmental activists (Extinction Rebellion) in Jyvaskyla and sprayed liquid manure over them. Law enforcers detained them.

On 7 August 2022, 300 No MUOS activists gathered in Niscemi (Caltanissetta, Sicilia) to demand the dismantling of three local antennas of the US navy's satellite transmission system. Police officers in riot gear and DIGOS officers quelled the protest with water cannons and allegedly with tear gas containing CS gas. .

On 8 August 2022, law enforcers dispersed a permanent camp organized by environmental groups in a protected area in the Rzeszow district and detained at least some of the people present. The activists had been on the spot for several months, effectively preventing cutting trees in the area.
On 8 August 2022, three activists staged a series of anti-war pickets in St. Petersburg, because of the Russian military invasion of Ukraine. Police arrested all protesters.

On 10 August 2022, riot police guarding a construction crew used tear gas at protesting demonstrators against the construction of a metro station at Exarchia square in Athens - Central Athens. The protesters attempted to block the site when the contractor's crew cut tree branches before setting up a fence. Local residents and others also tried to block a crew of surveyors in Strefi Hill, adjacent to Exarchia, who were taking measurements for the redevelopment of the hill and confronted them verbally. Police detained 19 people. Anarchist and leftist groups oppose state presence and commercial activity in the area.

On 13 August 2022, Hard Line (Stram Kurs) party members, including the party leader Rasmus Paludan, staged an anti-Islamic demonstration in Norrliden, Kalmar, where they were met by a group of counter-protesters. Police personnel were present at the venue of the protest to ensure the security of the event. Two individuals were arrested following an attempt to throw stones at the activists.

On 13 August 2022, around 30 people, including members of Extinction Rebellion, blocked traffic on the Kohlbrand Bridge in Hamburg - Hamburg-Mitte (Hamburg) and glued themselves on the road to draw attention to the consequences of modern colonialism and for climate protection. Police intervened to remove them.

On 15 August 2022, Ultima Generazione activists glued their hands to the dolphin tanks at Genoa Aquarium (Genova, Liguria) to protest against the reopening of decommissioned coal-fired power plants and plans for new drilling for natural gas exploration and extraction, and to demand an increase in the use of renewable energy. Police officers intervened to quell the protest and brought away the activists.

On 17 August 2022, around 30 activists from Restore Wetlands and Extinction Rebellion blocked motorway traffic in Stockholm to demand the government to restore drained wetlands in the country. Later, police personnel removed activists from the road.

On 17 August 2022, Extinction Rebellion activists staged traffic blockades in various locations of Stockholm, demanding to abolish government subsidies to fossil fuel-related companies, to declare a climate emergency, and to draw attention to the climate crisis. A total of 12 people were arrested at the event.
On 18 August 2022, 3 anti-war protesters staged a series of pickets at different locations in Moscow, because of the Russian military invasion of Ukraine. Police arrested all protesters.

On 18 August 2022, around 15 people demonstrated in the Alma neighborhood of Roubaix. They denounced a police operation where police officers seized quad bikes used in illegal motorbike 'rodeo' rides. The police made one arrest.

On 18 August 2022, three Extinction Rebellion activists demonstrated during a political debate at a political event in Arendal, demanding to declare a climate emergency. All the three people were arrested and removed from the venue.

On 18 August 2022, Extinction Rebellion activists stood and blocked traffic in Stockholm demanding to declare a climate emergency and call for the national broadcasters to pay more attention to the climate crisis. Later, police personnel removed activists from the road.

On 20 August 2022, the Alliance of Nationalists held a 188 Kukkavirta-named protest in Turku to commemorate a knife attack that took place there five years ago, carrying Finnish flags and 'White lives matter' banners. At the same time, several tens of anti-fascist activists held a Turku Without Nazis named protest as a counter-demonstration, demonstrating against fascism. Two people were briefly detained by the police for security reasons.

On 21 August 2022, 3 Last Generation activists chained themselves to a balustrade in the Scrovegni Chapel in Padua (Padova, Veneto) to demonstrate against the waste of water and energy. The police tried to convince the activists to interrupt the protest, then, seeing their refusal, they cut the chains with shears and physically took the demonstrators away.

On 22 August 2022, about 50 people gathered in Pardaugava near a Soviet monument in Riga, Latvia calling against the Latvian government's decision to demolish the monument. Police intervened in the protest and 7 protesters were detained.

On 23 August 2022, several dozen people gathered near a Soviet monument in Riga, Latvia calling against the Latvian government's decision to demolish the monument. Police intervened in the protest and 14 protesters were detained.

On 23 August 2022, demonstrators from Just Stop Oil and their supporters blocked access to an oil depot in Essex [coded to Colchester] to demonstrate against fossil fuel industries and a lack of significant action on behalf of the government to help counter climate change. The event, which was organized in conjunction with a similar protest in Warwickshire, resulted in 35 arrests overall among activists.

On 23 August 2022, Just Stop Oil activists and their supporters blocked access to an oil depot in Warwickshire [coded to Warwick] to demonstrate against fossil fuel industries and a lack of significant action on behalf of the government to help counter climate change. The event, which was organized in conjunction with a similar protest in Essex, resulted in 35 arrests overall among activists.

On 24 August 2022, several dozen protesters staged a 'silent protest action' in Yekaterinburg in support of Yevgeny Roizman, a former mayor of Yekaterinburg and a prominent opposition politician who was arrested earlier on the same day on charges of 'discrediting' the Russian army. Police arrested one protester, using force, and took photos of others, threatening to use them to identify the participants and charge them with an administrative offence for participating in an unauthorized demonstration.
On 24 August 2022, 4 protesters staged anti-war protest actions at different locations in Moscow, due to the Russian military invasion of Ukraine. Police arrested all protesters.

On 25 August 2022, overnight, an unknown number of prisoners rebelled and climbed onto the roof of the Administrative Detention Center in Mesnil-Amelot, against their inability to obtain foodstuffs at the center during visits. BAC police reinforcements were called to support the 15 prison guards on duty and used gas canisters to force the individuals to come down from the roof.

On 28 August 2022, around 30 Extinction Rebellion attempted to occupy a building in Humlegaarden area of Stockholm demanding to declare a climate emergency and draw attention to climate crisis. Later, police personnel removed activists, at least 32 people were reported for various offenses.

On 29 August 2022, up to 10 members of Just Stop Oil blocked an oil tanker on a route in Grays to block a key oil delivery route. Demonstrators climbed on the vehicle and deflated its tires. Police forces arrested 8 people on suspicion of 'offenses including going equipped to cause criminal damage'.

On 29 August 2022, an unknown number of XR activists tried to prevent the felling of 120 trees in Almelo (Overijssel). They denounced that healthy bog oaks were being cut down in the process, citing environmental concerns. The police arrested and took away an unknown number of activists.

On 30 August 2022, about 25 to 30 people, including an LFI Savoie MP, an EELV regional councilor, Italian No TAV Movement affiliates, residents of Villarodin-Bourget and Avrieux and activists of the Vivre & Agir en Maurienne movement, gathered for a sit-in to block the Lyon-Turin high-speed railway route in Avrieux, to prevent the passage of trucks with concrete, against the Lyon-Turin high-speed railway tunnel project and the ecological damage it would do. The co-president of the Vivre & Agir en Maurienne movement was arrested by gendarme officers and taken into custody, and the sit-in was subsequently lifted.

On 2 September 2022, around 50 climate activists from Extinction Rebellion superglued themselves around the Speaker's chair in the House of Commons and locked themselves to the railings outside the Houses of Parliament entrance in London - Westminster to denounce the government's lack of action on climate change. Police forces arrested eight people involved in the protest.
On 3 September 2022, KPRF activists staged a protest action in Moscow against electoral fraud. Police intervened in the event, arresting 4 protesters.
On 4 September 2022, 3 protesters staged pickets at different locations in Moscow against political repressions. Police arrested all protesters.

On 4 September 2022, animal rights activists from Animal Rebellion group staged a sit in protest at Muller's Severnside distribution site near Stonehouse as part of a national action day against dairy firms calling for a plant-based future to tackle climate change. Police forces arrested eight protestors.

On 5 September 2022, around 150 environmental activists marched and later sat and blocked traffic in Aarhus to oppose the planned expansion of an industrial port in the city. Eighteen people were arrested for disorderly conduct, and most were later released.

On 5 September 2022, an unknown number of XR activists staged a protest in Rotterdam (Zuid-Holland) in the context of the African Adaptation Summit taking place in the city that day. The protesters demanded more climate justice. The police arrested two activists.

On 5 September 2022, animal rights activists from Animal Rebellion staged protest and blocked the road leading to the Queen Elizabeth II conference center in London - Westminster, calling for a plant-based future to tackle climate change. The protest happened ahead of the announcement of the new Prime Minister. Police forces arrested one protestor.

On 5 September 2022, around 30 residents blocked a road in Poltavskaya, protesting against a landfill near their village, which pollutes the environment and affects the health of the residents. Police tried to arrest one protester, but were prevented from doing that by other protesters.

On 6 September 2022, around 10 people staged a protest action in Amsterdam, chaining themselves to the entrance of the Krasnapolsky hotel, where the Regenerative Agriculture & Food Systems Summit was about to take place, to denounce the social, ecological and health impact of the big food production companies. Police forces intervened and arrested the protesters.

On 6 September 2022, 5 climate activists blocked the federal highway (460) in Heppenheim to demand climate protection. Three of them glued themselves to the road. Police forces arrested all five demonstrators.

On 7 September 2022, activists from Animal Rebellion group staged a demonstration on front of the Houses of Parliament in London - Westminster and threw white paint to the walls and glue themselves to the stairs. The demonstration was part of a national action against dairy firms calling for a plant-based future to tackle climate change. Police forces arrested ten demonstrators.

On 7 September 2022, in the afternoon, 3 Last Generation activists smudged the PD headquarters' door in red paint and one of them chained himself inside the headquarters in Corso Garibaldi in Milano - Municipio 1 (Milano, Lombardia) to demand PD's leader to include the eco-climate emergency on his political agenda. Police and DIGOS officers intervened to quell the protest and identified the activists.

On 8 September 2022, environmental activists from Greenpeace blocked a vessel carrying Russian oil in Swedish waters near Nynashamn (Stockholm County). Activists demanded the government to stop importing Russian oil and natural gas amid Russian invasion of Ukraine. Later, the police personnel intervened and removed activists from the location.

On 10 September 2022, Hard Line (Stram Kurs) party members, including the party leader Rasmus Paludan, staged an anti-Islamic demonstration in Lulea, Norrbotten where they were met by a group of counter-protesters. Police personnel were present at the venue to ensure the security of the event, several counter-protesters were temporarily detained during the demonstration. A total of about 100 people participated in the event.

On 12 September 2022, 4 Last Generation members demonstrated in Wien - Inner City (Wien) and blocked traffic by gluing themselves on the road at Franz-Josefs-Kai to call for a speed limit of 100 km/h on highways as an immediate measure against fossil destruction. Demonstrators called for climate protection. The police removed the protesters from the street and reported the activists.

On 13 September 2022, about 40 XR and Quit with Coal activists staged a protest action at the Port of Amsterdam (Noord-Holland), blocking a railway used for coal transportation, denouncing the government's support of fossil fuels. 18 activists were arrested by police forces.

On 14 September 2022, 50 protestors from Just Stop Oil group blocked the main entrance of Kingsbury Oil Terminal near Tamworth to demand the British government to end new oil and gas projects in the UK. Police forces made a number of arrests.

On 15 September 2022, members of Rouvikonas protested outside the home of alternate interior minister in Athens scattering fliers and writing slogans on the walls, following his statement that 'whoever does not adjust, dies'. 3 protesters were detained briefly.

On 16 September 2022, a group of citizens gathered in front of the municipal court in Zagreb to demand the release of Marko Franciskovic, a leader of the anti-vaccination movement, who was arrested for organizing a series of violent anti-vaccination protests. The police detained six people for endangering public peace and order.

On 16 September 2022, around 20 people staged a protest on the Coolsingel in Rotterdam. Though protest motives were not specified, police forces arrested 11 demonstrators, including one for carrying a knife, and ten others for 'public intoxication'.

On 17 September 2022, members of Extinction Rebellion demonstrated and blocked traffic in Berlin - Friedrichshain-Kreuzberg for climate protection and against fossil fuels. Police broke up the gathering physically (carrying demonstrators away).

On 17 September 2022, between 600 (according to the police) and 800 people (according to organizers) people, including feminists, the LGBT community, the association 'What the Fuck', Alliance for Sexual Self-Determination (BSS) members, Grannies Against the Right, The Greens, and DGB delegates, gathered for a counter-demonstration in Berlin (Brandenburg Gate, Charlottenburg-Wilmersdorf, Potsdamer Platz, Friedrichstrasse, to the city center) in favor of the right to abortion. Police officers intervened and used physical force against protesters in Berlin - Mitte as they were blocking traffic.

On 18 September 2022, hundreds of supporters of the 'Let Women Speak' campaign rallied in Victoria Gardens in Brighton to participate in a 'Speaker's Corner Tour' by Kellie-Jay Keen, also known as Posie Parker. LGBTQ+ campaigners gathered for a counter-demonstration to criticize Kellie-Jay Keen's alleged transphobic views. Police forces arrested three people during the rally.

On 20 September 2022, around 50 people, including ARCI, Pride, feminists groups, civil rights associations and Non una di meno activists, held a protest in Palermo (Palermo) against FdI's leader who was hosting a rally in front of the Politeama. Protesters were blocked and encircled by police officers who used truncheons to quell the protest. One activist was later transported to the police station.

On 20 September 2022, 3 FFF-affiliated students held a protest outside their school in Voghera (Pavia, Lombardia) to call for more climate justice from public authorities. Police officers intervened to quell the protest and two demonstrators were later transported to the police station.

On 20 September 2022, dozens of farmers assembled in Rijswijk to stage a tractor protest procession against the Dutch agricultural policy and planned cuts to nitrogen emissions to Den Haag [coded to Den Haag], where the Prinsjesdag celebrations for the monarchy were being held. While several farmers were signaled in Den Haag, the majority was blocked by police forces. 5 people were arrested, and 6 tractors confiscated.

On 21 September 2022, people gathered in Arkhangelsk, protesting against a mobilization announced in Russia to fill up the ranks of the Russian forces in Ukraine. Anti-mobilization protests were announced by a Russian opposition movement Vesna ('Spring'). Police dispersed the demonstration and arrested at least 8 protesters, including at least 2 journalists.
