Police entered into scuffles with protesters.

On 26 October 2022, activists from Just Stop Oil staged a protest and sprayed paint on the facade of Ferrari and Bentley on Berkeley Square and Bruton Street in London - Westminster to denounce the government's lack of action on climate and call for the government to halt all new oil and gas licenses. Police forces arrested two protestors. This event was part of a six-week campaign to occupy Westminster in central London.

On 26 October 2022, activists from the Just Stop Oil movement sat and blocked traffic in Trondheim calling on the government to stop issuance of new state licenses for oil and gas exploration. Later, police personnel removed activists by force, several people were arrested.

On 26 October 2022, several members of ALG demonstrated in Berlin - Charlottenburg-Wilmersdorf at Messedamm and Jakob-Kaiser-Platz and blocked traffic to call for a 100km/h speed limit on highways, a 9-Euro ticker for public transportation, and climate protection. Police officers intervened to remove them.

On 26 October 2022, several members of ALG demonstrated in Berlin - Friedrichshain-Kreuzberg at Frankfurter Allee and blocked traffic to call for a 100km/h speed limit on highways, a 9-Euro ticker for public transportation, and climate protection. Police officers intervened to remove them. Demonstrators climbed on two gantries on the city highway.

On 26 October 2022, members of ALG demonstrated in Berlin - Mitte at the main train station and blocked traffic to call for a 100km/h speed limit on highways, a 9-Euro ticker for public transportation, and climate protection. Police officers intervened to remove them.

On 27 October 2022, SOR party supporters tried to enter the general prosecutor's office building in Chisinau - Centru, to protest against the investigation of a SOR MP, but were prevented by the police to do so. 2 protesters were arrested.

On 27 October 2022, 3 Belgian Extinction Rebellion activists staged a protest action in the Mauritshuis museum in Den Haag, gluing themselves to a famous Vermeer painting to protest the lack of attention for climate change. The activists were arrested by the police, and two of them were convicted to one month of imprisonment the week after.

On 27 October 2022, 23 people blocked access to the Iranian Consulate in Frankfurt am Main against the Iranian government, following the death of a 22-year-old Kurdish woman in police custody in Iran on 16 September 2022. One person was arrested.

On 28 October 2022, SOR party supporters tried to block with tens the street outside the Parliament building in Chisinau - Buiucani, to protest against the PAS government, but were prevented by the police to do so. According to the police, the protesters left the scene without confrontations. Throughout the early morning, 3 to 4 protesters were arrested for disobeying police orders.

On 28 October 2022, activists from Just Stop Oil staged a protest and sprayed paint on a Rolex shop in Knightsbridge in London - Kensington and Chelsea to denounce the government's lack of action on climate and call for the government to halt all new oil and gas licenses. Police forces arrested two protestors. This event was part of a six-week campaign to occupy Westminster in central London.

On 29 October 2022, around 30 to 40 activists from the Nordic Resistance Movement activists marched in Oslo to promote national socialist values and oppose multiculturalism. Later, the activists were detained by the police due to the lack of a permit for the demonstration. Activists from Swedish and Danish branches of the movement participated, 31 of whom were deported from the country in relation to the incident.

On 29 October 2022, activists from Just Stop Oil blocked off Kensington High St in London - Kensington and Chelsea to denounce the government's lack of action on climate and call for the government to halt all new oil and gas licenses. Some participants also glued themselves to the tarmac. Police forces arrested a total of 33 demonstrators across London on that day. This event was part of a six-week campaign to occupy Westminster in central London.

On 29 October 2022, activists from Just Stop Oil blocked off Harleyford St in London - Lambeth to denounce the government's lack of action on climate and call for the government to halt all new oil and gas licenses. Some participants also glued themselves to the tarmac. Police forces arrested a total of 33 demonstrators across London on that day. This event was part of a six-week campaign to occupy Westminster in central London.

On 29 October 2022, activists from Just Stop Oil blocked off Blackfriars Road in London - Southwark to denounce the government's lack of action on climate and call for the government to halt all new oil and gas licenses. Some participants also glued themselves to the tarmac. Police forces arrested a total of 33 demonstrators across London on that day. This event was part of a six-week campaign to occupy Westminster in central London.

On 29 October 2022, 8 Extinction Rebellion activists staged a protest outside and inside an ING bank office in Utrecht to denounce the bank's investments in fossil fuels. One activist was physically removed and brought outside the bank by police forces, but no one was arrested. The action took place in the context of a nationwide Extinction Rebellion protest in ING bank offices.

On 29 October 2022, 8 XR activists staged a protest at an ING bank office in Amsterdam (Noord-Holland) to denounce the bank's investments in fossil fuels. Police arrested two activists. The action took place in the context of a nationwide Extinction Rebellion protest in and around ING bank offices in the country.

On 29 October 2022, members of Scientist Rebellion, including a French PhD graduate in ecology, demonstrated and took over a BMW showroom in Munchen to call for climate protection. They unfurled banners, threw paint, and then stuck themselves to a car. Demonstrators were arrested. They called for a 100km/h speed limit on highways, and the perpetuation of public transportation tickets at 9 euros.

On 29 October 2022, an unknown number of XR activists staged a protest at an ING bank office in Nijmegen (Gelderland) to denounce the bank's investments in fossil fuels. The police removed and arrested four activists. The action took place in the context of a nationwide Extinction Rebellion protest in and around ING bank offices across the country.

On 30 October 2022, about 200 people gathered by a Soviet monument that was going to get dismantled in Daugavpils, Latvia. The protesters showed their dissatisfaction by shouting and whistling. The police dispersed the crowd and arrested 37 protesters while doing so.

On 30 October 2022, activists from Just Stop Oil blocked off Commercial Street in London - Tower Hamlets to denounce the government's lack of action on climate and call for the government to halt all new oil and gas licenses. Some protesters also glued themselves to the tarmac. Police forces arrested 11 protesters in total. This event was part of a six-week campaign to occupy Westminster in central London.

On 31 October 2022, 3 activists staged a protest action in front of the governor's administration office in Perm, demanding to make the promised payments to the mobilized and their families. They scattered flyers and unfolded a banner asking 'where is the money'. Police arrested the protesters.

On 31 October 2022, activists from Just Stop Oil staged a protest and threw paint on four Central London buildings (Home Office, MI5, The Bank of England and News Corp headquarters) in London - Westminster to denounce the government's lack of action on climate and call for the government to halt all new oil and gas licenses. Police forces arrested six protesters. This event was part of a six-week campaign to occupy Westminster in central London.

On 31 October 2022, 6 Last Generation activists dressed in Halloween costumes blocked Viale Marconi in Rome - Ostiense (Roma, Lazio) to call for more climate justice from public authorities and to protest against the use of coal and gas. Police officers later intervened to take away the activists from the road and restore car circulation.

On 1 November 2022, at night, draftees staged a protest outside the military training center in Ulyanovsk, demanding payment of mobilization benefits. OMON forces arrived at the center and broke up the gathering.

On 1 November 2022, around 30 people protested on Antiaeriana street in Bucharest, demanding safety measures for pedestrians, following a deadly accident in the area. The police forcibly removed a protester who was not cooperating.

On 1 November 2022, 22 activists from Just Stop Oil staged a protest and stormed the gates at Downing Street in London - Westminster to denounce the government's lack of action on climate and call for the government to halt all new oil and gas licenses. Some of the group attempted to scale the gates, while a second group sat down in the road with banners to block Whitehall, where some glued themselves to the tarmac. Police arrested a number of protesters. This event was part of a six-week campaign to occupy Westminster in central London.

On 1 November 2022, 3 students, affiliated with Last Generation and Extinction Rebellion, blocked the motorcade attending a fair in Padua (Padova, Veneto) to protest against pollution. DIGOS police officers failed to quell the protest and later brought the activists to the police station to be reported.

On 1 November 2022, an unknown number of activists of Extinction Rebellion staged a protest at an ING bank office in Amsterdam to denounce the bank's investments in fossil fuels. The action took place in the context of a nationwide Extinction Rebellion protest in ING bank offices. Police forces ended the action and arrested 10 activists.

On 2 November 2022, at least 20 environmental activists, as well as EELV and LFI MPs, gathered for a protest organized by the environmental group Derniere Renovation (Last Renovation) and blocked traffic in front of the National Assembly in Paris, demanding the maintenance of the 12 billion euros of credits for the thermal renovation of buildings in the country. They also denounced the prime minister's intention to resort to the 49.3 constitutional article to pass the budget. 9 activists were arrested by the police.

On 2 November 2022, six Last Generation activists staged a demonstration on the GRA in Rome (Roma, Lazio) with the intention to block the traffic to demonstrate against the continued use of gas and coal as energy sources. Car owners repeatedly tried to remove the demonstrators from the road, before police officers intervened and definitively removed the protesters from the beltway.

On 3 November 2022, five ALG activists staged a road blockade at a traffic light at the corner of Bismarckallee and Wilhelmstrasse in Freiburg im Breisgau to demand more climate action, and notably a 100-km/h speed limit on highways. All five activists were removed from the street by the police.

On 3 November 2022, in the morning, 17 ALG activists staged a road blockade near Karlsplatz in Munchen, obstructing traffic, to demand climate action. The activists were taken into custody by the police, and released in the afternoon. 15 of the activists subsequently staged another road blockade, and some of them glued themselves to the road. They were removed by the police and some of them were arrested.

On 4 November 2022, activists gathered on the central square in Ulan-Ude, where a pro-government rally was supposed to take place. Police started to arrest everyone, arriving at the square, and finally were forced to cancel the rally, fearing that it would be disrupted by anti-war protesters. At least 8 activists were arrested.

On 5 November 2022, Extinction Rebellion activists stood and blocked a road in Copenhagen to oppose the government's urban development plan that includes the widespread construction of new highways across the country. Later, the activists were removed and detained by the police personnel.

On 5 November 2022, about 500 activists from several environmental organizations, political parties, and neighborhood groups staged a protest at Schiphol Airport in Schiphol (Noord-Holland) against its planned enlargement. The action was a joint initiative of MD, GL, PvdD and neighbors of the airport. XR and Greenpeace activists staged an action in the context of the protest, breaking into the private jet area of the airport to denounce the environmental impact of the private flight economy. Police forces arrested 413 activists across the board.

On 5 November 2022, 15 Extinction Rebellion activists gathered for a protest in front of terminal 2 at Nice Cote d'Azur airport in Nice, against private jets and 'the climate crimes of the ultra-rich.' Police arrested 12 of the activists.

On 6 November 2022, around 1700 SOR supporters and members, including MPs and council members, as well as PACE representatives, rallied in Chisinau - Buiucani against the PAS government, demanding its resignation and demanding snap parliamentary elections. Police scuffled with protesters and arrested around 65 demonstrators before and during the protest, after finding that some intended to commit violent acts, held knives, or that they were wanted.

On 6 November 2022, 3 members of ALG tried to spray paint on the walls of the Bavarian State Chancellery in Munchen to call for climate protection but police officers stopped the action and arrested them.

On 7 November 2022, activists, including KOD members, gathered for a rally in Ostroda during the visit of a government-affiliated official, protesting against alleged poor performance of the cabinet and criticizing the ruling party. One of the activists was briefly detained.

On 7 November 2022, a dozen Extinction Rebellion activists staged a sit-in during the municipal council gathering in Emmen to denounce the continuous use of the controversial Zwarte Piet blackface figure in the city's yearly Sinterklaas celebration for children. After occupying the Council Chamber for one hour and a half, the activists were removed from the building by police officers.

On 7 November 2022, during a four-day campaign, activists from Just Stop Oil climbed onto motorway gantries at several locations on the M25 highway and blocked the roads in London to demand the government halt all new oil and gas licenses. Police forces had to intervene and arrest the protestors.

Around 7 November 2022 (as reported), environmental activists from Last Generation organization gathered on the GRA beltway (Grande Raccordo Anulare) in Rome (Roma, Lazio) with the intention to block the traffic to demonstrate against the continued use of gas and coal as energy sources. The police removed the protesters from the beltway.

On 7 November 2022, around 600 people gathered in Leipzig for a counter-demonstration (at Gottschedstrasse and Thomaskirchhof) against a Querdenken protest and to prevent those demonstrators from circling the city center with a sit-in blockade. One counter-demonstrator was arrested for spraying water at a police officer with a water gun.

On 7 November 2022, 5 members of ALG demonstrated and blocked traffic in Munchen (at the Stachus, Altstadtring) to call on the government to do more to tackle climate change. They also denounced previous arrests. Police officers arrested the activists.

On 8 November 2022, 5 activists blocked the road to prevent the construction company's drivers to access the Bitzevsky Forest in Moscow, during the action to protect the forest from the ongoing construction works. The company's workers attacked the activists. Later, the police arrived at the place and arrested everyone.

On 9 November 2022, a dozen passengers occupied the train tracks in Noyon to protest against the SNCF's permanent cancellation of a morning train. The protesters were removed by gendarmes after one hour, with no clashes.

On 9 November 2022, Last Generation activists staged a demonstration on the GRA in Rome (Roma, Lazio) with the intention of blocking traffic to demonstrate against the continued use of gas and coal as energy sources. The police removed the protesters from the beltway.

On 10 November 2022, Ugandan protesters gathered for a protest and stormed a UN Human rights conference in Geneva, with a list containing names of at least 1,277 citizens who were allegedly abducted by security forces in Uganda, against torture by the current government of Uganda. The group chanted 'Uganda is bleeding. Police briefly arrested 5 protesters.

On 10 November 2022, a group of students, including members of the 'Union pirate' and the 'AG des luttes' collective, who had broken off from an earlier CGT-backed demonstration [coded as a separate event] were tear gassed and clubbed by police officers on Siam Street in Brest for unspecified reasons. Three participants were subsequently arrested.

On 10 November 2022, around 15 Scientist Rebellion, Extinction Rebellion, Last Generation activists staged a demonstration blocking the Linate airport in Segrate (Milano, Lombardia) to protest against private jets and raising environmental concerns. Students and scientists participated in the protest. Demonstrators chained themselves to the entrance of the airport and set off the fire alarm. Police officers removed activists from the entrance they were blocking.

On 11 November 2022, about 100 000 activists , including members of the All-Poland Youth and other nationalist and far-right groups, gathered for an Independence March in Warsaw, praising the Polish sovereignty and traditional values and criticizing, liberalism, feminism and pro-LGBT movements. During the march, minor scuffles occurred and flags of a feminist movement and the EU were burned. 27 participants were detained.

On 11 November 2022, about 20 ORP activists gathered to protest against a nationalist march of independence in Warsaw and blocked the expected route by sitting on the road. Law enforcers removed them from the street and blocked them from the other participants. The activists complained that the police forcibly kept them away in cold weather for several hours.

On 11 November 2022, about 4000 activists gathered for an independence march in Wroclaw, praising the Polish sovereignty and criticizing liberal values. Some were also criticizing the influx of Ukrainians into the country. Law enforcers detained at least one person.

On 11 November 2022, for the second consecutive day, 46 inmates in the Vallette prison in Torino (Torino, Piemonte) blocked the entrances and barricaded themselves inside the facility, piling up beds and objects against the doors, to protest against the condition of health care, judged insufficient by the prisoners. Prison officers in riot gear broke into the facility using water cannons on the demonstrators.

On 11 November 2022, five Last Generation activists staged a demonstration at the Colosseum in Rome - City Center (Roma, Lazio) with the intention of blocking the traffic to demonstrate against the continued use of gas and coal as energy sources. The police removed the protesters from the street.

On 11 November 2022, three environmental activists, including citizens of Finland, Denmark and Germany, attempted to glue themselves to Edvard Munch's painting at the National Museum in Oslo. The activists were arrested by the police and removed from the venue.
On 12 November 2022, activists gathered in Wadowice, protesting against a PiS deputy to the city and criticizing the government performance. Two of them were detained.

On 12 November 2022, some protesters who were taking part in a demonstration against fossil fuels in Campo Pequeno in Lisbon, moved away from the main gathering and reached the Faculty of Letters of the University of Lisbon. There the police detained four participants.

On 13 November 2022, around 3600 SOR supporters and members, including a SOR MP and former police forces, marched in Chisinau, demanding the resignation of the PAS government and of the president Maia Sandu. 63 protesters, out of which 39 were minors, were arrested for provocative behavior.

On 14 November 2022, activists from Extinction Rebellion staged a protest by throwing black paint over a branch of Barclays bank in Birmingham, calling for the bank to end its investment in the fossil fuel industry. Police forces arrested four protestors. This event was part of the national day of action against Barclays bank.

On 14 November 2022, four activists from the Extinction Rebellion group staged a protest and chained themselves in front of a branch of Barclays bank on North Street in Brighton, calling for the bank to end its investment in the fossil fuel industry. Police forces arrested all four protestors. This event was part of the national day of action against Barclays bank.

On 14 November 2022, activists from Extinction Rebellion group staged a demonstration and chained themselves to the St David's Way Barclays bank branch in Cardiff, calling for the bank to end its investment in the fossil fuel industry. Police forces had to intervene and arrest seven protestors. This event was part of the national day of action against Barclays bank.

Around 17 November 2022 (as reported), Last Renovation activists gathered for a protest and blockage of the A6 in Paris, to bring attention to the climate crisis. The activists glued their hands to the street. Police arrived and removed them.

On 18 November 2022, around 3000 SOR supporters and members, including a SOR MP, marched in central Chisinau to the general prosecutor's office, demanding the resignation of the prosecutor general and of the president Maia Sandu. 16 protesters, one of which was wanted and three were minors, were arrested.

On 18 November 2022, 9 environmental activists from Last Renovation gathered for a protest and blockage of M7 in Lyon, against inaction on the climate crisis. Police arrived and removed them from the road.

On 18 November 2022, a dozen activists with Last Renovation gathered for a protest and blockage of the ring road between the Canal du Midi bridge and the Rangueil exit in Toulouse, during rush hour traffic, to alert public opinion to the climate emergency and in favor of energy renovation of buildings. Police were called and quickly removed the protesters.

On 19 November 2022, at least 680 Yellow Vests, gathered in Paris, on the occasion of the fourth year of the movement, to demand higher wages amid inflation. The police intervened using truncheons and made three arrests.

Around 19 November 2022 (as reported), about 20 Rome Climate Strike activists briefly occupied the private jet terminal at Ciampino airport in Ciampino (Roma, Lazio) to protest against the use of private jets, which have a detrimental impact on climate and increase noise pollution. A small group entered the external space adjacent to the track, displayed a banner and lit a smoke bomb. Police officers intervened to clear the runway, identify activists and escort them outside the terminal.

On 20 November 2022, an unknown number of PEGIDA activists staged a protest action in Den Haag against the alleged Islamization of the West. The Dutch chairman of the organization was arrested during the action.

On 21 November 2022, 3 members of ALG demonstrated and blocked traffic in Magdeburg to call for climate protection. Demonstrators demanded a highway speed limit of 100km/h and a permanent 9-euro ticket for buses and trains. They glued themselves to a main road and police officers intervened physically to remove them.

On 23 November 2022, MAT riot police chased away protesters who rallied outside and inside the Evelpidon court complex in Athens - Central Athens in solidarity with 78 people, who were arrested when they attacked police during a raid in a squat that led to the arrest of a suspected member of Thousands of Suns of the Night the day before. Defence lawyers reported that police used excessive force against those arrested, protesters and lawyers alike, and that they had confiscated mobile phones to prevent people from recording the scene. 1 person was injured in the head.

On 23 November 2022, 4 activists of Extinction Rebellion staged a protest action inside the Naturalis biodiversity museum in Leiden, displaying themselves naked among skeletons of extinct species to raise awareness for the potential consequences of climate change. Police forces arrested all 4 activists.

On 23 November 2022, activists from the Just Stop Oil movement held a protest performance outside of Equinor office in Trondheim demanding sustainable changes from the company in order to reduce the negative impact on the environment from oil and gas production. Later, two activists were arrested by the police.

On 24 November 2022, in the morning, 7 ALG activists staged a protest on Innere Kanalstrasse in Koln, with five of them gluing themselves to the road and blocking traffic, to demand urgent climate action. Glued activists were eventually 'freed' by police forces and firefighters using a solvent. Shortly after, one activist sought to block the road again and was consequently taken into custody by the police.

On 24 November 2022, in the afternoon, at least 6 ALG activists cut through fences and entered the grounds (from two distinct points) of the Berlin Brandenburg Airport in Schoenefeld, where some of them held banners, while others glued their hands to the tarmac or rode bicycles through the shunting area, thus briefly blocking air traffic. They demanded urgent climate action. Several activists were taken into custody by the police and faced charges linked to 'dangerous interference with air traffic' at the time of reporting.

On 26 November 2022, 250 XR activists staged a protest action in Den Haag (Zuid-Holland), blocking the A12 Utrechtsebaan between the Ministry of Economic Affairs and the Tweede Kamer Parliament building, to call on the government to stop subsidizing fossil fuels. Police forces put an end to the blockade and arrested 150 participants.

On 26 November 2022, more than 1,400 people demonstrated from Berlin - Neukolln to Oranienplatz in Berlin - Friedrichshain-Kreuzberg against the ban on the Kurdistan Workers' Party (PKK) and in the wake of Turkey's aerial campaign against Kurdish militant bases in northern Syria. Demonstrators called for the PKK to be removed from the 'terrorist' list. 7 people were arrested for insulting police officers and carrying PKK symbols.

On 28 November 2022, 3 members of ALG demonstrated in Linz and blocked traffic to call for a 100km/h speed limit on highways, climate protection, and a ban on new oil and gas drilling. Two of them glued themselves to the roadway at the Hafenstrasse highway exit. The two people allowed the officers to remove them from the road without any scuffles.

On 28 November 2022, 9 activists from the Last Renovation collective gathered for a protest and blockage of the Levallois bridge in Levallois-Perret, to draw attention to environmental issues related to the renovation of housing and buildings. Police eventually arrived and removed and arrested the 9 protesters.

On 28 November 2022, around 50 activists of the OccupyEUR environmental group, an action group of students and university personnel, occupied the Sanders building on the university campus in Rotterdam to demand the university quit its support for fossil fuel production. When a dozen protesters refused to clear the building by the evening, police forces ended the action and arrested them.

On 28 November 2022, activists from the Just Stop Oil movement sat and blocked traffic in Trondheim calling on the government to stop issuance of new state licenses for oil and gas exploration. Later, police personnel dispersed protesters, several people were detained.

On 29 November 2022, demonstrators interrupted a parliamentary session in Copenhagen, protesting the decision of the Social Democrats not to vote for the bill extending temporary child support for vulnerable families. Later, the activists were removed from the venue by the police personnel.

On 29 November 2022, Extinction Rebellion activists demonstrated in Oslo in connection with the Norwegian state-owned energy company conference, demanding to abolish plans for the development of an oil field in the North Sea as well as that the company make sustainable changes in order to reduce the negative impact on the environment. Later, the activists entered the building, following which the police dispersed the activists. At least 8 people were arrested.

On 29 November 2022, activists from the Just Stop Oil movement staged a protest performance in Trondheim calling on the government to stop issuance of new state licenses for oil and gas exploration. Later, police dispersed activists, two people were detained.

On 30 November 2022, refugees protested over the closure of the Elaionas camp in Athens. The remaining 57 refugees, including families with minors attending schools, were removed from the camp in the middle of the school year. The demonstrators also protested that they were informed of the move just one hour before the camp's closure. Police detained some protesters.

On 30 November 2022, at least 20 Extinction Rebellion activists gathered outside the RAI headquarters in Milano - Municipio 8 (Milano, Lombardia) to protest against the lack of information about the climate crisis conveyed by the national public service media company of Italy. Some demonstrators glued themselves to the entry door, others threw green paint on it and some others blocked Via Villasanta, a nearby street. Police officers intervened and took away the activists. 20 demonstrators were identified and 14 of them were denounced.

On 1 December 2022, several dozen farmers, including members of AgroUnia, demonstratively occupied the regional authority office in Lublin. They were protesting against allegedly uncompetitive prices of wheat and other agricultural products imported from Ukraine. Law enforcers removed them from the premises and detained several.

On 1 December 2022, dozens of farmers staged a protest outside the city hall in Zwolle to denounce the lack of governmental response to their demand that PFAS nitrogen fines be put on hold. When they blocked the road with tractors, police forces intervened and arrested 3 people.

On 1 December 2022, dozens of people assembled at the University of Gent in Gent in an attempt to prevent the lecture of a Vlaams Belang party chairman about the Great Replacement. Beer and glitter were thrown at his fellow party members, and police forces had to escort the Vlaams Belang members inside. Protesters kept on disturbing the speaker's lecture. Later that night, 9 people were arrested after the protest continued at a different location in the city.

Around 1 December 2022 (as reported), an unknown number of activists of Last Renovation staged a protest in Boulogne-sur-Mer, blocking the Pont d'Issy bridge, presumably to demand more action against climate change. Eventually the police arrived and physically removed protesters from the road.

On 2 December 2022, at the call of COBAS and USB, workers took to the streets in Torino (Torino, Piemonte) to protest against the socio-economic policies adopted by the newly elected Italian government. Police officers intervened to take away some demonstrators.

On 2 December 2022, in the morning, 4 members of ALG blocked traffic on the city ring road in Leipzig to call for climate protection. They demanded a 100km/h speed limit and a 9-euro public transportation ticket for all. Police officers intervened physically to remove two activists who glued themselves to the road and arrested all 4 activists.

On 3 December 2022, several dozen activists gathered in Zielona Gora, protesting against a visit of a government-affiliated official to the city and criticizing the ruling party. One man was detained.

On 3 December 2022, around 150 people, including leftists and Ende Gelaende members, gathered from Ernst-August-Platz to the Luther Church in Nordstadt in Hannover to denounce bombings of the Turkish government on Kurdish areas in northern Iraq and northern Syria. 2 people were arrested.

On 4 December 2022, Just Stop Oil Norway activists attempted to disrupt the ski race in Lillehammer, Innlandet, calling on the government to stop issuance of new state licenses for oil and gas exploration. Later, police dispersed the activists, two people were detained.

On 4 December 2022, between 300 and 400 people, including Grannies Against the Right members and Antifa affiliates, demonstrated at Augustinerplatz in Leverkusen against the presence of Nazis gathered for a reason not specified in the report. Police forces intervened physically against the demonstrators. They marched across the Deutzer Bridge to Ottoplatz.

On 5 December 2022, 9 members of ALG blocked traffic, glued themselves to the roadway at Karlsplatz, and others climbed with posters onto gantries on highways A9 and A96, in Munchen to call for climate protection. They demanded a 100km/h speed limit and a 9-euro public transportation ticket for all. Police forces intervened to arrest the demonstrators and removed them from the road.

On 5 December 2022, around a dozen people, mostly members of ALG and an elected official (The Greens), demonstrated and blocked traffic at the Weender Tor in Gottingen to call for climate protection. Demonstrators were carried off the street by police officers and firefighters helped remove the glue from those who stuck themselves to the road.

On 5 December 2022, around 100 people demonstrated in Hannover against the clearing of the 'Leinemasch Stays' camp and the expansion of the southern highway. Police intervened to clear the camp and one person was arrested for trying to climb over a fence to get into the clearing area.

On 6 December 2022, around 50 demonstrators, protested in Gothenburg (Goteborg), to oppose the Iranian government's violent crackdown on protesters following the death of a 22-year-old Kurdish woman in police custody in Iran. Later, a group of activists attempted to enter a panel discussion on the situation in Iran and were dispersed by the police. At least one person was arrested.

On 6 December 2022, at least 40 people, mainly migrants, blocked the street next to Porte de la Chapelle in Paris, to demand the regularization of their status. Police officers, making use of tear gas, removed them from the spot.

On 6 December 2022, on the 14th anniversary of the killing of teenager Alexandros Grigoropoulos by a police special guard in Exarchia, police officers were recorded using force and teargas during a protest in Diavata, where a police officer shot and critically injured a Roma teenager during a police car chase. An OPKE police officer chased a protester and threw him on a van before he started kicking him and hitting him with a baton. More police officers arrived and they all started hitting the man.

On 6 December 2022, 11 members of ALG gathered at several places in Munchen, at the intersection of Prielmayerstrasse/Karlsplatz, around the highway A9, and A96, and blocked traffic to call for climate protection. Police officers intervened to disperse the blockades.

On 6 December 2022, around 50 people, including students and members of 'End Fossil: Occupy', occupied a lecture hall in Frankfurt am Main to call for climate protection. Police officers intervened physically to evict the students and arrested 3 people.

On 6 December 2022, 25 striking prison guards blocked access to the detention center in Roanne, following the 'Union federale autonome penitentiaire' mobilization, to demonstrate against the 'brutal' management at the center. Law enforcers removed them from the spot.

On 7 December 2022, 5 Last Generation activists rallied and hurled paint at the La Scala theater's entrance walls ahead of the season's premiere in Milano - Municipio 1 (Milano, Lombardia) to call for more climate action. Some of them carried protest banners. The action was brought to an end after the intervention of police officers, who took the activists to the police headquarters.

On 8 December 2022, between 550 and 700 people, including representatives of the Andorra Union organization staged a demonstration in Andorra la Vella (Andorra la Vella) demanding the national government measures to unify the country. Demonstrators were calling for a country in which they can not only work, but also live. Police intervened arresting one demonstrator accused of having verbally insulted a police officer.

On 8 December 2022, about 15 members of Last Renovation gathered for a protest and blockage of the ring road at the Borderouge exit in Toulouse, to demand the energy renovation of buildings in France. Police arrived and cleared out the demonstrators.

On 8 December 2022, members of Last Renovation gathered for a protest and blockage of the Champs-Elysees in Paris, to demand action against climate change. Police arrived and removed the protesters from the street, taking several of them into custody.

On 8 December 2022, 7 members of ALG demonstrated and blocked traffic in Dresden around Nurnberger Street at the Technical University (TU) to call for climate protection. Police officers intervened physically (by using oil) to remove the demonstrators glued to the street.

On 9 December 2022, around 20 members of Last renovation and Ultima Generazione gathered for a protest and blockage of the Mont-Blanc tunnel in Chamonix, to demand the French and Italian governments take climate action. Police intervened and arrested 6 people.

Around 9 December 2022 (as reported), Last Generation activists blocked the Mont Blanc tunnel exit in Courmayeur (Valle d'Aosta, Valle d'Aosta) to protest against the use of gas and coal. Police officers later intervened to take away the activists, cutting the chains they had used to slow the clearing down, and transported them to the police headquarters.

On 9 December 2022, around 10 members of ALG blocked the Konstanzer Strasse highway exit (A100) in Berlin - Charlottenburg-Wilmersdorf to call for climate protection. Police officers detached the protesters from the road and carried them away.

On 9 December 2022, 6 members of ALG demonstrated in Mainz and blocked traffic on a main access road to denounce the climate emergency. Police officers intervened to remove the demonstrators who glued themselves to the road.

On 12 December 2022, citizens protested in Podgorica against the adoption of amendments to the Law on the President, which limits the competencies of the head of state. DPS, LP, SD and SDP representatives supported the protests and addressed the crowd, leading to increasing tensions. Police fired stun grenades and tear gas at demonstrators to halt the throwing of objects at the Assembly building and police members.

On 12 December 2022, during the morning, 3 members of ALG demonstrated and blocked traffic on Lendkai street in Graz to call for climate protection and a 100km/h speed limit on highways. Police officers intervened to remove the demonstrators from the road.

On 12 December 2022, 5 members of ALG, including one German ALG activist, demonstrated and blocked traffic on Amraser Street in Innsbruck to call for climate protection and a 100km/h speed limit on highways. Police officers intervened to remove the people who glued themselves to the road.

On 12 December 2022, during the afternoon, around 44 members of ALG demonstrated, while 3 of them blocked traffic, at Innsbrucker Platz in Berlin - Tempelhof-Schoneberg to call for climate protection, a 9-euro public transport ticket, and a 100km/h speed limit on highways. They also demanded the end of fossil fuel energies. 2 people were arrested.

On 13 December 2022, around 350 homeless asylum seekers gathered near the La Chapelle metro station in Paris, to demand emergency accommodation solutions. Police officers, making use of tear gas, removed them from the spot.

On 14 December 2022, around 10 Last Generation activists, among whom students and workers, staged a demonstration at the Liberta bridge in Venice (Venezia, Veneto) with the intention of blocking the traffic to demonstrate against the continued use of gas and coal as energy sources. The police removed the protesters from the street.

On 15 December 2022, LaMeva workers, operating at the ItalTrans warehouse in Calcio (Bergamo, Lombardia) staged a demonstration asking for better working conditions and increased salaries. Police officers and ItalTrans private security officers beat up demonstrators with batons, injuring one of them. The USB organized the demonstration.

On 15 December 2022, campaigners from the Animal Justice Project group staged a protest by climbing on the Department for the Environment, Food and Rural Affairs head office building in London - Westminster to highlight the 'catastrophic' impact of spreading bird flu through chicken sheds. Police forces arrested three protestors.

On 15 December 2022, 9 members of ALG blocked traffic around the Reichstag building (at Paul Loebe House and Marie Elisabeth Luders House) in Berlin - Mitte to bring the issue of climate protection to the attention of the members of parliament. Police officers detached the peaceful demonstrators from the street and took them away.
On 16 December 2022, taxi drivers demonstrated in Reykjavik to oppose the new bill regulating the rules of cab work in the country. Later, the police 'stopped' the protest.

On 17 December 2022, during the afternoon, around 30 members of ALG demonstrated and blocked traffic at Potsdamer Platz in Berlin - Mitte to call for climate protection and denounce the detention of members of ALG in Bavaria. Police forces tried to remove the 5 blockers from the roadway.

On 19 December 2022, 12 members of ALG demonstrated and occupied both lanes of Federal Highway 3 in Freiburg im Breisgau to call for climate protection. Police officers intervened to remove demonstrators.

On 20 December 2022, activists from Animal Rebellion broke into the premises of MBR Acres, a dog breeding facility in Wyton, to protest against the holding of beagle puppies at the facility and seek to free them. Police forces arrested three activists.

On 20 December 2022, 8 members of ALG demonstrated and blocked traffic at the intersection Seestrasse, corner Beusselstrasse near the A100 in Berlin - Charlottenburg-Wilmersdorf to call for climate protection, a 100km/h speed limit, a 9-euro public transportation ticket for all, and an end to fossil fuel energies. Police officers intervened to remove the demonstrators who glued themselves to the road.
On 20 December 2022, at least 10 members of ALG demonstrated and blocked traffic at the Stachus station on Sonnenstrasse in Munchen to call for climate protection. 10 people were arrested.

On 21 December 2022, 36 XR activists staged a protest action in Den Haag (Zuid-Holland), spray-painting slogans on the Ministry of Economical Affairs building to denounce governmental support to fossil fuels. The protesters were stopped by police forces and carried into police vans. Six protesters were arrested.
On 21 December 2022, at least 10 members of ALG demonstrated and blocked traffic in Munchen to call for climate protection. 10 people were arrested.

On 22 December 2022, 4 ALG activists demonstrated and blocked traffic in Berlin - Tempelhof-Schoneberg (Hauptstrasse exit) around the highway A100 to call for climate protection. Police officers intervened to unblock the road.

On 23 December 2022, protesters organized by women's groups rallied outside the court in Athens - Central Athens shouting slogans in solidarity with a woman, who was pimped by a police officer in Ilioupoli, found guilty of trafficking. Following the court's decision to free the police officer under conditions, the audience erupted in protest and were removed from the courtroom by MAT riot police, who used tear gas outside the court building.

On 23 December 2022, NBP members ('Nazbols') staged a protest action in St. Petersburg. They were holding signs, saying 'The banker is the enemy of the soldier'. Police intervened, arresting all participants.

On 23 December 2022, about 150 Kurdish people gathered for a protest between La Canebiere and the prefecture in Marseille, against the killing of 3 Kurdish people by a shooter in Paris earlier in the day. 4 people were arrested on the sidelines of the demonstration.

On 23 December 2022, an unknown number of Extinction Rebellion activists staged a protest in front and inside of the Cru supermarket in Gent, blocking the fish section to denounce the cooking of lobsters while they are still alive during Christmas and New Year's celebrations. 4 activists were arrested by police forces.

On 2 January 2023, several hundred protesters gathered in Kayakent, demanding an impartial investigation into the death of a young resident. According to the protesters, the authorities do not properly investigate the case because of the suspect's connections to law enforcement. Police broke down the protest, arresting and beating the participants with batons.

On 2 January 2023, in the morning, the police cleared a university building occupied by students affiliated with Changing Course in Bologna (Bologna, Emilia-Romagna). The students had occupied the building in November to denounce the lack of space for teaching and working in the University of Bologna itself.

On 2 January 2023, 5 Last Generation activists threw orange paint on the facade of the Palazzo Madama in Rome - City Center (Roma, Lazio), where the Italian Senate is located, to call for more climate action, to demand the immediate halting of the reopening of decommissioned coal-fired power plants and the cancellation of new drilling for natural gas exploration and extraction. Carabinieri onsite blocked the protesters and three activists were arrested.

On 2 January 2023, a group of activists and members of the group Extinction Rebellion protested and attempted to tape themselves to a road in Hamburg - Hamburg-Mitte (Hamburg) in St. Georg. They called for the immediate implementation of a 100-km/h speed limit on German highways, as well as stricter speed limits in cities as immediate climate protection measures. Police officers arrived at the scene and prevented protesters from implementing their protest and taping themselves to the road, removing them from the road.

On 3 January 2023, residents gathered outside the Our Lady of Mercy Secondary School in South-West Dublin to protest after information was circulated on social media that male refugees were being housed inside the school. During the protest, police forces arrested a woman for public order offenses.

On 4 January 2023, members of anti-establishment groups attempted to retake a university building that was housing the anarchist squat 'Terra Incognita' in Thessaloniki since 2004. The building had been cleared by police in August 2020. The demonstrators hung banners from the rooftop in solidarity with an anarchist on hunger strike imprisoned on terrorism charges, who was demanding to return to the Korydallos prison in Athens. Police cleared the building and detained 29 people, 21 of which were arrested, 13 men and 8 women, including an Italian national.

Around 4 January 2023 (as reported), Last Renovation activists staged a protest action outside Hotel de Matignon, the residence of the Prime Minister, in Paris, spraying orange paint on the entrance of the building, to raise awareness about the consequences of climate change and call on the Prime Minister to address the issue. Two activists were arrested at the scene.

On 4 January 2023, three ALG members demonstrated outside the Federal Ministry of Transport in Berlin - Mitte and attempted to damage the street with jackhammers. Demonstrators denounced freshly paved and consolidated roads, which they claimed would lead to the intensification of climate change. Police officers intervened before the activists could connect the jackhammers to power sources, removing the demonstrators and preventing any form of damage.

On 6 January 2023, a dozen activists of Active for Justice staged a protest action in a restaurant in Utrecht, denouncing the consumption of foie gras at the venue. Police forces intervened, arresting six protesters, while one bystander was injured in the commotion.

Around 6 January 2023 (as reported), Last Renovation activists staged a protest action outside the Ministry of Ecological Transition in Paris, spraying orange paint on the entrance of the building, to demand urgent climate action. Three activists were arrested at the scene.

On 6 January 2023, an unknown number of Extinction Rebellion activists staged a protest action in an H&M store in Haarlem, denouncing the environmental impact of cheap clothing. Police forces arrested the protesters.

On 9 January 2023, nine activists of ALG blocked streets at several spots across Vienna, demanding immediate climate action and declaring support to their peers in Lutzerath. Law enforcers removed them from the spots.

On 9 January 2023, seven activists of the Last Generation glued themselves to a highway in Mainz, demanding immediate climate action and declaring support to their peers in Lutzerath. Law enforcers removed them from the spot.

On 10 January 2023, activists gathered in Warsaw, protesting against the alleged politicization of the so-called Smolensk tragedy by the current regime. Law enforcers seized their loudspeakers and ended the event.

On 10 January 2023, around 20 No Border activists gathered in Ventimiglia (Imperia, Liguria) to protest against country borders and the recent death of a migrant who was trying to cross the Italy-France border, with some blocking train tracks. Police officers put an end to the protest and removed the activists from the train tracks.

On 10 January 2023, several dozen Last Generation activists, including scientists, gathered in the Praterstern area in Vienna - Inner City, demanding immediate climate action. 18 activists then blocked the traffic, but police forces removed them from the streets.

On 10 January 2023, several activists affiliated with the Last Generation movement blocked a highway in Berlin - Charlottenburg-Wilmersdorf by sitting on it, demanding immediate climate action and declaring solidarity with activists protesting in Lutzerath. Law enforcers removed them from the spot.

On 12 January 2023, 5 Last Generation activists blocked traffic in Milano - Municipio 1 (Milano, Lombardia), sitting on the road in Cinque Giornate square, to demonstrate against the continued use of gas and coal as energy sources. The police removed the protesters from the street.

On 13 January 2023, ALG activists protested against climate change and the state's indolence regarding this issue in Vienna - Mariahilf. Activists glued themselves to the streets, after which the police reacted and arrested 12 activists. At some point, a cyclist drove into the group of protesters and punched the activists.

On 13 January 2023, ALG activists protested against climate change in Berlin - Charlottenburg-Wilmersdorf, blocking the roads with their bodies and vehicles. Police intervened and removed several activists from the main road.

On 13 January 2023, a group of activists from the AQ16 laboratory staged a demonstration in front of the IREN headquarters in Vittoria square in Reggio Emilia (Reggio nell'Emilia, Emilia-Romagna) against the recently-officialized collaboration agreement between IREN and the Mekorot Israeli water company. Activists entered IREN's offices, disrupting the work of operators. Police officers removed the demonstrators from the premises and proceeded to identify some of them.

On 14 January 2023, about a dozen environmental activists gathered in Berlin - Mitte, near the local representation of Nordrhein-Westfalen, and demonstratively removed a letter from their slogan on the building. They were protesting against coal-based energy production, the proposed demolition of Lutzerath and demanding climate action. Law enforcers later briefly detained two of them.

Around 15 January 2023 (as reported), EsseNon activists, among them students and environmental activists, gathered in Torino to oppose the construction of an Esselunga supermarket in Alfonso La Marmora park. The police charged the demonstrators to stop the protest march at least seven times and hit them with clubs. Over 15 demonstrators were injured by the police.

On 15 January 2023, Last Generation activists gathered in Affari Square, Milano - Municipio 1. Three activists staged a sit-in, while others threw yellow paint at the L.O.V.E. sculpture to protest against banks financing fossil fuels projects. The police intervened and physically removed the activists from the Square. Three activists were taken to the police station.

On 16 January 2023, dozens of Extinction Rebellion and Mokum Kraakt activists and students staged a protest action at the University of Amsterdam, occupying the Binnengasthuis building, to denounce the university's ties with oil company Shell for green energy research. Towards the evening, the occupation was ended by an intervention of police forces, which was criticized by the student organization ASVA as being too violent. 30 activists were arrested.

On 16 January 2023, activists of the Ende Gelaende blocked the entrance of a building, where an international summit on energy was being held, in Berlin, calling for the declaration of a climate emergency and protesting against the expansion of coal mining in Lutzerath. Law enforcers later removed them.

On 17 January 2023, about a dozen ALG activists glued themselves to an Interior Ministry building in Dusseldorf, calling for the declaration of a climate emergency and protesting against the expansion of coal mining in Lutzerath - and alleged police brutality of law enforcers intervening there during the weekend. Law enforcers removed them from the location.

On 17 January 2023, ALG activists glued themselves to a road in Koln, calling for the declaration of a climate emergency and protesting against the expansion of coal mining in Lutzerath. Law enforcers removed them from the location.

On 17 January 2023, about 70 German and international environmental activists, including Greta Thunberg and other members of the FFF movement, returned to Lutzerath and gathered by the mine area, protesting against the proposed demolition of the village. Law enforcers dispersed the gathering.

On 17 January 2023, about 130 environmental activists blocked a railway for cargo trains heading to a local plant in Neurath, demanding an immediate declaration of climate emergency and opposing coal-based energy production. Law enforcers removed them, and traffic resumed.

On 17 January 2023, police arrested 3 protesters who tried to stop the construction works in the Troitsky Forest in Moscow. The protesters were later ill-treated and physically assaulted by police at the police station.

On 18 January 2023, 4 people gathered in Moscow near a spontaneous memorial in memory of the victims of the Russian missile attack on Dnipro. While 2 of them were laying flowers at the memorial, police arrested all the participants. Flowers-laying ceremonies at the monuments to Ukrainian cultural personalities have been taking place across Russia since the day of the missile attack.

On 18 January 2023, for a third consecutive day, environmental activists from Extinction Rebellion and Greenpeace blocked a logging site in Aalistunturi, Kolari, which is owned by a state-run logging company, calling for an end to logging in the area. Later, police forces intervened and removed activists from the venue, eight people were arrested.

On 20 January 2023, an unknown number of activists from Extinction Rebellion and the Quit with Coal staged a protest on the grounds of steelmaking plant Tata Steel in Velsen-Noord, against the pollution and nitrogen emissions caused by the plant. Protesters temporarily blocked a railroad on the terrain. Police arrested two protesters.

On 20 January 2023, Last Generation activists glued themselves to the road and blocked the traffic with their bodies in Manheim, protesting against climate change and the federal government's inadequate climate politics. The activists were removed from the street and detained by the police.

On 20 January 2023, police cleared the last treehouse occupied by environmental activists in Frankfurt (Oder). Activists were calling for the protection of the wooden area and opposed a local highway construction project. The police detained the activists.

On 21 January 2023, people and activists protested in Collado Villalba (Madrid) in favor of the occupation of a building. Police agents proceeded to vacate the building and arrested six people for attempted usurpation, disobedience and disturbance of public order.

On 23 January 2023, students of the 'Ecole des Hautes Etudes Sciences Sociales (EHESS)', including SUD members, occupied a room at the Condorcet campus in Aubervilliers, to oppose the government's pension and retirement age reform. Police arrived and removed the protesters from the campus, taking 29 of them into custody.

On 23 January 2023, at night, garbage collectors chained themselves to the gates of their company's plant in Ottaviano (Napoli, Campania) to demand better working conditions. Police officers arrived onsite to quell the protest and unleash the chained demonstrators.

On 24 January 2023, environmental activists demonstrated at a logging site in Aalistunturi, Kolari, which is owned by a state-run logging company. The activists called for an end to logging in the area. Later, police arrested two activists following an attempt to halt the operation of working machines.

On 27 January 2023, around 50 people, including 11 members of the leftist initiative 'Free Space RSE' occupied an empty building at Bahnhofstrasse 23 in Oldenburg to denounce the issue of vacancy and homelessness. After the police removed the occupiers, 40 other activists gathered outside to express their support.

On 28 January 2023, animal rights activists, including members of the Coalition to Abolish the Fur Trade (CAFT), protested outside of a luxury chain store in Copenhagen calling on brand representatives to stop using animal products, including natural fur and leather. Later, several activists were detained by police.

On 28 January 2023, around 1,200 people participated in a protest action by Extinction Rebellion in Den Haag. Hundreds of activists blocked the Utrechtsebaan A12 highway by laying down and attaching themselves to each other and the tarmac, while hundreds of people assembled around the highway and on the Malieveld. Police forces intervened to remove the protesters. Hundreds of them were arrested, but released soon after. The action was supported by Greenpeace, FNV, Urgenda, the Aidsfonds, Cordaid, COC, Fietsersbond, Humanistisch Verbond, Milieudefensie and Stichting Vluchteling.

On 30 January 2023, nine environmental activists, including the Swedish Forest Rebellion movement's members, attempted to block a state-owned logging site in Aalistunturi, Kolari demanding a halt to logging activities in the area. Police personnel intervened and arrested eight people.

On 30 January 2023, farmers, who were demonstrating for compensation for lost income for products that were sold below cost, damages due to adverse weather conditions, and were demanding reduction of production costs, tax-free oil and electricity prices, attempted to climb on to the E65 highway in Karditsa and set up a blockade, but were stopped by police using tear gas. The farmers walked onto the highway and held a general meeting. A coordination committee announced that the blockade with the farmers' tractors would be moved under the E65 on the old Karditsa-Athens national road and on the Larissa-Karditsa road.

On 30 January 2023, 3 Futuro Vegetal Climate activists protested in the Chamber of Congress in Madrid - Centro (Madrid) and glued their hands to the microphones in a climate protest to denounce the climate emergency. They were removed by the authorities shortly after. No further incidents were recorded.

On 31 January 2023, for the second consecutive day, Einstein high school students continued occupying their school in Via Bologna in Torino (Torino, Piemonte) and prevented the teachers and the headmaster from entering the premises. At the call of the latter, police officers intervened to help students blocked inside and who did not want to take part in the occupation to come out. Tension and scuffles were registered between the police officers and the occupying students, though no injuries were reported. About 30 students affiliated with the 'Prendocasa' Antagonist Movement continued the occupation at night.

On 1 February 2023, residents held a protest in Alicante (Valencia) against the eviction of a pensioner with a child with disabilities. Police agents had to intervene to clear the entrance but no further incident was recorded.

On 2 February 2023, three ALG activists blocked a street in the center of Flensburg (Schleswig-Holstein, Flensburg), gluing themselves to the tarmac, to call for more climate action. The participants were removed from the street by the police.

On 3 February 2023, Hard Line (Stram Kurs) party members led by the party leader Rasmus Paludan, held an anti-Islamic demonstration in Copenhagen. Later, police personnel removed the activists from the venue, allegedly due to security concerns.

On 3 February 2023, 7 ALG activists demonstrated in Koln (Nordrhein-Westfalen) for more climate action by blocking Universitatsstrasse and gluing themselves to the asphalt. Police forces removed the protesters from the street using special solvents.

On 6 February 2023, at least 3 members of ALG demonstrated and blocked Deisterkreisel Street in Hannover to call for climate protection. On 6 February 2023, 5 members of ALG blocked traffic at Graf-Adolf-Platz in Dusseldorf to call for climate protection. Police forces intervened to remove the demonstrators who were glued to the road.

On 6 February 2023, 5 members of ALG demonstrated and blocked traffic in the Lobtau district in Dresden to call for climate protection, a 100km/h speed limit on highways, and a 9-euro ticket for public transportation. On 6 February 2023, 6 members of ALG blocked a road in the area of Maximilianallee (B2) in Leipzig to call for climate protection. Police remove the demonstrators from the road.
On 6 February 2023, 6 members of ALG blocked a road in Jena to call for more ambition in the fight against global warming. Police officers removed the activists from the road.

Police shot tear gas at protesters.

On 7 February 2023, about half a dozen ALG activists blocked a street at the Dreisterkreisel in Hannover (Niedersachsen, Region Hannover), with three activists gluing themselves to the tarmac, to call for more climate action. The participants were removed from the street by the police.

On 7 February 2023, three ALG activists blocked the Alicenbrucke in central Mainz (Rheinland-Pfalz, Mainz), gluing themselves to the tarmac, to call for more climate action. The participants were removed from the street by the police.

On 8 February 2023, students held a protest at the Complutense University in Madrid - Chamberi (Madrid) due to the presence of the ambassador of Israel, Rodica Radian-Gordon, and in favor of Palestine. During the protest, police agents arrested two activists and dispersed the demonstrators.

On 9 February 2023, in the morning, around 20 people occupied a building in the Paquis neighborhood of Geneva. They denounced real estate speculation in Geneva and called for collective housing and social and cultural alternatives. Police forces dispersed the demonstration in the early afternoon, and several demonstrators, including a 'Ensemble a gauche' MP, were injured. Several people were arrested.

On 9 February 2023, the police evacuated the city hall in Rennes, occupied the previous day by people, including students, as part of a protest action against the government's pension and retirement age reform proposal.

On 9 February 2023, 7 ALG activists blocked a street near Groner Tor in Gottingen (Niedersachsen, Gottingen), gluing themselves to the tarmac, to call for more climate action. The participants were removed from the street by the police.

On 9 February 2023, 5 ALG activists blocked Saarstrasse in central Bremen (Bremen, Bremen), gluing themselves to the tarmac, to call for more climate action. The participants were removed from the street by the police.

On 10 February 2023, ALG activists staged a sit-in blockade on Waldeggstrasse in Linz (Oberosterreich, Linz), gluing themselves to the tarmac to call for more climate action. The participants were removed from the street by the police.

On 10 February 2023, 4 ALG activists blocked St. Petersburger Street in Dresden (Sachsen, Dresden), gluing themselves to the tarmac, to call for more climate action. The participants were removed from the street by the police.

On 10 February 2023, 6 ALG activists blocked Saarstrasse in central Mainz (Rheinland-Pfalz, Mainz), gluing themselves to the tarmac, to call for more climate action. The participants were removed from the street by the police.

On 10 February 2023, three ALG activists blocked the Invalidenstrasse in Berlin - Mitte (Berlin, Berlin), gluing themselves to the tarmac, to call for more climate action. The participants were removed from the street by the police.

On 11 February 2023, around 30 far-right protestors and members of the Patriotic Alternative group gathered outside the Tate Britain in London - Westminster ahead of the Drag Queen Story Hour event for children to show their opposition to such an event. On 11 February 2023, protesters staged a picket at a stadium in Krasnogorsk against the opening of a private lyceum instead of a public school in the city. Police arrested at least 6 protesters.

On 12 February 2023, environmental activists from the Finnish Forest Movement and the Swedish Forest Rebellion attempted to block a logging site in Aalistunturi, Kolari demanding a ban on logging activities in the area. Later, police personnel arrested and removed from the venue several activists.

On 13 February 2023, environmental activists from the Finnish Forest Movement and the Swedish Forest Rebellion attempted to block a logging site in Aalistunturi, Kolari demanding a ban on logging activities in the area. Later, police personnel arrested and removed from the venue several activists.

On 13 February 2023, 4 members of ALG demonstrated and blocked the exit of the A96 in the Sendling district in Munchen to call for climate protection and the introduction of a 100km/h speed limit on highways. Police officers intervened to remove the demonstrators.
On 13 February 2023, 4 members of ALG demonstrated and blocked traffic on Rudolphsplatz in Marburg to call for climate protection. Police officers intervened to remove the activists from the road.

On 13 February 2023, 4 members of ALG, including students, blocked the intersection of Harkort and Beethovenstrassee in the South Center in Leipzig to call for climate protection and alert on climate catastrophe. Police officers carried away some demonstrators. This was under the motto 'For the love of survival'.

On 13 February 2023, around 1,000 leftists, at the call of the Technical University student union and Jusos, gathered and carried out sit-in blockades around the Dippoldiswalder Platz in Dresden against historical distortion, Nazis, and far-right appropriation of the Dresden commemoration march of the destruction of Dresden in the Second World. On 14 February 2023, anti-government protesters rallied outside the municipal library of Kozani, where the Prime Minister would be delivering a speech, and they were pushed away by police officers using their batons, when the demonstrators attempted to enter the library.

On 14 February 2023, 3 members of ALG blocked traffic and glued their hands on a road in front of the exit of the fire station, in the intersection Hadikgasse-Nisselgasse in Vienna - Penzing to call for climate protection. They were removed by police officers.

Police forces arrested five protestors and one other individual who assaulted a protestor.

On 14 February 2023, around 20 environmentalists, including members of Last Generation, Scientist Rebellion and Extinction Rebellion, tried to block the access to the private flights terminal of the Malpensa airport in Ferno (Lombardia, Varese) and daubed the structure with paint to raise awareness about climate crisis. On 16 March 2023, between 1,800 (according to the police) and 10,000 (according to unions) people, including CGT, FSU members, and SNCF striking employees, gathered at the Place du Capitole in Toulouse to oppose the government's pension and retirement age reform bill and its decision to pass it through the use of the Article 49.3 of the French Constitution. For unclear reasons, 30 police officers started to charge and disperse a group of demonstrators, eventually arresting 13 people.

On 16 March 2023, people demonstrated in Lille to oppose the government's pension and retirement age reform bill and its decision to pass it through the use of the Article 49.3 of the French Constitution. Police officers (CRS) used tear gas against demonstrators.

On 16 March 2023, several thousand people assembled in Grenoble to oppose the government's pension and retirement age reform bill and its decision to pass it through the use of the Article 49.3 of the French Constitution. Police forces intervened with tear gas to disperse the rally after tension rose.

On 16 March 2023, over 200 workers and USB representatives staged a sit-in before the gates of Italtrans in Calcio (Lombardia, Bergamo) to protest against the subcontracting system and ask for dignified wages. The police intervened and forcibly dispersed the protesters.

On 16 March 2023, over 1,000 people, including students, gathered at Place de la Concorde in Paris (Ile-de-France) to oppose the government's pension and retirement age reform bill and its decision to pass it through the use of Article 49.3 of the French Constitution. Towards the end of the demonstration, police officers from the BRAV-M unit used tear gas to disperse the demonstrators. Journalist Amar Taoualit claimed that he was pushed to the ground by the BRAV-M police officers.

On 16 March 2023, between 1,000 and 3,000 people assembled in Amiens to oppose the government's pension and retirement age reform bill and its decision to pass it through the use of the Article 49.3 of the French Constitution. Police officers (CRS) used tear gas to prevent certain protesters to head into the city center. CGT union delegates participated in the action.

On 16 March 2023, striking garbage collectors continued to block a depot in Vitry-sur-Seine to oppose the government's pension and retirement age reform. Police officers intervened to unblock the depot on the 11th day of the blockade.

On 17 March 2023, around 60 people assembled on a roundabout in Brest, blocking the traffic and lighting fires to oppose the government's pension and retirement age reform bill and its decision to pass it through the use of the Article 49.3 of the French Constitution. Police forces cleared the blockade later during the day.

On 17 March 2023, at the call of UNEF, between 300 and 400 students, including members of Le Poing Leve, blocked several high schools (Turgot and Henri-IV) and the University of Paris 1 (La Sorbonne) in Paris to oppose the government's pension and retirement age reform bill and its decision to pass it through the use of the Article 49.3 of the French Constitution. When the students started a procession to join a picket held by garbage collectors in Ivry-sur-Seine, police officers used tear gas and batons to disperse them. 5 people were arrested.

On 17 March 2023, 5 ALG activists blocked a street in front of the courthouse in Heilbronn, gluing themselves to the tarmac, to call for climate action. The activists were removed from the street by the police.
On 17 March 2023, around 20 ALG activists blocked the Sulzgurtel in Koln, gluing themselves to the tarmac, to call for climate action. The activists were removed from the street by the police.
On 17 March 2023, 4 ALG activists blocked the Stauffenbergallee in Dresden, gluing themselves to the tarmac, to call for climate action. The activists were removed from the street by the police.

On 18 March 2023, an unknown number of people gathered in Amiens to oppose the government's pension and retirement age reform bill and its decision to pass it through the use of the Article 49.3 of the French Constitution. Two participants were arrested by police forces for spray-painting political messages on public buildings.

On 19 March 2023, several hundred people gathered at Les Halles in Paris to oppose the government's pension and retirement age reform bill and its decision to pass it through the use of the Article 49.3 of the French Constitution. Police forces arrested 17 people.

On 19 March 2023, in the afternoon, SUD union affiliates occupied a road toll on the A1 in Senlis and made the passage free of charge to oppose the government's pension and retirement age reform bill and its decision to pass it through the use of the Article 49.3 of the French Constitution. Four demonstrators were taken into custody.

On 20 March 2023, in the evening, about 100 people spontaneously took to the streets of Bordeaux to demonstrate against the government's pension and retirement age reform bill and its decision to pass it through the use of the Article 49.3 of the French Constitution. They were repeatedly teargassed by the police.

On 20 March 2023, about 1,000 people took to the streets in Lorient to oppose the government's pension and retirement age reform bill and its decision to pass it through the use of the Article 49.3 of the French Constitution. Towards the end of the march, the police dispersed about 300 remaining protesters.

On 20 March 2023, in the evening, people spontaneously took to the streets in Toulouse to oppose the government's pension and retirement age reform bill and its decision to pass it through the use of the Article 49.3 of the French Constitution. The police used tear gas bombs to disperse the demonstrators.

On 20 March 2023, 5 members of ALG demonstrated and blocked traffic on Waldeggstrasse in Linz to call for climate protection. They called for a ban on new oil and gas drilling and a speed limit of 100 km/h on highways. Police forces intervened to carry away the demonstrators and remove them from the streets.

On 20 March 2023, 100 people gathered in front of the Puy-de-Dome prefecture in Clermont-Ferrand to oppose the government's pension and retirement age reform bill and its decision to pass it through the use of the Article 49.3 of the French Constitution. They tried disrupting traffic via a sit-in but were dislosged, and then tried erecting barricades with trash cans but were prevented from doing so. Police and BAC resorted to tear gas. Two people were arrested.

On 21 March 2023, in the morning, more than 30 people including local CGT members held a protest in Toulon and along the A57 highway between Sollies and Toulon at the call of the Energy inter-union, blocking several roads, firing pallets and distributing leaflets to oppose the government's pension and retirement age reform bill and its decision to pass it through the use of the Article 49.3 of the French Constitution. During the roadblock, gendarmerie went to the scene, arresting a union member under the pretext that the protest had not been declared.

On 21 March 2023, an unknown number of railway workers and union delegates gathered in Rouen to oppose the government's pension and retirement age reform bill and its decision to pass it through the use of the Article 49.3 of the French Constitution. Police forces tried to disperse the crowd with tear gas. Later that day, an unknown number of people staged a protest action around the Pont Mathilde and slowed traffic down.

On 21 March 2023, between 4,100 (according to the authorities) and 10,000 (according to the unions) people gathered in Nantes to oppose the government's pension and retirement age reform bill and its decision to pass it through the use of the Article 49.3 of the French Constitution. Shortly after the start of the march, police forces fired tear gas to disperse the crowd.

On 21 March 2023, around 60 people gathered in Toulouse to oppose the government's pension and retirement age reform bill and its decision to pass it through the use of the Article 49.3 of the French Constitution. While they were marching on a tram track in the city center, police forces charged them, using tear gas and batons, and subsequently arresting 3 people.

On 21 March 2023, two groups of people spontaneously gathered for an unauthorized protest in Grenoble to oppose the government's pension and retirement age reform bill and its decision to pass it through the use of the Article 49.3 of the French Constitution. They were dispersed by police forces with tear gas.

On 21 March 2023, 5 ALG members demonstrated from Rathenauplatz on the roadway across the Carola Bridge in the direction of Albertplatz and blocked traffic on the corner of Albertstrasse and Archivstrasse in Dresden to call for climate protection. Police officers intervened to take the demonstrators aside.

On 22 March 2023, striking bus drivers from National Express, represented by Unite, picketed outside the bus depot in Coventry over a pay dispute and working conditions. Striking workers prevented busses from leaving the depot. Police forces arrested a woman on suspicion of obstructing the highway.

On 22 March 2023, 5 Last Renovation activists staged a protest action in front of the prefecture in Tours, spraying paint on the building's walls, to raise awareness about the thermal renovation of buildings and demand urgent measures to tackle climate change. Police eventually arrived and removed and arrested the protesters.

On 22 March 2023, several ALG members demonstrated and blocked traffic across the Ringstrasse and in front of the Ministry of Health in Vienna - Inner City to call for climate protection. They denounced the consequences of climate change on people's health. Police officers intervened and arrested one activist.

On 22 March 2023, 6 members of ALG demonstrated and blocked traffic at the Loschwitz bridge in Dresden to urge the government to do more for climate protection. Police officers intervened to carry away the demonstrators.

On 23 March 2023, between 500 (according to the police) and 700 (unions) people took to the streets in Prades. The event was part of a ninth national and cross-sector day of strike and demonstration called by CFDT, CGT, FO, CFE-CGC, CFTC, UNSA, SUD, and FSU to oppose the government's pension and retirement age reform bill, and denounce its passing by means of Article 49.3 of the French Constitution. Around 20 demonstrators tried to rush through a police cordon, which had briefly opened to let an ambulance through, with the intention to block traffic on the RN116 road, pushing a gendarme to the floor and trampling a second one. The police then teargassed demonstrators, including children.

On 23 March 2023, between 3,700 (according to the police) and 4,000 (reporters) people took to the streets of Ancenis-Saint-Gereon to demonstrate.
