The event was part of a ninth national and cross-sector day of strike and protest called by CFDT, CGT, FO, CFE-CGC, CFTC, UNSA, SUD, and FSU to oppose the government's pension and retirement age reform bill, and denounce its passing by means of Article 49.3 of the French Constitution. During the march, demonstrators blocked traffic at different points. At the Ancenis Bridge, which was blocked for five hours, police and gendarme officers used tear gas to disperse the participants. An isolated male participant said to have damaged some vehicles was arrested.

On 23 March 2023, in the early afternoon, between 3,900 (according to the police) and 7,000 (CGT) people took to the streets of Vannes (Morbihan, Bretagne) to demonstrate. The event was part of a ninth national and cross-sector day of strike and protest called by CFDT, CGT, FO, CFE-CGC, CFTC, UNSA, SUD, and FSU to oppose the government's pension and retirement age reform bill, and denounce its passing by means of Article 49.3 of the French Constitution. A group of demonstrators spontaneously blocked the RN165 road, and police forces used tear gas to disperse the blockade.

On 23 March 2023, in the morning, people, including unions' delegates, took to the streets of Coulommiers to demonstrate. The event was part of a ninth national and cross-sector day of strike and protest called by CFDT, CGT, FO, CFE-CGC, CFTC, UNSA, SUD, and FSU to oppose the government's pension and retirement age reform bill, and denounce its passing by means of Article 49.3 of the French Constitution. Five participants were arrested after affixing a banner criticizing the use of Article 49.3 outside the house of Minister Delegate for Parliamentary Relations Franck Riester. They were released at 3 pm.

On 23 March 2023, in the morning, union delegates blocked access to the GDH fuel depot in Frontignan in Occitanie, preventing the refueling of about thirty tanker trucks. The event was part of a ninth national and cross-sector day of strike and protest called by CFDT, CGT, FO, CFE-CGC, CFTC, UNSA, SUD, and FSU to oppose the government's pension and retirement age reform bill, and denounce its passing by means of Article 49.3 of the French Constitution. Police officers used tear gas to disperse the blockade.

On 23 March 2023, between 7,500 (according to the police) and 13,000 (CGT) people took to the streets of Metz to demonstrate. The event was part of a ninth national and cross-sector day of strike and protest called by CFDT, CGT, FO, CFE-CGC, CFTC, UNSA, SUD, and FSU to oppose the government's pension and retirement age reform bill, and denounce its passing by means of Article 49.3 of the French Constitution. Some demonstrators tried to access A31 motorway, and were sprayed with tear gas by the police.
On 23 March 2023, at the call of Komba, around 10,000 people demonstrated close to the Hans-Sachs-Haus in Gelsenkirchen (Altstadt) to call for better pay. One man was arrested.
On 23 March 2023, about 10,000 public sector employees and members of the Komba labor union gathered for a rally in Gelsenkirchen, demanding higher wages. One man was detained.

On 23 March 2023, 6 members of ALG demonstrated and blocked traffic at the Kohlbrand Bridge in Hamburg - Hamburg-Mitte to call for climate protection. Police officers intervened to remove the demonstrators from the road.
On 23 March 2023, 5 Last Generation activists glued themselves to a road in Mainz, demanding immediate climate action. Law enforcers removed them.
On 23 March 2023, about 200 activists gathered for a rally in Grevesmuhlen, protesting against the current management of the refugee affairs. One man was detained.
On 24 March 2023, several dozen Polish football fans gathered for a march in Prague, protesting against alleged machinations with tickets for the matches. Law enforcers detained a few of them.

On 24 March 2023, in the evening, people, including GJ activists, staged a demonstration in front of the prefecture in Montpellier, to oppose the government's pension and retirement age reform bill, and denounce its passing by means of Article 49.3 of the French Constitution. Police officers tried to arrest participants, with some of them resisting their arrest.

On 24 March 2023, people, including CGT affiliates, staged a blockade at the TotalEnergies refinery in Gonfreville-l'Orcher to oppose the government's pension and retirement age reform bill, and denounce its passing by means of Article 49.3 of the French Constitution. The police intervened to disperse them and lift the picket line.

On 24 March 2023, about 100 people blocked a distribution center of supermarket chain Delhaize in Zellik, to demand better working conditions at the distribution center and to oppose Delhaize's plans to turn many stores into independent franchises. Among the protesters were representatives of the union ABVV-FGTB. Police arrested two protesters.
On 24 March 2023, 6 Last Generation activists glued themselves to a road in Munchen, demanding immediate climate action. Law enforcers removed them.

On 25 March 2023, 100% Animalisti activists blocked the entrance of the A22 highway at Verona North toll booth in Verona (Verona, Veneto) and displayed a banner to protest against the decision to cull MJ5, a bear that recently attacked a hiker. Their protest action lasted until police officers identified the activists and removed them from the toll booth entrance to restore car circulation.

On 25 March 2023, around 2:30 pm, between 1,900 (according to Police) and 3,000 people (according to labor unions) took to the streets of Caen to oppose the pension reform bill and demand its withdrawal. During the event, police used tear gas near the university to disperse the crowd, while blocking access to bridges.

On 25 March 2023, members of the right-wing group Patriotic Alternative held a demonstration in Llantwit Major against the council's plan to turn an old primary school into a temporary accommodation for Ukrainian refugees. Members of the Socialist Revolutionary Welsh Underground Network and residents gathered in the town center for a counter-demonstration. The demonstration was mainly peaceful. However, there were some minor shoving and pushing, and police forces arrested two people.

On 25 March 2023, between 300 and 500 people staged a protest, called for by Extinction Rebellion, on and around Eindhoven Airport in Eindhoven, demanding that the airport stop environmental pollution, stick to climate regulations, and decrease the number of leaving flights. Action groups Scientist Rebellion and De Luchtfietsers also attended. A few hundred protesters occupied the private jet terrain, while around 20 protesters blocked the entrance to the private jet terminal. Royal Marechaussee and police arrested 104 protesters.

On 25 March 2023, ALG activists blocked the Elbbrucke bridge in Hamburg - Hamburg-Mitte, gluing themselves to the tarmac, to call for more climate action. One of the activists was physically attacked by a lorry driver, who kicked the former in the stomach. The activists were removed from the street by the police.

On 25 March 2023, at around 5:30 am, people including LFI members, gathered and blocked an entrance to a bus depot in Aubervilliers amid a garbage collectors' strike to oppose the pension reform bill. LFI members claimed two people were injured by the police.

On 25 March 2023, in the evening, people held a gathering in Nancy denouncing the pension reform bill. A fight broke out between far-right and far-left activists (who were taking part in the demonstration) on the sidelines of the gathering, leading to the arrest of two far-right activists by the police. The event was part of a national day of mobilization against racism called by UCIJ to oppose a new asylum and immigration bill proposed by Interior Minister Gerald Darmanin, and calling for solidarity with foreigners and undocumented migrants.

On 26 March 2023, around 50 people gathered outside a hotel in Newquay against the housing of asylum seekers in the hotel. Around 150 people also assembled for the counter-demonstration in support of the refugees. Police forces arrested two people on suspicion of assault.

On 26 March 2023, at the call of the action group European Action Coalition for the Right to Housing and the City, about 1,000 people participated in a protest march in Brussels - Ville de Bruxelles, to demand affordable housing in the context of 'Housing Action Day'. During the march, some protesters occupied a building at the Stalingradlaan. Among these protesters were refugees. Police used violence to end the occupation and arrested five people.

On 27 March 2023, at the call of BlockGas, around 50 people gathered at the Hotel am Parkring in Vienna - Inner City, to protest against the conference of the gas lobby taking place during these days and demand climate action. The protesters were dispersed by the police using tear-gas.

On 28 March 2023, in the afternoon, police forces fired tear gas canisters towards around 6,000 demonstrators (according to the police) who had taken to the streets of Nancy since dawn. The event was part of a tenth national and cross-sector day of strike and demonstration called by eight unions (CFDT, CGT, FO, CFE-CGC, CFTC, UNSA, SUD, and FSU) and five student organizations (UNEF, VL, FIDL, FAGE, and MNL) to oppose the passing of a pension reform bill by means of Article 49.3 of the constitution by the government, and call for the withdrawal of the bill. In total, 9 individuals were arrested during the demonstration.

On 28 March 2023, between 8,500 (according to the police) and 15,000 (unions) people took to the streets of Saint-Nazaire to demonstrate. The event was part of a tenth national and cross-sector day of strike and demonstration called by eight unions (CFDT, CGT, FO, CFE-CGC, CFTC, UNSA, SUD, and FSU) and five student organizations (UNEF, VL, FAGE, FIDL, and MNL) to oppose the passing of a pension reform bill by means of Article 49.3 of the constitution by the government, and call for the withdrawal of the bill. Police forces intervened and fired tear gas canisters at demonstrators to disperse them.

On 28 March 2023, people took to the streets of Vichy to demonstrate. The event was part of a tenth national and cross-sector day of strike and demonstration called by eight unions (CFDT, CGT, FO, CFE-CGC, CFTC, UNSA, SUD, and FSU) and five student organizations (UNEF, VL, FAGE, FIDL, and MNL) to oppose the passing of a pension reform bill by means of Article 49.3 of the constitution by the government, and call for the withdrawal of the bill. Police forces intervened and fired tear gas canisters to disperse demonstrators in front of the train station. 2 demonstrators were arrested.

On 28 March 2023, around 10 Extinction Rebellion activists staged a protest performance at the headquarters of one of the largest Danish banks in Copenhagen against the bank's investments in fossil fuel companies. Later, three activists were detained in relation with the protest.

On 28 March 2023, ALG activists blocked the Veddeler Damm in Hamburg - Hamburg-Mitte, gluing themselves to the tarmac, to call for more climate action. The activists were removed from the street by the police.

On 29 March 2023, in the morning, an unknown number of people continued the protest blockade of the oil storage plant in Frontignan to oppose the government's pension and retirement age reform bill and its decision to pass it through the use of the Article 49.3 of the French Constitution. Police forces ended the occupation, resulting in 6 arrests.

On 29 March 2023, 4 members of ALG demonstrated and blocked traffic around the State Bridge in Salzburg to call for climate protection, an end to new oil and gas drilling, an immediate measure for better air, fewer CO2 emissions, and a 100km/h speed limit on highways. Police officers intervened to carry the demonstrators, glued on the road, off the streets.

On 29 March 2023, 3 far-right affiliates staged a protest and climbed onto scaffolding in front of the Rosa-Lila-Villa in Vienna - Mariahilf against the LGBT community and readings of children's books held by drag queens at this location. They attached a banner and dropped several hundred flyers. The three men were arrested.

On 29 March 2023, 3 members of Ende Gelaende and Kangaroo Collective demonstrated and 2 of them climbed a vent to unfurl a huge banner with the inscription 'Exit Gas Now' in Erlangen. They called for climate protection and the end of gas as an energy source. Demonstrators gathered on the occasion of the European Gas Conference in Vienna. Police officers rappelled them down the inside of the chimney.

On 30 March 2023, police dispersed squatters, who were protesting over the deadly Tempe rail disaster on 28 February and had been occupying the main building of the National and Kapodistrian University of Athens (EKPA) in Athens - Central Athens for 18 days. There were no damages to the building and no tension between police forces and the squatters. 10 protesters were arrested.

On 30 March 2023, between 100 and 200 people, including CGT delegates and CP affiliates, gathered in Savines-le-Lac during the visit of French President Emmanuel Macron to the town to present his water policy, to denounce the French government's pension and retirement age reform bill and its decision to pass it through the use of the Article 49.3 of the French Constitution. CP delegates also denounced the government's managemente of the water reservoir in Sainte-Soline and water policies in general. Police forces dispersed the demonstrators with tear gas after some blocked traffic with a sit-in.

On 30 March 2023, at 10:30 pm, after an official demonstration called by Uprising of the Earth and CP was drawn to a close, people staged an unauthorized protest through the streets of Paris to denounce police violence. 7 people were arrested by law enforcement.

On 30 March 2023, climate activists disrupted the Scottish Parliament session in Edinburgh by shouting as First Minister Humza Yousaf took questions from opposition leaders for the first time. After the protests, members of the public were removed from Parliament's public gallery by security forces.

On 30 March 2023, Scientist Rebellion and Futuro Vegetal climate activists threw red paint on the lions at the door of the Congress of Deputies in Madrid - Centro (Madrid) as a protest against climate change emergency. Police officers arrested the activists.

On 30 March 2023, about 30 Extinction Rebellion protesters staged a protest in the town hall in Amsterdam, against the use of the city's port for coal transports. Protesters disturbed a committee meeting and chained themselves to bicycles in the town hall's main hall. Police arrested 13 protesters who refused to leave the town hall upon the building's closing time.

On 30 March 2023, around 300 people, including SLT and other environmental activists, assembled in Besancon to denounce police violence during the SLT protest action in Sainte-Soline on 25 March 2023, as well as the pension reform. When protesters tried to march in the direction of the Prefecture, police forces used tear gas to disperse the crowd. The event was part of a national demonstration day called by SLT to denounce police violence and oppose plans by the Interior Ministry to shut down the association.
On 31 March 2023, at 4:30 am, police evacuated 39 people, including students, who had occupied a university campus for ten days in Bordeaux to denounce the pension reform bill.

On 31 March 2023, 3 ALG members demonstrated and blocked traffic at the Kohlbrand Bridge in Hamburg - Hamburg-Mitte to call for climate protection. Police officers intervened to remove the demonstrators glued on the road and arrested all 3 of them.

On 31 March 2023, 3 Last Generation activists protested in Munster (Nordrhein-Westfalen) by blocking the street at the main train station with a sit-in to raise awareness about the dangers of global warming and demand an end to the use of oil, gas and coal. Two of them glued themselves onto the road. The police intervened and dissolved the protest by carrying the activists off the road.

On 1 April 2023, three Last Generation activists threw charcoal into the fountain of Piazza di Spagna in Rome - City Center (Lazio, Roma) to call for more climate action and protest against the usage of fossil fuels. The police intervened by dragging the activists away. They were subsequently detained by carabinieri officers.

On 1 April 2023, between 630 and 800 people, mostly Querdenken members, demonstrated in Gottingen under the motto 'Spring awakening for more humanity', calling for peace and opposing coronavirus-related measures. Between 500 and 600 people, including members of DGB, Antifa, and Alliance Against the Right, organized several counter-rallies in the city to oppose the Querdenken march. Police forces intervened physically to remove counter-demonstrators who were carrying out road bloackades.

On 1 April 2023, 7 members of ALG demonstrated along Rovershager Chaussee toward the city center and blocked a street in Rostock to call for climate protection, a 9-euro ticket for public transport, and a 100km/h speed limit on highways. Police officers intervened to carry some of the demonstrators away.

On 1 April 2023, at 3:15 pm, between 3,100 (according to police) and 5,000 (unions) people gathered at a roundabout and took to the streets in Vire to denounce the pension reform bill. Around 5:00 pm, when attendees wanted to head to a local Renaissance MP's office office in Vire, police dispersed them with tear gas.

On 3 April 2023, members of ALG demonstrated and disrupted an SPD event in Lohbrugge in Hamburg - Bergedorf to call for climate protection. The people in the event loudly protested against climate protests. An elderly man stormed the stage and tried to reach the mayor. Bodyguards pushed him away, and police officers arrested him.
On 4 April 2023, 9 members of ALG demonstrated and blocked traffic on the Kohlbrand Bridge in Hamburg - Hamburg-Mitte to call for climate protection. Police officers arrested all the demonstrators.
On 4 April 2023, police forces intervened and dispersed by force a strike in Ivry-sur-Seine. The reason behind the strike was not reported.

On 5 April 2023, Momentum MPs, as well as one independent MP, protested outside the government building in Budapest - I, unbundling the fence around the building, trying to raise awareness about the lack of openness in government. The protesters entered into mild scuffles when police tried to re-erect the fence, pushing an independent MP on the ground, which led him to get his face bruised.

On 5 April 2023, 4 ALG activists blocked the Neue Kant street in Berlin - Charlottenburg-Wilmersdorf, gluing themselves to the tarmac, to call for climate action. The activists were removed from the street by the police.

On 6 April 2023, police dispersed the protesters in Poltavskaya, who had been blocking the road for two days to prevent trucks from transporting garbage to a nearby landfill through a neighborhood in which people live.

On 6 April 2023, at 10:00 am, between 2,100 (according to police) and 4,000 (unions) people held a gathering at Maison du Peuple before heading towards the city center in Belfort, with some blocking the A36 motorway. The event was part of an eleventh national and cross-sector day of strike and demonstration called by eight unions (CFDT, CGT, FO, CFE-CGC, CFTC, UNSA, SUD, and FSU) and five student organizations (UNEF, VL, FAGE, FIDL, and MNL) to oppose the passing of a pension reform bill by means of Article 49.3 of the constitution by the government, and call for the withdrawal of the bill. People who had gathered at the entrance of Belfort city, blocking traffic, to demonstrate were teargassed by police forces, and several of them were arrested.

On 6 April 2023, people took to the streets in Le Meux. The event was part of an eleventh national and cross-sector day of strike and demonstration called by eight unions (CFDT, CGT, FO, CFE-CGC, CFTC, UNSA, SUD, and FSU) and five student organizations (UNEF, VL, FAGE, FIDL, and MNL) to oppose the passing of a pension reform bill by means of Article 49.3 of the constitution by the government, and call for the withdrawal of the bill. Police forces arrested 1 civilian, accusing him of attempting to damage the gendarmerie vehicle. Also, 1 protester was injured.

On 6 April 2023, between 10,000 (according to the prefecture) and 170,000 (unions) people took to the streets in Marseille. The event was part of an eleventh national and cross-sector day of strike and demonstration called by eight unions (CFDT, CGT, FO, CFE-CGC, CFTC, UNSA, SUD, and FSU) and five student organizations (UNEF, VL, FAGE, FIDL, and MNL) to oppose the passing of a pension reform bill by means of Article 49.3 of the constitution by the government, and call for the withdrawal of the bill. Police forces intervened and dispersed the protesters.

On 6 April 2023, after the procession of the day over the pension reform was drawn to a close, about 20 people headed towards a barracks in Grenoble to denounce the pension reform bill. They were quickly dispersed by police, who used tear gas.

On 6 April 2023, between 1,100 (according to the authorities) and 1,500 (according to the unions) people staged a protest in Vesoul. The event was part of an eleventh national and cross-sector day of strike and demonstration called by eight unions (CFDT, CGT, FO, CFE-CGC, CFTC, UNSA, SUD, and FSU) and five student organizations (UNEF, VL, FAGE, FIDL, and MNL) to oppose the passing of a pension reform bill by means of Article 49.3 of the constitution by the government, and call for the withdrawal of the bill. Police forces used tear gas against the crowd.
On 6 April 2023, 9 ALG activists blocked the a street at Elbtunnel in Hamburg - Altona, to call for climate action. The activists were removed from the street by the police.

On 6 April 2023, five ALG activists blocked a street at Elbbrucken in Hamburg - Hamburg-Mitte, gluing themselves to the tarmac, to call for climate action. The activists were removed from the street by the police. Close-by, at Veddeler Damm, six activists tried to glue themselves to the street, yet were removed by the police before they could do so.

On 8 April 2023, members of the civil society collective Menoume Energoi protested on the Acropolis Hill in Athens - Central Athens, unfurling a giant banner in solidarity with a 12-year-old girl, who had been sexually abused and procured to prostitution. Police detained 4 protesters.

On 10 April 2023, about 20 Extinction Rebellion activists protested in the departures hall of Schiphol Airport in Schiphol, against the winning of a court case against Schiphol Airport by airline KLM, which allows KLM to maintain its current number of flights. Protesters argued that KLM is polluting and contributes to global warming. Royal Marechaussee arrested 3 protesters who refused to leave the departures hall.

On 11 April 2023, around 50 students, including Syndicat de Combat Universitaire de Montpellier (SCUM) affiliates, staged a demonstration in the Les Pres d'Arenes area of Montpellier, briefly blocking railway tracks. They opposed the government's pension reform bill. Police forces intervened and arrested 3 students for obstructing railway traffic.

On 12 April 2023, in the morning, people, including a group of about 100 people, blocked several roads with improvised barricades in and around Nantes (notably at Porte de la Chapelle, Carquefou, and Belle-Etoile), disrupting traffic and the city's bus network, to oppose the passing of the pension reform bill. This event was part of a 'dead city operation' launched on social networks by ultra-left groups. Police forces intervened to clear some of the blockades.

On 13 April 2023, members of Rouvikonas protested at the Presidential Mansion in Athens - Central Athens, demanding the protection of a 12-year-old girl, who had been sexually abused and procured to prostitution, after the girl was attacked in her home in an act of intimidation. There were 13 detentions.

On 13 April 2023, between 9,900 (according to authorities) and 22,000 (unions) people staged a protest march starting from Place Marechal Lyautey in Lyon. The event was part of a 12th national and cross-sector day of strike and demonstration called by eight unions (CFDT, CGT, FO, CFE-CGC, CFTC, UNSA, SUD, and FSU) and five student organizations (UNEF, VL, FAGE, FIDL, and MNL) to oppose the passing of a pension reform bill by means of Article 49.3 of the constitution by the government, and call for the withdrawal of the bill. Towards the end of the protest march, police forces charged on the head of the procession with tear gas on Place Hernu de Villeurbanne.

On 13 April 2023, 3,000 people took to the streets in Vannes to demonstrate. The event was part of a 12th national and cross-sector day of strike and demonstration called by eight unions (CFDT, CGT, FO, CFE-CGC, CFTC, UNSA, SUD, and FSU) and five student organizations (UNEF, VL, FAGE, FIDL, and MNL) to oppose the passing of a pension reform bill by means of Article 49.3 of the constitution by the government, and call for the withdrawal of the bill. Police forces intervened and fired tear gas canisters at protesters to disperse them, injuring one protester. Two participants were arrested.

On 13 April 2023, an unknown number of people associated with the Quit with Coal blocked a railroad in the port area in Amsterdam, to protest against the use of the port for coal transports. Police arrested 4 protesters.

On 14 April 2023, animal rights activists, holding placards reading 'there is no excuse for animal abuse' and chanting slogans against the slaughter of animals (protesting against the Greek Easter lamb feast tradition), approached the clerics during the Good Friday Epitaph procession. Police removed the protesters as the procession entered Syntagma square in Athens - Central Athens.

On 14 April 2023, a group of Labour representatives affiliated to one truck company gathered for a rally in near the embassy of Germany in Warsaw, protesting against allegedly unfair and too strict actions taken by the German police against Polish cargo drivers. Law enforcers briefly detained 19 individuals for alleged provoking unrest and chaos, but released them shortly after.

On 14 April 2023, at the call of the inter-union group (CFDT, CGT, FO, CFE-CGC, CFTC, UNSA, SUD, and FSU), around 200 people took to the streets of Poitiers to oppose the passing of the pension reform bill, following the Constitutional Council's approval of key elements of the bill on 14 April 2023. Police forces fired tear gas to disperse the demonstrators near the Leon Blum footbridge.

On 14 April 2023, around 400 people assembled at the Miroir d'Eau in Nantes to oppose the passing of the pension reform bill, following the Constitutional Council's approval of key elements of the bill on 14 April 2023. Police forces intervened with tear gas to end the protest.

On 14 April 2023, in the evening, following the end of a spontaneous protest action to oppose the passing of the pension reform bill, following the Constitutional Council's approval of key elements of the bill on 14 April 2023, several people took to the streets of Strasbourg to demonstrate. Police forces used tear gas to disperse them.

On 14 April 2023, around 1,000 people, including an LFI MP, assembled on Place de l'Hotel de Ville in Paris to oppose the passing of the pension reform bill, following the Constitutional Council's approval of key elements of the bill on 14 April 2023. The crowd staged a protest march toward Republique Square. At Bastill Square, a large police force was mobilised to disperse participants with tear gas.

On 14 April 2023, early morning, 16 members of ALG demonstrated and blocked traffic in the district Geidorf (Geidorfplatz/Parkstrasse/Ringstrasse/Glacisstrasse) in Graz to call for climate protection. They demanded a 100km/h speed limit on highways and a ban on new oil and gas demands. Police officers intervened to carry away the demonstrators.

On 15 April 2023, about 3000 pro-life activists, including representatives of the Catholic church, gathered for a march in Prague, protesting against abortions and demanding their restriction. A group of pro-choice activists tried to block the pro-life march in Prague, demanding preservation of the abortion rights. Law enforcers detained 4 counter-protesters and prevented them from blocking the streets

On 15 April 2023, around 6:00 pm, nearly 300 people including NPA, EELV and SUD members gathered at the Grand square in Lille. Police dispersed the gathering later in the evening. The event opposed the passing of the pension reform bill following the Constitutional Council's approval of key elements of the bill on 14 April 2023.

On 15 April 2023, dozens of activists from Animal Rising climbed the fences and attempted to enter the Grand National horse race in Aintree to protest the event and its use of animals, and cause disruption before the race. Police forces arrested 118 protesters.

On 16 April 2023, in the evening, several thousand people including health workers and CGT members gathered in Paris, with police dispersing crowds and making 138 arrests. The event opposed the passing of the pension reform bill following the Constitutional Council's approval of key elements of the bill on 14 April 2023.

On 16 April 2023, around 100 people, mostly far-right affiliates, members of FPOE, IBOE, and hooligans, gathered in front of the Rosa Lila Villa in Vienna - Inner City against an event of a reading by a drag queen to children. They tried to block traffic on the Ring but police officers used tear gas to disperse them. Two people did the Nazi salute. Between 400 and 500 people, including the LGBTQ+ community, gathered for a counter-demonstration against Nazi propaganda and for LGBTQ+ rights.

On 17 April 2023, in the morning, people gathered at a university in Caen to block it, occupy a building and denounce the passing of the pension reform bill ahead of the French President's televised address to the nation to justify the reform. Police intervened to evacuate the building.

On 17 April 2023, in the evening, between 500 and 1,000 people gathered at the old port before heading to the town hall in Marseille to denounce the passing of the pension reform bill during the French President's televised address to the nation to justify the reform. Police arrested six attendees. The event was called for by Attac.

On 17 April 2023, at 8:00 pm, 1,000 people including farmers gathered for a pot- and pan-banging protest in front of the town hall and then Lices square in Rennes to denounce the passing of the pension reform bill during the French President's televised address to the nation to justify the reform. The police using tear gas to disperse the crowd. The event was called for by FO, NPA and Attac.

On 17 April 2023, between 15 and 20 members of ALG demonstrated and blocked traffic on the Reichsbrucke in Vienna - Donaustadt to call for climate protection, a 100km/h speed limit on highways, and a ban on new oil and gas drilling. 6 people were arrested.

On 18 April 2023, 3 Restore Wetlands Movement activists interrupted a parliamentary session in Stockholm demanding a total ban on import of Russian oil and natural gas. The activists were removed by the security personnel.

On 18 April 2023, people gathered to oppose the presence of the Minister of Labor Olivier Dussopt in Chartres, and denounce the government's pension reform. Gendarmerie members used tear gas to disperse protesters.

On 18 April 2023, Restore Wetlands Movement blocked traffic in Stockholm to demand the government restore drained wetlands in the country and to draw attention to environmental issues. Later, the police intervened and stopped the demonstration, at least 15 people were detained.

On 19 April 2023, before 10:30 am, 100 people, including an LFI MP and union delegates, gathered for a pot- and pan-banging protest at a wood factory in Muttersholtz, during a visit of President Emmanuel Macron, to denounce the passing of the pension reform bill following the French President's televised address to the nation to justify the reform on 17 April. The police cordoned off the village's center, leading the attendees to gather at the entrance of the village.

On 19 April 2023, an unknown number of people joined a protest action of CGT in the Chateau des Ducs in Nantes, occupying the castle's walls to denounce the pension reform of the government. They were later joined by SLT activists, opposing plans by the Interior Ministry to dissolve their association. A young man was arrested by police officers near the scene of the demonstration, on the grounds that he was carrying a Molotov cocktail.

On 19 April 2023, an unknown number of people protested in front of a Delhaize supermarket in Mons, blocking access to the store, against the plans of Delhaize's management to turn many of its stores into independent franchizes. Among the protesters were representatives of unions CNE and ABVV-FGTB. Police handcuffed and took away one protester.

On 20 April 2023, Restore Wetlands Movement blocked traffic in Stockholm to demand the government restore drained wetlands in the country and to draw attention to environmental issues. Later, police personnel blocked the way, aiming to stop the demonstration.

On 21 April 2023, 250 protesters including unionists gathered for a pot- and pan-banging protest in Montreuil, to denounce the passing of the pension reform bill during the French President's televised address to the nation to justify the reform. Police Forces pushed back the protesters and fired tear gas towards them when they tried to bypass the police blockade outside the Cap Horn health center which was being visited by the French Minister of Social Affairs and Health.

On 22 April 2023, people, including left-wing activists, Young Ecologists (youth branch of EELV), Young Communists, CGT, NUPES, and Yellow Vests members, gathered for a pot- and pan-banging protest at the SNU village (General National Service) and in city center in Caen against the government's plan to generalize the General National Service, with some denouncing a potential 'militarization of youth', and to oppose the government's pension reform. Around 1 pm, police pushed back and clubbed some demonstrators who were preventing access to the SNU facility.

On 22 April 2023, activists from the Animal Rising group climbed the fences and attempted to enter the Scottish Grand National horse race in Ayr to protest the event and its use of animals, and cause disruption before the race. Police forces arrested some 25 participants.

On 22 April 2023, ALG activists gathered at Kurfurstendamm in Berlin - Mitte, to spray paint onto the windows of various luxury boutiques, calling for an end to the increased emissions that rich people account for and demanding climate action. The activists were taken into custody by the police.

On 22 April 2023, seven Extinction Rebellion activists were involved in a protest at the ING Bank in Nijmegen (Gelderland), as part of a nationwide protest protesting the bank's investment in fossil fuels, and chaining themselves to a pillar, causing damage to the floor. They were arrested and convicted for local peace breach and property damage.

On 23 April 2023, 4 ALG activists blocked the start section of the Vienna City Marathon at Wagramer Strasse in Vienna - Donaustadt, attempting to glue themselves to the tarmac, to call for climate action. The activists were removed from the street by the police.

On 23 April 2023, six ALG activists blocked the racing track at a Formula-E race in Berlin - Tempelhof-Schoneberg, to protest against the emissions caused by motorsports, and call for climate action. The activists were first removed from the track by security personnel, and later taken into custody by the police.

On 24 April 2023, several hundreds of students, joined by teachers, including of the PDSZ union, marched from the Interior Ministry to the government seat building in Budapest, demanding better conditions for teachers and students, but also condemning the introduction of a draft law limiting the academic freedom in schools. When trying to push through the wire fence around the government building, the police used teargas and pushed back the crowd. The teargas also affected a journalist, who says he was not warned about the upcoming teargas use. Two independent MPs, as well as Momentum MPs, took part in the rally. The police started an investigation on the unsanctioned rally. The rally ended with a sit-in, which the Parbeszed mayor of Budapest and an MSZP MP attended.

On 24 April 2023, environmental activists blocked motorway traffic in Stockholm to demand the government restore drained wetlands in the country, to ban peat mining and to draw attention to environmental issues. Later, police personnel stopped the activists, at least 16 people were arrested.

On 24 April 2023, during the day, environmental activists from Futuro Vegetal vandalized with black paint the headquarters of PP in Madrid - Chamberi against their climate change policies. Police arrested three people following the vandalization.

On 24 April 2023, during the day, environmental activists from Futuro Vegetal vandalized with black paint the headquarters of PSOE in Madrid - Moncloa-Aravaca against their climate change policies. Police arrested two people following the vandalization.

On 24 April 2023, an unknown number of climate activists associated with action groups Extinction Rebellion, Environmental Defence, and Fossil Free NL staged a protest during a shareholders' meeting of the bank ING in Amsterdam, against ING's investment in fossil fuels. Protesters protested both outside and inside the venue, disrupting the meeting by chanting slogans. Police arrested one protester who blew a whistle and announced that he would stay stuck to the floor until ING stops fossil investments.

On 24 April 2023, at the call of ALG, protesters blocked the Hauptstrasse in Berlin - Tempelhof-Schoneberg, to call for climate action. The protesters were removed from the street by the police. The protest was part of a series of protests by ALG in Berlin that day.

On 24 April 2023, at the call of ALG, protesters blocked the highway entries Spandauer Damm and Kaiserdam, Hohenzollerndamm, as well as a street at Ernst-Reuter-Platz in Berlin - Charlottenburg-Wilmersdorf, to call for climate action. The protesters were removed from the street by the police. The protest was part of a series of protests by ALG in Berlin that day.

On 24 April 2023, at the call of ALG, protesters blocked the Landsberger Allee in Berlin - Friedrichshain-Kreuzberg, to call for climate action. The protesters were removed from the street by the police. The protest was part of a series of protests by ALG in Berlin that day.

On 24 April 2023, at the call of ALG, protesters blocked the Frankfurter Allee in Berlin - Lichtenberg, to call for climate action. The protesters were removed from the street by the police. The protest was part of a series of protests by ALG in Berlin that day.

On 24 April 2023, at the call of ALG, around 40 protesters blocked traffic at Alexanderplatz while others blocked the intersection of Muhlendamm and Fischerinsel, Mullerstrasse, Heidestrasse, and the Strasse des 17. Juni at Tiergarten in Berlin - Mitte, to call for climate action. The protesters were removed from the street by the police. The protest was part of a series of protests by ALG in Berlin that day.

On 24 April 2023, at the call of ALG, protesters blocked the crossing of Petersburger Strasse and Danziger Strasse in Berlin - Pankow, to call for climate action. The protesters were removed from the street by the police. The protest was part of a series of protests by ALG in Berlin that day.

On 24 April 2023, at the call of ALG, protesters blocked the Puschkinallee in Berlin - Treptow-Kopenick, to call for climate action. The protesters were removed from the street by the police. The protest was part of a series of protests by ALG in Berlin that day.

On 25 April 2023, at the call of the action group Occupy RUG, around 100 students occupied the main hall of the Academy Building at the University of Groningen (RUG) in Groningen (Groningen) to protest against the executive board's refusal to reinstate former professor Susanne Tauber, who had criticized the university's gender equality policies. Police forcibly evacuated the students, dragging one down the stairs by their legs and striking an assistant professor with a baton. No arrests were made. The event was condemned by some participants for 'disproportionate police violence'.
On 25 April 2023, 15 ALG activists blocked an exit of highway A7 in Linz, gluing themselves to the tarmac, to demand a speed limit of 100 km/h on national highways.

On 25 April 2023, at the call of ALG, protesters blocked the Hauptstrasse and Tempelhofer Damm in Berlin - Tempelhof-Schoneberg, to call for climate action. The protesters were removed from the street by the police. The protest was part of a series of protests by ALG in Berlin that day.

On 25 April 2023, at the call of ALG, protesters blocked the highway entry Hohenzollerndamm, Spandauer Damm, Rudolf-Wissel-Brucke, Ernst-Reuter-Platz, and Wexstrasse in Berlin - Charlottenburg-Wilmersdorf, to call for climate action. The protesters were removed from the street by the police. The protest was part of a series of protests by ALG in Berlin that day.

On 25 April 2023, at the call of ALG, protesters blocked the Frankfurter Allee and Landsberger Allee in Berlin - Lichtenberg, to call for climate action. The protesters were removed from the street by the police. The protest was part of a series of protests by ALG in Berlin that day.

On 25 April 2023, at the call of ALG, protesters blocked the intersection Sonnenallee and Hermannplatz in Berlin - Neukolln, to call for climate action. The protesters were removed from the street by the police. The protest was part of a series of protests by ALG in Berlin that day.

On 25 April 2023, at the call of ALG, protesters blocked the Schonhauser Allee and Prenzlauer Allee, and Greifswalder Strasse in Berlin - Pankow, to call for climate action. The protesters were removed from the street by the police. The protest was part of a series of protests by ALG in Berlin that day.

On 26 April 2023, 7 Last Generation activists gathered on the GRA beltway (Grande Raccordo Anulare) in Rome - Aurelio (Roma, Lazio) with the intention to block the traffic to demonstrate against the continued use of gas and coal as energy sources. The police removed the protesters from the beltway.

On 26 April 2023, 7 Last Generation activists gathered on the GRA beltway (Grande Raccordo Anulare) in Rome - San Basilio (Roma, Lazio) with the intention to block the traffic to demonstrate against the continued use of gas and coal as energy sources. The police removed the protesters from the beltway.

On 27 April 2023, around 200 people attempted to reach the castle of Joux in La Cluse-et-Mijoux, where President Macron was on an official visit, to oppose his government's pension reform. Police forces pushed back the demonstrators with shields, batons and tear gas.

On 27 April 2023, in the evening, around 200 far-left activists peacefully gathered in Terreaux Square in Lyon to denounce the cancellation of a concert on the roof of the Fourviere Basilic due, among other things, to 'threats of serious attacks from the far right'. They were dispersed by police forces after seeking to take to the streets.

On 28 April 2023, environmental activists, including Extinction Rebellion and Vegan Activism members, blocked traffic in Copenhagen, calling for a transformation of farmland into protected natural areas, with a goal of reaching 30% of Denmark's total land area and to draw attention to environmental issues. Later, police personnel intervened and removed activists from the venue.

On 28 April 2023, a dozen of people protested in St. Petersburg against the installation of cellular communication equipment on the tower next to a residential building. Police arrested one protester for refusing to follow the order to leave.

On 28 April 2023, 250 anti-militarists marched from Villasor to Decimomannu air base and back to Villasor (Sud Sardegna, Sardegna) to protest against the three upcoming military training, notably NATO's Noble Jump, Defense's Joint Stars and Open Sea. Police officers dispersed and repelled protesters standing in front of the air base with tear gas and water cannons. No injured were reported.

On 28 April 2023, anti-militarists and pacifist activists staged a demonstration outside the military air base in Decimomannu (Sardegna, Cagliari), denouncing its existence. The police dispersed the demonstrators using water cannons and tear gas.

On 29 April 2023, an unknown number of ABVV-FGTB and ACV-CSC affiliates protested in front of a Delhaize supermarket in Gent, against the decision by Delhaize's management to turn many of its stores into independent franchises. Protesters blocked the entrance to the store with shopping carts. Police intervened to clear access for customers, and arrested 6 protesters who refused to show their IDs.

On 29 April 2023, 22 Greenpeace activists took to the streets of the port of Zeebrugge (Vlaanderen), to demand that the Belgian gas company Fluxys stop starting new gas projects. Protesters entered Fluxys's gas terminal in the port with kayaks, climbed the terminal's docks, and hung up banners. Police arrested 14 protesters from Belgium, Austria, Germany, Netherlands, France, and the United Kingdom.

On 29 April 2023, 18 ALG activists blocked the Tauentzienstrasse in Berlin - Tempelhof-Schoneberg, gluing themselves to the tarmac, to call for climate action. The activists were removed from the streets by the police.

On 30 April 2023, more than 3,000 FLINTA, German abbreviation for 'Frauen, Lesben, Intergeschlechtliche, nichtbinare, trans and agender' meaning women/females, lesbians, intersex, non-binary, trans and agender people, protested in Berlin - Friedrichshain-Kreuzberg (Berlin) under the motto 'Take Back the Night' for the destruction of the patriarchy. The police intervened, interrupted the protest multiple times, allegedly beat some protesters and arrested 3 people.
On 1 May 2023, 3 people staged pickets at different locations in Yekaterinburg, protesting against the Russian military invasion of Ukraine. Police interrupted the pickets, arresting all protesters.

On 1 May 2023, around 700 people gathered in Gera (Thuringen) at the call of the far-right, though no protest motives were specified. A counterprotest took place with around 500 people. The police were criticized for their intervention and for keeping demonstrators encircled for hours.

On 1 May 2023, at the call of 'Schwarz-Roter 1. Mai', around 800 people staged a protest march from Hagenbeck Tierpark to Theodor-Heuss-Platz in Hamburg - Eimsbuttel (Hamburg), to protest for workers rights on the occasion of International Worker's Day. Around 2,700 people gathered at the call of 'Wer hat, der gibt' ('He who has, gives') and staged a protest march from Eppendorfer Baum to Bahnhof Dammtor for the same reasons. A police officer pushed a demonstrator, whose head hit the ground violently, the 19-year-old was treated at a hospital.
On 2 May 2023, 8 ALG activists blocked the Opernring in Vienna - Inner City, gluing themselves to the tarmac, to call for climate action. The activists were removed from the streets by the police.
On 2 May 2023, ALG activists blocked the Wahringer Gurtel in Vienna - Wahring, gluing themselves to the tarmac, to call for climate action. The activists were removed from the streets by the police.

On 2 May 2023, ALG activists blocked the Kaiserdammbrucke, Hohenzollerndamm, and Rudolf-Wissel-Brucke in Berlin - Charlottenburg-Wilmersdorf, gluing themselves to the tarmac, to call for climate action. The activists were removed from the streets by the police.

On 2 May 2023, ALG activists blocked the Frankfurter Allee in Berlin - Friedrichshain-Kreuzberg, gluing themselves to the tarmac, to call for climate action. The activists were removed from the streets by the police.

On 2 May 2023, around 100 ALG staged a protest march on Karl-Marx-Allee purposefully going slowly to block traffic, while other ALG activists blocked the Fennstrasse in Berlin - Mitte, gluing themselves to the tarmac, to call for climate action. The activists were removed from the streets by the police.
On 2 May 2023, ALG activists blocked the Sonnenallee in Berlin - Neukolln, gluing themselves to the tarmac, to call for climate action. The activists were removed from the streets by the police.

On 2 May 2023, ALG activists blocked the Prenzlauer Allee, Eberswalder Strasse and Landsberger Allee in Berlin - Pankow, gluing themselves to the tarmac, to call for climate action. The activists were removed from the streets by the police.

On 2 May 2023, ALG activists blocked the Sachsendamm, Tempelhofer Damm, and Dominicusstrasse in Berlin - Tempelhof-Schoneberg, gluing themselves to the tarmac, to call for climate action. The activists were removed from the streets by the police.

On 3 May 2023, around 100 students, joined by PDSZ members, as well as a Momentum MP, Parbeszed MPs and the mayor of Budapest, and an independent MP, marched to protest in the Buda castle outside the government seat in Budapest - I, demanding more academic freedom. When a group of students attempted to break a fence, the police used teargas against the students. At least 5 people were arrested.
On 3 May 2023, several dozen activists gathered for a rally in Warsaw, protesting against alleged politicization of the so-called Smolensk tragedy. At least one of them was detained.

On 3 May 2023, several hundred people, including Yellow Vests members, held a protest in Nantes to oppose the pension reform of the government and call for its withdrawal. BAC police forces intervened and arrested one protest. The reasons behind the arrest were not reported.

On 3 May 2023, in the afternoon, people, including GJ activists, gathered outside the Municipality of Paris to protest against the pension reform. Two participants were arrested by the police, after a police cordon tried to push back the crowd.

On 3 May 2023, members of Just Stop Oil staged a slow march and blocked traffic from Downing Street to Parliament Square in London - Westminster, demanding that the Government stops all new UK oil and gas projects. Police forces arrested 23 protesters.

On 3 May 2023, around 20 Greenpeace activists staged a protest and climbed on the roof of the state parliament in Hannover against natural gas drilling plans. Some protesters were carried away by members of the SEK federal police unit and of the Saxon anti-riot police.

On 4 May 2023, municipal workers held a protest during the ordinary plenary session in Logrono (La Rioja) to demand better working conditions. Police agents physically escorted the protesters out of the building but no further incident was recorded.

On 5 May 2023, 7 Kurds and 3 Greek Cypriots, who started a hunger strike outside the Supreme Court in solidarity with a Kurdish political refugee and activist were removed from the spot by police, together with a journalist filming the event. The previous day the refugee, who was being held in Nicosia Central Prison on terrorism charges for being a member of PKK, had started an indefinite hunger strike to protest his extradition to Germany and demanding his release. Police moved the hunger strikers to a nearby venue and they were forbidden to set up a tent.

On 6 May 2023, several hundred activists gathered for a rally in Prague, demanding immediate resignation of the government, leaving EU and NATO and cancelling support to Kyiv during the ongoing war with Russia. Several former government officials and members of the Communist Party also participated. At least one individual was detained for alleged approval of genocide - for wearing the Wagner Group patch.
On 6 May 2023, around 650 people assembled in the city center of Lyon to stage a protest against the pension reform of the government. Police forces responded with tear gas and arrested 4 protesters.

On 6 May 2023, hundreds of republican people gathered on Trafalgar Square in London - Westminster to protest against King Charles' coronation and the monarchy. Demonstrators waved placards including 'Not my King'. Police forces arrested at least six people, including the organizer.

On 6 May 2023, a group of ALG activists blocked traffic, gluing their hands to the street, near the main train station in Berlin - Mitte (Berlin) to demand more climate action from the federal government.

On 7 May 2023, around 1,500 SOR party supporters and members, including the Orhei district council president, protested in Chisinau - Buiucani, demanding the resignation of president Maia Sandu and snap elections. Police arrested 27 persons, accused of suspicious activity and holding inflammable liquids. A journalist had his phone broken by a pole thrown by one of the protesters. A group of counter-protesters protested against the SOR party.

On 9 May 2023, a group of 70 activists affiliated with the student action group Occupy EUR occupied a building of the Erasmus University in Rotterdam, to protest against the university's ties with fossil fuel companies and the inaccessibility of the campus for people with physical disabilities. Police arrested 14 protesters who refused to leave the building by the end of the day.

On 10 May 2023, between 200 and 300 taxi drivers protested in Amsterdam, blocking several roads with their cars, against the municipality's new traffic circulation plans. Police arrested 2 protesters.

On 10 May 2023, activists from Extinction Rebellion blocked entrance to a refinery factory near Porvoo, Uusimaa, calling to stop using of Russia-sourced oil as well as to reduce production level. Later, police personnel removed activists from the venue, 42 people were arrested.

On 10 May 2023, several groups of activists interrupted the convention of VW corporation in Berlin. Among them, environmental activists demanding more responsible climate policy - someone pelted a cake on the company representatives. Other activists protested against the company's ignorance of human rights violations in China, especially related to Uyghur forced labor. They were removed from the premises by the police. Another group of activists, including ALG, gathered outside the location with pickets.

On 10 May 2023, about 500 activists gathered for a rally in Schleusingen, protesting against a proposed opening of a new facility for refugees. A far-right activist Axel Schlimper also participated and was detained.

On 10 May 2023, several activists aimed to block traffic in Wolfsburg, demanding immediate climate action and a city infrastructure more friendly to pedestrians and wheelchair-users at the expense of cars. Law enforcers briefly detained most of them before the action could be completed.

On 10 May 2023, between 30 and 40 activists of End Fossil: Occupy, including many students, occupied a building of the technical university in Delft (Zuid-Holland), to demand that the university cut its ties with fossil fuel companies. In the evening, the university called the police to end the occupation. Twelve protesters stayed past midnight, after which police physically removed them from the building.

On 11 May 2023, about 15 End Fossil: Occupy activists, including many students, occupied a building of the university of applied sciences in Velp (Gelderland), to demand that the university cut its ties with fossil fuel companies and include more information on climate change in its curricula. Police called upon protesters to terminate their action, and dragged out one protester who refused to leave.

On 12 May 2023, hundreds of environmental activists took part in the 'Free the Earth' protest, staging demonstrations and obstructing traffic across various locations in Copenhagen. Activists called for a transformation of farmland into protected natural areas, with a goal of reaching 30% of Denmark's total land area as well as to draw attention to environmental issues and to demand the declaration of climate emergency. As a result, multiple individuals were apprehended and taken into custody. Activists from Extinction Rebellion, Greenpeace, NOAH, International Socialists, Global Action (GA), Grandparents' Climate Action and the Green Student Movement took part in the event, among others.

On 12 May 2023, in the morning, ALG activists staged simultaneous sit-ins on Franz-Josefs-Kai and Schwedenbrucke in Vienna - Inner City, gluing their hands to the tarmac and blocking traffic, to demand more climate action, specifically a 100km/h highway speed limit and a ban on all new gas and fuel projects. Eight participants were temporarily arrested by the police.

On 12 May 2023, over 25 Extinction Rebellion activists protested at the Noord-Holland provincial government building in Haarlem, to demand the closure of the polluting steel plant Tata Steel in Wijk aan Zee. Police arrested between 18 (according to police) and 21 (according to protesters) protesters.
On 13 May 2023, ALG activists protested at Brandenburger Tor in Berlin - Mitte to call for climate protection. The police chiseled protesters' hands to remove them from the street.

On 15 May 2023, ALG activists and people from Cabaret Artists for Future in Vienna - Floridsdorf to call for climate protection. The activists glued themselves on Floridsdorfer Bridge and the North Bridge. The police intervened and arrested 40 people across several events organized on the same day in the city.

On 15 May 2023, ALG activists and people from Cabaret Artists for Future in Vienna - Landstrasse to call for climate protection. The activists glued themselves at Schwarzenbergplatz. The police intervened and arrested 40 people across several events organized on the same day in the city.

On 15 May 2023, ALG activists and people from Cabaret Artists for Future protested in Vienna - Leopoldstadt to call for climate protection. The activists glued themselves to blocked roads on Schwedenbrucke, Salztorbrucke, Reichsbrucke, and Praterbrucke. The police intervened and arrested 40 people across several events organized on the same day in the city.

On 15 May 2023, environmental activists from ALG protested in front of the Linken Wienzeile buildings in Vienna - Mariahilf to call for climate protection. They glued themselves on the street to block the road. The police removed the blockades.

On 15 May 2023, ALG activists protested in Berlin - Charlottenburg-Wilmersdorf to call for climate protection. They blocked roads by gluing themselves to cars. The police intervened and unscrewed the car wheels to remove the blockade.
On 15 May 2023, ALG activists protested in Berlin - Pankow to call for climate protection. They glued themselves to car tires. The police intervened and remove a protester with an angle grinder.

On 15 May 2023, law enforcers ordered about 100 environmental activists to vacate an occupational camp in the Wuhlheide area (Berlin - Treptow-Kopenick) and the camp was liquidated. The activists were protesting against a proposed construction of a new highway in the area. Some of them were detained.

On 16 May 2023, Kurds and Greek Cypriots rallied outside the Supreme Court in solidarity with Kurdish political refugee and activist Kenan Ayaz, who was being held in Nicosia Central Prison on terrorism charges for being a member of PKK. Ayaz was on an indefinite hunger strike demanding his release since 4 May. 3 Kurds, including the brother of Kenan Ayaz, who had also started a hunger strike protesting outside the Supreme Court, were arrested in the morning before the court rejected the appeal of Ayaz, paving the way for his extradition to Germany. Since early on there was strong police presence and police had set up barriers blocking entry to the courthouse. There were reports of police abuse, keeping the 3 hunger strikers tied on chairs, while they were detained in the police station.

On 16 May 2023, around 80 Vertbaudet workers, most of them women, and CGT union delegates, staging a strike picket in front of the Vertbaudet facility in Marquette-lez-Lille since 20 March 2023 for higher wages, were dispersed by police forces. One woman, who was carried away by an officer who clutched her throat, subsequently required hospital treatment.

On 16 May 2023, about 50 health workers and activists associated with the labor unions ABVV-FGTB, ACLVB-CGSLB, ACV-CSC, and CNE staged a protest in Brussels - Ville de Bruxelles, to demand better working conditions in the health and social work sectors. Protesters first gathered in Brussels - Saint-Josse-Ten-Noode, in front of the office of Flemish Minister for Welfare Hilde Crevits of the CD&V party, who came out to meet protesters. They then marched to the office of federal Health Minister Frank Vandenbroucke, of the Vooruit party, in Brussels - Ville de Bruxelles. An unknown number of CNE activists forced entry to the office, and were evicted by police forces. Vandenbroucke later also came out to meet protesters.

On 16 May 2023, environmental activists from ALG and FFF Ukraine and Austria protested in front of the Hofburg and Heldenplatz in Vienna - Inner City during the Austrian World Summit. They criticized the country's dependency on Russian fossil fuels and demanded changes. The ALG members also glued themselves on the street to block the road at Heldentors and Wiener Ring. The police removed the blockades.

On 16 May 2023, around 28 members of Just Stop Oil held a slow march from Newington Causeway towards the Crown Court in London - City of London demanding that the British government stops all new oil and gas projects and contracts. Police forces had to intervene to remove the protestors from the road.

On 16 May 2023, about 100 activists (many of whom students) associated with the action groups End Fossil: Occupy and Amsterdam Autonomous Coalition occupied a university building in Amsterdam, to demand that the University of Amsterdam cut its ties with fossil fuel companies. Police arrested 14 activists who refused to leave the building by the end of the day.

On 16 May 2023, ALG activists protested in Berlin - Charlottenburg-Wilmersdorf to call for climate protection. They staged the protest on the A100 highway between Spandauer Damm and Kaiserdamm and Bundesallee/Durlacher Street. The police chiseled protesters' hands out of the asphalt to remove them from the street.
On 16 May 2023, ALG activists protested on Prenzlauer Allee/Danziger Street in Berlin - Pankow to call for climate protection. The police chiseled protesters' hands to remove them from the street.

On 16 May 2023, ALG activists protested in Berlin - Tempelhof-Schoneberg to call for climate protection. They staged the protest on the Tempelhofer Damm/Hoeppnerstrasse and Hauptstrasse/Dominicusstrasse roads. The police chiseled protesters' hands to remove them from the street.

On 16 May 2023, ALG activists protested in Berlin - Treptow-Kopenick to call for climate protection. They staged the protest at Puschkinallee/Treptower Park. The police chiseled protesters' hands to remove them from the street.

On 18 May 2023, ALG activists blocked the Kurfurstendamm and an exit of highway A100, and Adenauerplatz in Berlin - Charlottenburg-Wilmersdorf, gluing themselves to cars and the tarmac, to call for climate action. The activists were removed from the cars by police forces and firefighters.

On 18 May 2023, ALG activists blocked the Frankfurter Allee in Berlin - Friedrichshain-Kreuzberg, gluing themselves to the tarmac, to call for climate action. The activists were removed from the streets by police forces.

On 18 May 2023, ALG again blocked the traffic at several places across Berlin by gluing themselves to roads or vehicles, demanding immediate climate action. One group blocked the traffic at Berlin - Lichtenberg and was removed by the policemen.

On 18 May 2023, ALG again blocked the traffic at several places across Berlin by gluing themselves to roads or vehicles, demanding immediate climate action. One group blocked the traffic at the Main Train Station (Berlin - Mitte) and was removed by the policemen.

On 19 May 2023, around 1500 students, along with teachers, independent MPs, Momentum MPs, MSZP MPs, DK MPs, Budapest's 9th district mayor, and Parbeszed MPs, marched from Kossuth square to Lendvay street in Budapest - VI, condemning the plans to limit academic freedom for teachers and students in schools. The crowd shortly scuffled with the police outside the Fidesz party headquarters. The police claimed the protesters threw beer cans and water bottles at the police fence. The protest was also met by a counter-protest of the 5-6 members of the Identitarian Movement, who criticized the students for depicting themselves as victims of the regime.

On 19 May 2023, ALG activists blocked the Spandauer Damm, Messedamm, Funkturm, Hohenzollerndamm, Bundesallee and Rudolf-Wissel-Brucke in Berlin - Charlottenburg-Wilmersdorf, gluing themselves to the tarmac, to call for climate action. The activists were removed from the streets by the police.

On 19 May 2023, ALG activists blocked the Frankfurter Allee in Berlin - Friedrichshain-Kreuzberg, gluing themselves to the tarmac, to call for climate action. One group also blocked the traffic in Elsenstrase. The activists were removed from the streets by police forces.
On 19 May 2023, ALG activists blocked the Mullerstrasse in Berlin - Mitte, gluing themselves to the tarmac, to call for climate action. The activists were removed from the streets by the police.

On 19 May 2023, ALG activists blocked the Prenzlauer Allee and Eberswalder Strasse in Berlin - Pankow, gluing themselves to the tarmac, to call for climate action. The activists were removed from the streets by the police.

On 19 May 2023, ALG again blocked the traffic at several places across Berlin by gluing themselves to roads or vehicles, demanding immediate climate action. One group blocked the traffic at Rudolf-Wissell Bridge (Berlin - Spandau) and was removed by the policemen.

On 19 May 2023, ALG activists blocked the Tempelhofer Damm and Dominicusstrasse in Berlin - Tempelhof-Schoneberg, gluing themselves to the tarmac, to call for climate action. The activists were removed from the streets by the police.

On 19 May 2023, ALG activists blocked the Puschkinallee in Berlin - Treptow-Kopenick, gluing themselves to the tarmac, to call for climate action. The activists were removed from the streets by police forces.

On 20 May 2023, seven activists from the Animal Rising group held a sit-in protest at Cail Bruich, a Michelin-star restaurant in Glasgow, to demand a plant-based future. The protesters were holding up placards showing conditions in meat factory farms in the UK. Police forces intervened and arrested five people.

On 21 May 2023, 9 Last Generation activists entered the Trevi fountain in Rome - City Center (Roma, Lazio) and turned its water black using vegetable charcoal to protest against the use of fossil fuels. The demonstrators were removed by the police after a few minutes.

On 22 May 2023, around 70 environmental activists, including members of Extinction Rebellion, took action by blocking the road leading to a paper mill located in Kouvola, Kymenlaakso. Their aim was to bring attention to the company's management, accusing them of employing unsustainable methods to produce paper within the company's factories located in Uruguay. Following their refusal to comply with police orders, 38 activists were subsequently arrested.

On 22 May 2023, around 30 people staged a protest in Rouen, to demonstrate 'against everything that's going on at the moment'. One person was arrested for tagging 'ACAB' in red paint on the big clock monument.

On 22 May 2023, around 45 members of Ende Gelaende blocked the entrance of the Hyperion Hotel on Amsinckstrasse in Hammerbrook and demonstrated in Hamburg - Hamburg-Mitte against a liquefied natural gas terminal (LNG) and the lobbying of the fossil gas industry. Demonstrators were carried away by police officers. They gathered on the occasion of the 5th Global LNG Forum. They denounced the 'climate catastrophe.'

On 22 May 2023, members of ALG demonstrated at the building of the Federal Constitutional Court in Karlsruhe to call for climate protection. Police officers temporarily arrested a demonstrator who tried to damage the name lettering on the building with a jackhammer, but was stopped before doing it.

On 22 May 2023, while the Minister of Culture was taking part in an event at the Federico II university, university students affiliated, among others, with FFF, 'Lea ClimaX', LINK, 'Mezzocannone Occupato', 'Ex Opg' and 'Animal Save' staged a protest in Napoli (Napoli, Campania) against the construction of a liquefied natural gas depot in San Giovanni a Teduccio, whose green light for the construction rests with the superintendency of the Ministry of Culture. As the demonstrators tried to hang a banner, they were blocked and pushed away by police officers in riot gear.

On 23 May 2023, early in the morning, an unknown number of End Fossil: Occupy activists continued their occupation of a university building in Wageningen, to demand that Wageningen University cut its ties with fossil fuel companies. Police ordered protesters to leave the building, and dragged out those activists who refused to leave.

On 23 May 2023, around 27 members of ALG demonstrated and blocked traffic at the intersection Kranebitter Allee/Fischerhauslweg in Innsbruck to call for climate protection. A passer-by poured a cup of a beverage (like a yogurt) over the head of a protester. One demonstrator was arrested.

On 24 May 2023, Extinction Rebellion associated groups occupied of the Danish Ministry of Climate, Energy, and Utilities in Copenhagen. Their demand was the resignation of the minister, whom they accused of incompetence in fulfilling his responsibilities. Later, as a result of their non-compliance with police instructions, several activists were removed from the venue and temporarily detained.

On 24 May 2023, members of ALG demonstrated in front of the Parliament in Vienna - Inner City to call for climate protection. Police officers intervened to pull away protesters. They called for a 100 km/h speed limit on highways and a ban on new oil and gas drilling, and the 93 demands from the Climate Council.

On 24 May 2023, 39 Just Stop Oil activists staged a slow march on Marylebone road through London - Islington (Greater London, England) as part of an attempt to block busy traffic to demand more climate action from the British government. Police intervened and made six arrests, forcing the rest of the protesters from the street onto the sidewalks.

On 24 May 2023, around 10 people continued the occupation of a wooded area near Bramsche (Osnabruck district) to call for climate protection. Police officers intervened to carry out an investigation and arrested an activist who was not cooperating. Demonstrators occupied the forest since the beginning of February.

On 25 May 2023, at least three Just Stop Oil activists threw orange paint on a garden display in London - Kensington and Chelsea (Greater London, England) as part of their ongoing environmentalist actions. Police intervened and arrested the three.

On 26 May 2023, residents of Kalamia in Kozani were removed by strong riot police forces when they lined up at the site where construction work had started for the installation of photovoltaic panels, preventing the vehicles of the construction company from entering the field. 1 protester was lightly injured and taken to hospital and another 4 were arrested and taken to the police headquarters in Kozani.

On 26 May 2023, activists blocked the road to the landfill in Poltavskaya, protesting against the inaction of the local authorities to prevent garbage trucks from passing through the town. Police arrested 10 protesters.

On 26 May 2023, police in military gear charged demonstrators in the Pantano Street area in Milano - Municipio 1 (Lombardia, Milano) after demonstrators threw tomatoes and eggs at the police. The demonstration, organized by USB under the framework of a national strike, started as a peaceful protest and saw students, workers, Changing Course activists, and self-managed social centers activists demonstrate against the government's economic and social policies.

On 26 May 2023, several hundred climate activists of different organizations staged a sit-in protest action at the Pleyel conference hall in Paris to block access to the shareholders of Total Energies, whose annual meeting was about to begin there, and try to enter the building. Police forces forcibly removed the activists with tear gas and batons, arresting at least four protesters. The action was held to put pressure on Total Energies' shareholders to reduce the oil company's negative impact on climate change and environmental decline. During the action, a reporting journalist was violently pushed down by police and private security forces.

On 26 May 2023, for the second consecutive day, people blocked the entrance to the port of Gothenburg (Goteborg) to oppose the fossil fuel industry and urging immediate action to combat climate change. As a result of their non-compliance with police instructions, several activists were removed from the venue and temporarily detained.

On 26 May 2023, 40 Just Stop Oil activists staged a slow march through central parts of London - City of London (Greater London, England) calling for an end to the use of fossil fuels. Police intervened and broke up the largest group of marchers.

On 27 May 2023, anti-bullfighting activists, including members of Anjou, staged a protest action in Nimes, to call for the banning of the tradition. The activists infiltrated the queues as the bullfight was about to begin, shouted 'murderers' and other slogans to the crowd, and sat down on the ground. The police intervened to remove them, and made 13 arrests.

On 27 May 2023, some 7,000 Extinction Rebellion affiliates protested in Den Haag, against Dutch government subsidies on fossil fuels. An unknown number of protesters participated in a blockade of the A12 highway in the city center. Police used water cannons to disperse blockading protesters, and arrested 1,587 protesters who blocked the highway. Affiliates of the action groups Scientist Rebellion, End Fossil: Occupy, Environmental Defence, and Christian Climate Action and the labor union FNV also took part, as well as a member of a provincial parliament for the GreenLeft party, affiliates of PINK!, the youth organization of the Animal Party, and a number of Protestant Christian ministers.

On 30 May 2023, around 100 people entered the city hall of Saint-Etienne during the weekly reunion of the municipal government, demanding the resignation of the local mayor after he was implicated in a sex tape blackmail scandal. The protesters were pushed back out by police forces, using tear gas.

On 31 May 2023, around 10 KPRF members staged pickets in front of the administration of Primorskiy Krai in Vladivostok, protesting against their party members' expulsion from the electoral commissions before the September elections. Protesters claim that this was done to be able to control the election results. Police arrested all participants.

On 31 May 2023, 66 Just Stop Oil protesters held a slow march and blocked the roads near West Kensington tube station in London - Hammersmith and Fulham to denounce the government's lack of action on climate and call for the government to halt all new oil and gas licenses. Police forces intervened and moved the protesters out of the road.

On 31 May 2023, 56 Just Stop Oil protesters held a slow march and blocked the roads near the Houses of Parliament in London - Westminster to denounce the government's lack of action on climate and call for the government to halt all new oil and gas licenses. Police forces intervened and arrested ten protesters.

On 31 May 2023, 33 Greenpeace activists gathered at the construction site of the highway A49 in Schwalmstadt, to protest against the expansion of highways and call for climate action. The activists glued themselves to machines and had to be removed by the police.

On 1 June 2023, around 200 people, including GJ activists, assembled in Millau to protest the government's pension reform during the visit of three government members to the city. Police forces dispersed the crowd with tear gas and charged it several times, during which one protesting aged woman was lightly injured. Some demonstrators were temporarily arrested.

On 1 June 2023, around 30 Mondo Convenienza workers gathered outside their company's warehouse in Campi Bisenzio (Firenze, Toscana) to protest against low wages and 'exhausting shifts'. The police tried to clear the picket line to let the trucks loaded with furniture through and dragged the demonstrators away. After a short time, the workers went back to the gates. S.I. COBAS supported the demonstration. As of 4 June 2023, the protest was ongoing.

On 1 June 2023, tens of XR activists protested at the Shell oil refinery in Pernis (Zuid-Holland), blocking the Vondelingenweg entrance against Shell's fossil fuel investments and the pollution they associate with climate change. Around 11:00 AM, roughly 15 protesters blocked access for trucks, some gluing themselves to the road and waving protest banners. Police began arresting activists around 2:30 PM after multiple warnings, detaining 15 individuals while others dispersed voluntarily.

On 1 June 2023, around 80 people, mostly teenagers and students, gathered at Johannisplatz in Leipzig, to protest for children's rights on the occasion of International Children's Day. The member of state parliament Juliane Nagel (The Left) was taken into custody by the police. Police claimed that she assaulted them beforehand, while the parliamentarian argued she was insulted and pushed before being arrested.

On 2 June 2023, around 24 people held a protest in Ballybrit Business Park in the outskirt of Galway against the accommodation of 300 male refugees as several buses arrived at the facility. Police forces arrested one protester in relation to a public order offense.
On 2 June 2023, activists staged a protest action in the Bitsevsky Forest in Moscow, trying to stop construction works there. Police arrested 3 protesters.
On 2 June 2023, activists staged a protest in the Bitsevsky Forest in Moscow - Southern, trying to stop construction works there. Police used force to disperse the protest and arrested 7 people.

On 3 June 2023, activists from the Animal Rising group climbed the fences and attempted to enter the Epsom Derby horse race in Epsom (England) to protest the event and its use of animals and cause disruption before the race. Police forces arrested some 31 people including 19 on the morning before the race started.

On 4 June 2023, people gathered at different locations in Moscow in support of the Russian opposition politician Navalny. Navalny's Anti-Corruption Foundation earlier called on his supporters to take to the streets and show their support in different cities across the world. Police arrested over 60 protesters.

On 4 June 2023, several people staged pickets at different locations in St. Petersburg in support of the Russian opposition politician Navalny.
