Navalny's Anti-Corruption Foundation earlier called on his supporters to take to the streets and show their support in different cities across the world. Police arrested all protesters, including a journalist. 22 people in total were arrested, including those who didn't participate in the protest.

On 4 June 2023, 4 activists staged pickets at different locations in Krasnodar in support of the Russian opposition politician Navalny. Navalny's Anti-Corruption Foundation earlier called on his supporters to take to the streets and show their support in different cities across the world. Police arrested all protesters.

On 5 June 2023, Mondo Convenienza workers gathered outside their company's warehouse in Campi Bisenzio (Firenze, Toscana) to protest against low wages and 'exhausting shifts'. The police tried to clear the picket line to let the trucks loaded with furniture through and dragged the demonstrators away. After a few hours , the workers went back to the gates and the police cleared the picket line again. S.I. COBAS supported the demonstration.

On 5 June 2023, activists from Just Stop Oil held a slow march and blocked the roads from Gants Hill Roundabout to B192 Beehive Lane in London - Redbridge (England) to denounce the government's lack of action on climate and call for the government to halt all new oil and gas licenses. Police forces intervened and arrested two activists.

On 5 June 2023, ALG activists blocked the Leopoldring in Freiburg im Breisgau (Baden-Wurttemberg), by gluing themselves to the tarmac, to call for climate action. The activists were removed from the streets by the police.

On 5 June 2023, around 15 ALG activists blocked streets around Frankfurter Tor in Berlin - Friedrichshain-Kreuzberg (Berlin), by gluing themselves to the tarmac, to call for climate action. The activists were removed from the streets by the police.

On 7 June 2023, several dozen activists gathered for a rally in Prague, declaring support to their fellow activist during his court hearing over his activities opposing the coronavirus-related restrictions. One of the supporters was detained.

On 7 June 2023, 150 people, called by the Anti-Monarchy Coordinator, held a protest in Girona (Cataluna) against the events planned by the Fundacio Princesa de Girona (FPdGi). One of the protesters was arrested after attacking one of the police agents.

On 7 June 2023, SI COBAS representatives and workers employed by Mondo Convenienza's subcontractor RL2, some of which were members of the Pakistani community, staged a picket in Campi Bisenzio (Toscana, Firenze) to protest against their working conditions and demand fair wages. They were forcibly removed by the police. The municipal councilor of Florence Antonella Bundu ('Sinistra progetto comune' group) and 'Former GKN Workers Collective' activists visited the picket to express solidarity with the workers.

On 9 June 2023, about 30 people, including Pays-de-Retz anti-fascist members, gathered at the entrance of a venue where a book-signing session by Eric Zemmour was taking place in La Baule-Escoublac, denouncing the politician's far-right ideas. Police forces present used tear gas and pushed attendees away.

On 9 June 2023, as part of a permanent protest, SI COBAS representatives and workers of the company RL2, a Mondo Convenienza's subcontractor, staged a picket outside the company's headquarters in Campi Bisenzio (Toscana, Firenze) to demand better working conditions and tied themselves to each other with chains to prevent the dissolution of the picket. The police broke the chains and physically removed protesters.
On 10 June 2023, protesters staged a mass picket in Khabarovsk in support of the jailed governor of the region. Police intervened and arrested two protesters.

On 10 June 2023, in the evening, around 40 LGBTQ+ activists assembled for an unauthorized 'Radical Pride' march in Lille (Hauts-de-France), to defend the rights of their community. Police forces dispersed the crowd with batons and charged it several times, during which one demonstrator was knocked to the ground.

On 10 June 2023, ten Extinction Rebellion activists staged a protest in an office of the bank ING in Eindhoven (Noord-Brabant), against ING's investments in fossil fuel projects. Police dragged the protesters, who refused to leave, out of the office.

On 11 June 2023, early in the morning, about 50 demonstrators, likely in solidarity with a jailed anarchist on hunger strike, participated in a motorcade to SKAI TV station in Faliro, Athens - South Athens, where they scattered fliers and wrote slogans on the walls. There were 14 detentions, one of which turned into an arrest.

On 12 June 2023, 5 members of ALG demonstrated and blocked traffic on Licher Street in Giessen to call for climate protection. Police officers physically intervened on the people who glued themselves to the road to remove them.

On 12 June 2023, during the morning, 6 members of ALG demonstrated and blocked traffic on the corner of Paracelsusstrasse and Dessauer Strasse in Halle (Saale) to call for climate protection. Police forces intervened to remove the demonstrators glued to the road.

On 13 June 2023, between 7,000 (according to police) and 11,000 people (according to protesters) held a protest march from the Brussels-North railway station in Brussels - Schaerbeek (Brussels) to the Brussels-South railway station in Brussels - Saint-Gilles (Brussels), to demand better working conditions and more staff in the non-profit sector. Members of the labor groups CNE and ABVV-FGTB attended the protest, alongside health workers and MPs and politicians from the Flemish Interest, Groen, Vooruit, and PVDA-PTB parties. After the presence of the far-right Flemish Interest party caused unrest among protesters, police asked Flemish Interest members to remove themselves from the march. A scuffle between police and Flemish Interest members ensued, during which a policeman slapped VB leader Tom Van Grieken in the face.

On 13 June 2023, as part of a permanent protest, workers employed by RL2, a subcontractor for Mondo Convenienza, and representatives of SI COBAS staged a picket outside the company gates in Campi Bisenzio (Toscana, Firenze) to protest against their working conditions. The police physically removed protesters.

On 14 June 2023, in the context of the Zurich march for the feminist strike day, around 300 people blocked the tramways At the Paradeplatz for a while, after which police forces intervened with tear gas to disperse them.
On 14 June 2023, around 25 ALG blocked the Kranebitter Allee in Innsbruck (Tirol), to call for climate action. The activists were removed from the street by the police.

On 14 June 2023, Restore Wetlands Movement activists staged a protest action in at the National Museum in Stockholm to draw attention to environmental problems and to restore drained wetlands in the country. The people were arrested in relation with the incident.

On 14 June 2023, around 16 ALG activists staged a sit-in protest at Ritz-Carlton luxury hotel in Berlin - Mitte (Berlin), calling for climate action. The activists were removed from the street by the police.

On 14 June 2023, 5 ALG activists gathered at a golf club in Wenningstedt-Braderup (Sylt) (Schleswig-Holstein), to symbolically plant crops and protest against the water use of golf courses amid water shortages. The activists were removed from the course by the police.
On 15 June 2023, 7 ALG activists blocked the Europe Bridge (coded to Patsch), to call for climate action. The activists were removed from the street by the police.

On 16 June 2023, environmental activists took part in demonstrations across various locations before ultimately blocking the venue of the national climate meeting in Stockholm. The activists criticized politicians for their perceived lack of action in addressing the climate crisis and called for an official declaration of a climate emergency. Subsequently, law enforcement personnel intervened and removed the activists from the premises. Extinction Rebellion activists participated in the event, among others.

On 16 June 2023, for a second consecutive day, environmental activists blocked entrance to the oil port in Malmo to draw attention to environmental problems and to demand action against climate change. Subsequently, a number of activists, including Greta Thunberg, were apprehended on charges of unlawful entry and non-compliance with law enforcement officers.

On 16 June 2023, 7 ALG activists blocked a street at the party bureau of CDU in Berlin - Mitte (Berlin), gluing themselves to the tarmac, to call for climate action. The activists were removed from the street by the police.

On 16 June 2023, 6 ALG activists gathered in Kampen (Sylt) (Schleswig-Holstein), to color the facade of a luxury boutique to protest against the emissions of rich people. The activists were taken into custody by the police.

On 17 June 2023, about 100 people protested outside a Delhaize supermarket in Brussels - Ixelles (Brussels), against the plans of Delhaize's management to turn many of its stores into independent franchises. Police forces pushed back protesters to make space for an arriving transport truck.

On 17 June 2023, for a third consecutive day, environmental activists blocked entrance to the oil port in Malmo to draw attention to environmental problems and to demand action against climate change. Afterward, following their non-compliance with police instructions, several activists were removed out of the premises.

On 17 June 2023, around 3,500 people gathered in Freiburg im Breisgau (Baden-Wurttemberg), to protest against a prior prohibition of music equipment in public parks by throwing a party. The gathering was dispersed by police forces.

On 17 June 2023, around 18 people occupied an empty house in Schoenefeld (Brandenburg), to protest against the planned construction of a travel center at the BER airport. The activists claimed that the center would function as a prison for those that have to leave the country. Police forces cleared the building.

On 17 June 2023, at the call of Smash Cruisehit, around 15 people blocked the departure from port of a cruise ship in Warnemunde (Mecklenburg-Vorpommern), to protest against the emissions cause by the cruise ship industry and call for climate action. The activists were removed from the water by police forces.

On 18 June 2023, No TAV activists staged a protest at the construction site in San Didero (Piemonte) to protest against the TAV Turin-Lyon high-speed railway connection project. Protesters were dispersed by the police with water cannons and tear gas.

On 19 June 2023, 7 activists of Renovate Switzerland staged a protest action in Zurich, blocking traffic on several streets to demand more action against climate change. At the arrival of police forces, the activists glued themselves to the tarmac, after which they were arrested.
On 19 June 2023, 3 ALG activists blocked the Ludwigstrasse in Munchen (Bayern), gluing themselves to the tarmac, to call for climate action. The activists were removed from the streets by the police.

On 19 June 2023, members of Last Generation protested on Frauntorgraben in Nurnberg (Bayern) for more climate protection, blocking traffic. The police intervened and removed the climate activists from the road.

On 20 June 2023, 3 activists of Renovate Switzerland, including an EPFL student, staged a protest action in Sion (Valais), blocking traffic on the Rhone bridge to demand more action against climate change. Police forces intervened to remove the protesters after 15 minutes.

On 20 June 2023, seven Extinction Rebellion activists staged a short protest action on the A12 highway in Den Haag (Zuid-Holland), against Dutch government subsidies on fossil fuel. Police arrested all protesters for illegally walking on the highway.

On 21 June 2023, police prevented relatives of the victims of the Tempe rail disaster from protesting during the Thessaloniki pre-election rally of New Democracy leader, Konstantinos Mitsotakis, pushing them back. The protesters were allowed to raise their banner after the ND rally was over.

On 21 June 2023, around 300 left-wing activists gathered outside the town hall in Limoges (Nouvelle-Aquitaine) against the visit of ex-presidential candidate and Reconquest Party leader Eric Zemmour to the city, denouncing far-right ideas. A man was taken into custody for anti-Semitic and racist insults, according to the CGT.

On 21 June 2023, a dozen ANV-Cop 21 and XR activists staged a protest during the community council in Saint-Sixt (Auvergne-Rhone-Alpes), against the Velodrome Arena project, citing environmental concerns. Police forces forcibly removed the activists.

On 22 June 2023, members of the Connolly Youth Movement interrupted the opening remarks of Micheal Martin, the deputy prime minister of the Republic of Ireland at the Consultative Forum on International Security Policy in Cork (Cork) to express their opposition to Ireland's foreign policy. Protesters held banners and shouted 'No to NATO'. Police forces intervened and removed the protesters.

On 23 June 2023, at the call of FFF and ALG, people protested on the Nibelungen Bridge in Linz to call for climate protection. They demanded a 100km/h speed limit on highways as well as no new drilling for oil and gas. Demonstrators also called on the federal government to implement the 93 recommendations of the Climate Council. One man glued himself to the road and was carried away by police officers.

On 24 June 2023, hundreds of Greenpeace activists broke through a fence and protested on the terrains of the steel plant Tata Steel in Velsen-Noord (Noord-Holland), against the pollution caused by the factory. Scientist Rebellion and Extinction Rebellion activists also participated in the protest. An unknown number of Extinction Rebellion members chained themselves to a railway used for coal transports just outside the Tata Steel grounds. Police forces removed these activists but did not make any arrests. On 25 June 2023, around 70 AfD affiliates gathered in Wurzburg against the fatal knife attack by a mentally ill man on passers-by occurred on 25 June 2021. On 26 June 2023, a sailboat with four Greenpeace activists attempted to block a chemical tanker near Stigsnaes peninsula (coded to Agerso) to prevent it from delivering toxic waste water to the RGS Nordic plant in Southern Denmark. Later, the activists were arrested by the police personnel.

On 28 June 2023, around 30 members of ALG blocked traffic in front of the Rose Garden in Mannheim to call for climate protection. They were carried away by police officers.

On 29 June 2023, around four Motvind Norge activists continued their blockade of Roan wind farm near Roan, Trondelag, to protest the continued operation of wind power mills in the Fosen district, despite a supreme court ruling that the license was invalid. Later, the police personnel removed several activists from the venue after they failed to comply with the police's demands.

On 29 June 2023, at 8:00 pm, people including LFI members gathered at Capitole square in Toulouse to denounce police violence and in memory of Nahel M., when police pushed back attendees and dispersed the demonstration. On 29 June 2023, several hundred farmers assembled in Den Haag to demonstrate against the government's agricultural policy and the newly proposed agriculture deal. From there, several demonstrators attempted to walk back to the parliament building but were blocked by police forces. 7 people were arrested for not complying with the police's directive, or for attempting to drive into the city center with tractors. During one arrest, 2 police officers were lightly injured.

On 30 June 2023, campaigners held a march from Falmouth Event Square to A&P's HQ in Falmouth (England) against the company's work on changing a barge into a refugee detention center. Police forces intervened to remove the protesters.

On 30 June 2023, an unknown number of people gathered to protest in Brussels - Ville de Bruxelles (Brussels), to denounce police violence and demand justice in the wake of the shooting and subsequent death of 17-year-old Nahel M. by a police officer in Nanterre, France on 27 June 2023. Police performed identity checks and made about 94 preventive arrests during the gathering to prevent any violence.

On 30 June 2023, an unknown number of people gathered to protest in Liege (Wallonie), to denounce police violence and demand justice in the wake of the shooting and subsequent death of 17-year-old Nahel M. by a police officer in Nanterre, France on 27 June 2023. Police performed identity checks and made about 30 preventive arrests during the gathering to prevent any violence.

On 30 June 2023, a group of approximately 16 Extinction Rebellion activists staged a blockade at Roskilde airport, calling for a ban on private jets due to their purportedly higher CO2 emissions. As a result of the demonstration, 11 activists were subsequently arrested.

On 1 July 2023, three animal rights activists from the Animal Rising group scaled a large scaffold in the center of the Towcester Racecourse in Towcester to protest the cruelty of the event and prevent the English Greyhound Derby Final from taking place.

On 1 July 2023, around 30,000 LGBTQ+ community members and their supporters marched from Hyde Park and Whitehall in London - Westminster (England) as part of the annual Pride March to celebrate diversity and the queer community and denounce discrimination against LGBTQ+ people. Police Forces intervened and arrested seven Just Stop Oil protesters and the parade continued.

On 1 July 2023, an unknown number of people gathered to protest in Brussels - Ville de Bruxelles (Brussels), to denounce police violence and demand justice in the wake of the shooting and subsequent death of 17-year-old Nahel M. by a police officer in Nanterre, France on 27 June 2023. On 2 July 2023, far right activists and members of Les Remparts demonstrated in Lyon (Auvergne-Rhone-Alpes) to protest against immigration, which they deemed linked to insecurity, and protest against the national wave of riots and demonstrations denouncing police violence and demanding justice in the wake of the shooting and subsequent death of 17-year-old Nahel M. by a police officer in Nanterre on 27 June 2023. On 3 July 2023, 5 Last Generation activists staged a demonstration in Florence (Toscana, Firenze) in solidarity with 2 activists sentenced to 9 months in prison and to pay a fine of 1,500 EUR each for having glued themselves to the base of a statue in the summer of 2022 during a climate protest. The police removed the protesters, who engaged in passive non-violent resistance.

On 3 July 2023, Last Generation activists blocked a road in Berlin - Mitte by gluing themselves to a road, demanding immediate climate action. Police detained six of them - some before they managed to apply the glue.

On 5 July 2023, around 100 protesters from the Our Republic campaign gathered outside the High Court on the Royal Mile and outside of the Scottish Parliament in Edinburgh (Scotland) during the royal visit to express their opposition to the monarchy. Police arrested two people over alleged breach of peace.

On 5 July 2023, seven activists from the Restore Wetlands Movement attempted to disrupt operation of a peat mining factory near Mosas, Jonkoping, demanding a full ban of peat mining and to draw attention to environmental issues. Later, the activists were arrested by police.

On 5 July 2023, climate activists from Just Stop Oil ran onto the Wimbledon courts and disrupted the match several times in London - Bromley (England) to denounce the government's lack of action on climate and call for the government to halt all new oil and gas licenses. On 29 August 2023, local coordinator of the Other Russia party and three members of National Bolsheviks held single-person pickets in St. Petersburg. The pickets were held for the release of the former 'Minister of Defense of the DPR' Igor Girkin. They were all detained.

Some of the protesters glued themselves onto the road and the police intervened, removing the activists and arresting 9 people.

On 29 August 2023, at dawn, 6 people, 3 of whom affiliated with antagonist movements, climbed onto the roof of an occupied building in Esterle street in Milano - Municipio 2 (Milano, Lombardia) to protest against the eviction that was taking place. An additional 60 affiliates of antagonist collectives gathered in the same street in support. Police officers and carabinieri blocked the street and removed protesters from the area.

On 29 August 2023, climate activists participated in road blockages organized by Last Generation on multiple streets in Munchen (Bayern), including at the intersections of Leopoldstrasse and Karl-Weinmair Strasse, of Schenkendorfstrasse and Leopoldstrasse as well as of Einsteinstrasse and Leuchtenbergring. Police forces intervened and removed the activists from the street.

On 30 August 2023, campaigners from the Public Child Protection Wales group held a protest in Newport (Wales) against a drag artist storytelling event for children for the upcoming annual Pride celebrations. Police forces arrested one person during the demonstration for breaching the peace.

On 30 August 2023, at the call of Last Generation, around 30 members gathered at Schwetzinger Terrasse in Heidelberg (Baden-Wurttemberg) and demonstrated on Speyerer Street to call on the government to do more for climate protection. Several activists were arrested by the police.

On 30 August 2023, over 80 people, mostly members of Last Generation, demonstrated and slowed traffic down from the Isartor to the Bavarian State Parliament in Munchen (Bayern) to call for climate protection. 11 sat down on the street and were carried away by police officers. Around 10 people threw paintballs at the building of the Bavarian State Parliament.

On 31 August 2023, 5 members of Last Generation blocked traffic by gluing themselves to August-Bebel Street and demonstrated in Rostock (Mecklenburg-Vorpommern) to call on the federal government to do more for climate protection. Protesters demanded the reintroduction of the 9-euro ticket for public transport, a speed limit of 100 km/h on highways, and a social council. They were physically removed by police officers.

On 1 September 2023, throughout the day, at least 5 climate activists, members of Last Generation and Robin Wood, carried out several actions and blocked traffic at the intersection of Sonnenstrasse and Priemlayerstrasse, Donnersberger Street, and Arnulfstrasse in Neuhausen, in Munchen (Bayern). Other blockades happened simultaneously at Furstenrieder Street, Ammerseestrasse, and Feldherrnhalle. They called for climate protection. A Robin Wood activist put a banner on Odeonsplatz against the International Motor Show (IAA) to denounce car companies' greenwashing. 10 activists were arrested by the police.

On 1 September 2023, in the morning, between 30 and 40 members of Animal Rebellion blocked roads, occupied a building, and demonstrated with pyrotechnics in front of the Ammerland dairy in the Dringenburg part of Wiefelstede (Niedersachsen) against the dairy industry. They called for factories to switch to plant-based milk alternatives for animal welfare and climate protection. Several demonstrators climbed on the roof of a milk truck but also one of the dairy roofs and hung a large banner against greenwashing. 5 people were physically removed by police officers.

On 2 September 2023, 3 members of Last Generation glued themselves to the road, blocked the B37 highway west of the Theodor Heuss Bridge and protested in Heidelberg to call for more actions to achieve the 2023 climate protection plan. Demonstrators were arrested.

On 2 September 2023, around a dozen members of Last Generation and Science Rebellion (XR) blocked traffic on Adenauerallee (B9) at the same time near the Koenig Museum in Bonn to call for climate protection. Police officers intervened to remove the glue from those who stuck themselves to the road.

On 3 September 2023, several people staged an anti-Islam demonstration and set fire to a Quran book in Malmo. A group of around 100 counter-protesters gathered to oppose the burning. Subsequently, personnel stopped the demonstration and removed protesters from the venue due to the high security risks. At least 3 persons were arrested in relation with the demonstration.

On 4 September 2023, 11 members of Last Generation gathered on Innviertler Street (B137), on Wiener Street (B1), and blocked traffic on the Osttangente (East bypass) as well as Hans-Sachs-Street towards the city center in Wels for climate protection. 5 people were arrested. Demonstrators were against the fossil fuel industry.

On 4 September 2023, 5 people, mostly members of Last Generation and Grannies Against the Right, glued themselves to the road as well as demonstrated at Schwarzenbergplatz in Vienna - Inner City. They called on the government to do more for climate protection and the safety of people's future, especially students. 5 people were arrested. Demonstrators were against the fossil fuel industry.

On 4 September 2023, 4 members of Last Generation blocked traffic on Invalidenstrasse at Europaplatz in front of Berlin Central Station in Berlin - Mitte to denounce the criminalization of the movement, show support to 27 people in Bavaria who have been in preventive detention, and call for more climate protection. Emergency services (including police officers) intervened to remove the activists from the road.

On 4 September 2023, a group of members of Last Generation demonstrated and blocked traffic at the exit of the B100 road in Halle (Saale) to call for climate protection. Police officers intervened to remove several activists who glued themselves to the road.

On 5 September 2023, 6 Last Renovation activists sprayed orange paint in front of the Ministry of the Interior on Beauvau Square in Paris (Ile-de-France) to denounce the French government's lack of action against climate change. Police took all six demonstrators into custody.

On 6 September 2023, around 100 locals protested near the Sarykum hill near Shangoda, Republic of Dagestan, against the construction of a landfill. Police arrested 8 protesters and later released them.

On 6 September 2023, Last Generation activists protested with a sit-in in front of the train station in Stuttgart (Baden-Wurttemberg) to show solidarity with fellow activists in Munich, especially those taken into preventive custody until the end of the International Mobility Show Germany (IAA Mobility) taking place in the city. Moreover, 12 Last Generation activists protested on Arnulf-Klett-Platz with a slow protest march, against the climate policies of the government and the imprisonment of other activists. The police intervened in both cases, carrying the activists off the road.

On 6 September 2023, multiple Last Generation activists protested in Hamburg - Hamburg-Mitte (Hamburg). First, the protesters started a protest march at Stephansplatz but the police intervened and stopped the protesters. Later, multiple activists protested at the train station Sternschanze, and three activists protested with a slow protest march towards Weidenalleee. Police intervened, stopped the protesters by pushing them aside and issued expulsions.

On 7 September 2023, more than 50 people gathered near Sarykum hotel to protest against construction of a landfill between the Sarykum dune and the village of Novaya Urada. Police detained 8 activists from the protest who were then taken to the Kumtorkalinskiy district police department.

On 7 September 2023, Greenpeace activists protested, by laying four inflatable boats in front of a departing ship transporting new pipelines as well as by occupying a crane, in the harbor in Mukran (Vorpommern-Rugen, Mecklenburg-Vorpommern) against a new LNG terminal. Police forces intervened and took several activists off the site, recorded their details, and sent them off. Three of the four boats drove away.

On 7 September 2023, 13 Last Generation activists protested against the International Mobility Show Germany (IAA Mobility) by blocking a part of the Mittlere Ring in Munchen (Bayern). A passing driver poured coffee over the head of one of the activists. The police intervened and removed the activists from the road.
On 7 September 2023, about 20 climate activists, partly belonging to the group 'Geschwister for Future' held a protest march in Munchen (Bayern). The police intervened and stopped the protesters.

On 8 September 2023, Last Generation activists protested by blocking the Wiener Ring in Vienna - Inner City (Wien 1-Innere Stadt) to raise awareness for the climate crisis and to demand a 100 km/h speed limit on Austria's roads and a fracking ban. The police intervened, broke up the protest and restored traffic.

On 9 September 2023, residents and members of the tenants' union CATU gathered outside of a private residence in Waterford (Waterford City and County) to protest the tenant being evicted. Police forces were dispatched to the scene, and detained one of the protesters.

On 9 September 2023, around 15,000 sympathizers of Extinction Rebellion, including 20 to 30 XR activists, staged a protest action in Den Haag (Zuid-Holland), blocking traffic on the Utrechtsebaan A12 highway, to call on the government to stop the funding of fossil fuel companies. Police forces intervened straight away with a water cannon, striking some protesters with batons, and arrested up to 2,400 people, who were later taken to the ADO football stadium.

On 9 September 2023, several dozens of protesters organized by Let Women Speak, opposing the transgender law as they claim it puts an end to women's rights, and a few hundred counter-demonstrators organized by anti-fascist groups, gathered in Park Paardenveld in Utrecht (Utrecht). Tensions rose as counter-protesters pushed through barricades but were stopped by police using batons. Despite the initial unrest, the event ended peacefully after over two hours, with one person arrested for disruptive behavior. Both demonstrations were described as orderly by the police.

On 9 September 2023, different groups of activists protested in Munchen (Bayern) against the International Motor Show Germany (IAA). Around 10 am, 7 climate activists protested on Innsbrucker Ring by holding a sit-in and blocking the road, 5 of the activists glued themselves onto the road. The police intervened, and took activists into custody. Around 12.30 pm, about 100 activists belonging to 'No Future for IAA' blocked Bavariastrasse with a human chain and symbolically occupied an empty building. The police intervened and ended the protest by carrying the protesters away one by one. Around 80 climate activists, belonging to 'Smash IAA', protested at the Donnersberger Brucke. The police intervened with batons and pepper spray and tried ending the protest. As a result, around 15 activists sat on the road under the Donnersberg Bridge and blocked traffic and around 30 activists protested in front of the Mercedes-Benz car dealership on the corner of Arnulfstrasse and Donnersbergerbrucke.

On 10 September 2023, an unknown number of activists and sympathizers of Extinction Rebellion staged a protest action in Den Haag (Zuid-Holland), blocking traffic on the Utrechtsebaan A12 highway, to call on the government to stop the funding of fossil fuel companies. On 11 September 2023, 4 Last Generation activists protested in front of the Sacre Coeur school in Graz (Steiermark) by gluing themselves onto the road. The police intervened, removed the protesters and filed reports.

On 11 September 2023, 6 Last Generation activists protested at the Prinz Eugen exits on the A7 Muhlkreis highway in Linz (Oberosterreich) in both directions by partly gluing themselves onto the road. The police intervened, removed the protesters and carried them to the side of the road.

On 11 September 2023, dozens of climate activists from Extinction Rebellion held a protest in Plaza de Espana in Madrid - Moncloa-Aravaca to denounce the government's climate inaction. Several activists chained themselves to block the Gran Via road. Police intervened and dispersed the protesters.

On 11 September 2023, dozens of XR activists and supporters staged a protest action in Den Haag (Zuid-Holland), blocking traffic on the Utrechtsebaan A12 highway, to call on the government to stop the funding of fossil fuel companies. On 13 September 2023, dozens of activists and sympathizers of Extinction Rebellion staged a protest action in Den Haag (Zuid-Holland), blocking traffic on the Utrechtsebaan A12 highway, to call on the government to stop the funding of fossil fuel companies. On 13 September 2023, 7 members of Last Generation demonstrated, including 5 who glued themselves on the road, on the corner of Karntnerstrasse and Schmittstrasse in Knittelfeld to call for climate protection. Police officers intervened physically to remove the demonstrators.

At the call of 'Colorful Luckenwalde', people, including members of Jusos, The Green Youth, Left Youth Solid, and 'Democratic Alliance Teltow-Flaming' members, gathered for a counter-demonstration against AFD and for human rights. They wanted to spread messages of peaceful coexistence and tolerance regarding immigration matters.

On 13 September 2023, throughout the day, around 200 people, including Last Generation members, slowed down traffic and demonstrated in the Moabit district, at Europaplatz, and the main train station in Berlin - Mitte to call for climate justice as well as the end of fossil fuel industry. On 14 September 2023, around 100 health workers gathered outside the Regional Health Agency (ARS) in Quimper (Bretagne) to protest against the closure of the Carhaix-Plouguer emergency unit at night. After a few hours, police intervened and physically removed the protesters from the building.

On 15 September 2023, around 20,000 people, including Last Generation members, demonstrated from Wien-Mitte train station in Vienna - Landstrasse to Heldenplatz, via the Parliament, in Vienna - Inner City for climate protection. On 15 September 2023, students from the Student Climate Strike held a protest in Oeiras (Lisboa) in solidarity with the activists detained the day before for blocking the entrance to the Council of Ministers as part of a climate crisis protest. One student was detained during the protest.

On 15 September 2023, hundreds of XR activists and supporters staged a protest action in Den Haag (Zuid-Holland), blocking traffic on the Utrechtsebaan A12 highway, to call on the government to stop the funding of fossil fuel companies. Police deployed water cannons to disperse demonstrators from the highway and arrested approximately 650 participants.

On 16 September 2023, at the call of the Alliance for Democracy and Diversity, between 350 (according to the police) and 500 people, including the mayor (independent), Camp-Zang members, an MP (SPD), The Greens members, and Grannies Against the Right, demonstrated from the town hall across Hamburger Strasse, through Lindenstrasse and Kirchweg past the industrial area in Henstedt-Ulzburg against far-right extremism, fascism, Nazis, and the AFD. Although the vast majority of participants protested peacefully, the police officers used tear gas against several people who tried to break through a barrier. The paint of a patrol car was slightly scratched because of a barrier fell and one person tried to hit an officer but only touched them lightly without injuring anyone.

On 17 September 2023, activists associated with Extinction Rebellion attempted to disrupt operations at Bromma Airport in Stockholm, demanding a ban on private jets and the declaration of a climate emergency. Police later removed the activists from the area, and at least 17 people were arrested and suspected of aviation sabotage.

On 17 September 2023, an unknown number of activists and sympathizers of Extinction Rebellion staged a protest action in Den Haag (Zuid-Holland), blocking traffic on the Utrechtsebaan A12 highway, to call on the government to stop funding fossil fuel companies and projects. Police forces responded with a water cannon and arrested up to 400 people.

Members of anarchist collectives and the extra-parliamentary left participated in the march. Before the march, police detained 8 people as a precaution, 1 of which was arrested for disobedience. There was strong police presence.

On 18 September 2023, on the 10th anniversary of the murder of anti-fascist rapper Pavlos Fyssas by Golden Dawn, there was a large gathering by anti-fascist organizations and the friends and family of the artist, at the site of the killing in Keratsini, which was followed by a march. During the march police detained 11 people as a precaution, 1 of which was arrested for disobedience. Traffic was disrupted. There was a call for anti-fascist rallies in another 16 cities across the country.

On 18 September 2023, hundreds of activists and sympathizers of Extinction Rebellion staged a protest action in Den Haag (Zuid-Holland), blocking traffic on the Utrechtsebaan A12 highway, to call on the government to stop funding fossil fuel companies and projects. On 18 September 2023, a man sprayed tear gas at the face of several Last Generation members who gathered and blocked traffic at Prenzlauer Promenade (A114), corner of Pasewalker Street, Prenzlauer Street, Granitz Street, Prenzlauer Allee, and Frobel Street in Berlin - Pankow to call for climate protection. He also tried to kick them. Another man poured a Coca-Cola drink on a demonstrator. Police officers intervened to remove the demonstrators who glued themselves to the road.

On 18 September 2023, Last Generation members gathered and blocked traffic at Ernst Reuter Square and Spandauer Damm/Sophie-Charlotten-Street in Berlin - Charlottenburg-Wilmersdorf to call for climate protection. On 18 September 2023, Last Generation members gathered and blocked traffic at Hallesches Ufer/Mehringdamm and Kotti/Adalbertstrasse, in Berlin - Friedrichshain-Kreuzberg to call for climate protection. Police officers intervened to remove the demonstrators who glued themselves to the road.

On 18 September 2023, Last Generation members gathered and blocked traffic in Berlin - Spandau to call for climate protection. On 18 September 2023, Last Generation members gathered and blocked traffic at Saarstrasse (A103) towards Schoneberg and S Tempelhof, at the A100 highway heading out of town, in Berlin - Tempelhof-Schoneberg to call for climate protection. On 18 September 2023, Last Generation members gathered and blocked traffic at Kopenicker Landstrasse/Eichbushallee in Berlin - Treptow-Kopenick to call for climate protection. Police officers intervened to remove the demonstrators who glued themselves to the road.

On 19 September 2023, eleven activists from the Restore Wetlands Movement blocked motorway traffic in Stockholm demining to restore drained wetlands in the country and to draw attention to environmental problems. On 19 September 2023, several hundred XR activists and supporters staged a protest action in Den Haag (Zuid-Holland), blocking traffic on the Utrechtsebaan A12 highway, to call on the government to stop funding fossil fuel companies and projects. On 19 September 2023, an unknown number of people participated in several protest actions in Den Haag (Zuid-Holland), with some of them holding the Dutch flag upside down, during the annual Prinsjesdag festivities to honor the Dutch royal family. Several people from the organization Together For The Netherlands (Samen Voor Nederland), an organization that regularly demonstrated against government policy at the time of reporting, also joined in. One man was arrested by police for unclear reasons.

On 20 September 2023, around 200 far-right activists gathered outside the parliament in Dublin (Dublin) for a protest as the parliament returned following the summer recess. Demonstrators held signs featuring slogans such as 'Irish lives matter', and opposed transgender rights, migration and planned hate speech laws. Police forces arrested 13 people following the protest.

On 20 September 2023, 6 Last Generation activists, all women, blocked the traffic on Fulvio Testi boulevard in Cinisello Balsamo (Milano, Lombardia) to demand more climate action. Police officers took the demonstrators away and restored car circulation after fifteen minutes.

On 21 September 2023, almost two dozen of housing activists from the House to Live, Planet to Inhabit platform held a protest in the galleries of the Assembly of the Republic in Lisbon (Lisboa) against the More Housing package. Police officers evacuated the protesters from the room.

The police intervened, removed the protesters from the ship, and took some of them into custody.

On 23 September 2023, around 130 people, including Last Generation activists, protested in Berlin - Charlottenburg-Wilmersdorf (Berlin) for climate reasons and blocked the intersection Potsdamer Strasse/Kurfurstendamm with a sit-in. On 23 September 2023, around 200 people, including representatives of the Left, protested on Friedrichsplatz in Kassel (Hessen) against the appearance of AfD deputy Stephan Brandner for a election campaign event. On 29 September 2023, 5 Last Generation activists blocked traffic at via Priora and Largo dei Colli Albani in Rome - Tuscolano (Lazio, Roma), displaying a banner and calling for more climate action. The police removed the demonstrators, who were taken to the local police headquarters and reported.

On 30 September 2023, members of anti-establishment groups marched in central Heraklion against the eviction of the Evangelismos anarchist squat. On 30 September 2023, fifteen Extinction Rebellion activists staged a protest action in Eindhoven (Noord-Brabant), occupying and painting the facade of the ING bank headquarters to denounce the company's investments in fossil fuels. On 30 September 2023, around 40 people gathered on Hermannplatz in Berlin - Neukolln for a pro-Palestine protest. 7 people were temporarily taken into custody to determine their identity as they sang statements that are forbidden and defined as anti-Semitic in Germany. They were released later on.

On 1 October 2023, people protested in Barnaul (Altai) in support of 3 poets detained for their anti-war position in 2022 (in the so-called 'Mayakovsky case'). The protesters read poetry next to the Pushkin memorial in Barnaul, and one of them was detained.

On 1 October 2023, hundreds of Extinction Rebellion activists staged a protest action in Den Haag (Zuid-Holland), blocking the Utrechtsebaan A12 highway for traffic to demand a stop to government funding of fossil fuel companies. On 2 October 2023, an unknown number of Extinction Rebellion activists staged a protest action in Den Haag (Zuid-Holland), blocking the Utrechtsebaan A12 highway for traffic to demand a stop to government funding of fossil fuel companies. Police forces arrested 79 people.

On 3 October 2023, the police cleared a building occupied by about 40 people, both Italians and foreigners, who occupied an abandoned property in Florence (Toscana, Firenze) to protest against the housing crisis.

On 3 October 2023, 10 activists from Climaximo held a protest in Lisbon (Lisboa) against the use of fossil fuels. The activists temporarily blocked access to the the Second Circular street next to the Galp offices and police officers arrested some of them.

On 3 October 2023, hundreds of Extinction Rebellion activists staged a protest action in Den Haag (Zuid-Holland), blocking the Utrechtsebaan A12 highway for traffic to demand a stop to government funding of fossil fuel companies. Police forces arrested 73 people.

On 3 October 2023, climate activists blocked access roads to the Olympiastadion on the Rudolf-Wissell Bridge and glued themselves to the road in Berlin - Charlottenburg-Wilmersdorf to call for climate protection. On 4 October 2023, people protested in Dorogomilovo district in Moscow - Western (Zapadnyy, Moscow) against the construction of townhouses that would see a local kindergarten demolished. The police detained 3 of the protesters.

On 4 October 2023, the police cleared the 'Circolo del Romito' occupied by anarchists of the Corsica Boulevard Anarchic Collective in Scipio Slataper street in Florence (Firenze, Toscana) to protest against the housing crisis. 4 anarchist climbed onto the roof against the eviction.

On 4 October 2023, around 20 Extinction Rebellion activists protested in front of the Landhaus in Bregenz (Vorarlberg) by blocking the entrance to the underground parking with a concrete spider, against the large-scale construction project Feldkirch city tunnel and for the implementation of environmental measures. The police intervened, broke up the blockade, took two protesters from the hammocks in a wooden mesh with the help of a climber, took protesters from the roof, and carried them outside through the interior of the building. Several activists were arrested and the police will report the protesters to the district authorities.

On 4 October 2023, Just Stop Oil protesters locked themselves to the stage and halted a performance of Les Miserables at the Sondheim Theatre in London - Westminster (England) as part of their ongoing campaign to call for the government to halt all new oil and gas licenses. Police forces intervened and arrested five people.

On 4 October 2023, activists from Climaximo gathered in Lisbon (Lisboa) and blocked traffic on Sao Bento Street to protest against the use of fossil fuels. Police officers arrested three of them at the scene.

On 4 October 2023, hundreds of Extinction Rebellion activists staged a protest action in Den Haag (Zuid-Holland), blocking the Utrechtsebaan A12 highway for traffic to demand a stop to government funding of fossil fuel companies. Police forces intervened with the water cannon and arrested 110 people.

On 5 October 2023, Extinction Rebellion activists staged a protest action in Den Haag (Zuid-Holland), blocking the Utrechtsebaan A12 highway to call for a stop to governmental funding for fossil fuel companies. Police forces arrested 78 people.

On 5 October 2023, at least 40 Greenpeace activists protested at the Uniper Headquarters in Dusseldorf (Nordrhein-Westfalen) against a gas production project off the west coast of Australia for environmental and animal protection concerns. On 6 October 2023, Futuro Vegetal activists held a protest in Granada (Andalucia) against European politicians and the organization of the European Council Summit in the city, citing environmental concerns. The police intervened, led, dragged, and carried away the activists and gradually dislodged the glued ones from the street.

On 7 October 2023, around 30 Extinction Rebellion activists staged a protest on the Markt in Brugge (Vlaanderen) to demand more government action against climate change. 3 activists were arrested after not complying to police directives to end the action.

On 8 October 2023, around 20 Extinction Rebellion activists blocked traffic near the Copenhagen Airport in Kastrup, Hovedstaden, demanding to ban private jets. Later, police personnel removed activists, at least 14 people were temporarily detained.

Protesters shouted 'Palestine will be free' and waved Palestinian flags. Police forces were present at the scene and arrested two protesters who attempted to climb fences and threw paint. A few protesters burned a small Israeli flag, leaving it with flowers and sympathy cards outside the embassy.

On 9 October 2023, in the evening, around 150 people, including 'Fausse aux lions' far-left collective members, gathered for an unauthorized demonstration in the Guillotiere neighborhood of Lyon (Auvergne-Rhone-Alpes) to show support for Palestine after Hamas' offensive against Israel on 7 October 2023, and denounce the subsequent Israeli air strikes on the Gaza Strip. Demonstrators were charged by the police after 'insulting slogans' were uttered, and four participants were taken into custody.

On 10 October 2023, citizens protested in front of the local hospital in Niksic, seeking justice and responsibility for the death of a child under unresolved circumstances. Several individuals attempted to assault the hospital's director but were stopped by the local police, by forming a police cordon in front of the hospital.

On 10 October 2023, at the call of Collectif Marseille Gaza Palestine, between 150 and 200 people demonstrated in Marseille (Provence-Alpes-Cote d'Azur) to show support for Palestine and condemn Israeli airstrikes on Gaza after Hamas' offensive against Israel on 7 October 2023. Police dispersed the demonstration and took some protesters into custody.

On 10 October 2023, 7 Climaximo activists protested in Lisbon (Lisboa) by blocking the access of the intersection of Avenida de Berna and Avenida 5 de Outubro. The activists protested against fossil fuels, highlighting the urgency for sustainable energy alternatives. The members were arrested by police officers for cutting off road traffic.

On 11 October 2023, demonstrators, mostly Sami people, gathered outside of the Norwegian parliament in Oslo to protest the continued operation of wind power mills in the Fosen district, despite a Supreme Court ruling that the license was invalid. Later, a group of activists entered the parliament building and refused to leave, resulting in their removal by police officers. Activists from the Youth Committee of the Norwegian Sami Association (NSR-N) and the Nature and Youth Norway (NU) participated in the event.

Around 11 October 2023 (as reported), people held a protest in Lyon (Auvergne-Rhone-Alpes) in solidarity with Palestinians following recent escalations in the region. During the event, police fired tear gas at attendees to disperse the crowd.

On 11 October 2023, between 50 and 100 people gathered in Nantes (Pays de la Loire) in solidarity with Palestine following a recent escalation in the region. During the event, police arrested three individuals and issued eighteen fines to attendees.

On 11 October 2023, around 100 people demonstrated in Toulouse (Occitanie) to show support for the Palestinian people and condemn the Israeli airstrikes on the Gaza Strip. Police used tear gas to disperse the demonstration, which was unauthorized.

On 11 October 2023, hundreds of people gathered in the Hermannplatz and Sonnenallee area in Berlin - Neukolln for a pro-Palestine demonstration despite a ban on the event. Police officers intervened and scuffles broke out. There was no further information.

On 12 October 2023, in the evening, several hundred pro-Palestinian protesters gathered in Republique Square in Paris (Paris) to support Palestine amid the 2023 Israel-Hamas war, with some participants condemning Israel and likening 'Zionists' with 'terrorists'. On 12 October 2023, around 50 people gathered Lille (Hauts-de-France) in support of the Palestinian people following recent escalations in the region. During the event, police arrested ten individuals for rebellious acts and for refusing to disperse.

On 12 October 2023, at the call of the Collective Palestine Will Prevail, around 100 people gathered in Toulouse (Occitanie) to show support for the Palestinian people and condemn the Israeli airstrikes on Gaza. As the protest was unauthorized, police used tear gas to disperse the demonstration.

On 13 October 2023, people staged a sit-in protest and attempted to block entrances to 11 ministries in Oslo to oppose the continued operation of wind power mills in the Fosen district, despite a Supreme Court ruling that the license was invalid. Activists from the Youth Committee of the Norwegian Sami Association (NSR-N), the Nature and Youth Norway (NU) and Fridays For Future Sweden participated in the event. On 13 October 2023, several thousand people gathered in Strasbourg (Grand Est), for an unauthorized demonstration in support of Palestine following a recent escalation in the region. The police intervened and arrested 13 people.

On 13 October 2023, students blocked access to the Balzac high school in Tours (Indre-et-Loire, Centre-Val de Loire) with several garbage bins to demand answers to various labor-related concerns. Two students were temporarily detained by the police, who lifted the blockade.

On 13 October 2023, Last Generation activists blocked traffic in Bologna (Emilia-Romagna, Bologna) to demand more climate action. The police removed the protesters, restoring traffic flow. No violent act took place.

On 13 October 2023, around two dozen people gathered for a spontaneous demonstration at the main train station in Hamburg - Hamburg-Mitte to call for solidarity with Rojava and Palestine. Police forces intervened physically by arresting several demonstrators and pushing them to the ground.

On 14 October 2023, SIAN movement activists staged an anti-Islam demonstration in Oslo. Subsequently, law enforcement officers intervened and removed the activists from the venue due to security concerns.

On 14 October 2023, hundreds of people gathered at Republique Square in Paris (Ile-de-France), for an unauthorized demonstration in support of Palestine following a recent escalation in the region. The police intervened to disperse the protest and arrested 19 people.

On 14 October 2023, a few dozen people gathered in the Belsunce area and rue des Petites-Maries in Marseille (Provence-Alpes-Cote d'Azur) for an unauthorized demonstration in support of Palestine following a recent escalation in the region. During the event, police temporarily arrested four women after they refused to disperse.

On 14 October 2023, 150,000 (according to the Friends of Al Aqsa campaign) members of the Palestinian community in the UK and their supporters gathered outside BBC's headquarters in Portland Place and marched to Whitehall in London - Westminster (England) calling for a free Palestine and condemning the actions of the Israeli army in Gaza following the attack by Hamas. Protesters carried banners and waved Palestinian flags. There were minor disorders during the protests and police forced detained 15 protesters. The protest was organized by the Palestine Solidarity Campaign, Friends of Al-Aqsa, Stop the War Coalition, the Muslim Association of Britain, the Palestinian Forum in Britain, and the Campaign for Nuclear Disarmament. Labour MP Jeremy Corbyn also addressed the crowd.

On 14 October 2023, between 20 and 30 people gathered at Sudtirolerplatz and demonstrated towards Herrengasse in Graz for a free Palestine. On 14 October 2023, Climaximo activists held a protest and blocked Avenida 24 de Julho road in Lisbon (Lisboa), disrupting traffic for 30 minutes, to demand immediate action against climate change. Five activists were arrested by the police.

On 14 October 2023, people, including Antifa members, gathered in Vienna - Inner City (Wien 1-Innere Stadt) against two ongoing demonstrations (one of the Querdenken movement, the other against abortion rights). 3 people were arrested as the demonstration was spontaneous and some of them covered their faces.

On 14 October 2023, around 100 people demonstrated on Manteuffelstrasse in Berlin - Friedrichshain-Kreuzberg against the forced eviction of an apartment. Up to 10 people stood in front of the apartment's entrance and police officers pushed violently the protesters. 14 people were arrested.

On 15 October 2023, around 500 people demonstrated in Oslo to oppose the Hamas offensive against Israel . Meanwhile, around 50 people gathered to oppose the pro-Israel demonstration. Later, several people were detained and arrested, including attempting to throw stones at pro-Israel protesters.

On 15 October 2023, at the call of Plant an Olive Tree (Plant een Olijfboom), around 15,000 people joined a demonstration march from the Dam to the Westerpark in Amsterdam (Noord-Holland) to support the Palestinian people in the face of an ongoing Israeli military campaign in Gaza. Tensions rose when a pro-Israel demonstration was met around the Beursplein, where some pro-Palestinian demonstrators sought to disrupt the pro-Israeli gathering. The police held them at bay with horses and dogs, and three arrests were made among the pro-Palestinian demonstrators, one for holding a Hamas flag, and two for threatening the police.

On 16 October 2023, about 20 Last Generation activists blocked traffic around the Fiera Milano City area in Milano - Municipio 8 (Lombardia, Milano) in two different spots to demand more climate action and the institution of a 20 billion euro reparation fund for the victims of the climate emergency. Police physically removed the activists.

On 17 October 2023, people started to protest in Makhachkala (Republic of Dagestan) in support of Palestine, but were almost immediately dispersed by the police, who also arrested several people. The arrestees were given conscription notices.

On 17 October 2023, Extinction Rebellion activists stood and blocked traffic near Helsinki protesting against the planned logging in Stansvik forest within the city. Subsequently, personnel stopped the demonstration and removed the activists from the site.

On 17 October 2023, during the night, about 700 Palestinians and Syrians in the Samos migrant center moved towards the gates shouting slogans in solidarity with Palestine and against Israel, following reports of an Israeli strike at a hospital in Gaza. Riot police, police motorcyclists and the personnel of the migrant center managed to move the migrants back to their dormitories after they attempted to open the gates and leave the premises. There were 7 detentions, 5 of which turned into arrests.

On 17 October 2023, around 50 students and UNEF affiliates, all members of the Sans-Facs collective, occupied and demonstrated inside the Universite Lumiere Lyon 2 building in Lyon (Auvergne-Rhone-Alpes) to demand the registration of 29 students who were left without a spot in a masters' or bachelor's program. Police intervened to remove the protesters and clear the facility.

On 17 October 2023, Paris-Vincennes racetrack employees gathered for a picket line and blocked the race tracks of the Hippodrome de Vincennes in Paris (Ile-de-France) to demand higher pensions. Police intervened to remove the protesters.

On 17 October 2023, dozens of activists from Fossil Free London and Greenpeace gathered outside the Energy Intelligence Forum meeting at InterContinental London hotel in London - Westminster (England) against the fossil fuel companies and their role in climate change. Protesters blocked the roads with banners and shouted 'Oily money out'. Swedish Climate activist Greta Thunberg was also at the protest and was detained by police forces along with 26 other protesters.

On 18 October 2023, around 200 people demonstrated in Bergen, Vestland, to oppose the airstrike on Al-Ahli Baptist Hospital in Gaza and to show support and solidarity with the people of Palestine. Activists from the Struggle Committee took part in the event, among others. Two individuals were arrested on allegations of violence against law enforcement personnel, and protesters were pepper sprayed by police.

On 18 October 2023, XR and Elzeard en lutte activists blocked the Lure solar panel construction site in Cruis (Provence-Alpes-Cote d'Azur) to protest against the felling of trees and more broadly against the environmental damage caused by the project. Police intervened to remove the protesters.

On 18 October 2023, around 200 people participated in a prohibited pro-Palestine protest at Hauptwache in Frankfurt am Main (Hessen). Police forces intervened, requested the participants to leave the square and when they did not comply, surrounded them, checked identities, issued expulsions and dispersed the demonstration with a water cannon. After the protest was dispersed, 80 to 90 of the protesters joined new demonstrations on Zeil and on Grose Gallusstrasse. Police intervened, surrounded the participants, issued expulsions and dispersed the demonstrations.

On 18 October 2023, about 20 people participated in a pro-Palestine protest at Jungfernstieg in Hamburg - Hamburg-Mitte (Hamburg) against the Israeli attacks. The police intervened, dispersed the protest and arrested 4 young men. Later, in the early evening, people joined another pro-Palestine protest on Monckebergstrasse. The police intervened, surrounded the demonstrators, dispersed the protest and arrested around 50 people.

On 18 October 2023, numerous people came together on Bismarckplatz in Heidelberg (Baden-Wurttemberg) for a unannounced protest under the motto 'Stop the genocide in Gaza - Free Palestine'. The police demanded the protest to be ended and the participants to leave due to its unauthorized character and thereby dispersed the protest.

On 19 October 2023, at the call of CGT and 11 other associations, between 70 and 80 people gathered in Poitiers (Nouvelle-Aquitaine) to show support for the Palestinian people and condemn the Israeli airstrikes on Gaza. As the demonstration was unauthorized, the protesters split up into different groups and handed out leaflets. Police intervened to put a halt to their action, taking some protesters into custody.

On 19 October 2023, at the call of CAPJPO Europalestine and NPA, hundreds of people gathered on Place de la Republique in Paris (Ile-de-France) to show support for the Palestinian people and condemn the Israeli airstrikes on Gaza. Police used water canons and dispersed the protest. A group of police officers held their boots on the head of a protester who was being taken into custody.

On 19 October 2023, at the call of Together for Gaza, around 7,000 people marched between the Domplein and Jaarbeursplein in Utrecht (Utrecht) to support the Palestinian people amid Israel's military campaign in and around the Gaza Strip, with some demonstrators condemning the Israeli military campaign. The police made two arrests.

On 19 October 2023, more than 12 Last Generation activists protested in Berlin - Charlottenburg-Wilmersdorf (Berlin) for climate reasons by blocking traffic on the city highway at the height of Charlottenburg Palace with three vehicles and sit-ins. The police dispersed the protest around mid-day. Earlier in the day, Last Generation activists also blocked the Wissel-Bridge in Berlin - Charlottenburg-Wilmersdorf.

On 19 October 2023, 50 people participated in a pro-Palestine protest on Opernplatz in Hannover (Region Hannover, Niedersachsen) to raise awareness for the situation in Gaza and demand freedom for Palestine. Some protesters stated that they have no issue with the Jewish community but solely with Israel and condemn the one-sided reporting by the German media. During the speeches, a slogan that implies that the state of Israel should not exist was used, the police intervened and explained that the slogan is punishable.

On 19 October 2023, 70 people, many with Palestine flags, gathered on Rathausplatz in Kiel (Schleswig-Holstein) for a pro-Palestine protest which was previously prohibited by a short-term ban of the city. The police was present on the spot to enforce the ban and the participants left the square peacefully.

On 20 October 2023, several tens of people protested in Khasavyurt (Republic of Dagestan) in support of Palestine, but were dispersed by the police. The government has denied dispersing or detaining the protesters.

On 20 October 2023, 70 to 80 people participated in a prohibited pro-Palestine protest on Griesplatz in Graz (Steiermark) organized by 'Palastina Solidaritat Osterreich' (Palestine Solidarity Austria) and the 'Steirischen Friedensplattform' (Styrian Peace Platform). Although the police informed them that the gathering was not allowed to take place, most of the people did not want to leave the square and the policies established their identities and issued reports.

On 21 October 2023, at the call of AFPS, more than 80 people gathered in Vannes (Bretagne) to show support for the Palestinian people and condemn the Israeli airstrikes on Gaza, while some also condemned Hamas's attack on Israel on 7 October 2023. Police handed out fines and took some protesters into custody as the protest was unauthorized.

On 21 October 2023, estimated 300,000 (according to Palestine Solidarity Campaign) pro-Palestinian protesters marched from the Marble Arch to Downing Street in London - Westminster (England) in support of the besieged Gaza Strip and against Israeli air strikes. Protesters carried Palestine flags and chanted 'From the river to the sea, Palestine will be free' and carried signs saying 'Freedom for Palestine'. The protest was mainly peaceful but police forces arrested 10 people linked to the event. Palestine Solidarity Campaign and Stop the War Coalition organized the protest.

On 21 October 2023, 5 Last Generation activists blocked the traffic in Vittorio Emanuele II avenue in Torino (Torino, Piemonte) to call for more climate action. The demonstrators laid down on the road and chained themselves. The police officers on site removed the activists and restored car circulation.

On 21 October 2023, 11 Last Generation activists protested on Hauptstatter Strasse in Stuttgart (Baden-Wurttemberg) as a mourning march against the climate policies of the federal government and for the compliance with the climate protection law, and thereby blocked traffic. The police made the activists continue their protest march in only one lane to avoid major traffic obstructions. Later, around 13 o'clock, 5 Last Generation activists blocked the road in front of the main train station. The police intervened and carried the activists off the road.

On 21 October 2023, about 300 people participated in a prohibited protest at Steindamm and the surrounding streets in the district St. Georg in Hamburg - Hamburg-Mitte (Hamburg) in solidarity with Palestine. The police informed in German and Arabic about the existing ban on pro-Palestine demonstrations, announced that they would use water cannons and pepper spray if the protest was not stopped, and ended the protest within an hour and pushed the protesters from Steindamm towards the main train station. Some of the demonstrators resisted the forces, the police took about 100 protesters into custody and established the identity of many people and issued residing bans.

On 22 October 2023, around 300 people gathered in Nice (Provence-Alpes-Cote d'Azur) to show support for the Palestinian people and condemn the Israeli airstrikes on Gaza, while shouting 'Israel, assassin' and 'Estrosi [the mayor of Nice], assassin'. Police handed out fines and took some protesters into custody as the demonstration was unauthorized.
On 22 October 2023, people protested in front of Israel's Embassy in Moscow - Central (Tsentralnyy, Moscow) against Israel's actions in Gaza during the war. 8 people were detained.

On 22 October 2023, at the call of Rotterdam for Gaza, around 5,000 pro-Palestinian protesters, supported by local churches, staged a protest march in Rotterdam (Zuid-Holland), marching from the Erasmusbrug to the Wilhelminaplein, to protest in solidarity with Palestinians amid the Israeli military campaign in and around the Gaza Strip, waving Palestinian, Turkish, Syrian and other flags. It was part of a larger movement of support events in The Netherlands for Palestinians in Gaza. At the same time, about 30 counter-protesters stood in front of the municipality waving Israeli flags and shouting 'Go home to Gaza!' and 'Gaza genocide!' as pro-Palestinian sympathizers passed by. The insults and provocations from the counter-protesters escalated to the point where the police had to intervene. Thirteen counter-protesters were arrested for public intoxication, insults, racist slogans, and assaulting an officer.

On 22 October 2023, in the evening, about 800 (according to police) or more than 1,000 (according to people on site) people, including Ahmad Tamim, a relevant representative of the 'Generation Islam' (an initiative that is part of the Islamist organization 'Hizb ut-Tahrir' which advocates the rule of a comprehensive caliphate based on the traditional Islamic legal principles of Sharia law) participated in a pro-Palestine protest on Alexanderplatz in Berlin - Mitte (Berlin) under the title 'Near-East-Conflict' to show solidarity with Palestine. In addition to 232 custodial interdictions, 175 administrative offenses and 25 criminal charges were filed for suspected rewarding and approval of criminal acts, suspected incitement to hatred and resistance to law enforcement officers. Two police officers were injured.

On 23 October 2023, 5 Last Generation activists blocked the traffic in Verona (Verona, Veneto) to call for more climate action. The demonstrators laid down on the road and chained themselves. The police officers on site removed the activists and restored car circulation. The demonstrators called for the establishment of a 20 billion euro fund to repair the damage caused by disasters and extreme weather events.

On 23 October 2023, around 20 activists of Justice Now!, a sub-branch of Extinction Rebellion, staged a protest action inside the International Criminal Court (ICC) in Den Haag (Zuid-Holland) to express solidarity with Palestinians, denounce the Israeli military campaign in and around the Gaza Strip, and demand the Israeli government be persecuted for war crimes. Police forces ended the action and carried all protesters outside the building.

On 23 October 2023, about 40 Last Generation activists protested in 7 locations in Berlin (Berlin) and glued themselves onto the road to show their dissatisfaction with Chancellor Olaf Scholz (SPD) and for climate reasons. Three of these protests occurred on Stadtautobahn A100. The police dispersed the protest and removed the blockades.

On 25 October 2023, several dozen activists affiliated with the movement The Limits Are Us gathered in Prague. They launched a rally near headquarters of a media branch owned by a businessman engaged in coal mining, protesting against alleged manipulation of the climate-related agenda in media. Around 19 of them refused to leave when ordered by police and were briefly detained.

On 25 October 2023, around 40 environmental activists blocked entrance to a pulp mill in Kemi, Lappi, against alleged unsustainable forest management practices. Activists from Greenpeace and Extinction Rebellion took part in the event, including activists from Finland, Sweden Denmark, Norway, Poland, the Netherlands and Germany. Police subsequently arrested approximately some 29 protesters.

On 26 October 2023, around 20 environmental activists demonstrated in Helsinki, to oppose the ongoing logging in the Stansvik forest. Later, several activists attempted to disrupt the work resulting in at least 10 people being arrested.
On 26 October 2023, people protested in Khabarovsk (Khabarovsk) in support of jailed former governor Sergey Furgal. 4 of the protesters were later detained.

On 26 October 2023, several people blocked access to the airport by sitting down on the street in Innsbruck to call for climate protection. Police officers intervened physically to carry away demonstrators.

On 26 October 2023, between 4 and 6 members of Last Generation blocked the road on Hohenzollerndamm, at the corner of Rudolstadter, in Berlin - Charlottenburg-Wilmersdorf to call for climate protection. Police forces intervened to clear the blockade.

On 27 October 2023, environmental activists attempted to disrupt the ongoing logging in the Stansvik forest in Helsinki, demanding that the work be stopped. Several people were arrested during the demonstration.

On 28 October 2023, 500 people protested in front of the regional administration's building in Cherkessk (Cherkesskiy, Republic of Karachay-Cherkessia) demanding that the administrators not let any Israeli refugees into the region and deport all Jewish people currently living in the region. They also demanded that the regional government organize a fundraiser to support Palestinians. 34 of the protesters were detained by the police.

On 28 October 2023, at the call of the environmental group Public Benches (Bancs Publics), people gathered on the construction site of an underground parking lot on Aristide Briand Square in Sete (Occitanie) to demonstrate against the projects' impact on the environment. As the event was unauthorized, two BAC police officers intervened to remove the demonstrators. One of them, named Sylvain Pastor, resisted his arrest, and pushed away a police officer.

On 28 October 2023, at the call of multiple organizations, including collectif unitaire 31, 160 people gathered in Toulouse (Occitanie) to show support for the Palestinian people. As the protest was unauthorized, police officers handed out fines to several protesters. One participant was arrested for resisting public authority.

On 28 October 2023, at the call of the Collective of Compiegnois for Peace in Palestine, people gathered in Compiegne (Hauts-de-France) to show support for the Palestinian people and demand a ceasefire between Israel and Hamas. As the protest was unauthorized, police took the organizer into custody, leading to the peaceful dispersion of the gathering.

On 28 October 2023, between 3,000 and 4,000 people, including national deputies Aurelien Tache (The Ecologists) and Jerome Legavre (LFI) gathered in Paris (Ile-de-France) to show support for the Palestinian people and condemn the Israeli airstrikes on Gaza. Police used tear gas to disperse the protest, handed out fines to some demonstrators, and temporarily arrested 21 people.

On 28 October 2023, 100,000 pro-Palestine protesters marched in the center of the city in London - Westminster (England) in support of Palestine and demanding a ceasefire. Protesters were chanting 'From the river to the sea, Palestine will be free', carrying banners and placards and waving Palestinian flags. Palestine Solidarity Campaign and Stop the War Coalition organized the protest. The protest was mainly peaceful but police forces arrested two protesters. Dozens of people with Union flags gathered at the Cenotaph on Whitehall for a counter-demonstration.

On 28 October 2023, Last Generation activists blocked traffic and displayed a banner in front of the Adigeo shopping center in Verona (Veneto, Verona) to demand more climate action. Some passers-by and motorists tried to move the activists and free the road. The police intervened, physically removed the protesters, and prevented clashes between protesters and drivers.

On 28 October 2023, around 200 protesters held a 'Housing protest' ('Woonprotest') at Koekamp in Den Haag (Zuid-Holland), demanding the decriminalization of squatting and a fair housing market. Various political parties, such as Volt, BIJ1 and the PvdD, were represented at the protest. After the protest, around 20-25 protesters occupied the World Trade Center's hall in Den Haag, protesting against the Association of Institutional Investors in Real Estate, who allegedly serve the interest of lobbies and large real estate investors. The police and security personell physically dragged protesters out of the building and ended the protest. One person was subsequently arrested for vandalizing the tires of a police car.

On 28 October 2023, at the call of the group 'Against Watchtower Shunning,' ten former Jehovah's Witnesses gathered in Nijverdal to protest the practice of 'shunning,' which they say leads to the social isolation of members who leave the faith. The protest began in Nijverdal, but the group then traveled to Emmen (Drenthe) for the demonstration at the Jehovah's Witnesses headquarters. The leader of the group climbed over the fence of the headquarters, which led to his arrest by the police. The activists hope that the eventual legal proceedings following the arrest will highlight the social consequences of the shunning practice.

On 28 October 2023, at the call of Last Generation, between up to 600 (according to the police) and more than 1,000 (according to organizers), people, including members of Extinction Rebellion, Scientist Rebellion and BUND, staged a protest at the 17. Juni Street at the Victory Column in Berlin - Mitte to call for an exit from fossil fuel, with some gluing themselves to the street and being physically removed by the police. Between 60 and 154 members of Last Generation later gathered to block the street, gluing themselves to the road. Police officers intervened physically to remove the demonstrators from the street.

On 28 October 2023, people protested in Kosinskiy park in Moscow - Eastern (Vostochnyy, Moscow) against the destruction of the park. The police detained 4 of the activists. Though the local authorities have assured them that the cutting of trees in the park is necessary to make sure it abides by legal norms, locals argue that its destruction harms the environment.
On 29 October 2023, people protested in Makhachkala (Republic of Dagestan) in support of Palestine. Several protesters were detained by the police.

On 30 October 2023, people commemorated the Day of Remembrance of the Victims of Political Repressions in front of the memorial to the victims of repressions in Yoshkar-Ola (Republic of Mari El). One participant of the event was arrested for laying down a poster in Belarusian language that spoke of the 'The Night of the Shot Poets' - a mass political murder of Belarusian intelligentsia in 1937.

On 30 October 2023, 65 climate activists from Just Stop Oil held a slow march in Parliament Square in London - Westminster (England) to denounce the government's lack of action on climate and call for the government to halt all new oil and gas licenses. Police forces intervened and arrested 62 protesters and opened the road.

On 30 October 2023, about 15 Last Generation activists blocked Berti Pichat Street and Stalingrado Street in Bologna (Emilia-Romagna, Bologna) to demand more climate action and the allocation of 20 billion euros in funding to counter the effects of climate change. The police physically removed the activists and took 15 of them, who had passively resisted, to the police headquarters to identify them.

On 2 November 2023, a Parbeszed-affiliated left-wing MP and a Varos Mindenkie activists blockaded the entry into a flat in Budapest - XIX, protesting against the decision to evict a family with two children from the flat. The police removed the protesters forcibly.

On 2 November 2023, about 10 Last Generation activists blocked traffic in Bologna (Bologna, Emilia-Romagna) to demand more climate action. Two of them glued their hands to the tarmac. Police officers arrived on site shortly after, removed the activists and restored car circulation. At the same time, 3 Last Generation activists entered the Region's headquarters to demand the establishment of a climate reparation fund.

On 3 November 2023, about 5 people attempted to disrupt a parliamentary meeting at the Danish Parliament in Copenhagen in relation to the Hamas-Israel conflict and Israeli airstrikes on Gaza. Police later arrested all the activists.

On 3 November 2023, people held a protest in San Sebastian (Gipuzkoa, Pais Vasco) to express solidarity with Palestine, denouncing Israeli attacks in and around the Gaza Strip, and advocating for peace. One protester was arrested and accused of public disorder and attack on authority. The protest was summoned by Gazte Koordinadora Sozialista (GKS).

On 3 November 2023, hundreds of pro-Palestine protesters staged a sit-in protest at Kings Cross station in London - Camden (England) to show solidarity with Palestine and call for an immediate ceasefire.
