Protesters were chanting 'Free Palestine' and 'Stop killing children now'. Police forces intervened to disperse the crowd and arrested two protesters.

On 3 November 2023, at the call of several pro-Palestinian organizations, about 9,000 people, including members of the leftist scene, took to the streets in Berlin - Neukolln (Berlin), expressing solidarity with Palestine and condemning the military campaign of Israel in and around Gaza. At least 68 people were arrested for carrying or chanting 'provocative' slogans.

On 3 November 2023, about 850 people took to the streets of Frankfurt am Main (Hessen) for a pro-Palestinian demonstration, while also condemning the Israeli military campaign in and around the Gaza Strip. At least eight people were arrested by the police for carrying or chanting 'provocative' slogans against Israel.
On 4 November 2023, around 10,000 people gathered in Bern (Bern) to show support for the Palestinian people and condemn the Israeli airstrikes on Gaza. Several people were arrested by the police.

On 4 November 2023, 30,000 pro-Palestine protesters held a march in the city center and gathered at Trafalgar Square in London - Westminster (England) in solidarity with Palestinians, to condemn the Israeli military campaign in and around the Gaza Strip, and to demand a ceasefire between Israel and Palestine. Protesters carried Palestinian flags and chanted 'From the river to the sea, Palestine will be free'. Labour MP Jeremy Corbyn addressed the crowd. Palestine Solidarity Campaign and Stop the War Coalition organized the protest. Police forces arrested 29 protesters.

On 4 November 2023, about 150 people gathered for a rally in Steinen (Baden-Wurttemberg), protesting against a local convention of the AfD party, as well as against racism. Among them, there was an MP (Green party) and a local SDP representative. Four participants were detained for attempting to block an approaching vehicle of the AfD party.

On 4 November 2023, hundreds of people, including members of a Palestinian group, marched in Bucharest, demanding a ceasefire to the Israel-Hamas conflict and shouting slogans in support of a free Palestine. Three protesters were taken to the police for questioning, after pepper spray and a firecracker were found on them.

On 5 November 2023, a group of people protested in Tallinn, Estonia, in support of Palestine. Police detained 5 protesters who were holding a banner saying 'From the river to the sea, Palestine will be free'.

On 5 November 2023, thousands of pro-Palestine protesters gathered for a rally in Birmingham (England) in solidarity with Palestinians. The protest was mainly peaceful with no incidents. Police forces detained three teenagers for minor disruptions and released them after the protest, while also detaining one man for 'possession of an offensive weapon'.

On 6 November 2023, around 3,800 people held a protest in front of the PSOE headquarters on Ferraz Street in Madrid - Chamberi (Madrid) to voice their opposition to the deal that Spain's PSOE acting prime minister, Pedro Sanchez, sealed with JuntsXCat and ERC, which also includes an amnesty pact, in the hopes of securing an additional term. Vox leaders and vice president of Castilla y Leon (Vox) attended the protest. Police launched tear gas, rubber balls and smoke canisters, and arrested three protesters.

On 6 November 2023, 6 Last Generation activists blocked the traffic in Messina (Messina, Sicilia), along Garibaldi street, to call for more climate action. The demonstrators laid down on the road and chained themselves. The police officers on site removed the activists and restored car circulation. The demonstrators called for the establishment of a 20 billion euro fund to repair the damage caused by disasters and extreme weather events.

On 6 November 2023, at the call of Greenpeace, Alternatiba, Last Renovation, XR, SDN, ANV-COP21, Friends of the Earth, and 365.org, around 150 climate activists gathered outside the Ministry for Ecological Transition in Paris (Ile-de-France) to protest against the French government's lack of climate action. Police sprayed tear gas on the protesters to disperse the demonstration.

On 7 November 2023, people attempted to disrupt a parliamentary meeting at the Finnish Parliament in Helsinki. The activists called for the 'liberation of Palestine' and an immediate ceasefire in the ongoing Hamas-Israel conflict. Police officers removed the activists from the venue.

On 8 November 2023, 8 Last Generation activists blocked the traffic in Enna (Sicilia, Enna) to protest against coal and hydrocarbon power plants for energy purposes. The police physically removed the protesters.

On 8 November 2023, at the call of many left-wing parties and associations, nearly 200 people gathered at Liberte Square in Brest (Bretagne) to express solidarity with the Palestinian people and condemn the Israeli military campaign in and around the Gaza Strip. Despite the peaceful march, the police intervened to arrest a young man, apparently drunk and shouting 'free Palestine' on the grounds that he was violent for other demonstrators.

On 8 November 2023, Just Stop Oil protesters held a slow march and blocked traffic on Waterloo Bridge in London - Westminster (England) to denounce the government's lack of action on climate and call for the government to halt all new oil and gas licenses. Police forces intervened and arrested more than 40 participants.

On 9 November 2023, pro-Palestine protesters climbed the roof of the Scottish Parliament in Edinburgh (Scotland) to demand the Scottish government 'Stop arming and funding Israel'. Protesters hung banners and Palestinian flags from the building. Police forces intervened and arrested five protesters.

On 9 November 2023, at the call of the National Watchgroup for Trees (GNSA) and La Voie est Libre, climate activists, including Thomas Brail, climbed on trees in Lacroisille (Occitanie) to protest against the construction of the A69 highway between Toulouse and Castres, which the protesters deemed damaging to the environment. Two activists were taken down from the trees by the police and brought to the police station.

On 9 November 2023, residents of Exarchia continued to rally at Exarchia square Athens - Central Athens against the pruning and removal of trees during construction work for a new metro station. The demonstrators confronted strong riot police forces guarding the site, who pushed them away. There was 1 arrest.

On 10 November 2023, residents of Exarchia continued to rally at Exarchia square, Athens - Central Athens, against the pruning and removal of trees during construction work for a new metro station. Police detained 4 people.

On 11 November 2023, activists gathered for an Independence march in Warsaw, praising the Polish sovereignty. Among the participants, there were invited guests from the Hungarian movement MHM: Our Homeland, Polish initiatives National Movement, National Radical Camp and All-Poland Youth, the Confederation party and Catholic groups. At least some were demanding Poland leaving the EU, and condemned liberal LGBTQ+ values. 56 people were detained for various violations of public order.

On 11 November 2023, hundreds of pro-Palestine protesters including members of the Palestinian community held a rally on Buchanan Street in Glasgow (Scotland) to show solidarity with Palestine and demand an immediate ceasefire. Protesters were chanting 'Ceasefire now', 'free Palestine' and 'From the river to the sea, Palestine will be free'. The protest was mostly peaceful but police forces arrested seven people. Keith Brown, Depute Leader of SNP also addressed the crowd.

On 11 November 2023, 7 members of Last Generation blocked traffic by gluing themselves to the road on the Brenner motorway (A13) near Matrei am Brenner (Tirol, Innsbruck-Land) in the direction of Italy to call for climate protection. An unknown road user tried to carry an activist off the road and got super glue in her eye. The activists were eventually carried off the streets by the police.

On 11 November 2023, Extinction Rebellion associated group blocked traffic outside Copenhagen Airport in Kastrup, Hovedstaden, demanding a ban on private jets and a halt to the airport expansion. The activists were later removed by police personnel.

On 11 November 2023, six environmental activists gathered in Warsaw, protesting against the ongoing independence march. They linked the participants with fossil industry and demanded immediate climate action. Police removed them from the street.

On 11 November 2023, around 2,600 (according to the police) people gathered in Berlin - Friedrichshain-Kreuzberg (Berlin) for a pro-Palestine demonstration. They called for freedom for Palestine and spoke of genocide to define Israel's military operation in the Gaza Strip. Police officers temporarily arrested some demonstrators for carrying banners that they judged had 'criminal content'.

On 11 November 2023, at the call of Die Partei, around 50 people gathered in front of the Europagalerie in Saarbrucken (Saarland, Regionalverband Saarbrucken) against a simultaneous demonstration against abortion rights called by Christen fur das Leben (Christians for Life), in which around 200 people, including 2 AFD MPs, took part in front of the Pro Familia building. Police officers used physical force to push away several demonstrators called by Die Partei in the area of Paul-Marien-Strasse, Bahnhofstrasse, at the corner of Dudweilerstrasse and Viktoriastrasse.

Around 11 November 2023 (as reported), people demonstrated in Halle (Saale) (Sachsen-Anhalt) as part of a pro-Palestinian demonstration, though condemning Hamas, which they described as a fascist organization. They gathered under the motto 'Don't give anti-communism, fascism, racism and anti-Semitism a chance!' and criticized the current actions of the Israeli government while calling for the right to do so. Police officers forcibly prevented a protester from giving a speech, speech manuscripts were confiscated, and the rally was broken up as a result.

On 12 November 2023, about 50 residents of Exarchia continued to rally in Exarchia square, Athens - Central Athens, against the pruning and removal of trees during construction work for a new metro station. There were detentions and arrests.

On 12 November 2023, around 2,000 people, called by Vox and PP, protested in front of the PSOE headquarters in Albacete (Castilla-La Mancha) to voice their opposition to the deal that Spain's PSOE acting prime minister, Pedro Sanchez, sealed with JuntsXCat and ERC, which also includes an amnesty pact, in the hopes of securing an additional term. The regional deputy (Vox) and councilor in the Albacete City Council (Vox) attended the protest. Police arrested 3 people after an ideological dispute between different groups.

On 12 November 2023, between a hundred and several hundred people, called by PP and Vox, held protests in Bilbao (Bizkaia, Pais Vasco) to voice their opposition to the deal that Spain's PSOE acting prime minister, Pedro Sanchez, sealed with JuntsXCat and ERC, which also includes an amnesty pact, in the hopes of securing an additional term. PP representatives and parliamentarians attended the protest. Police detained one protester.

On 13 November 2023, 5 Last Generation activists blocked Roma street in Cagliari (Cagliari, Sardegna) to protest against the government's inaction for the protection of the environment. They held a banner saying 'we don't pay the fuel' and two glued their hands to the street. The police pulled away the demonstrators to clear the street.

On 13 November 2023, around 70 antifascist activists gathered for a demonstration in Lyon (Auvergne-Rhone-Alpes) to show support for the victims of the attack of a conference by far-right activists on Gaza on 11 November. Protesters also showed support for the Palestinian people and condemned Israel's offensive in Gaza. Police dispersed the protest with tear gas.

On 13 November 2023, seven environmental activists blocked traffic at a motorway exit near Orestad, Copenhagen, calling to abolish use of highways and large roads. Later, police personnel removed activists from the venue, several were detained.

On 13 November 2023, Last Generation activists blocked the traffic in Lucania street in Milano - Municipio 4 (Milano, Lombardia) to protest against the government's inaction for the protection of the environment. Some drivers tried to pull away the demonstrators. The police pulled away demonstrators to clear the street.

On 14 November 2023, 7 La lutte des sucs climate activists blocked archeological excavations in Saint-Hostien (Auvergne-Rhone-Alpes) to protest against the construction of the RN88 road, which they deemed damaging to the environment. The protesters were taken into custody by the police.

On 14 November 2023, around 20 people and human rights activists blocked a bus carrying 15 migrants outside the Center for Asylum Seekers (CARA) in the Pian del Lago district of Caltanissetta (Sicilia) to protest against the repatriation centers (CPR) and ask for the implementation of good practices for the reception and inclusion of asylum seekers and migrants. After blocking the bus, two activists chained themselves to the vehicle to prevent the transport of migrants. The police removed the protesters.

On 15 November 2023, 3 student climate activists held a protest in Lisbon (Lisboa) against the use of fossil fuels in the form of a lecture at the Faculty of Psychology in Lisbon. The activists were detained by police forces while doing that.

On 15 November 2023, at least 7 Last Generation activists staged a protest and threw paint at the 'Arco della Pace' monument in Milano - Municipio 1 (Lombardia) to demand more climate action. The police removed the protesters.

On 15 November 2023, around 80 people, including members of XR, protested in front of the Landhaus in Bregenz (Vorarlberg) against a planned road tunnel project and for a sustainable mobility shift. Some of the participants glued themselves to one another, the police intervened by separating the participants and dissolving the protest.

On 15 November 2023, 5 Last Generation activists protested on the main road outside the courthouse in Munster (Nordrhein-Westfalen) to raise awareness about climate change and demand climate actions from politicians, by sitting on the intersection. Three of the protesters glued themselves onto the road. The police intervened by detaching the activists from the road and dissolving the protest.

On 16 November 2023, around 200 people, including students, staged a protest action on the campus of the University of Lausanne (Vaud), to demonstrate against the visit of French President Emmanuel Macron and his stance on the war between Israel and Hamas. They marched chanting 'Macron complicit' and carrying banners reading 'Stop genocide' and 'Free Palestine'. The police intervened using pepper spray, while no injuries nor arrests were reported.

On 17 November 2023, at the call of XR: Justice Now!, 15 pro-Palestinian activists stormed the premises of the local office of Thales Group in protest in Delft (Zuid-Holland), accusing the company of creating and distributing parts for planes currently involved in Israeli military airstrikes in and around Gaza. 10 protesters were arrested for trespassing.

On 18 November 2023, climate activists, including Last Renovation affiliates, blocked traffic on the M7 road in Lyon (Auvergne-Rhone-Alpes), to alert public opinion on the challenges of climate change. Police forces intervened to remove the activists.

On 18 November 2023, people, including Yellow Vest, took to the streets of Nantes (Pays de la Loire) to demonstrate. Motives were not specified. Police officers intervened and used tear gas to disperse the crowd.

On 18 November 2023, in the morning, dozens of people, including Yellow Vests and Last Renovation activists, staged a protest action in Paris (Ile-de-France), for the 5th anniversary of the Yellow Vests movement. They sprayed yellow paint on the Arc de Triomphe traffic circle, the scene of violent clashes in 2018. Police forces intervened and 8 activists were arrested.

On 18 November 2023, at the call of Last Generation and under the framework of the campaign 'Reparation Fund' (a governmental fund to repair damage from climate disasters), 10 activists staged a march and walked to the police headquarters in Pavia (Lombardia) to stage a fake retirement party for the Police Commissioner Alessio Cesareo and protest against his management of the public order. Protesters were equipped with trumpets and gifts and a participant read a diploma reporting the ironic merits of his work. The police stopped protesters who wanted to occupy Repubblica street and brought them to the police headquarters.

On 18 November 2023, around 100 pro-Palestine protesters staged a sit-in protest at Waterloo Street station in London - Lambeth (England) to demand an immediate ceasefire in Gaza. Protesters were chanting 'Free Palestine', 'From the river to the sea, Palestine will be free' and waving Palestine flags. Protesters later moved to Parliament Square and were joined by Just Stop Oil protesters. Police forces arrested 5 protesters. The event was part of a national day of action for Palestinians affected by Israel's bombardment.

On 18 November 2023, in the afternoon, at the call of PSR and Let Women Speak (LWS), 200 female civil society representatives protested at Paardeveld in Utrecht (Utrecht), calling for respect for the dignity and privacy of women. The protesters accused the transgender community of having a privileged position within the society. More than 60 LGBTQ+ activists counter-demonstrated at Jaarbeursplein and started marching toward Paardenveld towards the other protesters. A police presence prevented interactions between both groups, with officers temporarily closing a traffic lane, and redirecting demonstrators to Weerdsingel Westzijde. One counter-demonstrator was arrested by the police for making threats using a megaphone.

On 18 November 2023, eight Last Generation activists disrupted a World Ski Cup race in Gurgl (Tirol), spraying an orange color on the finish line, and calling for immediate climate action. The police intervened by removing the activists from the slope, and dragging some of them away by their feet.

On 19 November 2023, several dozen student and climate activists held a protest in front of the parliament in Lisbon (Lisboa) against the use of fossil fuels. 3 students climbed on the building to paint the stairs. The activists were detained by police forces while doing that.

On 19 November 2023, at the call of the Rotterdam Palestine Coalition, between 6,000 to 15,000 people marched through Rotterdam (Zuid-Holland), starting and ending at the Binnenrotte near Blaak, calling for a ceasefire in Gaza and expressing solidarity with the Palestinian population. Speeches were held by representatives of the Islamic center Centrum de Middenweg, Plant an Olive Tree (Plant een Olijfboom), and Palestine Solidarity Rotterdam. The organization Samidoun, as well as SP members, including fraction leader and MP Theo Coskun, were also present. The protesters condemned the Israeli government's actions and criticized the Dutch government for supporting them. A small group of pro-Israeli people staged a counter-demonstration, waving Israeli flags, at the Coolsingel in front of the city hall. A pro-Palestinian demonstrator, who approached the pro-Israel group, was arrested. The police made a total of five arrests during the event, two for failing to show identification and three for disturbing the public order, including charges of insults.

On 19 November 2023, around 20 environmental activists from Extinction Rebellion sat and blocked traffic in Aarhus in support of a car-free city. Four activists were later arrested after refusing to leave the road.

On 20 November 2023, around a thousand people held a protest on Ferraz street, where the PSOE headquarters is located, in Madrid - Moncloa-Aravaca (Madrid) to voice their opposition to the deal that Spain's PSOE Prime Minister, Pedro Sanchez, sealed with JuntsXCat and ERC, which also includes an amnesty pact, securing him an additional term. A far-right agitator was arrested.

On 20 November 2023, 5 university students from Coimbra Fim ao Fossil organization protested and blocked entrances at the university in Coimbra (Coimbra) to demand the end of fossil fuels by 2030. Police removed the 5 activists.

On 20 November 2023, Greenpeace activists gathered and dumped liquid manure in front of the Ministry of Agriculture in Paris (Ile-de-France), to demand a national moratorium on factory farms and to call on the government not to open any new intensive animal farm, in the name of animal welfare and the protection of the planet. 11 activists were arrested by the police.

On 20 November 2023, 5 Last Generation members blocked traffic in Grassi street in Padua (Veneto, Padova) to protest against climate change. Protesters displayed a banner to raise awareness. The police intervened to remove them and brought them to the police headquarters.

On 21 November 2023, at the call of CGT-Spectacle, around 30 contractual show business workers demonstrated in Nantes (Pays de la Loire) to demand more social security. Police took one participant into custody. Other demonstrators claimed this was done 'arbitrarily'.

On 22 November 2023, several dozen members of the far-right group Les Remparts Lyon gathered outside a bar in Lyon (Auvergne-Rhone-Alpes) to protest and pay tribute to Thomas, a 16-year-old youth who was stabbed and consequently died after a brawl in Crepol on 18 November 2023, claiming he was killed because he was white. Police intervened as the protest was unauthorized and took a protester into custody.

On 23 November 2023, hundreds of people held a protest in Madrid - Centro (Madrid) as part of an ongoing protest against the deal that Spain's PSOE Prime Minister, Pedro Sanchez, sealed with JuntsXCat and ERC, which also includes an amnesty pact. 4 people were detained by police officers for public disorder.

On 23 November 2023, police forces intervened to disperse a picket line staged by striking undocumented Emmaus workers in Saint-Andre-lez-Lille (Hauts-de-France). Police clubbed some demonstrators and resorted to tear gas. Two protesters had to be taken to the hospital for medical treatment.

On 23 November 2023, in the afternoon, at the call of End Fossil LU/TUD, climate activists, including students from the University of Leiden, TU Delft, and Erasmus University Rotterdam, gathered inside the Lipsius building at the University of Leiden in Leiden (Zuid-Holland), occupying two classrooms, to protest the university's ties with fossil fuel companies. The university ordered all buildings closed at 17:00, and when the activists refused to leave, the police cleared the building, physically removing 30 activists through the back entrance of the building.

On 24 November 2023, several tens of people demonstrated in Congaz, blocking a national road, demanding that the central government unblock a payment of 1000 lei for each pensioner in Gagauzia, but also that the government does not impede the gas delivery by a new company. Police arrested a demonstrators.

On 24 November 2023, around 50 students and 'Fim ao Fossil' (No More Fossils) climate activists staged a protest at the Ministries of Infrastructure and Environment in Lisbon (Lisboa) as part of a demonstration in favor of ending fossil fuels by 2030. At least three activists were detained by police officers.

On 25 November 2023, people gathered for a protest in Nantes (Pays de la Loire), as a part of the International Day for the Elimination of Violence Against Women, against violence done to women. A 26-year-old woman, suspected of being behind a tag insulting the Minister of the Interior on the facade of the town hall, was arrested by the police at the end of the demonstration.

On 25 November 2023, pro-Palestine protesters gathered outside the Egyptian Embassy in London - Westminster (England) in support of Palestine. The protest was organized by Hizb ut-Tahrir. Police forces arrested two women and charged them with a racially aggravated public order offense when they were observed holding signs displaying content likely to provoke harassment, alarm, or distress.

On 25 November 2023, tens of thousands of pro-Palestine protesters marched from Park Lane to Whitehall in London - Westminster (England) to call for a permanent ceasefire in Gaza and show solidarity with Palestine. The protest was mostly peaceful but police forces arrested 18 protesters.
On 25 November 2023, about 1,600 activists gathered for a pro-Palestine rally in Frankfurt am Main. Law enforcers detained several members for suspected promotion of hatred.

On 26 November 2023, around 40 far-right activists staged several protest actions in downtown Romans-sur-Isere (Auvergne-Rhone-Alpes) to pay tribute to Thomas, a 16-year-old youth who was stabbed and consequently died after a brawl during a village festival in Crepol on 18 November 2023, calling for justice. Police forces dispersed the demonstrations and arrested 7 people, including three far-right activists and four youngsters from the town's Monnaie neighborhood, who had taken to the streets against the far-right demonstrations. Most of the people arrested were 'carrying weapons' according to the police.

On 26 November 2023, estimated 100,000 people marched from the Royal Courts of Justice to Parliament Square in London - Westminster (England) against antisemitism amid the rise in hate crime in the UK since the Israel-Palestine war began. The Campaign Against Antisemitism organized the protest. Protesters carried placards reading 'Shoulder to shoulder with British Jews' and 'Never again is now'. Conservative MP Boris Johnson also attended the march. The far-right group, English Defence League founder Tommy Robinson also attended the protest. However, later he was arrested by police forces since he was asked by organizers not to attend the protest. Chief Rabbi Sir Ephraim Mirvis also addressed the crowd.

On 26 November 2023, around 2,600 feminist activists marched through Brussels (Brussels) on the occasion of the International Day for the Elimination of Violence against Women against violence against women. Several protesters were arrested at the beginning of the march for possessing material assumed to be used for the degradation of public buildings. Some protesters also voiced the violence in and out of the Gaza Strip and tried to deviate from the planned route but were prevented by the police with tear gas.

On 26 November 2023, around 100 people, including Antifa and far-left members, gathered outside the cult bar 'Elbschlosskeller' in Hamburg - Altona, to voice their opposition to the presence of fraternity members, claimed to have links with the far right. The police formed a cordon between the demonstrators and the fraternity members, preventing physical violence, and eventually arrested 18 protesters.

On 27 November 2023, around 300 people gathered outside the PSOE headquarters in Madrid - Chamberi (Madrid) as part of an ongoing protest against the deal that Spain's PSOE prime minister, Pedro Sanchez, sealed with several pro-Catalan independence parties, which also includes an amnesty pact. A woman was arrested by the police for 'resistance' and 'disobedience to authority' during the demonstration.

On 27 November 2023, in the evening, around 100 far-right activists staged an unauthorized protest action in Lyon (Auvergne-Rhone-Alpes), at the call of the collective Les Remparts, to pay tribute to Thomas, a 16-year-old youth who was stabbed and consequently died after a brawl during a village festival in Crepol on 18 November. They chanted anti-Islam and anti-immigration slogans. Eight people were arrested by the police.

On 29 November 2023, more than 100 students demonstrated at the University of Helsinki premises to show support and solidarity with the people of Palestine and advocating for 'free' Palestine. Later, at the 13 people were detained in connection with the demonstration.

On 29 November 2023, 9 Greenpeace activists held a protest at Puerta del Sol in Madrid - Centro (Madrid) to denounce the climate crisis. The activists were arrested by the police for 'public disorder', 'disobedience', and 'resistance to authority'.

On 29 November 2023, Last Generation activists protested in Vienna - Inner City (Wien 1-Innere Stadt) for more climate action by the government by holding a sit-in protest on the crosswalk at Schutzweg during the green phase for cars. The police intervened and removed the activists from the road.

On 30 November 2023, thousands of people held a protest in Vitoria-Gasteiz (Araba, Pais Vasco) to demand a better public healthcare system. Two participants were detained by the police for 'public disorder' and were released an hour later.

On 30 November 2023, at the call of Last Renovation, climate activists gathered at the Christmas market and sprayed orange paint on the Christmas Tree on Kleber Square in Strasbourg (Grand Est) to call for an end to fossil fuel extraction. Police intervened and took the protesters into custody.

On 30 November 2023, approximately 100 people, including members of the 'International Women's Alliance', the 'Erasmus School of Color', BIJ1-Rotterdam and 'Revolutionaire Eenheid' (Revolutionary Unity), protested on Ahoyweg in Rotterdam (Zuid-Holland) against the international arms fair taking place in Ahoy. Police fired a warning shot during the protest due to suspicion of a weapon among the demonstrators, after which it arrested four participants.

On 1 December 2023, environmental activists from the Emergency Brake movement stood and blocked traffic in Hellerup, Hovedstaden, demanding an end to motorway construction in the country. The police later removed the activists from the site.

On 1 December 2023, 6 Last Generation activists, including some working in craft-related professions, protested in Berlin - Friedrichshain-Kreuzberg (Berlin) by gluing themselves onto and blocking Blucherstrasse close to the Chamber of Crafts to raise awareness about the consequences of the climate crisis on trade, industry and agriculture. The police intervened to detach and remove the activists from the road.

On 2 December 2023, pro-Palestine protesters gathered on Windrush Square in London - Lambeth (England) to call for an immediate ceasefire following Israel's resumed attack on Gaza. The Palestine Solidarity Campaign organized the protest. Police forces arrested one protester.
On 2 December 2023, about 2,000 people participated in a pro-Palestine protest in Berlin - Mitte (Berlin) under the motto 'Stop the genocide in Gaza'. The police arrested some of the participants.

On 3 December 2023, Climaximo activists painted the facade and covered in red ink the staircase of the Museum of Art, Architecture and Technology (MAAT) in Lisbon (Lisboa) as a protest to denounce the climate crisis and against the use of fossil fuels, while specifically criticizing the environmental impact of Energias de Portugal (EDP). Two of the activists were detained by police officers.

On 5 December 2023, six activists from Climaximo painted and glued themselves to a plane at Cascais aerodrome in Cascais (Lisboa) against private jets and to denounce the climate crisis. The police detained all the activists.

On 6 December 2023, around 30 people blocked the entrance to a Danish defense and aerospace company's factory in Lystrup, Midtjylland, to oppose the company's delivery of weapons and jet parts to Israel. Later, as a result of their non-compliance with police instructions, two activists were removed from the venue and detained.

On 6 December 2023, around 10 people demonstrated during a service at the Helsinki Cathedral to show their support and solidarity with the people of Palestine. Later, the police removed the activists from the site.

On 6 December 2023, more than 1000 people, including activists from the Helsinki Without Nazis movement, gathered in Toolontori, Helsinki, in connection with the Finnish Independence Day and the planned '612 March for Freedom'. The police dispersed the demonstration and at least 54 people were detained on suspicion of violating the assembly rules.

On 6 December 2023, far-right activists held a 'Finland Awakening' march in the central Helsinki in connection with Finland's Independence Day. Activists from the Blue and Black Movement (SML) and the Soldiers of Odin took part in the event, among others. At least 14 people were arrested on various charges during the demonstration.

On 6 December 2023, Last Renovation activists staged a protest and blocked traffic on the Concorde Bridge in Paris (Ile-de-France) to alert public opinion on the challenges of climate change. Police forces intervened to remove the activists.

On 6 December 2023, people held a protest in Sant Climent Sescebes (Cataluna) against the construction of an offshore wind farm. Two police officers ran over a protester who fell to the ground without serious injuries. The demonstrators stopped the occupants of the car, who identified themselves as police officers, which was confirmed by the Mossos d'Esquadra and Sumar deputies in the Congress who demanded answers from the Headquarters of the Civil Guard and Mossos officials about this event. The licence plates of the police vehicles weren't valid. In addition, other sources report that it could have been two civil guards in civilian clothes.

On 7 December 2023, during the Athens visit of Turkish President Erdogan for the 5th Greece-Turkey High Level Cooperation Council, and during a ban on all public gatherings, 15-20 Greek Cypriot students protesting against President Erdogan's visit were surrounded by MAT riot police and detained outside the Turkish embassy in Athens - Central Athens. The protesters, organized by the student organization DRASIS-KES, often described as far-right nationalist, had unfolded a banner and chanted slogans. Another 10 Kurdish protesters were also detained in central Athens. They were all released later in the day.

On 7 December 2023, between 50 and 60 people staged a sit-in in the Central Station of Groningen (Groningen) in support of the Palestinian people in the context of the Israel-Hamas war. When 10 police agents asked the crowd to evacuate the station. Most protesters left the station quietly, while some tried to stay and the police arrested 2 people.

On 7 December 2023, pro-Palestine protesters gathered at Central Station in Glasgow (Scotland) to protest against Sir Keir Starmer, the Labour Party leader, as he refused to back the call for a ceasefire in Gaza. As he arrived, protesters were waiting at the station with Palestinian flags and signs. The protest was mainly peaceful but the police forces arrested two protesters.

On 7 December 2023, about 20 supporters of the socialist trade union ACOD disrupted the plenary session of the Brussels Parliament and threw flyers in Brussels - Ville de Bruxelles (Brussels) to ask more money for the public sector. They were escorted outside by the military police without incident.

On 7 December 2023, in a symbolic action, 6 members of Last Generation daubed the exterior of St. Mark's Basilica in Venezia (Veneto) with fire extinguisher fluid, Nesquik, and mud to demand more climate action. Protesters also demanded the allocation of a preventive and permanent fund of 20 billion euros to repay the damage caused by extreme climate events. The police removed the protesters.

On 8 December 2023, at the call of XR, almost 100 activists blocked the access to the Rotterdam (Zuid-Holland) port at the Saarweg and Merwedeweg with Moezelweg intersections, blocking roads, and calling the port 'the most polluting of Europe', while demanding its transition away from fossil fuels. The protest caused traffic disruptions on the A15, and tensions rose when some motorists verbally confronted the protesters, some of whom the police had to physically remove.

On 8 December 2023, members of Last Generation blocked traffic by gluing themselves to a road at the intersection between Kaldenkirchener Street and Schurenweg in Monchengladbach (Nordrhein-Westfalen) to call for climate justice and an end to fossil fuel energy. Police officers intervened to remove the activists from the road.

On 8 December 2023, at the call of OTKM - Offenes Treffen gegen Krieg und Militarisierung Stuttgart (Open meeting against war and militarization Stuttgart), around 80 people gathered for a pro-Palestine demonstration in Stuttgart (Baden-Wurttemberg), condemning the Israeli military campaign in and around Gaza. Five people were arrested, including 3 who were forcibly pulled out of the demonstration by police officers. Police officers also confiscated several placards on the grounds that they read 'denigrating content against German politicians'.

On 9 December 2023, activists from the Nordic Resistance Movement staged a torchlight procession in Vasteras, Vastmanland, to promote the movement's national socialist values and to commemorate their fallen comrades. Later, police personnel temporarily detained several activists who were later released.

On 9 December 2023, No TAV activists gathered at the San Didero (Piemonte) work site and hit the fences to demonstrate against the high-speed Turin-Lyon railway project. The police used tear gas against the demonstrators.

On 9 December 2023, at the call of Alternatiba, General Anti-Fascist Assembly (Assemblee generale anti-fasciste), Le Mans Feminist Collages (Collages feministes Le Mans), Anti-Fascist Collective (Collectif anti-fasciste), and SLT, over 150 people gathered in Le Mans (Pays de la Loire) to demonstrate against fascism and in favor of solidarity. Three people, found to be in possession of drugs and knives, were arrested.

On 9 December 2023, between 400 people (according to the prefecture) and 1,500 (according to the organizers) people, including students, 'Lauragais sans bitume collective' affiliates and other climate activists, staged a protest march from Saint-Germain-des-Pres (Occitanie) to a bitumen factory near Puylaurens (Occitanie), to demonstrate against the environmental impact of the A69 highway project between Toulouse and Castres and the establishment of bitumen plants for the project. Police forces made use of tear gas but were not able to prevent participants from entering the plant.

On 9 December 2023, thousands of pro-Palestine protesters marched from Bank Junction to Parliament Square in London - Westminster (England) to call for a ceasefire between Israel and Hamas. Police forces arrested 13 protesters for offensive placards.

On 9 December 2023, at the call of XR, Last Generation, and Scientist Rebellion, between 150 (according to the police) and 400 (according to organizers) people blocked traffic on the Elsenbrucke (Elsen bridge) in Berlin - Friedrichshain-Kreuzberg (Berlin) against the fossil fuel industry and the expansion of the city highway A100. Police officers intervened to remove some activists who had glued themselves to the road.

On 10 December 2023, around 25 to 30 Extinction Rebellion associated group blocked traffic outside Copenhagen Airport in Kastrup, Hovedstaden, demanding a ban on private jets. The activists were later removed by police personnel, 8 people were arrested.

On 11 December 2023, after the order of a local mayor, law enforcers dispersed the truck drivers blocking border crossing point with Ukraine in Dorohusk. The activists announced a court appeal against the mayor's decision and decided to prolong blockades of other large border crossing points in Hrebenne, Korczowa and Medyka, condemning allegedly unfair conditions for Ukrainian transport and trade companies and demanded stronger state oversight.

On 11 December 2023, at the call of SLT, XR and FFF, several dozen hooded environmental activists gathered and tried to occupy a Lafarge concrete production premise in Saint-Herblain (Pays de la Loire) to denounce the environmental and societal impact of cement and concrete production. Police forces intervened to disperse the activists and arrested 12 people. The event was part of a national protest action against the concrete industry, notably Lafarge-Holcim, named 'Whirlwind Against Concrete' (Tourbillon Contre le Beton) called by SLT and other organizations.

On 11 December 2023, about 60 activists blocked the entrance of the OIP company, the daughter company of Israeli firm Elbit, in Oudenaarde (Vlaanderen) to denounce the supply of weapons to Israel. The police evacuated the protesters and arrested three dozen people.

On 12 December 2023, a large group of university students and pro-Palestine activists gathered outside the university's academic senate in Padua (Veneto) to present an appeal for Peace in Gaza and the West Bank and protested against the massacre of Palestinian civilians. Demonstrators tried to storm the building but were blocked and pushed away by the police.

On 13 December 2023, activists from Sindicat d'Habitatge de Salt held a protest in Salt (Girona, Cataluna) against an eviction in the town. 3 activists were arrested by police officers for resistance and disobedience.

On 13 December 2023, about 80 activists gathered in Bregenz (Vorarlberg) and blocked a local road, demanding immediate climate action. Police officers ordered them to disperse. About 34 activists refused to leave and were removed, and 12 were detained.

On 13 December 2023, in the evening, at the call of KOZP and XR, a group of people gathered to demonstrate and disrupted a municipal council meeting in Naaldwijk (Zuid-Holland). They entered the meeting hall with a banner and manifestos about the country's colonial past and suspected racism, demanding a conversation with the mayor about the presence of Zwarte Pieten at a recent Sinterklaas event. The protesters, refusing to leave, were removed by police, resulting in five arrests.

On 14 December 2023, workers organized by ADEDY, POE-OTA and POEDIN during a protest-strike marched to the ministry of the Interior in Athens - Central Athens demanding substantial wage increases and the hiring of more permanent staff among other issues. Police pushed the protesters back and used tear gas when they demanded to meet a representative of the government.

On 14 December 2023, Climaximo activists held a protest in Lisbon (Lisboa) and blocked access to Avenida Duarte Pacheco to show their rejection of the use of fossil fuels. 11 activists were detained by police officers.

On 14 December 2023, 15 Last Generation activists staged a demonstration by marching slowly and blocking the traffic along Flaminia Street (near Saxa Rubra) in Rome (Lazio) to demand more climate action and the implementation of a fund to repay the damage caused by extreme climate events. The police removed the protesters and cleared the road.

On 14 December 2023, between 50 and 60 students and activists from 'Students for Free Palestine' occupied a lecture hall at Free University in Berlin - Steglitz-Zehlendorf (Berlin) and prevented Jewish students from entering. Police officers intervened and forcibly removed the activists from the lecture hall. During the occupation, there were also physical confrontations between pro-Palestinian activists and university students who tried to stop the occupation by tearing down flyers and posters. A police spokesman said several reports of assault had been made. Two demonstrators were slightly injured and complained of pain.

On 14 December 2023, striking MaxiDi workers and SI COBAS representatives staged a picket and blocked the company gates in Belfiore (Veneto) to demonstrate against their working conditions and demand wage increases. The police intervened and physically removed the demonstrators. After being displaced by the police, demonstrators staged another picket outside a nearby supermarket to protest against MaxiDi and explain their reasons.

On 15 December 2023, around 10 people gathered outside the police station in Calais (Hauts-de-France) to call for the resignation of Minister of the Interior Gerald Darmanin and protest against the new immigration law proposed by the government. The protest took place as Gerald Darmanin was visiting the local police station. Police officers took one protester into custody and pushed other participants back to the streets after some tried to enter the police station.

On 15 December 2023, around noon, around 100 XR activists blocked the Bezuidenhoutseweg in Den Haag (Zuid-Holland). The protest began with a rental van obstructing the road, followed by two activists attempting to retrieve 'oil barrels' from the vehicle before being swiftly arrested by police. The group then marched along the road near the offices of TotalEnergies. The demonstration opposed the construction of the East African Crude Oil Pipeline, managed by TotalEnergies, and aimed to raise awareness about the safety of climate activists in Uganda and Tanzania.

On 15 December 2023, about 15 Last Generation activists blocked streets at various places across Koln (Nordrhein-Westfalen), demanding immediate climate change. Law enforcers quickly removed them and resumed traffic.

On 16 December 2023, 600 protesters, at the call of Code Roode and with the support of XR, blocked access to a distribution hub for the online company Alibaba at the Liege Airport in Bierset (Wallonie), to denounce the firm's expansion on agricultural lands, its environmental impact, and the public subsidies it receives. Police arrested 62 people.

On 16 December 2023, activists from Extinction Rebellion blocked the mineral test drilling facility in the Viiankiaava protected area near Sodankyla, Lappi. The activists demanded that the work be stopped and banned by government because of its potential environmental impact. Later, police personnel removed activists from the venue, three people were arrested.

On 19 December 2023, law enforcers detained all remaining protesters occupying the building of a former printer house in Frankfurt am Main (Hessen). The activists demanded preservation of the building and its use as a cultural center.

On 20 December 2023, 16 Last Generation activists staged an unauthorised demonstration in Via del Corso in Rome - City Center (Lazio) against the Meloni government. Demonstrators also demanded more climate action and the implementation of a restoration fund to counter the damages caused by adverse climatic events. The police physically removed the protesters and freed the street. Demonstrators will be reported and sued for road blockade, aggravated private violence, and interruption of public service.

On 22 December 2023, around 100 students and members of self-managed social centers gathered near the Pantheon in Rome - City Center (Lazio) to demonstrate against the Meloni government. Then, demonstrators took to the streets and tried to reach the Parliament building but were blocked by the police and forcibly dispersed.

On 22 December 2023, 9 'Last Generation' activists from Germany and Austria staged a protest blocking the Inntal Autobahn (A12) at Kufstein Nord (Tirol), emphasizing environmental concerns; five individuals adhered themselves to the roadway. Police officers intervened to remove them.

On 22 December 2023, 140 Extinction Rebellion activists blocked traffic around the entrance of the Shell company headquarters in Den Haag (Zuid-Holland) to denounce its use of fossil subsidies and its lack of communication on the climate crisis. Police forces arrested 60 people.

On 23 December 2023, at the call of S.I. Cobas, workers of Montblanc gathered on Tornabuoni Street in Florence (Toscana) to protest against the precarious conditions, the relocation, and the risk of layoffs. Police officers pushed demonstrators to remove them from the entrance of a Montblanc shop. This event was part of a wider protest in Europe against Montblanc.

On 26 December 2023, animal rights activists staged a protest in Elham (England) during the town's annual Boxing Day hunt parade to denounce the violence of the tradition. Protesters tried to interrupt the hunt but police forces prevented them physically.

On 29 December 2023, at least 4 Last Generation activists staged a demonstration inside the Vittorio Emanuele Gallery in Milano - Municipio 1 (Lombardia) to demand more climate action and the implementation of a restoration fund to help offset the damages caused by adverse climate events. The police removed the activists, four of whom were taken to the police station to be identified.

On 29 December 2023, at the call of the association 'Land sichert Versorgung (LSV NRW)' (Land Secures Supply), up to 1,200 vehicles (according to the organizers) or 850 (according to the police), including farmers and freight forwarders, as well as members of 'Westfalisch Lippischer Landwirtschaftsverband' (Westphalian-Lippe Agricultural Association), medium-sized businesses and haulage companies, participated in a protest in Siegen (Siegen-Wittgenstein, Nordrhein-Westfalen) against the federal government's decision to end tax concessions for agricultural diesel and other vehicles. One tractor driver tried to break through a barrier, slightly injuring a police officer, and was taken to the police station. The event was peaceful and a convoy from Netphen joined the protest.

On 30 December 2023, an unknown number of XR activists blocked the A10 highway close to the former headquarters of ING in Amsterdam (Noord-Holland) to call on the financial company to stop financing fossil fuel projects. Police made 400 arrests among the demonstrators.

On 31 December 2023, at the call of the Voices from Within (Vozes de Dentro) collective, around 15 people protested in front of the prison in Lisbon (Lisboa) against the country's penitentiary system. Pro-Palestinian groups joined the protest. Police Rapid Intervention Team (EIR) officers arrested one of the organizers and physically assaulted a Fumaca journalist who filmed the arrest, with the journalist claiming that he was beaten twice and his leg was scarred as a result.

On 3 January 2024, activists from the Emergency Break movement blocked a motorway exit in Kongens Lyngby, Hovedstaden, calling an end to motorway construction in the country. Later, police personnel removed activists from the scene.

On 4 January 2024, Palestinian community members continued their demonstration at a protest camp outside of the Parliament of Norway in Oslo to show support and solidarity with Palestine in response to the Israeli offensive in Gaza. Police later dispersed the demonstrators and dismantled the camp. The camp has been in place since 11 November, 2023.

On 4 January 2024, hundreds of farmers blocked a ferry in Schluttsiel near Flensburg (Kreis Nordfriesland, Schleswig-Holstein) to stage a protest before Minister Robert Habeck's arrival, aiming to engage in dialogue regarding subsidy cuts. They required that the Minister speak to all protesters. The demonstration escalated as around 30 people tried to push their way through the ferry before its departure, leading to physical police intervention.

On 6 January 2024, around 30 Boycott, Divestment and Sanctions (BDS) activists, including SUD affiliates, gathered inside a Carrefour supermarket in Lattes (Occitanie) to protest against Carrefour's commercial relations with Israeli companies operating in the Palestinian Territories. After an altercation with a security guard, an activist was taken into police custody on the grounds of 'participation in a group to commit violence and damage'.

On 6 January 2024, dozens of protesters disturbed the event celebrating the beginning of the Belgian presidency of the European Union in Mechelen (Vlaanderen), by chanting pro-Palestinian slogans and waving Palestinian flags. Official participants tried to calm the demonstrators. While most activists left the event, police eventually proceeded to the arrest of 10 of them who had decided to stay.

On 8 January 2024, around 10 activists from the Emergency Break movement stood and blocked a major city road in Copenhagen calling an end to motorway construction in the country. Later, police personnel removed activists from the scene.

On 8 January 2024, around 2,000 farmers staged a protest with their tractors in front of the Europa-Park stadium and on highway entrances in Freiburg im Breisgau (Baden-Wurttemberg), as part of a nationwide farmers' demonstration movement against the German government's agricultural policies, notably the planned budget cuts to Agrardiesel and vehicle tax exemptions; the police intervened to clear blockades on highway entrances.

On 9 January 2024, farmers driving almost 30 tractors staged a protest in Emden (Niedersachsen) by blocking the entrance to the Volkswagen Factory; the police intervened to disperse the gathering. The event was part of a nationwide demonstration movement called by farmers to denounce the government's plan to cut agricultural sector subsidies.

On 10 January 2024, 16 Last Generation activists protested at Innsbrucker Platz in Berlin - Tempelhof-Schoneberg (Berlin) to raise awareness about the climate crisis and to denounce 'double standards' in the coverage of their protests and their climate demands, and those of the farmers, many of whom were protesting against planned cuts to agricultural subsidies at the time of reporting. The police intervened and carried the protesters off the street.

On 10 January 2024, 8 Last Generation activists protested in Bremen (Bremen) with a sit-in and by gluing themselves and some toy tractors onto the road. They protested against the climate policies of the federal government, for more social equality in the climate crisis and to denounce 'double standards' in the coverage of their protests and their climate demands, and those of the farmers, many of whom were protesting against planned cuts to agricultural subsidies at the time of reporting. Police forces intervened, removed the protesters from the road and brought them to the police station.

On 10 January 2024, 6 members of Last Generation blocked the lanes in both directions on a main street in Leipzig (Sachsen) to demand more climate protection. Police officers intervened by physically carrying the protesters off the road.

On 10 January 2024, Last Generation activists protested in Stuttgart (Baden-Wurttemberg) with a slow march from Heilbronner Strasse to the main train station and a sit-in to denounce 'double standards' in the coverage of their protests and their climate demands, and those of the farmers, many of whom were protesting against planned cuts to agricultural subsidies at the time of reporting. The police intervened, dissolved the protest and carried some of the protesters off the road.

On 10 January 2024, three Last Generation activists, including a BUND affiliate, blocked Bergheimer Street with a toy tractor and a wooden tractor in Heidelberg (Baden-Wurttemberg) to denounce 'double standards' in the coverage of their protests and their climate demands, and those of the farmers, many of whom were protesting against planned cuts to agricultural subsidies at the time of reporting. The activists were dragged away from the street by the police.

On 10 January 2024, farmers with several tractors demonstrated by driving up to the Congress Hall in Boblingen (Baden-Wurttemberg) against the planned abolition of diesel subsidies and the tax exemption for agricultural and forestry machinery. One demonstrator drove her tractor in the direction of a police officer and pushed him at walking speed for a few meters. The 20-year-old tractor driver only stopped after a patrol car was positioned in front of her. She resisted her subsequent arrest and faced criminal charges for dangerous interference with road traffic, coercion, and resisting law enforcement officers at the time of reporting.

On 11 January 2024, a group of farmers protested in Silute, Lithuania, calling against unfavourable conditions for farming in the country. A few protesters attempted to enter the city with heavy machinery. Police intervened in the protest and a few of the protesters were detained.
On 11 January 2024, a group of people protested against abortion near a maternity ward in Olesnica. Police seized pickets depicting dead foetuses and ordered the activists present to disperse.

On 11 January 2024, hundreds of people protested in Den Haag (Zuid-Holland) as the International Court of Justice started examining the request of South Africa to order Israel to stop the attacks in Gaza, calling it a genocide. One group, led by Christians for Israel, marched in the direction of the Court while a pro-Palestinian group, including Free Palestine activists, was there. A hundred meters away, between 13 Square and the ICJ headquarters, there was another pro-Israeli demonstration. The police were present and kept the two groups apart, while arresting one man (side not specified) who had motioned a flagpole in the direction of a police horse and led its rider to fall down and suffer minor injuries.

On 11 January 2024, farmers gathered in Valluhn (Mecklenburg-Vorpommern) to demonstrate. Police officers intervened to break up the demonstration. The event was part of a nationwide farmers' demonstration movement against planned agricultural subsidy cuts.

On 12 January 2024, around 8 activists from the Emergency Break movement stood and blocked a major city road in Osterbro, Copenhagen, calling an end to motorway construction in the country. Later, police personnel removed activists from the scene, several people were arrested.

On 13 January 2024, thousands of pro-Palestine protesters, including Palestinians living in the UK, marched from Queen Victoria Street to Parliament Square for a rally in London - Westminster (England) to demand an immediate ceasefire in Gaza and to show solidarity with Palestine. The protest was part of a global day of action organized by PSC. Labour MP Jeremy Corbyn and the president of Sinn Fein, Mary Lou McDonald, also addressed the crowd. The protest was mostly peaceful but police forces arrested nine protesters.

On 13 January 2024, several groups of Extinction Rebellion activists marched through Nijmegen (Gelderland) and blocked traffic to protest against the construction of a new energy plant in Nijmegen-West, citing environmental concerns. Police asked the protesters to move and arrested 92 people.

On 14 January 2024, an unknown number of protesters disturbed the New Year's party of the city of Gent in Gent (Vlaanderen) to denounce the situation in Gaza amid the Israel-Hamas War. The protesters started chanting when the mayor (Open Flemish Liberals and Democrats) wanted to start his speech. Police intervened and arrested 9 people.

On 15 January 2024, as part of an ongoing strike, GiTre workers and SI COBAS representatives staged a picket outside their workplace in Bellusco (Lombardia) to protest against their working conditions and demand they be granted paid sick leaves. During the demonstration, workers tried to prevent trucks from entering the factory's perimeter. Police intervened and disbanded the picket. Some protesters were then taken to the police station for questioning.

On 15 January 2024, more than 1,200 people, including environmental activists from FFF and Greenpeace, participated in an environmental protest at the protest camp 'Tumpeltown' in Hannover (Region Hannover, Niedersachsen) called for by 'Leinemasch stays' (Leinemasch bleibt) against the expansion of the southern expressway and the planned tree felling work. Some of the protesters occupied trees, tried to protect the tree houses with a moat, barbed wire and barricades and tied themselves to the trees with ropes. The police cleared treehouses and removed several activists with cranes.

On 16 January 2024, undocumented migrant workers employed by Emmaus gathered outside the town hall in Lille (Hauts-de-France) to demand the regularization of their immigration status. Police intervened to put an end to the action, pushing the protesters back with shields and clubs.

On 17 January 2024, several thousand people protested in Baymak (Baymakskiy, Ufa) in support of an ecoactivist who was sentenced to 4 years in a penal colony on that day. The police attempted to disperse the demonstrators with tear gas and stun grenades and beat them up with bats, with at least 22 people requiring medical attention afterwards. At least 17 people were arrested.

On 18 January 2024, people demonstrated blocked a Danish defense and aerospace company's factory in Soborg, Hovedstaden, to oppose the company's delivery of weapons and jet parts to Israel. Later, police personnel removed activists from the venue, four people were arrested.

On 18 January 2024, about 60 pro-Palestine protesters from the Palestine Action group gathered outside Aztec West Business Park in Bristol (England) against the private Israeli-owned defense company, Elbit System, and their role in arming Israel amid the Israel-Hamas War. Protesters expressed solidarity with Palestine and carried a banner that read 'Stop arming genocide'. Police forces arrested four people.

On 18 January 2024, environmental activists, including Extinction Rebellion members, blocked the entrance to an oil port in Gothenburg (Goteborg) to demand action against climate change and to oppose the use of fossil fuels. Several activists were later removed by police.

On 19 January 2024, 1,500 people protested in Ufa (Republic of Bashkortostan) in support of activist Fail' Alsynov who was sentenced to 4 years in prison for is ecoactivism the day before. Around 25 people were arrested.

On 19 January 2024, around 1,500 people protested in Ufa (Republic of Bashkortostan) demanding the release of a Bashkir ecoactivist who was recently sentenced to four years in prison. At least 10 people were arrested at the rally.

On 19 January 2024, about 100 activists, including members of far-left groupings, gathered for a march through Ljubljana, protesting against what they see as extensive gentrification and commercialization of the city center and calling for transforming the buildings to affordable housing instead. Along the way, they damaged the municipal equipment and decoration by spraying graffiti and paint. One of them was detained; a brief skirmish with police forces followed, as his peers tried to prevent his arrest.

On 19 January 2024, people blocked a Danish defense and aerospace company's factory in Ballerup, Hovedstaden, to oppose the company's delivery of weapons and jet parts to Israel. Later, police personnel removed activists from the protest site, several people were detained.

On 20 January 2024, at the call of Solidarity Network against the Occupation of Palestine (Red Solidaria contra la Ocupacion de Palestina, RESCOP), hundreds of people, including the Palestinian Community, BDS, and Al Yudur Palestine Youth (Movimiento de la juventud palestina Al Yudur), as well as three Commitment councilors, protested in Alicante (Valencia) in solidarity with the Palestinian people and against Israeli violence amid the ongoing war in the Gaza Strip. Police arrested two United Left councilors.

On 20 January 2024, about 15 Extinction Rebellion activists held a sit-in in the departure hall of the Maastricht Aachen Airport in Beek (Limburg) to ask for a good climate plan around the airport, a reduction of subsidies for the airline industry and a ban on private jets. Three activists tried to block access to stairs to an airplane and the police arrested them.

On 21 January 2024, at the call of March for Life (Marche pour la vie), between 6,000 (according to the police) and 15,000 (organizers) people, including conservative Catholic believers, marched from Saint-Sulpice Square to Denfert-Rochereau Square in Paris (Ile-de-France) to protest against the government's plan to include the right to abortion in the Constitution and its planned reform of euthanasia. A few Femen activists staged a counter-protest to defend the right to abortion, before being physically carried away from the scene by police officers.

On 23 January 2024, people demonstrated outside of the Iranian Embassy in Lidingo, Stockholmfor unspecified reasons. Police personnel were present to ensure the security of the event. A group of around five demonstrators entered the premises of the embassy and were later arrested by the police. The rest of the group was allowed to continue the protest.

On 23 January 2024, a Turkish Cypriot conscientious objector staged a protest outside parliament in Northern Nicosia after he was fined 800 Turkish Liras (24 euros) for not completing his military service. He refused to pay the fine and was arrested as he was protesting with his supporters, including 2 MPs of CTP.

On 24 January 2024, in the morning, a large crowd rallied outside the home of a retired journalist in Zografou, Athens - Central Athens, to protest her eviction after she lost her primary home in a foreclosure and the new owner filed a lawsuit against her. Police broke down the door and arrested her. MAT riot police used tear gas on the crowd, following verbal confrontations. The solidarity protesters then gathered outside Zografou police station shouting 'No home in the hands of a banker'. Police used tear gas and pushed the crowd that had formed a cordon out of the way, as they were transporting the retired journalist to the Evelpidon court. The Association of Photojournalists of Greece reported that police hit on the head a photo reporter covering the event at the police station. The crowd then moved to the court complex shouting slogans of encouragement as the retired journalist was released after a trial date was set, while labor unions organized a rally that attracted hundreds outside her home in the evening.

On 24 January 2024, around 60 people protested in Yakutsk (Republic of Sakha) demanding the prosecution of a man of Tajik origin who is allegedly responsible for killing a local. Several protesters were arrested.

On 24 January 2024, according to the breakaway authorities, around 50,000 people, joined by the leader of Transnistria and the first so-called president of Transnistria, protested in Tiraspol against the new uniform customs duty for goods exported from the Transnistrian region. The Transnistrian MGB arrested a Moldovan journalist and a cameraman, and later released them.

On 25 January 2024, people protested in front of the Moscow city court in Moscow - Eastern (Vostochnyy, Moscow) in support of Igor Strelkov/Girkin who on that day was sentenced to 4 years in prison for his criticism of the Russian Military of Defence's 'ineffectiveness' in the war against Ukraine. Strelkov is a nationalist who was instrumental in establishing Russian control over Donetsk in 2014 and has been deemed responsible for the destruction of Malaysia Airlines Flight 17 by Dutch courts. At least 3 of the protesters were arrested.

On 26 January 2024, farmers from Epanomi and nearby areas, who were demonstrating over high production, energy and fertilizer costs, among other issues, attempted to block the road with their tractors at the airport junction in the outskirts of Thessaloniki, but MAT riot police prevented them from moving forward, blocking the road with police vans.

On 27 January 2024, people protested in Barnaul (Altai) against the increase of public transit prices in the region. The rally was organized by a local youth KPRF branch, and a KPRF deputy who was in attendance was arrested.

On 28 January 2024, three activists from Extinction Rebellion attempted to disrupt operations at Aalborg Airport in Aalborg, Nordjylland, demanding a ban on private jets. Police later removed and arrested the activists.

On 28 January 2024, Extinction Rebellion activists blocked traffic near the Copenhagen Airport in Kastrup, Hovedstaden, demanding to ban private jets. Later, police personnel removed activists, several people were temporarily detained.

On 29 January 2024, people protested in Granada (Andalucia) in support of three SAT union members who faced trial at the time of reporting. Police arrested the national spokesperson of the Andalusian Workers Union (Sindicato Andaluz de Trabajadores, SAT) during the rally.

On 29 January 2024, around 9 activists from the Emergency Break movement stood and blocked a major city road in Osterbro, Copenhagen, to call for an end to motorway construction in the country and to denounce the new infrastructure development plan proposed by the Ministry of Transport. Police later removed the activists from the scene and several people were detained.

On 1 February 2024, students blocked access to the Voltaire school (Paris) in solidarity with their teachers. Police intervened to put an end to the action. The event was part of a national strike and protest movement called by CGT, FO, SUD Education, UNSA Education, SNUIPP-FSU, SNALC, and SGEN CFDT to demand higher wages and better working conditions at public schools after Minister of Education Amelie Oudea-Castera issued comments they deemed disrespectful to teachers.

On 1 February 2024, students blocked access to the Saint-Juste school in Lyon (Auvergne-Rhone-Alpes) in solidarity with teachers. Police intervened to disperse the protest. The event was part of a national strike and protest movement called by CGT, FO, SUD Education, UNSA Education, SNUIPP-FSU, SNALC, and SGEN CFDT to demand higher wages and better working conditions at public schools after Minister of Education Amelie Oudea-Castera issued comments they deemed disrespectful to teachers.

On 1 February 2024, about a hundred people protested at the Central Station in Den Haag (Zuid-Holland) to show solidarity with the Palestinian people in the context of the Israel-Hamas war. The action was unannounced and the police disbanded the demonstration by order of the mayor. One person was arrested for insulting a police officer.

On 2 February 2024, around 10 to 15 activists from the Emergency Break movement sat and blocked traffic in Gentofte, Hovedstaden, to call for an end to motorway construction in the country. Later, as a result of their non-compliance with police orders, four activists were removed from the venue and arrested.

On 2 February 2024, farmers protested in Wilhelmsburg in Hamburg - Hamburg-Mitte (Hamburg) and tried blocking the harbor. The police intervened and stopped the traffic blockades. The event was part of a nationwide farmers' demonstration movement against several agricultural policies of the federal government, including planned agricultural subsidy cuts.

On 3 February 2024, tens of women protested in Moscow - Central (Tsentralnyy, Moscow) demanding that the government bring back their male relatives who were mobilized to fight in the war in Ukraine. The police detained all male journalists present at the event - 23 people - and one of the protesters who held up a sign with the demand.

On 3 February 2024, antifascist collectives rallied in Kolonaki and marched towards Rigillis square in Athens - Central Athens to counter-demonstrate against an event planned by Golden Dawn to mark the anniversary of the 1996 Imia crisis, when Greece and Turkey almost went to war, despite a police ban of all public rallies in the area, citing 'a risk to public safety'. Police lined up blocking access to Rigillis square. 10 antifascists, who attempted to rally at the square, were detained.

On 3 February 2024, between 10,000 and 20,000 pro-Palestine supporters gathered at Portland Place and headed towards Whitehall in London - Westminster (England) with banners calling for an immediate ceasefire in Gaza, a free Palestine and the boycott of Israel. The event was organized by the Palestine Solidarity Campaign (PSC). Two women were arrested during the event for chanting slogans 'inciting racial hatred' and on suspicion of setting off a smoke bomb and a flare. Labor Party member and MP Jeremy Corbyn and trade unionist Mick Lynch (RMT) addressed attendees during the event.

On 5 February 2024, between 1,000 and 1,500 people, including NP, IF, and IFP members, gathered at Parnell Square and headed to the Custom House Quay in Dublin (Dublin) for an anti-immigrant rally, carrying banners with slogans including 'Ireland first' and 'Irish Lives Matter'. The event was mostly peaceful but eleven people were arrested for attempting to cause traffic disruption. On the same day, between 200 and 300 counter-protesters gathered along O'Connell Street in Dublin (Dublin) to push back against the anti-immigrant rhetoric and racism. The counter-protest was organized by United Against Racism (UAR) and Garda police officers kept both groups of attendees separated.

On 5 February 2024, police prevented some 400 protesters, including students, from occupying the Democritus University of Thrace in Komotini, as they attempted to prevent other students, as well as university staff, from entering the campus law department during exams. They were opposing the government's plans to establish private universities. The operation followed a request for assistance from university authorities. No clashes were reported. There were 18 detentions. 6 were released later in the day. Later, there were claims that police used unnecessary force, throwing students to the ground and hitting them.

On 6 February 2024, people demonstrated at a school in Oslo during a visit by Norwegian Prime Minister Jonas Gahr Store. The activists expressed their dissatisfaction with the government's political position on the ongoing Gaza conflict and called for action to secure a lasting ceasefire in the conflict between Hamas and Israel. One person attempted to confront the Prime Minister and was removed by police security service.

On 6 February 2024, around 40 farmers with tractors protested in Zamora (Castilla y Leon), entering the city center with their tractors and marching to the regional government building. The event was part of a nationwide farmers' demonstration movement, called by UdU on that day, against the ratification of the EU's free-trade agreements until partner third countries comply with the EU's agricultural standards, and in favor of fair production prices for Spanish farmers, relief measures to offset the consequences of droughts and the import of agricultural products from Ukraine, as well as better working and social conditions in their sector. Police arrested a man for attacking a police officer.

On 6 February 2024, students demonstrated outside the parliament in Reykjavik to call for a permanent ceasefire in Gaza and to show support and solidarity with the people of Palestine. Two students were subsequently arrested for throwing eggs and obstructing police.

On 7 February 2024, activists gathered for a rally in Prague, protesting against what they see as unjust and politicized sentences for their colleagues; these received sentences for spreading disinformation and other related crimes. At least one was detained.

On 7 February 2024, people stood and blocked entrance to the annual arms industry conference venue in Copenhagen to call for an end to arms sales to Israel. Later, as a result of their non-compliance with police orders, activists were removed from the venue.

On 7 February 2024, ahead of the mass rally against the government's draft bill allowing the establishment of private universities, a small group of students unfurled a banner at Syntagma square, Athens - Central Athens, before they were encircled by DRASI police officers. Police detained 8 students.

On 7 February 2024, farmers with around 15 tractors participated in a motorcade from Calvarrasa to Salamanca (Castilla y Leon). The Civil Guard intercepted and disbanded the motorcade. The event was part of a nationwide farmers' demonstration movement called by UdU against the ratification of the EU's free-trade agreements until partner third countries comply with the EU's agricultural standards, and in favor of fair production prices for Spanish farmers, relief measures to offset the consequences of droughts and of the import of agricultural products from Ukraine, as well as better working and social conditions in their sector.

On 8 February 2024, 15 to 20 leftist students from Panteion University managed to reach Maximos Mansion, the PM's office in Athens - Central Athens, but when they attempted to stage a protest, unfurling a banner against the government's draft bill allowing the establishment of private universities, riot police pushed them towards the opposite sidewalk. Following a brief confrontation, police dispersed the students from the area. 1 of the protesters was showing his injured hand to the camera.

On 8 February 2024, about 200 farmers with tractors participated in a motorcade in Burgos (Castilla y Leon), blocking the AP-1 near Rubena. The Civil Guard intervened to break up the protesters and arrested two people. The event was part of a nationwide farmers' demonstration movement called by UdU against the ratification of the EU's free-trade agreements until partner third countries comply with the EU's agricultural standards, and in favor of fair production prices for Spanish farmers, relief measures to offset the consequences of droughts and of the import of agricultural products from Ukraine, as well as better working and social conditions in their sector.

On 8 February 2024, between 1,000 and 2,000 XR activists blocked the A12 road in Den Haag (Zuid-Holland), protesting against the government's support to the fossil industry. The police arrested 1.000 people.

On 9 February 2024, Polish farmers arrived with their machines from various directions to Bydgoszcz, protesting against what they see as a low state support to the national agriculture, including excessive bureaucracy and environmental restrictions, and against ongoing import of grains from Ukraine. They also set tires on fire in the vicinity of the municipal building. Following a short skirmish, law enforcers used tear gas to prevent them from entering the municipality.

On 9 February 2024, police detained 30 members of Rouvikonas, who were protesting outside the oncology hospital Agios Savvas in Athens - Central Athens. They had unfurled a banner and scattered fliers against the devaluation of the National Health System.

On 9 February 2024, 500 farmers with around 200 tractors participated in a motorcade in Merida (Extremadura), blocking the A-5 and the A-66. Civil Guard intervened and launched tear gas to evict demonstrators. The event was part of a nationwide farmers' demonstration movement called by UdU against the ratification of the EU's free-trade agreements until partner third countries comply with the EU's agricultural standards, and in favor of fair production prices for Spanish farmers, relief measures to offset the consequences of droughts and of the import of agricultural products from Ukraine, as well as better working and social conditions in their sector.

On 9 February 2024, activists from the Emergency Break movement sat and blocked traffic in Copenhagen to call for an end to motorway construction in the country. Later, as a result of their non-compliance with police orders, activists were removed from the venue and temporarily detained.

On 9 February 2024, activists from the Emergency Break movement sat and blocked traffic in Gentofte, Hovedstaden, to call for an end to motorway construction in the country. Later, as a result of their non-compliance with police orders, activists were removed from the venue and temporarily detained.
