On 10 February 2024, MAT and YMET police hurled a stun grenade at protesters and journalists to break a protest in solidarity with Palestinians at Syntagma square in Athens - Central Athens. They also smashed the front window of McDonald's as they were trying to disperse the protesters. A MAT police officer hit a seller of 'Shedia', the social project magazine supporting homeless people, with his shield. There were 2 detentions.

On 10 February 2024, over 10 women protested in Moscow - Central (Tsentralnyy, Moscow) demanding that the government bring back their male relatives who were mobilized to fight in the war in Ukraine. The police detained journalists present at the event.

On 10 February 2024, people protested in Yekaterinburg (Ekaterinburg, Sverdlovsk) in support of the 'A Path Home' (Put' Domoi) movement of wives of soldiers that demands that the government bring back their soldiers mobilized to fight in the war in Ukraine. The police arrested 5 protesters, including two activists of the youth branch of the Yabloko party.

On 12 February 2024, around 20 farmers with their tractors and a variety of pick-up trucks held a protest outside the rural affairs minister's office in Wrexham (Wales) against the Welsh Government's plans for a new Sustainable Farming Scheme (SFS) to support the country's producers. The protest was peaceful however in an isolated event one man was arrested.

On 12 February 2024, at the call of NT and several unspecified unions, several dozen protesters gathered outside the Prefecture in Rennes (Bretagne) to protest against the visiter of the ministers of the Interior and of Public Affairs. The police removed some protesters from the area.

On 13 February 2024, activists from Extinction Rebellion blocked the venue of the Oslo Energy Forum in Holmenkollen, Oslo, and called on the government to stop issuing new state exploration licenses. The activists also called for a halt to investment in fossil fuel companies. As a result of their non-compliance with police orders, several activists were later removed from the venue and temporarily detained.

On 13 February 2024, at the call of Napoli Network for Palestine (Rete Napoli per la Palestina), around 200 activists staged a protest in front of the national public broadcasting company RAI in Napoli (Campania) against the statement written by the CEO, and read on live TV to distance the channel from the rapper Ghali's statement 'stop the genocide' in support of Palestinians on Sanremo music festival stage. The statement was written after the Israeli ambassador accused the channel of being biased. The police intervened and some people, including one S.I. COBAS activist were injured. This event is part of a nationwide demonstration against the narratives used by national media to explain the conflict in the Middle East.

On 14 February 2024, a group of activists protested during a parliamentary session in Stockholm to call for an end to arms sales to Israel and to oppose the ongoing Israeli offensive in Gaza and Rafah. The activists were later removed by police, seven people were arrested.

On 14 February 2024, about 250 farmers participated in a protest in Aranda del Duero (Castilla y Leon), blocking the A-1 road. Civil guard officers tried to physically remove the protesters. One of them was arrested after confronting them. Nearly 100 farmers then protested near the police station of Aranda del Duero to call for the liberation of the arrested farmer. The event was part of a nationwide farmers' demonstration movement against the ratification of the EU's free-trade agreements until partner third countries comply with the EU's agricultural standards, and in favor of fair production prices for Spanish farmers, relief measures to offset the consequences of droughts and of the import of agricultural products from Ukraine, as well as better working and social conditions in their sector.

On 14 February 2024, pro-Palestine activists from Palestine Action blocked the entrance of the Bristol HQ of Israeli weapons firm, Elbit Systems in Bristol (England) to demand an end to British complicity in the Israeli occupation and war crimes in Palestine. Police forces attended the protest and arrested three activists.

On 14 February 2024, people attempted to block the road for a motorcade carrying he United States Special Presidential Envoy for Climate John Kerry, to oppose Kerry's participation in the Oslo Energy Forum, accusing the organisers of greenwashing. The activists were dispersed and arrested by police.

On 14 February 2024, in the evening, about 230 pro-Palestine demonstrators participated in a sit-in in Berlin - Friedrichshain-Kreuzberg (Berlin) in front of the Springer House where a conference between German and Israeli politicians on the Middle East conflict and growing anti-Semitism took place. The demonstrators gathered under the motto 'Free Palestine'. The police ordered the demonstration to be moved to another nearby location to keep escape routes clear, carried some demonstrators away and provisionally arrested 12 participants. In the early evening, about 50 people participated in a flashmob under the motto 'Free Palestine' whereby pro-Palestinian and anti-police slogans where shouted, causing the arrest of another 10 demonstrators. During the demonstration 3 police forces were injured.

On 14 February 2024, about 90 to 100 people, including farmers, with 30 to 35 vehicles, participated in a protest in Schorndorf (Baden-Wurttemberg) against the political Ash Wednesday of the Greens. The protesters hindered the departure of Federal Green Party Chairwoman Ricarda Lang and insulted her, the police intervened and stopped the protesters. The event was part of a nationwide demonstration movement against the federal government and its economic and agricultural policies.

On 14 February 2024, around 200 people staged a protest in front of the national public broadcasting company RAI in Napoli (Campania) to protest against the document written by the CEO, Roberto Sergio, and read by Mara Venier during the program 'Domenica In' after the stance taken by the Israeli ambassador for the 'stop the genocide' statement made by the rapper Ghali on Sanremo music festival stage. The police intervened and ten people were injured. This event is part of a nationwide demonstration against the narratives used by national media to explain the conflict in the Middle East.

On 15 February 2024, at the call of Young Palestinians (Giovani Palestinesi), people gathered under the national public broadcasting company RAI headquarters in Bologna (Emilia-Romagna). Some protesters threw objects to the police who reacted with truncheons and shield blows. No reported injuries. This event is part of a nationwide demonstration against the narratives used by national media to explain the conflict in the Middle East.

On 15 February 2024, several SOR-affiliated persons from Gagauzia, led by the regional governor, protested outside the Constitutional Court in Chisinau - Buiucani, requesting that the court reject the law forcing the autonomous unit to refund VAT. Following some light scuffles with a group of counter-protesters, which, according to a SOR MP, contained PAS members, police had to intervene forcefully and separate the groups.

On 15 February 2024, 40 XR activists blocked the entrance of the Ministry of Finance in Den Haag (Zuid-Holland) to protest against the presented fossil fuel subsidy phase-out plans that will be passed to the next administration. Police arrested 17 people.

On 15 February 2024, 3 Last Generation activists protested in the Federal Ministry of Transport in Berlin - Mitte (Berlin) against the politics of Minister of Transport Volker Wissing (FDP) and covered a wall with twelve posters. The protesters were temporarily arrested by the police.

On 15 February 2024, overnight, four activists from the environmental organization Robin Wood occupied an oak tree on the university campus in Vaihingen in Stuttgart (Baden-Wurttemberg) to protest against the clearing of a forest for a new university building. Special police forces intervened with the aid of the fire department to remove the protesters.

On 16 February 2024, around 50,000 people protested in Heroes' Square in Budapest - XIV, condemning the pardoning of a paedophile accomplice and condemning the actions of the Fidesz government, demanding its resignation. Budapest's mayor of Parbeszed, a Parbeszed MP, the former SZDSZ mayor of Budapest, MSZP MPs, DK MPs and one MEP, a Jobbik MP, two Momentum MPs, as well as two independent MPs, participated in the rally. A group of protesters scuffled with the police outside the Fidesz headquarters. Police arrested two people and identified a woman for using pyrotechnical means during a protest. A source estimated that 150 to 200 thousand people participated in the rally.

On 16 February 2024, about 100 asylum seekers and activists occupied a sports hall of the ULB - Free University of Brussels in Brussels - Ixelles (Brussels) to demonstrate. The action was organized by the collective Stop the Reception Crisis (Stop de Opvangcrisis). It was halted by a police intervention in the evening, at the request of the University.

On 17 February 2024, around 200 members of the Eritrean community gathered outside a building where people were having dinner in Villars-sur-Glane (Fribourg) to demonstrate against the event, which they claimed was organized by the Eritrean government. Police used tear gas to keep the demonstrators from entering the building and dispersed the crowd.

On 17 February 2024, between 200,000 and 250,000 pro-Palestine protesters held a march in the city center and gathered on Park Lane in London - Westminster (England) to call for a ceasefire in Gaza. Palestinian ambassador to the UK Husam Zomlot, and Independent MP Jeremy Corbyn also addressed the crowd. The protest was mostly peaceful but police forces arrested 12 people. The protest was organized by PSC.

On 19 February 2024, at the call of amongst others Migrantifa, more than 3,000 people, including Palestine supporters, participated in a demonstration in Berlin - Neukolln (Berlin) to commemorate the victims of the racist attack in Hanau 4 years ago. The demonstration was organized under the motto '4 years Hanau - The consequence is resistance' to denounce the handling of the attack and demand better investigation of right-wing violence. Some demonstrators climbed onto a house roof and set off pots of fog, others demanded an end of what they consider a genocide in Palestine and used anti-Israel slogans. The atmosphere became increasingly heated and the police arrested at least one demonstrator.

On 20 February 2024, farmers blocked a highway exit near Gorzyczki, protesting against ongoing imports of grains from Ukraine and also against what they see as an excessive bureaucracy related to the so-called Green Deal of the European Union. One farmer was detained over a poster calling for Russian intervention against the Polish government and the EU administration.

On 20 February 2024, people protested and blocked construction workers in Moscow - Western (Zapadnyy, Moscow) against the illegal felling of trees in the local park to make way for construction. The police detained 4 protesters.

On 21 February 2024, people, called by the Housing Union of El Raval (Sindicat d'Habitatge del Raval) and other housing rights associations, held a protest in Barcelona - Ciutat Vella (Cataluna), with the intention of protesting against and preventing a house eviction. The protesters blocked the building's entrance, prompting the intervention of the police to physically remove them.

On 21 February 2024, several dozen activists disturbed the plenary session of the Flemish Parliament in Brussels - Ville de Bruxelles (Brussels) to remind the MPs of their responsibility regarding Gaza and the Palestinian population, and calling them not to support a 'genocide'. They asked for the boycott of Israel and of the company ZIM, an Israeli shipping company that ships arms through the port of Antwerp. Some activists were detained by the police and the session was temporarily suspended.

On 23 February 2024, about 8 activists affiliated with the Kaputin group gathered in Prague for a protest happening and painted Ukrainian flags in front of apartments inhabited by Russians. Verbal skirmishes with the bystanding residents took place, when Russians called the activists 'Nazis'. Law enforcers briefly detained 8 people for and transferred them to a station to provide an explanation.

On 23 February 2024, several dozen farmers supported by the Solidarity Union gathered for a rally in Limanowa, protesting against ongoing imports of grains from Ukraine and also against what they see as an excessive bureaucracy related to the so-called Green Deal of the European Union. One activist was detained for displaying a poster depicting the PM with a linkage to holocaust.

On 23 February 2024, as part of a national demonstration in support of Palestine and to call for an end to the killing of civilians in Gaza by the Israeli military, more than 100 people, including students, representatives of USB, and members of Changing Course, demonstrated outside the Normale Superior School in Pisa (Toscana). The police charged and pushed back the demonstrators who tried to enter Cavalieri Square. Some students, including minors, were injured, and others were forcibly held back or pinned to the ground. Five demonstrators were transported to the hospital.

On 24 February 2024, women protested in Moscow - Central (Tsentralnyy, Moscow) demanding that the government bring back their male relatives who were mobilized to fight in the war in Ukraine. The police detained journalists present at the event.

On 24 February 2024, hundreds of XR activists blocked the A10 highway in Amsterdam (Noord-Holland) to denounce fossil fuels investments by the bank ING. The demonstration was banned by the mayor who indicated another road to demonstrate. Police put an end to the demonstration, took away 300 people by bus, and arrested 31 activists.

On 24 February 2024, several dozen Attac activists staged a protest action in Paris (Hauts-de-France) to demand fiscal, social and ecological justice. Three participants were arrested for unfurling a banner on a future Louis Vuitton luxury hotel.

On 25 February 2024, people attempted to demonstrate in memory of murdered opposition leader Boris Nemtsov in Kazan (Republic of Tatarstan) but were immediately dispersed by the police who deemed it an 'unsanctioned protest.'

On 26 February 2024, about 40 XR activists blocked access to 2 garages of the ING bank in Amsterdam (Noord-Holland) by placing barriers and gluing themselves to the ground. Protesters demanded an immediate stop to the financing of fossil fuels. Police arrested 27 XR activists.

On 26 February 2024, Last Generation activists staged a protest on the A23 near Wien - Favoriten (Wien), citing the government's lack of response to their demand for a fundamental right to climate protection, causing traffic disruptions. The event resulted in 38 arrests by the police.

On 27 February 2024, about 10000 farmers and other agricultural employees gathered for a rally in Warsaw, protesting against ongoing imports of Ukrainian grains to the EU and demanding higher state support to the national agriculture. Three were detained.

On 27 February 2024, members of Palestine Action held a protest outside the gates of the UAV Engines factory and blocked the entrance in Shenstone (England) over the company's cooperation with Elbit Systems, Israel's largest arms manufacturer in making drones used in the Israel army. Police forces arrested four of the demonstrators.

On 27 February 2024, protesters and pro-Palestine activists disrupted the commemorative event held in the Lower House in Den Haag (Zuid-Holland) for the late former prime minister Dries van Agt. They hung up a Palestinian flag and shouted 'Free free Palestine'. The police escorted them outside and arrested 4 activists.

On 28 February 2024, campaigners from This Is Rigged held a protest inside a Sainsbury's store in Edinburgh (Scotland) against the rising living costs and stagnating wages. Protesters picked up picnic items and hosted a 'picnic protest' with the stolen items. Police forces intervened and arrested four protesters.

On 28 February 2024, activists of End Fossil staged a protest in Lisboa (Lisboa) against the presence of the leader of the political party PS, Luis Montenegro, present at the Lisbon Tourism Exchange in Lisboa (Lisboa). One of the activists threw green paint at the politician and was arrested immediately by the police.

On 28 February 2024, 100 students occupied the Faculty of Letters in Vitoria-Gasteiz (Pais Vasco) to demand aid for housing and tuition-free master's degrees. The police evicted them without incidents.

On 28 February 2024, at the call of FO, around 15 taxi drivers occupied a conference room in the Uber headquarters in Aubervilliers (Ile-de-France) to protest against the launch of the UberPool offer, which they deemed unfair to drivers, and demand better working conditions. Police intervened and arrested 13 people.

On 28 February 2024, an unknown number of people protested in Rochefort (Wallonie) against the cutting of some trees on Amicale Square. Police intervened to dislodge a man who had climbed onto a tree.

On 1 March 2024, overnight, at the call of CR, around 200 farmers gathered and dumped hay to block traffic around the Triumph Arc in Paris (Ile-de-France) to pay tribute to farmers who committed suicide and protest against the lack of financial state support for farmers. Police intervened and arrested 66 protesters.

On 1 March 2024, around 20 people, including environmental activists, gathered to demonstrate and to try and join a permanent demonstration occupation of a piece of land in Saix (Occitanie) against the construction of the A69 highway between Toulouse and Castres, which they deemed damaging to the environment. They were stopped by the police, who used tear gas to fend them off.

On 2 March 2024, about 150 pro-Palestinian protesters gathered in front of the Embassy of Israel in Den Haag (Zuid-Holland) to shout slogans and hold banners calling for a boycott of Israel. The police forced the protesters to move away from the embassy by pushing and pulling them. A protester was arrested for resisting and refusing to follow police's instructions.

On 2 March 2024, Last Generation activists participated in a protest in Berlin - Mitte (Berlin), smearing the facade of the Federal Chancellery with orange paint, while several of the activists lay or sat down in front of it. The protesters called on the German government to take on its responsibility for the younger generation with regard to climate change. The police intervened to stop the protest and temporarily arrested 16 activists aged 13 to 16. The methods used during the police intervention caused criticism and led to investigations as one policeman knelt on the head of a Last Generation activist making it difficult for her to breathe.

On 2 March 2024, at the call of XR and Youth for Climate (FFF), around 300 people gathered outside an Arkema factory in Pierre-Benite (Auvergne-Rhone-Alpes) to protest against the environmental damage caused by the chemicals produced by the company. Between several dozens and around 150 activists trespassed on the premises. Police, as well as CRS and BAC police units, intervened and used tear gas grenades to fend the protesters off. Eight activists were subsequently arrested by the police.

On 3 March 2024, far-right activists broke into Thiverval-Grignon Castle, a property managed by Emmaus and offering African nationals, notably coming from Mayotte, refuge, in Thiverval-Grignon (Ile-de-France) to demonstrate against immigration. The participants racially insulted some of the refugees and lit up flares inside the buildings. Gendarmerie officers intervened and brought the demonstrators outside.

On 4 March 2024, animal rights activists and members of 'StopCasteller' demonstrated outside the Office of the Province in Trento (Trentino-Alto Adige) against the keeping of bears at the Wildlife Center Castellar, a bill for the culling of large carnivores, and the regional authorities. An activist was arrested after entering the building to interrupt the ongoing meeting. At this point, demonstrators threw paint at the facade of the building. Police officers pushed back demonstrators with their shields.

On 4 March 2024, overnight, farmers participated in a protest on the B5 road near the Elstal area of Wustermark (Brandenburg), spreading manure and slurry over several hundred meters along the road, and blocking traffic with tractors, which caused 3 traffic accidents and 5 injuries among car owners. The police intervened and removed the vehicles with towing trucks. The event was part of a nationwide farmers' demonstration movement against several agricultural policies of the federal government, including planned agricultural subsidy cuts.

On 5 March 2024, around 20 people belonging to a well-known criminal family in the area, protested in front of the Civil Guard barracks in Barbate (Andalucia) to criticize and denounce a police operation. They gathered following a traffic incident in Vejer de la Frontera, where two police officers intercepted four men in a speeding car that tried to run over one of the police officers. Two of those involved in the traffic incident participated in the protest and were arrested by police.

On 5 March 2024, at least 25 pro-Palestine activists and members of 'Justice Now' demonstrated in support of Palestine in the hall of the Lower House in Den Haag (Zuid-Holland). An unknown number of them also disrupted the question time in the House of Representatives three times by shouting slogans in support of Palestine and against Israel. The police physically dragged away and removed the demonstrators from the building.

On 6 March 2024, campaigners from This Is Rigged group staged a protest and sprayed paint on a UK Government building in Edinburgh (Scotland) against the UK government's position on the War in Gaza and being 'complicit' in Israel's war crimes. Police forces arrested five people. This Is Rigged campaigners also scaled Queen Elizabeth House and removed the Union flag replacing it with a Palestinian flag.

On 6 March 2024, several hundred AUR affiliated people, including an MP and an MEP, gathered in front of the Romexpo center in Bucharest during the Congress of the European People's Party to protest Ursula von der Leyen's registration as a candidate for the position of President of the European Commission. The protesters attempted to force their way into the building, with the gendarmerie stopping them. The gendarmerie arrested two protesters. According to the Moldovan police, individuals affiliated with SOR protested together with AUR in Bucharest against Moldova's President Maia Sandu, calling her a 'despot'. An AUR leader denied the claims.

On 7 March 2024, 3000-4000 farmers and representatives of their associations and unions gathered for a demonstrative ride and a rally in Prague, protesting against ongoing imports of grain from Ukraine to EU and against the so-called Green Deal. Two of them were detained for minor offenses.

On 7 March 2024, several farmers with tractors held a protest at the premises of the Parliament of Navarra in Pamplona (Pais Vasco) blocking both the front exit of the building and the rear and insulting and whistling the politicians. Dozens of farmers tried to break into the building resulting in police charges.

On 7 March 2024, protesters from the Social Democratic Party of Kosovo disrupted an event organized by the government in the national library in Pristina on teacher's day, brining in speakers and unrolling posters criticizing the ministry of education. They were arrested and removed from the scene.

On 8 March 2024, around 75 farmers blocked the A6 near Adanero (Castilla y Leon). The police broke up the protest by using rubber balls and tear gas. The event was part of a nationwide farmers' demonstration movement against the ratification of the EU's free-trade agreements until partner third countries comply with the EU's agricultural standards, and in favor of fair production prices for Spanish farmers, relief measures to offset the consequences of droughts and of the import of agricultural products from Ukraine, as well as better working and social conditions in their sector.

On 8 March 2024, at least 95 pro-Palestinian protesters blocked the intersection of Theresia Street and Prins Claus Avenue in Den Haag (Zuid-Holland) to demonstrate. The demonstration was not authorized. The police intervened, and, by order of the mayor, removed and temporarily detained about 95 protesters.

On 8 March 2024, on the occasion of International Women's Day, activists gathered in Ravensburg (Baden-Wurttemberg) to protest in favor of women's rights. Two of them rappeled from a pedestrian bridge over the B32, condemning catcalling. Police intervened to remove the activists.

On 9 March 2024, Climaximo activists blocked a road in Lisboa (Lisboa) to demand more attention be given to the climate emergency ahead of the general elections held the day after. Police arrested tree activists.

On 9 March 2024, around 30 activists from Extinction Rebellion blocked a mineral exploration drilling in the Viiankiaava protected area near Sodankyla, Lappi, while 13 of them chained themselves to the drilling equipment. The activists demanded that the work be stopped and banned by the government due to its possible negative impact on the environment. Later, police personnel removed activists from the site, 2 activists were arrested.

On 11 March 2024, people blocked the entrance to the Danish defense and aerospace company's factory in Lystrup, Midtjylland, to oppose the company's delivery of weapons and jet parts to Israel. Later, as a result of their non-compliance with police instructions, two activists were removed from the venue and detained.

On 12 March 2024, around 100 workers and trade unions blocked the entrance to the construction site in Nordhavn, Copenhagen, accusing the owner of social dumping and breaching the collective agreement. The police later intervened and dispersed the activists.

On 12 March 2024, despite a police ban on all public gatherings in Thessaloniki following mob violence during the weekend, a large crowd of students and other citizens protested against transphobia and rallied outside the flagship Olympion theater in Aristotelous square in support of the film 'Stray bodies', which was exploring body autonomy and women's rights and was being screened at the Documentary Film Festival of Thessaloniki. Strong MAT police forces, who had lined up outside the theater early on, pushed the protesters away due to the ban and to prevent them from reaching a group of 5 people protesting against the film. At the same time, members of the wider anti-establishment sector rallied at Venizelou square, but they were also pushed away by MAT forces due to the ban. The protesters then set off from Olympion for an antifascist march in the city center.

On 12 March 2024, for a second consecutive day, people blocked the entrance to the Danish defense and aerospace company's factory in Lystrup, Midtjylland, to oppose the company's delivery of weapons and jet parts to Israel. Later, as a result of their non-compliance with police instructions, several activists were removed from the venue. Activists from Vegan Activism movement took part in the event, among others.

On 12 March 2024, around 200 farmers with around 110 tractors participated in a motorcade in Almeria (Andalucia), blocking the entrance to the port. One person was arrested. The event was part of a nationwide farmers' demonstration movement called by ASAJA, COAG, and UPA against the ratification of the EU's free-trade agreements until partner third countries comply with the EU's agricultural standards, and in favor of fair production prices for Spanish farmers, relief measures to offset the consequences of droughts and of the import of agricultural products from Ukraine, as well as better working and social conditions in their sector.

On 12 March 2024, for a second consecutive day, environmental activists blocked the entrance to the Swedish Parliament in Stockholm calling on the government to take action against climate change and declare climate emergency. The police personnel later intervened and dispersed the activists.

On 13 March 2024, five activists belonging to Let's burn everything (Bruciamo tutto) blocked the traffic for several minutes in Lungotevere in front of the Principe Amedeo Savoia Aosta Bridge in Roma - City Center (Lazio) to protest against violence against women, to ask for an improvement of a financial contribution given to women victims of violence. Protesters held a banner and poured paint on the asphalt. The police intervened and brought them to the police station.

On 14 March 2024, Sciences Po university students gathered outside campus in Paris (Ile-de-France) to express solidarity with the Palestinian people and condemn the Israeli military offensive on Gaza. Police intervened to disperse the protest, which was unauthorized.

On 15 March 2024, several groups of several thousands of people held protests against the Orban government and its corruption across Budapest: MKKP and its members, including the 9th district mayor on the Freedom bridge; Robert Puzser, Szikra movement, and teacher groups outside the National Museum; Peter Magyar and his supporters on the Andrassy boulevard. Police forcibly escorted out a former independent MP from the crowd outside the National Museum.

On 16 March 2024, several police units, including OPKE, DRASI, Security police, traffic police and the crime subdivision of Northern Greece, launched a large operation at the School of Sciences in the Aristotle University of Thessaloniki, following a call by the rector after a large group of people (also opposing education reforms and private universities) attempted to reoccupy a former anarchist hangout in the Biology department, where a new library was under construction. There were 49 arrests. Police seized 22 wooden poles, 4 naval type flares and incendiary devices, balaclava masks, 12 gas masks, 11 fire extinguishers filled with paint, sledgehammers, a stun grenade and a tear gas canister and other evidence. The rector made statements denying rumours that the rioters managed to breach the entrance of a basement room with a small nuclear reactor used for academic purposes.

On 16 March 2024, around 50 to 60 environmental activists, including members of Extinction Rebellion, blocked the entrance to an oil port in Gothenburg (Goteborg) to oppose the continued exploitation of fossil fuel deposits in the North Sea. A number of activists were later removed from the site after failing to comply with police instructions. The blockade was part of a global action that took place in at least 6 countries.

On 16 March 2024, under the motto 'Democracy needs honesty', around 130 Last Generation activists staged a protest in Berlin - Friedrichshain-Kreuzberg (Berlin), while around 20 of them blocked Warschauer Strasse with sit-ins, to raise awareness about social inequality, the climate crisis and its negative health effects, and to demand more democracy. The police intervened, carried the protesters off the street, and prevented them from staging other blockades. The action was part of a series of so-called 'disobedient assemblies' taking place across the country that day.

On 16 March 2024, about 150 people, including Last Generation activists, participated in a protest in Freiburg im Breisgau (Baden-Wurttemberg) and blocked roads near the main train station to demand better climate protection measures. The police intervened and carried the protesters off the road. The action was part of a series of so-called 'disobedient assemblies' taking place across the country that day.

On 16 March 2024, 150 (according to organizers) or up to 50 (according to police) people, including Last Generation activists, participated in a protest in Karlsruhe (Baden-Wurttemberg), blocking Durlacher Allee, to demand better climate protection measures. The police intervened and carried the protesters off the road. The action was part of a series of so-called 'disobedient assemblies' taking place across the country that day.

On 16 March 2024, dozens of Last Generation activists staged a protest in Leipzig (Sachsen), blocking traffic around Wilhelm-Leuschner Platz with sit-ins, to call on politicians to do more in the fight against global warming and demand a reduction of greenhouse gas emissions. The police intervened and carried the protesters off the road. The action was part of a series of so-called 'disobedient assemblies' taking place across the country that day.

On 16 March 2024, between around 30 and about 54 people, including Last Generation activists, participated in a protest near the LNG terminal in Mukran (Mecklenburg-Vorpommern), blocking one access road lane, to demonstrate against the use of LNG and denounce its environmental impact. The police intervened and carried the protesters off the road. About 25 protesters moved to a green space nearby to continue their protest. The action was part of a series of so-called 'disobedient assemblies' taking place across the country that day.

On 16 March 2024, about 150 climate activists, including Last Generation activists, participated in a protest in Regensburg (Bayern) and blocked an intersection to demand better climate protection and call for the abandonment of coal, oil, and gas. The police intervened, carrying more than 25 protesters off the road and temporarily arresting two participants. The action was part of a series of so-called 'disobedient assemblies' taking place across the country that day.

On 20 March 2024, people blocked several entrances to the Norwegian parliament in Oslo calling on the government to cease all military cooperation with Israel. A number of activists were later removed from the site after failing to comply with police instructions and free the entrance.

On 20 March 2024, people staged a pro-Palestinian demonstration during a youth football tournament match in Skien, Vestfold og Telemark, to oppose the Israeli offensive in Gaza and to show support and solidarity with the people of Palestine. Police later intervened and removed the activists from the venue.

On 22 March 2024, the collective Solidarity with Migrants reported with video evidence MAT police forces pushing forcibly with their shields 46 hunger striking prisoners in the Corinth detention center and hitting them with batons. The migrant prisoners were protesting in the yard over arbitrary detentions and humiliating conditions of incarceration in their cells. The collective reported that there were injuries and humiliating police checks in the cells. Police said they intervened when the prisoners refused to return to their cells and set fire to cartons and that there were no injuries.

On 22 March 2024, about 200 protesters and counter-protesters protested in front of a mosque in Rotterdam (Zuid-Holland). The main demonstration was an initiative of Bring Them Home, a pro-Israeli group, and the PEGIDA leader Edwin Wagensveld was among those who joined the gathering, which called for attention to the fate of the Israeli hostages held by Hamas. The PEGIDA leader carried a Palestinian flag, mimicked to wipe his buttocks with it, and finally kicked the flag. A group of counterdemonstrators waving Palestinian flags gathered nearby, with some participants throwing eggs at Edwin Wagensveld. The police arrested three participants of the counter-demonstration: one for throwing eggs, another for not being able to show his ID and a third for wearing a balaclava.

On 23 March 2024, members of the LGBTQ+ community and Antifa activists held a demonstration in London (England) to protest against a medical conference that they deemed to propagate transphobic and homophobic messages and ideas. Police forces intervened, using pepper spray against the protesters and forcibly pushing them away until the protesters disbanded.

On 23 March 2024, at least 106 XR and Scientist Rebellion activists staged a demonstration at the Eindhoven Airport in Eindhoven (Noord-Brabant) to demand more climate action, the reduction of the number of flights, and the end of private jet flights. Activists glued themselves to the concrete outside the airport and tried to climb a fence to enter the airport's grounds. Police intervened and arrested 106 activists.

On 23 March 2024, around 20 environmental activists, including Extinction Rebellion members, blocked traffic near Copenhagen Airport in Kastrup, Hovedstaden, calling for a ban on private jets. The activists were later removed from the road for failure to comply with police instructions.

On 25 March 2024, during the Greek Independence Day military parade in Lamia, members of the Labor Center of Lamia and the association of employees of LARCO, a Mining and Metallurgical company in financial hardship, attempted to march at the end of the parade to protest against the government's plans for the factory, but they were pushed back by strong police forces.

On 25 March 2024, during the Greek Independence Day military parade in Trikala, the family of 3 sisters, who were killed at the Tempe rail disaster, held a protest opposite the dignitaries' stage against the government and over the lack of respect to the family's drama. They started booing uniformed officers, who turned their face towards the officials as a show of respect, before they were removed by police. Previously, they had applauded and shouted thanks to the student formation, who paraded past the dignitaries with their eyes straight in protest.

On 25 March 2024, during the Greek Independence Day military parade in Athens - Central Athens, 7 foreign nationals waving Palestinian flags briefly halted the movement of tanks before they were detained by police for obstructing the parade. They were protesting in solidarity with the Palestinian people and against Israeli attacks on Gaza. Soon after they were released.

On 25 March 2024, an unknown number of pro-Palestine activists and students demonstrated, reportedly by preventing people from freely accessing classes or carrying out exams, at the Amsterdam University College campus in Amsterdam (North Holland) to protest against the Israel-Hamas conflict and demonstrate solidarity with the Palestinian civilians. The police arrested an unknown number of people.

On 25 March 2024, dozens of demonstrators participated in an unauthorized Kurdish protest march in Wien - Favoriten (Wien) against the 'Grey Wolves' Turkish movement. The protest escalated when participants attempted to breach police barriers, but police officers pushed them back.

On 26 March 2024, at the call of CR, students symbolically occupied for some hours the rectorate of Sapienza University in Roma - Tiburtino (Lazio) to demand the stop of all collaborations with Israel-based universities and demonstrated in support of Palestinian civilians. The police intervened physically and were able to prevent around 200 other students from entering the university and joining the others. Students also protested outside of the university.

On 26 March 2024, at least 5 pro-Palestinian activists and students blocked a bridge on the Amsterdam University College campus in Amsterdam (Noord-Holland) to protest against the Israel-Hamas war and demonstrate solidarity with the Palestinian civilians. The police arrested 5 protesters.

On 27 March 2024, activists from the Emergency Break movement blocked in motorway exit in Avedore, Hovedstaden, calling an end to motorway construction in the country. Later, police personnel removed activists from the scene.

On 29 March 2024, women, members of the LGBTQ+ community, and members of the transfeminist movement 'Let's set it all on fire' (Bruciamo Tutto), stormed the exhibition on the works of painter Artemisia Gentileschi at the Palazzo Ducale in Genova (Liguria) to protest against violence against women, femicide, and the patriarchy. Demonstrators covered the paintings of Agostino Tassi, who was the painter's teacher but also her rapist, with black sheets and then poured blood-red paint on the floor of the room. The police intervened and dragged the protesters away.
On 29 March 2024, around 100 people participated in an unregistered pro-Palestine protest in Berlin - Mitte (Berlin). The police intervened and arrested several participants.

On 30 March 2024, 30 XR activists protested on the A10 highway in Amsterdam (Noord-Holland) to denounce the investments of the bank ING in fossil fuels. The protesters wanted to block the highway but the police arrested 25 people to prevent it. Alternatively, some protesters then held a musical protest.

On 30 March 2024, three pro-Palestine protesters held a protest and attempted to block US military planes at Shannon Airport in Shannon (Clare) to show support for Palestine and denounce US support for Israel. IPSC organized the protest and three protesters were arrested by police forces.

On 30 March 2024, more than 200,000 pro-Palestine protesters took to the streets of London - Westminster (England) to demand an immediate ceasefire in Gaza and to commemorate the anniversary of Palestinian Land Day. PSC, Stop the War, and the CND organized the protest. Labour MP Jeremy Corbyn also addressed the crowd. Police forces arrested four people during the protest.

On 31 March 2024, after a 48-hour occupation with a rave party and negotiations with the police, about 400 people, including youths and activists, left the former Stamoto military facility on Felsina Boulevard in Bologna (Emilia-Romagna) and took to the city streets to demonstrate against police repression and real estate speculation. Protesters also demanded free meeting spaces and more liveable cities. The police identified over 250 people and temporarily arrested 12 activists without identity documents at the police station.

On 3 April 2024, anti-meat activists staged a protest and occupied the slaughterhouses of the Cranswick food facility on Brandon Road in Watton (England) against unethical practices in the British pig industry. Police forces intervened and arrested seven protesters.

On 4 April 2024, Last Generation activists symbolically washed dishes in the fountain of the recently inaugurated Trapezoidal Mall in Palermo (Sicilia) as a protest against the drought emergency and the emergency plan designed by the water company Amap. Activists called for a more sustainable management of water. The police intervened to remove the activists.

On 4 April 2024, pro-Palestine protesters from the Palestine Action group staged a protest and blocked the entrance of the council building in Taunton (England) over the council's suspected ties to Elbit Systems, an Israeli weapon firm. They also denounced the recent killing of seven aid workers by Israeli armed forces in Gaza. Some protesters sprayed the council building with red paint, with police forces eventually arresting four protesters.

On 4 April 2024, around 100 people gathered in Rennes (Bretagne) to protest against the dissolution of the far-left group DefCo. Police intervened to disperse the demonstration, which had not been authorized.

On 6 April 2024, several hundred feminist activists gathered in Prague and occupied a bridge, attempting to block a pro-life march taking place around the city. Simultaneously, they demanded preservation of free abortions for women and equal rights for LGBTQ+ people. Law enforcers detained five of them.

On 6 April 2024, anti-ULEZ protesters held a protest close to the house of the mayor of London in Tooting (England) against his Ultra Low Emission Zone (ULEZ) plans for London. Protesters claimed police forces used 'excessive force' against them (the shoving of some to the ground and the pulling of a female demonstrator's hair) during clashes at the rally following the arrest of a participant.

On 6 April 2024, 6 Last Generation activists staged a demonstration at the Gallerie dell'Accademia Museum in Venezia (Veneto), gluing their hands to the wall under a painting by Francesco Guardi, to demand more climate action and highlight the risks adverse climate events might bring for the city of Venice. The police put an end to the demonstration and temporarily detained the protesters.

On 6 April 2024, several hundred XR activists tried to block the A12 highway in Den Haag (Zuid-Holland) to protest against fossil fuels and to demand the end of subsidies to large corporations using fossil fuels. There were groups on the Malieveld, the Koekamp, the Zuid-Holland Avenue and the Koningskade. The police arrested more than 400 people, among which the climate activist Greta Thunberg.

On 6 April 2024, around 100 climate activists from Ende Gelaende gathered at the Scholven coal-fired power plant in Gelsenkirchen (Nordrhein-Westfalen), blocking access rails, to demand an immediate coal phase-out. The protest was dispersed by the police in the afternoon.

On 7 April 2024, 4 Last Generation activists staged a protest inside the Accademia Gallery in Firenze (Toscana), and chained themselves to the statue of David, to demand more climate action. The police dragged the demonstrators out to ensure access to visitors.

On 7 April 2024, Last Generation activists protested in Graz (Steiermark), disrupting a half marathon by sitting on the event's route with banners, before being removed by police forces. Some activists simultaneously erected a large banner with the message 'Time is running out' near the Clock Tower above the city, highlighting the urgent need to address the climate crisis.

On 8 April 2024, activists from the Youth Demand group staged a protest outside the Labour Party headquarters in London - Southwark (England), calling for an arms embargo on Israel and expressing solidarity with Palestine. Protesters also threw red paint over the building, prompting the intervention of police forces and the arrest of 12 activists.

On 8 April 2024, climate activists from the Disrupt movement gathered near the Mercedes-Benz plant in Bremen (Bremen), blocking two railway tracks, and causing disruptions to train services heading to Bremen and Hannover, thus disrupting the delivery of vehicles from the Mercedes-Benz plant. Protesters highlighted concerns about the environmental impact of resource-intensive manufacturing processes. Police forces intervened and dispersed the protest.

On 8 April 2024, an unknown number of people, including pro-Palestine activists, students, and representatives of several self-managed social centers, took to the streets of Napoli (Campania) to demonstrate against NATO and the Italian, US, and Israeli governments, and demand the end of the killing of Palestinian civilians in Gaza. At the end of Toledo Street, demonstrators tried to push past a police cordon to reach San Carlo Theater. The police, in riot gear, charged the demonstrators and used tear gas and truncheons against them. Eight demonstrators were injured, two of which were hit in the face and head. At the call of the Students' Network for Palestine (Rete Studenti Per La Palestina), students also occupied the rectorate of the headquarters of the Federico II University.

On 9 April 2024, demonstrators interrupted the speech of the Minister for Energy and the Minister for Business and Industry Ebba Busch (KD) in Gothenburg (Goteborg) to show their opposition to the government's political stance on the Hamas-Israel conflict and to express their support and solidarity with the people of Palestine. The activists were detained and removed by the police personnel. Other peaceful protesters continued their protest.

On 9 April 2024, people demonstrated and later attempted to block the road to the president's official residence in Alftanes to oppose the new government of Bjarni Benediktsson. The activists were later detained and removed from the scene.

On 9 April 2024, activists from the Youth Demand group staged a protest outside the home of Labour Party leader Keir Starmer in London - Westminster (England), calling for a two-way arms embargo on Israel and expressing solidarity with Palestine. Protesters hung a banner outside his house that read 'Starmer stop the killing'. Police forces arrested three participants.

On 9 April 2024, an unknown number of Justice Now and Christians Against Genocide activists staged a protest in the Lower House in Den Haag (Zuid-Holland) by waving Palestinian flags and chanting slogans. They demanded an immediate ceasefire and the end of all relations with Israel. Police arrested 9 demonstrators.

On 10 April 2024, feminist collectives rallied in Athens - Central Athens demanding 'femicide' be included in criminal law, in response to a murder of a woman by her ex partner who sought help and was turned away by the police moments before the killing. Police used tear gas and beat the protesters with batons. At least two women were hit with police shields, one of them requiring hospitalization. On 19 April, one of the two women who had been hospitalized reported officially that a police officer grabbed her by the neck and broke her arm when she intervened placing herself between the police officer and a friend, while the officer was beating him down.

On 10 April 2024, activists from the Restore Wetlands Movement staged a protest at a metro station in Stockholm to oppose an increase in transport fares. Police later used force to disperse one of the activists.

On 10 April 2024, around 15 XR activists staged a protest action outside the Bouches-du-Rhone prefecture in Marseille (Provence-Alpes-Cote d'Azur), blocking traffic, to call on state authorities to clear a pile of 12,800 tonnes of burnt-out garbage following a fire at an industrial waste storage site in Saint-Chamas, with some citing health and environmental concerns. 14 people were arrested by the police.

On 12 April 2024, a group of protesting squatters occupied a space within the premises of Democritus University of Thrace in Komotini. Authorities removed them the following day at the request of the university's rector authorities. No arrests were reported. The identity of the squatters or their protest demands were not reported.

On 12 April 2024, no more than 20 pro-Palestinian activists from the action group Friesland for Palestine disturbed a lecture of Israeli influencer Hananya Naftali in Surhuisterveen (Friesland). Four activists were grabbed and expelled from the concert hall by the police.

On 12 April 2024, an unknown number of XR activists and Quit with Coal activists blocked a road past the North Holland provincial government building in Haarlem (Noord-Holland) to demand that the province revoke the license of the company Tata Steel, citing environmental concerns. After an 18-hour blockade, the police arrested five participants.

On 13 April 2024, more than 20 XR activists blocked the street in front of ING bank offices in Leiden (Zuid-Holland) to protest against the bank's investment in fossil fuels. Police arrested about 25 protesters when they refused to clear the way.

On 13 April 2024, about 40 Last Generation activists participated in a climate protest in Berlin - Friedrichshain-Kreuzberg (Berlin) and tried blocking the road. The police intervened and prevented a blockade by pushing the activists away. The activists spoke of violence and repression to define the intervention. The protest was part of a nationwide protest week under the motto 'Resistance Spring' organized by the Last Generation to call for more climate protection.

On 13 April 2024, around 30 Last Generation activists staged a protest in Dusseldorf (Nordrhein-Westfalen) and blocked a bridge to raise awareness for climate change and demand more climate action and a speed limit for highways. The police intervened, broke up the protest and carried about a dozen activists onto the sidewalk. The protest was part of a nationwide protest week under the motto 'Resistance Spring' organized by the Last Generation to call for more climate protection.

On 13 April 2024, under the motto 'Democracy needs honesty', slightly more than 50 Last Generation activists staged a climate protest in Hamburg - Altona (Hamburg), formed a human chain and blocked a road near the Altona railway station to demand more climate protection. The police intervened physically and cleared the blockade. The protest was part of a nationwide protest week under the motto 'Resistance Spring' organized by the Last Generation to call for more climate protection.

On 13 April 2024, under the motto 'Let's make it uncomfortable for you', more than 700 people participated in a protest in Neureut in Karlsruhe (Baden-Wurttemberg) against the spring reception of the AfD state parliamentary group, racism and right-wing extremism. Members of the AfD had an information stand nearby and tried interrupting the protest which was prevented by the protesters causing the police to arrest two of them.

On 14 April 2024, at least 4 people conducted a series of single-person protests in Pushchino (Moscow Oblast) demanding that the city retain local self-governance, which is set to be eradicated with the regional authorities' decision to join Pushchino and Serpukhov into one city district. All 4 were detained by the police.

On 14 April 2024, people protested in Nakhodka (Nakhodkinskiy, Primorskiy) against the destruction of a local birch grove. Russian police detained 2 journalists who were covering the protest and one activist.
On 15 April 2024, 9 activists affiliated with the Last Generation movement blocked two bridges in Warsaw, demanding immediate climate action. Law enforcers removed them from the location.
On 16 April 2024, activists affiliated with the Last Generation movement blocked two bridges in Warsaw, demanding immediate climate action. Law enforcers removed them from the location.

On 17 April 2024, a small group of former Jehovah's Witnesses protested at the headquarters of the Jehovah's Witnesses in Emmen (Drenthe) to draw attention to the practice of 'watchtower shunning' and its consequences on people. The protest was organized by the Foundation Against Watchtower Shunning (Stichting Against Watchtower Shunning). The protesters demanded the end of this exclusion policy and to be able to maintain relationships with people who are still part of the group. Henri Dahlem, the president of the Foundation, refused to leave the premises and was arrested by the police.
On 17 April 2024, 6 activists affiliated with the Last Generation movement blocked two bridges in Warsaw, demanding immediate climate action. Law enforcers removed them from the location.

On 17 April 2024, a large group of people, including individuals from various political factions and the Querdenken movement, gathered in Ravensburg (Baden-Wurttemberg), disrupting an FDP election campaign event, with vocal opposition directed at FDP politicians such as Marie-Agnes Strack-Zimmermann. 3 people were briefly arrested by the police because they had glue with them.

On 17 April 2024, 12 Last Generation activists protested in Karlsruhe (Baden-Wurttemberg), by blocking the entrance to the Oberrhein oil refinery with kayaks, demanding climate action with a sign reading 'Stop - closed due to climate catastrophe'. The event aimed to draw attention to the environmental impact of fossil fuel operations. Police officers intervened and put an end to the action.

On 18 April 2024, for the second consecutive day, activists from Extinction Rebellion staged a blockade in Amager, Copenhagen, in a attempt to disrupt land reclamation works in connection with the creation of an artificial island named Lynetteholm that is supposed to house 35,000 residents. Activists claimed that the development project could harm both the marine and urban environment. The police later removed the activists from the site.

On 19 April 2024, pro-Palestinian activists blocked entrance to the national meeting venue of the Progress Party (FrP) in Gardermoen, Viken. The activists accused party members of complicity in the genocide in Gaza and called on the government to immediately cease all arms supplies to the Israeli military. Later, police personnel removed the activists from the venue after they failed to comply with police demands to disperse.

On 19 April 2024, for the third consecutive day, activists from Extinction Rebellion staged a blockade in Amager, Copenhagen, in a attempt to disrupt land reclamation works in connection with the creation of an artificial island named Lynetteholm that is supposed to house 35,000 residents. Activists claimed that the development project could harm both the marine and urban environment. The police later removed the activists from the site, four people were detained.

On 19 April 2024, on the occasion of the Global Climate Strike, around 300 people, including students and pro-Palestine activists, demonstrated in Napoli (Campania) against climate change, the meeting of the G7's foreign ministers in Capri, NATO, and the war in Palestine. At the Port of Naples, activists tried to reach the ferries to Capri but were blocked by police who charged and pushed back the demonstrators. Nobody was injured. Representatives of the Students Network for Palestine, the self-managed social center Insurgencia, FFF, Greenpeace, and Legambiente were present.

On 20 April 2024, six activists from Palestine Action staged a sit-in protest at a Barclays bank in Commercial Road in Portsmouth (England) over alleged links to Israel. Police forces had to intervene and arrest three people.

On 20 April 2024, about 100 XR activists blocked the roundabout to the office of TotalEnergies in Den Haag (Zuid-Holland) to demand the end of the construction of the EACOP oil pipeline in Uganda and Tanzania, arguing it caused ecological destruction and human rights violations. Police arrested an unknown number of people.

On 20 April 2024, around 101 Last Generation and 'Climate Network Heidelberg' (Klimanetz Heidelberg) activists gathered in Heidelberg (Baden-Wurttemberg), demanding increased climate action. Some activists staged a street blockade, which led to police officers carrying physically activists off the streets.

On 20 April 2024, around 100 Last Generation activists gathered in Bremen (Bremen), to protest against climate inaction, by blocking an intersection. Despite police intervention, approximately 60 individuals refused to vacate the roadway, resulting in their temporary detention and the physical dispersal of the demonstration.

On 20 April 2024, around 25 Last Generation activists gathered in Saarbrucken (Saarland), demanding increased government action on climate change, resulting in 6 participants being taken into custody by the police.

On 22 April 2024, a small group of Last Generation activists gathered outside the cinema of Venaria Reale (Piemonte) to demand more climate action and demonstrate against the G7 meeting taking place at the location. One of them spray-painted the facade of the cinema using a fire extinguisher and a green spray can. The police intervened, and the activist was taken to the police headquarters for questioning.
On 22 April 2024, activists affiliated with the Last Generation movement attempted to block traffic in Warsaw, demanding immediate climate action. Law enforcers removed them from the roads.

On 23 April 2024, pro-Palestinian demonstrators blocked the entrance of the central bank of Norway in Oslo urging the divestment from Israeli companies. Activists were later removed from the site for failure to comply with police instructions. Activists from the Norway's Palestine Committee and the Action Group for Palestine participated in the event.

On 25 April 2024, in the evening, around 80 students staged a demonstration and occupied the Sciences Po University Campus on Saint-Guillaume Street in Paris (Ile-de-France), at the call of the Palestine Committee of Sciences Po, to condemn the Israeli military campaign in and around Gaza and demand an end to Sciences Po's collaboration with all 'institutions or entities complicit in the systemic oppression of the Palestinian people'. Overnight, police evacuated around 60 students from the facility.

On 25 April 2024, an unknown number of Justice Now! XR activists disrupted the public hearings in the Lower House twice in Den Haag (Zuid-Holland) by gathering, chanting pro-Palestinian songs, and holding protest signs. The police physically removed eight activists from the hall.

On 25 April 2024, around 100 students affiliated with Occupy RUG occupied the Academy Building at the University of Groningen (Groningen) after a meeting with the university's Executive Board failed to secure the reinstatement of a former professor and social safety expert who was dismissed in March 2023 following disputes over her criticism of RUG's gender equality policies. Police forces intervened and evacuated the students. A female student was dragged down the stairs by her legs, with an assistant professor also indicating that police struck her with a baton. The protest was part of ongoing student mobilizations around social safety at RUG.
On 26 April 2024, activists affiliated with the Last Generation movement attempted to block traffic in Warsaw, demanding immediate climate action. Law enforcers removed them from the roads.

On 26 April 2024, more than 100 people staged a protest in front of the Bundestag in Berlin - Mitte (Berlin) after the police banned the camp of pro-Palestine activists and police officers physically intervened to enforce the ban and clear the camp, pulling and carrying away activists and removing the tents. During the eviction, about 20 to 30 activists resisted, leading to scuffles and verbal altercations with the police. The camp was set up two weeks ago to protest against Israel's military deployment in Gaza and the supply of German weapons to Israel. No further details were given about the 'scuffles'.

On 27 April 2024, people held a protest in Lisboa (Lisboa) participating in a slow march, against the governments and companies' implications in the fossil industry leading the climate crisis. Two activists of Climaximo were arrested by the police.

On 27 April 2024, an unknown number of XR activists blocked the A10 highway in Amsterdam (Noord-Holland) in front of the former office of the bank ING. The protesters demanded the end of the financing of the fossil fuel industry. The demonstration was disbanded by the police who picked up the individuals one by one and put them in buses. Police arrested about 130 people.

On 27 April 2024, activists from Extinction Rebellion blocked a road in Stureplan, Stockholm, demanding an end to subsidies for fossil fuel related companies and calling for climate justice. Later, the police personnel removed activists from the demonstration site.

On 27 April 2024, at least 31 Last Generation activists and cyclists staged a protest on Carolabrucke and Carolaplatz in Dresden (Sachsen) and blocked the bridge and a road with sit-ins for environmental reasons. The police intervened physically and broke up the blockade by carrying and pulling the protesters away.

On 28 April 2024, a large group of No TAV activists gathered outside the high-speed Turin-Lyon railway working site in San Didero (Piemonte) to hit the fences and block the road to demonstrate against the TAV project. The police intervened and used tear gas against the demonstrators.

On 28 April 2024, people held a protest in Lisboa (Lisboa) participating in a slow march, against the governments and companies' implications in the fossil industry leading the climate crisis. Four activists of Climaximo were arrested by the police.

On 28 April 2024, Extinction Rebellion associated group blocked traffic near Copenhagen Airport in Kastrup, Hovedstaden, calling for a ban on private jets and to oppose aviation industry. The activists were later removed from the road for failure to comply with police instructions.

On 29 April 2024, around 150 students, including three LFI MPs, staged a demonstration and set up tents at the Paris 1-Pantheon Campus of the Sorbonne University in Paris (Ile-de-France), to condemn the Israeli military campaign in and around Gaza and demand an end to Sorbonne's collaboration with all 'institutions or entities complicit in the systemic oppression of the Palestinian people'. At around midday, police evacuated around 50 students from the facility, physically dragging to the ground around 10 students.

On 29 April 2024, members of the Belleville Park Youth Collective (collectif des jeunes du parc de Belleville) staged a protest action at the Maison des metallos in Paris (Ile-de-France), to snatch accommodation places. Two participants were arrested for 'theft in assembly' and 'concerted obstruction with violence or assault of the exercise of freedom of expression of artistic creation'.

On 29 April 2024, around 100 anti-fascists demonstrated in front of the Court in Cagliari (Sardegna) against a neo-fascist commemoration ceremony. They tried to reach the ceremony but protesters were stopped by the police in anti-riot gear, with no reported clashes. The neo-fascist group was commemorating Sergio Ramelli, a member of a neo-fascist group killed in 1975 by a group of left militants.

On 29 April 2024, protesters gathered outside an immigration center in Solihull (England) after the news was revealed that the Home Office was launching a major operation to detain asylum seekers across the UK. Police forces intervened and arrested 13 protesters for blocking the entrance.

On 30 April 2024, around 100 students blocked access to the Sciences Po campus in Toulouse (Occitanie) to express solidarity with the Palestinian people, condemn what they deemed an Israeli 'genocide' of Gazans, and demand French universities to stop cooperating with Israeli universities. Police intervened and used batons to remove the protesters.

On 30 April 2024, for the second day in a row, students staged a sit-in and blocked access to the university campus in Saint-Etienne (Auvergne-Rhone-Alpes) to express solidarity with the Palestinian people, condemn what they deemed an Israeli 'genocide' of Gazans, and demand French universities to stop cooperating with Israeli universities. Police intervened to put an end to the action.
On 1 May 2024, KPRF members and supporters protested in Bratsk (Irkutsk) against the federal government's corruption. Police detained a KPRF member who gave a speech at the event.

On 1 May 2024, around 10,000 people demonstrated in Zurich (Switzerland). The event was part of a nationwide wave of demonstrations on the occasion of International Worker's Day to demand an increase in wages as well as peace in the world, notably in Palestine and Ukraine. Police intervened to disperse an unauthorized gathering of far-left affiliates taking place next to the main demonstration.

On 1 May 2024, protesters from the Workers for a Free Palestine group staged a protest outside the BAE System weapons manufacturer in Glasgow (Scotland) to protest the arms trade between the company and Israel and to demand an immediate ceasefire. They also wanted to show solidarity with Palestinian workers. Police forces arrested three protesters.

On 1 May 2024, on the occasion of International Workers' Day, at the call of the DGB, people gathered in Bonn (Nordrhein-Westfalen), demanding increased wages, fair compensation, and regulated working hours as fundamental rights for employees. The police briefly verbally stopped the demonstration due to a group of demonstrators not adhering to regulations, including the unauthorized use of smoke bombs and masks. The demonstration carried on.

On 2 May 2024, police forces intervened to remove around 100 students blocking access to the Sorbonne University campus in Paris (Ile-de-France). The students were protesting since 29 April to express solidarity with the Palestinian people, condemn what they deemed an Israeli 'genocide' of Gazans, and demand French universities to stop cooperating with Israeli universities.

On 2 May 2024, dozens of protesters gathered outside the Best Western Hotel in London - Southwark (England) to prevent sending migrants to the Bibby Stockholm barge. Protesters surrounded the bus and blocked the road. Police forces intervened and arrested 45 people.

On 2 May 2024, students blocked access to the Sciences Po Lille and ESJ campus in Lille (Hauts-de-France) to express solidarity with the Palestinian people, condemn what they deemed an Israeli 'genocide' of Gazans, and demand French universities to stop cooperating with Israeli universities. Early in the morning, a first demonstration was put to end by the police, who used tear gas to fend the protesters off.

On 3 May 2024, police intervened to remove around 50 students blocking access to the Sciences Po campus in Paris (Ile-de-France). The protest started a few days earlier to express solidarity with the Palestinian people, condemn what they deemed an Israeli 'genocide' of Gazans, and demand French universities to stop cooperating with Israeli universities.

On 3 May 2024, at least 22 people, including the Red Youth leader Amrit Kaur, demonstrated outside of the central bank of Norway office in Oslo urging the divestment from Israeli companies. Activists were later removed from the road for failure to comply with police instructions, 22 activists were detained.

On 3 May 2024, police intervened to remove around several dozen students blocking access to the Sciences Po campus in Lyon (Auvergne-Rhone-Alpes). The protest started a few days earlier to express solidarity with the Palestinian people, condemn what they deemed an Israeli 'genocide' of Gazans, and demand French universities to stop cooperating with Israeli universities.

On 3 May 2024, high school students blocked access to the Monet school with trash cans and other objects in Paris (Ile-de-France). Police intervened to put an end to the action. The students were gathering to oppose the government's education reform, especially the introduction of level groups for students, and demand more state funding for public schools.

On 3 May 2024, an unknown number of XR activists occupied KLM's Frequent Flyer Lounge at the Schiphol Airport in Schiphol (Noord-Holland) to demand the end of the Frequent Flyer Program that caused global warming. Police arrested 21 people.

On 3 May 2024, police intervened to remove around 15 students blocking access to the Sciences Po campus in Saint-Etienne (Auvergne-Rhone-Alpes). The protest started a few days earlier to express solidarity with the Palestinian people, condemn what they deemed an Israeli 'genocide' of Gazans, and demand French universities to stop cooperating with Israeli universities.

On 4 May 2024, around 40 XR affiliates gathered on Capital Square and dumped seeds and tapioca on the ground in Toulouse (Occitanie) to oppose the opening of concrete factories for the construction of the A69 highway between Toulouse and Castres, which they deemed damaging to the environment. Police intervened and arrested six participants.

On 4 May 2024, during the country's annual World War II remembrance ceremony, three people disturbed the ceremony in Amsterdam (Noord-Holland), by gathering and holding a banner to raise awareness about the 'genocide' in Uganda. Police arrested three people.

On 4 May 2024, several hundred XR activists from Belgium, the Netherlands, and Germany blocked Belliard Street in Brussels - Etterbeek (Brussels) to demand the end of fossil fuels subsidies and a national emergency plan to transition to a fossil-free economy. A spokesperson of FEYG - Federation of Young European Greens (the youth branch of the European Green Party) spoke at the event. Police asked the activists to clear the streets and those who refused were detained. In total, police forces arrested 132 people. The organization denounced excessive police brutality during the arrests.

On 4 May 2024, on the occasion of the city stop of the annual multiple-stage bicycle race 'Giro d'Italia', pro-Palestine activists and representatives of the self-managed social center Askatasuna demonstrated in Torino (Piemonte) to demand freedom and peace for Gaza and protest against Zionism, the Israeli government and army, and the participation in the sporting event of Israeli-based company Israel-Premier Tech. The police intervened to disperse the demonstrators and arrested a woman accused of resisting the officers and kicking them. The woman was released the following day. Another demonstrator was reported for possession of smoke bombs.

On 4 May 2024, at the call of XR, under the motto 'Stop Fossil Subsidies', over 100 people gathered in Munchen (Bayern), to protest against fossil fuel subsidies. Approximately 70 demonstrators blocked a street, as 20 people did not comply with the police request to disperse, police officers physically took them off the street.

On 6 May 2024, around 100 students, as well as national deputy Louis Boyard (LFI), blocked access to the Sciences Po campus in Paris (Ile-de-France) to express solidarity with the Palestinian people, condemn what they deemed an Israeli 'genocide' of Gazans, and call on French universities to stop cooperating with Israeli universities. Police intervened twice to put an end to the action, dispersing the gatherings and arresting two people.

On 6 May 2024, police intervened to remove around 30 students blocking access to the Sciences Po campus in Reims (Grand Est). The protest started a few days earlier to express solidarity with the Palestinian people, condemn what they deemed an Israeli 'genocide' of Gazans, and call on French universities to stop cooperating with Israeli universities.

On 7 May 2024, six activists from the Emergency Break movement blocked in motorway exit in Kongens Lyngby, Hovedstaden, calling an end to motorway construction in the country. Later, police personnel removed activists from the scene, five activists were detained.

On 7 May 2024, police intervened to remove around 80 students blocking access to the Sorbonne University campus in Paris (Ile-de-France). Several protesters were arrested. The protest started a few days earlier to express solidarity with the Palestinian people, condemn what they deemed an Israeli 'genocide' of Gazans, and call on French universities to stop cooperating with Israeli universities.

On 7 May 2024, around 40 Sciences Po students blocked access to the Moulin de la Housse campus in Reims (Grand Est) to express solidarity with the Palestinian people, condemn what they deemed an Israeli 'genocide' of Gazans, and call on French universities to stop cooperating with Israeli universities. Police intervened to put an end to the action, dragging some occupants away.

On 7 May 2024, ETHZ students blocked access to their university campus in Zurich (Zurich) to express solidarity with the Palestinian people, condemn their fate in the Gaza Strip, and call on Swiss universities to stop cooperating with Israeli universities. Police intervened to put an end to the action and arrested around 30 people.

On 7 May 2024, about 200 protesters, including students, occupied the courtyard of the University Library in Utrecht (Utrecht) to call on the university to speak out about the situation in Gaza and to cut its ties with Israeli universities. Activists from Utrecht in Solidarity with Palestine (Utrecht in Solidariteit met Palestina) and End Fossil: Occupy participated in the protest. At 11 pm, the police evacuated the protest camp. Police arrested 50 people who had remained seated after being ordered to leave.

On 8 May 2024, people blocked the entrance to the Norwegian Parliament in Oslo, calling for an end to Norwegian companies' arms supplies to Israel and against a possible Israeli offensive on Rafah. Police later removed the activists from the site after they failed to comply with police orders to free the entrance.

On 8 May 2024, people, called by the neighbor's platform, held a protest at the occupied building of Otxandategi Tower in Berango (Pais Vasco) against its eviction by the police. Protesters set up barricades made up of bales and wooden structures to block the entrance. Two people were injured during the police intervention and have been transferred to the hospital. One person was arrested.

On 8 May 2024, students and university staff of Utrecht University marched through the city and then protested in front of the Drift 25 building of the University of Utrecht (Utrecht), with about 50 participants occupying the building, to call on the university to speak out about the situation in Gaza and cut its ties with Israeli universities. The University Board Chairman issued an ultimatum for the protesters to leave after midnight. During the night, police took 40 protesters away by city buses but did not detain them. Three protesters were arrested in a street nearby.

On 8 May 2024, at least 11 Last Generation activists staged a protest in Wien - Favoriten (Wien) to demand more climate action from the government and blocked the road at Matzleinsdorfer Platz/Triester Strasse and Gudrunstrasse. Several activists glued themselves onto the road, two concreted themselves onto the roof of a car and 9 chained themselves onto the car. The police intervened physically and dissolved the protest. Other Last Generation activists protested on the road A23 in Wien - Favoriten and blocked the road.

On 8 May 2024, at the call of 'Action Alliance 8 May' (Aktionsbundnis 8. Mai), around 610 people protested in Demmin (Mecklenburg-Vorpommern) for peace and against the presence of around 260 people gathered for a commemorative event (the deaths of a mass suicide in May 1945) at the call of The Homeland. Around 150 participants of the counter protest staged a sit-in to block the path of the Homeland event, causing the police to intervene physically and carry protesters off the road to clear the path.

On 8 May 2024, about 50 pro-Palestine activists staged a protest and set up a protest camp in a building of the University in Bremen (Bremen) emphasizing that criticism towards Israel is not anti-Semitism. The police intervened physically and carried some of the camp participants out of the building. The police intervention led to more people joining spontaneously the protest and about 100 people gathered in front of the building.

Around 9 May 2024 (as reported), students gathered at the Auditorium of the Conciliation in Roma - City Center (Lazio) to protest against the presence of the Minister 'for the family, birth rate and equal opportunities' during a meeting on trends of birth rates. Students were blocked by the police, and after being identified by police officers, which lasted about an hour, the youths walked away.

On 9 May 2024, between 10000 and 12000 people demonstrated in Malmo, Skane, against the participation of the Israeli artist in the Eurovision Song Contest and called for its boycott. On the same day, several protesters attempted to breach the security fence, resulting in police using pepper spray on them, no one was detained in connection with the incident.

On 9 May 2024, people demonstrated in Malmo, Skane, against the participation of the Israeli artist in the Eurovision Song Contest and called for its boycott. Later, security personnel removed activists in connection with the ban on Palestinian flags at the contest venue at the Malmo Arena.
