On 9 May 2024, around 10 Renovate Switzerland activists staged a blockade on the A2 motorway lane leading to the Gotthard Tunnel in Wassen (Uri), calling on the Swiss government to ban the sale of new cars powered by fossil fuels from 2025 and to invest 'massively' in non-polluting forms of mobility and public transport. Some activists stuck themselves to the road before being removed by police officers.

On 9 May 2024, around 100 people including members of self-managed social centers, gathered in Venezia (Veneto) to protest against the G7 Ministers' meeting on Justice. Protesters tried to reach the venue of the summit by breaking through the cordon in Calle nova de San Simon, but were prevented from doing so by police in anti-riot gear, who pushed them back and led several dispersion charges against the participants. Members of the self-managed social center of North East convened with the slogan 'Against the G7 of (IN)justice, against the war, against the genocide in Palestine, for the freedom and rights of all'.

On 9 May 2024, overnight, about 100 pro-Palestine activists, including BDS supporters, staged a protest on Alser Strasse/Spitalgasse in Wien - Inner City (Wien) and blocked the road. The context of the protest was the police eviction of a pro-Palestine protest camp on the University campus organized by groups such as BDS and 'The Spark' (Der Funke). During the eviction, police forces carried some of the 40 protesters away and kept three in police custody to establish their identity.

On 10 May 2024, at the call of 'Fridays for Israel', 150 people, including Bundestag Member (FDP), the chairwoman of the 'Jewish Student Union Germany' (Judische Studierendenunion Deutschland) and the DIG chairman, participated in a protest at Humboldt-University in Berlin - Mitte (Berlin) against hostility towards Israel at Berlin universities and criticized an open statement by university professors relating to pro-Palestinian protests. The participation of pro-Palestinian activists Udi Raz (Board member of the 'Jewish Voice for Just Peace in the Middle East' (Judische Stimme fur gerechten Frieden in Nahost) and provocations of three others lead to an intervention of the police who pulled the activists out of the crowd.

On 10 May 2024, about 50 environmental activists staged a sit-in on road 23 near the Tesla premises in Grunheide (Mark) (Brandenburg) against the planned expansion of the Tesla factory site to the forest near the factory and to demand a production turn-around. Around 20 activists glued themselves onto each other, others blocked the road with tree trunks. The police intervened physically, separated the protesters and carried them off the road.

On 11 May 2024, around 30 to 40 activists occupied the office of the national broadcaster in Pasila, Helsinki, demanding that Israeli artist be withdrawn from the Eurovision Song Contest. The activists were later removed by police personnel, several people were detained.

On 11 May 2024, people demonstrated outside the Malmo Arena in Malmo, Skane, to oppose the participation of the Israeli artist in the Eurovision Song Contest and called for its boycott. The activists were later removed from the road for failure to comply with police instructions.

On 11 May 2024, an unknown number of XR activists demonstrated in front of the ING office in Den Bosch (Noord-Brabant) to denounce the financing of fossil fuels. At least ten of them protested inside the building and when they did not leave, police arrested 10 people.

On 13 May 2024, protesters marched in Exarchia, Athens - Central Athens, under strong police presence, following the sudden expansion of the Exarchia square metro station construction site. The protesters were led by the Assembly 'No metro in Exarchia square' carrying a banner. There was verbal confrontation with police and 2 detentions.

On 14 May 2024, students blocked access to the Maurice Genevoix High School in Montrouge (Ile-de-France) to express solidarity with the Palestinian people and condemn what they deemed an Israeli 'genocide' of Gazans. Some students shot mortar fireworks and threw objects at the police. Police subsequently reacted, physically blocking and containing the demonstrators and forcing the demonstration to end. Five students were temporarily detained, and two were arrested on charges of resisting arrest.

On 14 May 2024, police intervened to remove around 50 students blocking access to the Uni Mail campus in Geneva (Geneve). The protest started a few days earlier to express solidarity with the Palestinian people, condemn what they deemed an Israeli 'genocide' of Gazans, and demand Swiss universities stop cooperating with Israeli universities. Some of the demonstrators were taken to the police headquarters in handcuffs, but no violent event was reported.

On 14 May 2024, on Nakba Day, about 40 pro-Palestinian activists blocked access to the Israeli embassy in Brussels - Uccle (Brussels) to demand that the federal government cut political, diplomatic and economic ties with Israel and take concrete steps towards a ceasefire in the Middle East. The police dispersed physically the demonstration that had not been authorized.

On 15 May 2024, more than 100 people, called by No More Involvement with Israel (Prou Complicitat amb Israel) held a protest in front of the Department of ACTION, the Agency for Enterprise Competitiveness of the Government of Catalonia in Barcelona - Gracia (Cataluna), to demand the regional Government the closure of its office in Tel-Aviv and to cut all ties with Israel. Some protesters occupied the building while others protested outside to call for the support of Palestinians. A police unit dispersed the protesters by pushing them away from the entrance with sticks and shields as well as with police baton blows.

On 15 May 2024, as part of a national demonstration and on the occasion of the commemoration of the Nakba, more than 400 people, including students and pro-Palestine activists, took to the streets of Torino (Piemonte) to demonstrate against the war in Gaza, the massacre of Palestinian civilians, the University of Turin, and the Israeli government. Demonstrators reached the Mole and hoisted the Palestinian flag on top of the monument. Moreover, protesters tried to set the EU banner on fire but were prevented from doing so by the police.

On 15 May 2024, about 150 pro-Palestinian protesters protested in front of a building of the University of Utrecht in Utrecht (Utrecht) and at least 25 people occupied the building inside to call on their university to cut ties with Israel. Police intervened and took away protesters by bus, estimated to contain around 40 pro-Palestinian activists. When the protesters tried to block the bus, police used batons against the protesters.

On 15 May 2024, pro-Palestine protesters, representatives of Palestine Action, and members of the Palestinian community staged a protest and scaled the roof of the Teledyne company in Bradford (England) over the company's suspected ties to Israel. Police forces put and end to the demonstration and arrested 4 people.

On 15 May 2024, pro-Palestine protesters blockaded the entrance of the Thales factory, a defense and security company on Linthouse Road, Govan, Glasgow (Scotland) to demand a ceasefire in Gaza and to disrupt the supply of arms to Israel. Demonstrators claimed they were taking action to create their own arms embargo on Israel. Police forces intervenined, put an end to the demonstration and arrested at least 4 protesters.

On 16 May 2024, dozens of people, called by Housing Union of Raval (Sindicat d'Habitatge del Raval), Socialist Youth Organization (Organizacion Juvenil Socialista) and Old Massana (Antiga Massana), held a protest at the district headquarters in Barcelona - Ciutat Vella (Cataluna) against the eviction of La Tancada, a municipal building occupied by 37 individuals, some of them migrants. Police intervened with baton blows to stop the protesters.

On 16 May 2024, at least 13 Last Generation activists staged a protest in Condotti Street in Roma - City Center (Lazio) to demand more climate attention and highlight the disparities and social injustice of the current system by trowing red paint on the shop windows of several high-end fashion boutiques and shops, including Armani's. The police intervened and took 13 activists to the police headquarters to identify and report them.

On 17 May 2024, dozens of pro-Palestinian protesters have set up tents in the courtyard of a University of Amsterdam (UvA) building at Oudemanhuispoort in Amsterdam (Noord-Holland) to call for attention to the situation in Palestine and to demand that police stay away from protesters. Police put an end to the action with truncheon and pepper spray. Later, protesters participated to a spontaneous sit-in in front of the city hall. Police forced the group out, using truncheons, and arrested one person.

On 18 May 2024, 10 anti-bullfighting (corrida) activists staged a protest outside the bullring in Nimes (Occitanie) to denounce the practice and demand its prohibition. Seven participants were arrested by the police.

On 18 May 2024, thousands of pro-Palestine protesters marched through the city center in London - Westminster (England) to call for a ceasefire in Gaza and to mark the 76th anniversary of Nakba - the mass displacement of people after the creation of Israel in 1948. PSC Organized the protest. A group of pro-Israeli protesters also gathered at Piccadilly Circus for a counter-demonstration. The protest was peaceful, though police forces arrested seven people in total.

On 18 May 2024, around a dozen Last Generation and XR activists staged a protest on the A10 highway near Hallein (Salzburg) against the standstill in climate policy and to call for climate protection to be enshrined in the Austrian constitution, while blocking the road by gluing themselves onto it. Passers-by tried pulling activists off the road. The police intervened physically, dispersed the protest and carried the participants off the road.

On 18 May 2024, around 15 people staged a protest in Barmbek Nord in Hamburg - Hamburg-Nord (Hamburg) against right-wing extremism, gathering around an AfD election stand to disrupt the work of its affiliates. The police intervened, dispersed the protest, and arrested one person for resisting. AfD affiliates said Antifa and Black Bloc activists were behind the demonstration.

On 18 May 2024, about 40 to 50 people, including Last Generation activists, staged a protest on the Leipziger Ring in Leipzig (Sachsen), blocking the road, to call for more climate protection and warn of the dangers of climate change. The police called for the clearing of the street and carried 15 protesters off the road.

On 18 May 2024, 8 Last Generation activists staged a protest at the airport in Munchen (Bayern), 6 of them gluing themselves to feeder runways, causing the airport to close down for 2 hours, to draw attention to the environmental impact of the aviation industry and to call for more decisive political action against climate change. The police arrested the protesters.

On 18 May 2024, Last Generation activists staged a protest on Frankenschnellweg in Nurnberg (Bayern), causing traffic disruptions. Several activists refused to leave the street after the official end of the protest, police intervened and carried them off the road.

On 18 May 2024, up to 100 climate activists, including Last Generation members, participated in protests inside the terminal at the airport in Stuttgart (Baden-Wurttemberg), demanding measures against growing air traffic and calling for an end to private jets, short-haul flights, and subsidized kerosene, some refusing to leave the airport after the demonstration, causing the police to intervene and take them outside. At the same time and as part of the same, coordinated demonstration, around 75 climate activists, including Last Generation and MLPD, participated in a protest in front of the airport and the General Aviation Terminal, without any incidents.

On 19 May 2024, at the call of 'Initiative Hambach24', up to 625 people, including far-right activists and system-critical groups, as well as COVID-19 deniers, participated in a protest in Neustadt an der Weinstrasse (Rheinland-Pfalz), calling for the abolition of NATO, a stop to arms deliveries to Ukraine and the prosecution of Israel for 'genocide.' 31 people staged a counter-demonstration and blocked the path of the demonstration. As they did not leave after being asked to do so several times by the police, the police intervened, carried the counter-demonstrators off the street and took some away.

On 20 May 2024, 14 Last Generation activists demonstrated outside the Ministry of Justice in Roma - City Center (Lazio) to demand more climate action and social justice. Two activists sprayed black charcoal paint on the wall of the ministry, while other activists hung and glued posters. Some participants were immobilized by the police.

On 21 May 2024, around 100 students protested on the university campus of the University of Porto in Porto (Porto) with an ongoing student encampment in support of Palestine and Gaza. Police intervened and cleared the premises.

On 21 May 2024, about 60 No TAV activists demonstrated against the Turin-Lyon high-speed train project in San Didero (Piemonte). Some demonstrators tried to reach the construction site's fence but were repelled by the police, who used water cannons to disperse the crowd.

On 22 May 2024, around 50 activists occupied the Social Sciences Institute at Humboldt University in Berlin - Charlottenburg-Wilmersdorf (Berlin), to protest against Israel's military action in Palestine, while demanding unconditional solidarity with the Palestinian people. The police physically intervened to end the pro-Palestinian protest.

On 23 May 2024, activists gathered in Prague, protesting against the ongoing pre-election meeting of the SPD party, criticizing especially their pro-Russian position regarding the ongoing war in Ukraine. Three of them were detained for attempts to pelt eggs at the podium.

On 23 May 2024, at the call of the Student Committee for Palestine (Comite Etudiant pour la Palestine), several hundred students gathered inside an auditorium and blocked access to the Saint-Charles campus of the Aix-Marseille University in Marseille (Provence-Alpes-Cote d'Azur) to express solidarity with Palestinian people, condemn what they deemed an Israeli 'genocide' of Gazans, and demanded French universities to stop cooperating with Israeli universities. Police intervened to remove around 42 students on the same day.

On 23 May 2024, pro-Palestine students at Oxford University held a sit-in protest in an administration office building in Wellington Square in Oxford (England) in support of Palestine. Police forces intervened and arrested 16 protesters.

On 23 May 2024, around 60 left-wing activists, including Antifa affiliates, gathered outside the 'Mutter Wittig' restaurant in Bochum (Nordrhein-Westfalen) to protest against a meeting of JA affiliates at the venue. The police physically intervened to prevent clashes between the demonstrators and the meeting's participants. A member of JA later said that a tire of his car had been slashed, something the police were investigating at the time of reporting.

On 23 May 2024, the police forcibly evacuated the Institute for Social Sciences at Humboldt University in Berlin - Mitte (Berlin), where the previous day around 50 students started an occupation demanding a ceasefire in Gaza and an arms embargo on Israel. The police physically removed protesters, injuring a video journalist and several protesters during the intervention.

On 24 May 2024, an unknown number of students and Fossil Free activists who had been occupying the University of Ghent in Gent (Vlaanderen) since 7 May 2024 occupied the university's rectorate, to support Palestinians and demand that the University cut its ties with Israel. About five students climbed onto the roof of the building and waved Palestinian flags. Some windows were daubed with red paint. The Rector decided to call in the police, who arrested 10 activists, who later denounced the police action as disproportionate.

On 24 May 2024, about 25 students who had been occupying the De Valk College building of the University of Leuven in Leuven (Vlaanderen) since 13 May 2024 decided to occupy the entrance hall of the rector's office. They organized the action to show support to the Palestinians as well as to the pro-Palestinian protesters who were arrested earlier that day at the University of Ghent and to demand that their university cut its ties with Israel. The University called the police, who came to drag the protesters away from the rectorate.

On 25 May 2024, nearly 1,000 people, including SLT activists, gathered in Gennevilliers (Ile-de-France) to protest against the planned construction of an XXL Green Dock, i.e. a giant logistics warehouse. A small group of people broke away from the procession and attempted to head towards the port. Police intervened and 59 people were arrested.

On 25 May 2024, Last Generation activists disrupted the opening ceremony of the Krems-Au retention basin in Kirchdorf an der Krems (Oberosterreich), demanding climate action while criticizing political decisions regarding environmental policies. Some activists were physically removed from the stage of the ceremony by police officers.

On 25 May 2024, Extinction Rebellion associated groups blocked access to the Copenhagen Airport in Kastrup demanding to ban private jets and tax frequent flyers. Police later removed the activists from the site after they failed to comply with police demands.

On 25 May 2024, 64 Last Generation activists blocked a street outside the main train station in Berlin - Mitte (Berlin), demanding climate action and disrupting traffic. The police intervened as the area was needed as an evacuation route for the nearby Democracy Festival, which was celebrating the 75th anniversary of the Basic Law, carrying some demonstrators off the street.

On 26 May 2024, in the evening, police evacuated around 30 students from the Ecole Normale Superieure (ENS) University Campus in Paris (Ile-de-France). They were demonstrating to condemn the Israeli military campaign in and around Gaza and demand an end to Sciences Po's collaboration with all 'institutions or entities complicit in the systemic oppression of the Palestinian people.

On 27 May 2024, people demonstrated in front of the Israeli embassy in Hellerup, Hovedstaden, to show support and solidarity with the Palestinian people and to oppose the Israeli offensive in Gaza and Rafah. Later, several activists attempted to enter the embassy premises, while others started throwing red paint balloons at the embassy. Police intervened and dispersed the protesters, three people were arrested.

On 27 May 2024, in the morning, police evacuated students from the Department of Social Sciences of the University of Basel in Basel (Basel-Stadt). They were demonstrating to condemn the Israeli military campaign in and around Gaza. Various people had been identified and stopped in front of the building.

On 27 May 2024, at the call of Palestine Emergency (Urgence Palestine), in the evening, tens of thousands of people gathered in Paris (Ile-de-France) to express solidarity with the Palestinian people, condemn what they deemed an Israeli 'genocide' of Gazans, and condemn the Israeli air strike on a camp for displaced Palestinians in the southern Gaza city of Rafah. Several wild demonstrations then broke out from the square, towards La Republique Square, around Chatelet and Rivoli, in the Opera district and in the Montmartre district. The police intervened using tear gas, while no injuries nor fatalities were reported.

On 27 May 2024, students, called by End Fossil: Occupy, occupied the Nova University in Lisboa (Lisboa) to demonstrate in support of Palestine and against Israel amid the Israel-Hamas war and to call for an end to the use of fossil fuels. Police detained five activists and charged demonstrators with batons.

On 27 May 2024, activists from the Restore Wetlands Movement demonstrated at the Finnish embassy in Stockholm, demanding that the Finnish state-owned peat harvesting company be shut down due to its alleged negative environmental impact. The activists entered the premises of the embassy while some of the activists chained themselves. Police later removed the activists, five people were arrested.

On 27 May 2024, between 30 and 50 students occupied a wing on the second floor of the Erasmus building of the Radboud University in Nijmegen (Gelderland) and between 100 and 200 students gathered around them to express solidarity with Palestinian people and to demand that the University cuts its ties with Israel. There are pro-Palestinian encampments on the campus since 13 May 2024. The university asked the protesters to leave but they did not comply. Thirty police agents forced through a barricade and thirteen protesters who refused to leave were carried outside by officers and taken by bus to the train station, where they were released.

On 28 May 2024, at the call of LFI, NPA, FO, Palestinian Revolution (Revolution Palestinienne), and UJFP - French Jewish Union for Peace (Union Juive Francaise pour la Paix), around 4,500 people demonstrated in Paris (Ile-de-France) to demand a ceasefire in Gaza, express solidarity with the Palestinian people, and condemn what they deemed a 'genocide' of Gazans by the Israeli army. Some demonstrators blocked access to the bypass highway before being removed by the BRAV-M police unit. In the city center, police used tear gas to disperse the demonstration.

On 28 May 2024, over 10,000 pro-Palestine protesters descended on Downing Street and Whitehall in London - Westminster (England) against the Israeli forces' attack on Rafah refugee camps, to call for an immediate ceasefire in Gaza, and calling to stop arming Israel. PSC organized the protest. Police forces were present at the scene and arrested 40 protesters. One officer sustained a serious facial injury after she was hit by a bottle thrown from the crowd, while two officers had minor injuries.

On 28 May 2024, an unknown number of people, among which students, demonstrated in front of the Israeli Embassy in Brussels - Uccle (Brussels) to express solidarity with Palestinian people and to condemn the Israeli attack that took place in Rafah. The event was organized by Brussels Against Genocide and Universitaire Populaire. The demonstration was not authorized. When the demonstrators refused to leave, police used pepper spray and water cannons to keep the demonstrators away from the Embassy. One bottle was thrown at the mayor, who came on the spot to assess the situation, and police used batons against one demonstrator.

On 28 May 2024, an unknown number of people protested in front of the House of Representatives in Den Haag (Zuid-Holland) to express solidarity with the Palestinian people. Police moved a group standing behind the building to the front. In the evening, police asked the demonstrators to put away banners and flags and leave. When the demonstrators refused to do so, the police surrounded them and arrested dozens of people and took them away by bus. Two people were arrested for insulting police officers.

On 29 May 2024, people demonstrated at the KTH Royal Institute of Technology in Stockholm during a speech by the Christian Democratic Party's chairwoman, Ebba Busch. The activists showed their support and solidarity with Palestine amid the ongoing Israeli offensive in Gaza and Rafah. Later, the police dispersed the protest, at least 20 people were detained and 3 activists were arrested.

On 29 May 2024, around 30 students, called by Encampment for Palestine (Acampada per Palestina), held a protest at the campus of the University of Islas Baleares (UIB) in Ibiza (Islas Baleares) to demand the university's management board to end all ties with Israeli institutions complicit with the 'genocide' in Gaza. Some protesters chained themselves to the rectorate gates. Police intervened by cutting the chains and removing the protesters from the building.

On 29 May 2024, around 1,000 people, including UNEF affiliates, demonstrated in Paris (Ile-de-France) to demand a ceasefire in Gaza, express solidarity with the Palestinian people, and condemn what they deemed a 'genocide' of Gazans by the Israeli army. Police used tear gas to disperse the action. One student sustained an arm injury.

On 29 May 2024, at the call of AFPS, more than 70 people demonstrated in Vannes (Bretagne) to demand a ceasefire in Gaza, express solidarity with the Palestinian people, and condemn what they deemed a 'genocide' of Gazans by the Israeli army. Police used tear gas to disperse the action.

On 29 May 2024, thousands of people, among which students, demonstrated in front of the Israeli Embassy in Brussels - Uccle (Brussels) to express solidarity with Palestinian people, to condemn the attack that took place in Rafah and to demand that Belgium cut all ties with Israel. A group of demonstrators provoked the police not following orders and the police responded with tear gas. After that, violence escalated and police and demonstrators clashed. Demonstrators threw projectiles, and the water cannon being used by the police. The event was also a reaction to the protest that took place the day before during which the police used the water cannon against the protesters.

On 29 May 2024, about 30 to 35 people staged a pro-Palestine protest in front of the Technical University in Wien - Wieden (Wien), set up a protest camp in solidarity with Palestine, and chained themselves to one another, to demonstrate against what they claimed to be a genocide in Gaza and the university's persisting cooperation with Israeli institutions and weapon manufacturers. The police intervened, dissolved the protest, and temporarily arrested 16 people.

On 29 May 2024, several Shor members protested in the City Gates area by blocking Dacia Boulevard in Chisinau - Botanica against the visit of the US Secretary of State Antony Blinken. The councilor of the leader (Bashkan) of Gagauzia and other representatives from Gagauzia were also present at the event. Since the protest went against the decision of the Chisinau City Hall and the requirements of the Police not to block the carriageway, some of the protesters were detained.

On 29 May 2024, about 30, some of them partly masked, people staged a pro-Palestine protest at the university in Bonn (Nordrhein-Westfalen) and blocked the entrance to the main building with construction fences, some climbing onto a balcony, to call for a free Palestine, an end to the university's cooperation with the DIG and supporters of the weapon lobby. The police physically intervened to dissolve the blockade and the pro-Palestine protest camp organized by 'Students for Palestine' in the city's Hofgarten area. At the same time, about 50 to 70 people staged another pro-Palestine protest at the other side of the main building. People, including JU, JL, the university groups of CDU and FDP and the Jewish University Community, participated in a pro-Israel protest to call for the end of the protest camp.

On 30 May 2024, police personnel dispersed a pro-Palestinian student encampment at the University of Lund campus in Lund, Skane. At least 40 people were detained after they failed to comply with police demands.

On 30 May 2024, five pro-Palestinian demonstrators entered a university office building in Umea, Vasterbotten, and attempted to barricade themselves. Later, police later removed the activists from the site.

On 30 May 2024, a group of students staged a protest performance in an attempt to disrupt a board meeting at the University of Tampere in Tampere, Pirkanmaa. The activists called on the university management to impose a total ban on academic cooperation with Israeli universities. Police later removed the activists from the venue after they failed to comply with police demands and leave the premises.

On 30 May 2024, people demonstrated in Paris (Ile-de-France) to demand a ceasefire in Gaza, express solidarity with the Palestinian people, and condemn what they deemed a 'genocide' of Gazans by the Israeli army. Police used tear grenades to put an end to the action.

On 30 May 2024, under the motto 'Rethink Europe' and at the call of the AfD, around 100 people participated in a rally in Dusseldorf (Nordrhein-Westfalen) ahead of the 2024 European elections. At the call of the alliance 'Dusseldorf stands up' (Dusseldorf stellt sich quer), around 750 people, including Antifa activists, participated in a counter-demonstration against the AfD, exclusion, agitation, and right-wing extremism, as well as for respect, some staging a sit-in. The police intervened, dissolved the sit-in, and pulled a participant out of the Antifa protest.

On 31 May 2024, police intervened to remove around 50 students occupying the university campus the call of CEP HES - HES Student Coordination for Palestine (Coordination Etudiante pour la Palestine-HES) in Bern (Bern) to express solidarity with the Palestinian people, condemn what they deemed an Israeli 'genocide' of Gazans, and demand Swiss universities to stop cooperating with Israeli universities.

On 31 May 2024, around 100 people demonstrated and blocked traffic in Gothenburg (Goteborg) to show support and solidarity with the Palestinian people and to oppose the Israeli offensive in Gaza and Rafah. The police later removed those activists who refused to comply with police demands and unblock traffic.

On 31 May 2024, activists, called by EncampmentxPalestine (AcampadaxPalestina), held a protest in Madrid - Centro (Madrid) to demand the government and universities the end of all ties with Israeli companies and institutions. Activists displayed a banner on a building's facade. 3 people were arrested.

On 31 May 2024, demonstrators, including members of the Iceland-Palestine Association, demonstrated in Reykjavik to show support and solidarity with the people of Palestine and to oppose Israeli offensive in Gaza and Rafah. Later, the police used pepper spray against protesters for failing to follow police instructions. No one was arrested in connection with the demonstration.

On 31 May 2024, about 500 people protested in front of the Embassy of the United States in Brussels - Ville de Bruxelles (Brussels) to express solidarity with the Palestinian people and to denounce the United States' 'complicity in the genocide' as well as US arms deliveries to Israel. The event was organized by Intal and the Belgian-Palestinian Association (Association Belgo-Palestinienne). The demonstration was authorized until 6 pm and took place peacefully. After 6 pm, according to the police, a group wanted to start a parade and did not comply with the police orders to leave. Police administratively detained 30 people. According to the protesters, police intervened harshly and escalated the situation by kicking and punching.

On 31 May 2024, fourteen activists from the Emergency Break movement blocked a major road in Copenhagen, calling for an end to motorway construction in the country. Police later removed the activists and temporarily detained them.

On 1 June 2024, activists from Youth Demands held a demonstration and tried to block the York Road in London - Lambeth (England) to take direct action against the ongoing conflict in Gaza, condemning Israel and expressing solidarity with Palestine, by occupying roads and bridges. Police forces intervened and arrested nine people for breaching the Public Order Act.

On 1 June 2024, at the call of far-right activist Tommy Robinson, thousands of far-right protesters and groups from across the UK linked to football hooliganism marched from Victoria to Parliament Square, where they held a rally, in London - Westminster (England) prior to the final of the Champions League. Some participants chanted anti-Muslim slogans and 'We want our country back', while some carried a banner reading 'This is London, not Londonistan', and others waved British flags. Around 300 people attended a static counter-demonstration in Whitehall organized by SUTR with speeches from anti-racism activists. Two participants in the larger demonstration were arrested by the police, though the reasons were not specified.

On 1 June 2024, several dozen people, including around 12 Last Generation activists, staged a protest outside the National Council building in Wien - Inner City (Wien), gluing themselves to one another, to denounce the climate crisis and the government's inaction. The police intervened physically, and dissolved the protest by picking up the activists, before loading them onto a police van.

On 1 June 2024, under the motto 'Disobedient assembly: Stop fossil subsidies - New center without cars', about 30 Last Generation activists staged a protest in Ulm (Baden-Wurttemberg), blocking a road, to call for climate and traffic shift. The police intervened physically, carried the protesters off the street, and took around half a dozen participants to the police station for identification checks.

On 1 June 2024, dozens of XR activists protested on the Oversteek bridge in Nijmegen (Gelderland) to oppose the construction of a new gas power plant. Some demonstrators tied themselves to the bridge, while about 80 people participated in a demonstration supporting the blockade. They demanded the authorities stop investing in fossil fuels. Police arrested all the protesters on the bridge.

On 3 June 2024, members of the Primavera anarchist libertarian squat rallied at the university campus attempting to reoccupy a space in the School of Theology at the Aristotle University of Thessaloniki, which was raided by police earlier in the morning, following a request by the university authorities. Police seized propaganda material and several helmets. When MAT riot police returned to clear the squat, the protesters left of their own accord.

On 3 June 2024, a group of pro-Palestinian protesters attempted to occupy a graduation venue in Uppsala calling for an academic boycott of Israel. Police later removed the activists from the venue after they failed to comply with police demands and leave the premises.

On 3 June 2024, about 30 people participated in a protest action at the University of Technology in Delft (Zuid-Holland) to express solidarity with the Palestinian people and to call on their university to cut all ties with Israeli institutions. In the evening, police were dispatched to the scene to clear a building of occupants, arresting 15 participants. The encampment at the University of Technology of Delft started on 23 May 2024.

On 3 June 2024, an unknown number of protesters tried to disturb a conference on the future of Israel and Palestine in Brussels - Ixelles (Brussels) to oppose the presence of a former ambassador for Israel. The protesters have opposed the event for weeks and on 3 June 2024, the Free University of Brussels (ULB) announced that the conference was moved to Flagey Square. There, the police had sealed the neighborhood and did not allow the protesters near the event. Some protesters stayed in the surrounding streets, some went back to the university and some headed to the Israeli Embassy in Brussels - Uccle. Police arrested nine people.

On 4 June 2024, a group of pro-Palestinian protesters attempted to occupy a venue at Stockholm University in Stockholm to demand the university management to impose a total ban on academic cooperation with Israeli universities. Police later removed the activists from the venue after they failed to comply with police demands and leave the premises.

On 4 June 2024, an unknown number of people blocked a roundabout under the Bellevue bridge in Gent (Vlaanderen) to express solidarity with the Palestinian people and call on Belgium to cut all ties with Israel. The police intervened and arrested about 40 people.

On 4 June 2024, about 40 people, including XR activists, occupied the building of the umbrella organization Universities of the Netherlands in Den Haag (Zuid-Holland) to express solidarity with Palestinian people and call on Dutch universities to cut all ties with Israeli organizations. The protesters remained inside and outside the building, while another group was demonstrating nearby to support the activists. The police intervened and arrested about 50 people, using the aerial platform of a fire truck to take down activists who had climbed onto the building's balcony, while one person was also arrested on the square nearby on suspicion of insulting an officer.

On 5 June 2024, around 15 pro-Palestinian protesters entered and attempted to occupy the Linnaeus University in Vaxjo, Kronoberg. Police later removed the activists from the site after they failed to comply with police demands to leave the premises.

On 5 June 2024, a group of pro-Palestinian protesters entered and attempted to occupy a venue at the Stockholm University in Stockholm. Police later removed the activists from the site after they failed to comply with police demands to leave the premises.

On 5 June 2024, police intervened in Saix (Occitanie) and arrested 5 people occupying a piece of land to protest against the construction of the A69 highway between Toulouse and Castres, which they deemed damaging to the environment.

On 5 June 2024, about 20 protesters entered the Thomas Aquinas building of the Radboud University, barricaded the doors and spray-painted some of the building's walls in Nijmegen (Gelderland) to express solidarity with the Palestinian people and call on the university to cut all ties with Israeli institutions. According to the university, protesters also opened the fire hose inside the building. When the police entered the building, the protesters were gone. Police then dismantled the tent camp outside where about 100 protesters were staying, after which demonstrators peacefully left.

On 6 June 2024, around 20 people held a protest in Porto (Porto) during an AD party rally, in which the President of the European Commission was participating. Protesters called for a Free Palestine from Israel's bombardments and tried to interrupt the rally, leading to the intervention of the police, during which one person was arrested for resisting and 'coercing' a police officer.

On 6 June 2024, people gathered in Dusseldorf (Nordrhein-Westfalen) to protest for peace and against arms deliveries, while seeking to peacefully disrupt the FDP's final campaign event three days before the 2024 European elections, notably during speeches by FDP lead candidate Marie-Agnes Strack-Zimmermann and party chairman Christian Lindner. The protesters used heckling, whistles, and megaphones, leading to several participants being carried away from the political meeting by the police.

On 6 June 2024, around 50 students broke into the Helene-Boucher school and occupied the building in Paris (Ile-de-France) to demand a ceasefire in Gaza, express solidarity with the Palestinian people, and condemn what they deemed a 'genocide' of Gazans by the Israeli army. Police used tear gas to disperse the action and arrested 50 students. Some police officers claimed they were attacked by students, while the latter claimed the police intervened brutally. Video footage recorded by students revealed that police officers used tear gas inside the school, pointed at students with their revolvers and rubber-bullet guns, and insulted them while they performed body searches.

On 7 June 2024, a group of pro-Palestinian protesters entered and attempted to occupy a venue at the KTH Royal Institute of Technology in Stockholm. Police later removed the activists from the site after they failed to comply with police demands, at least 20 people were detained.

On 7 June 2024, an unknown number of XR and Quit with Coal activists blocked the N205 road in front of the province hall in Haarlem (Noord-Holland) to demand the closure of the Tata Steel Factory, citing environmental concerns, while supporters also gathered at the nearby parc of Haarlemmerhout. According to the activists, when they installed their tents, police cleared them and proceeded to arrest some of the participants.

On 8 June 2024, 17 Last Generation activists protested in Mainz (Rheinland-Pfalz), initially causing traffic disruptions by occupying streets. The police carried some activists away from the street and initiated 24 administrative proceedings.

On 10 June 2024, overnight, several dozen students occupied the Dean's Office of the Faculty of Philology of the University of Sevilla in Sevilla (Andalucia) in solidarity with Palestine and against Israeli violence amid the ongoing war in the Gaza Strip. At around 1 am, police entered the building and cleared it of the occupants, who blocked some of the entrances, forcefully removing some of the demonstrators, injuring at least one student.

On 10 June 2024, at the call of CGT, UNEF, and other organizations, around 3,000 people gathered on Republic Square and subsequently marched in Paris (Ile-de-France) to protest against far-right ideology and in support of an open society. The gathering took place after the National Rally (RN) came first in the European elections in France and President Emmanuel Macron announced the dissolution of the National Assembly on 9 June, raising fears of a government led by the far-right party. Towards the end of the demonstration, police intervened and used tear gas to disperse the action. Earlier that day, around 100 high school students gathered outside the Henri-IV school in Paris (Ile-de-France) for the same motives.

On 11 June 2024, a group of protesters entered the University of Gothenburg building in Gothenburg (Goteborg) and chained themselves demanding an academic boycott and an end to all cooperation with Israel. Police cut the chains and dragged them out of the building.

On 11 June 2024, several thousand people gathered on Republic Square in Paris (Ile-de-France) to demonstrate against far-right ideology and in support of an open society. The gathering took place after the National Rally (RN) came first in the European elections in France and President Emmanuel Macron announced the dissolution of the National Assembly on 9 June, raising fears of a government led by the far-right party. Towards the end of the demonstration, police intervened and used tear gas to disperse the action. Rioters clashed with the police.

On 11 June 2024, environmental activists, including Extinction Rebellion members, staged traffic blockades in various locations of Helsinki as a part of the 'Storm Warning' campaign aimed to draw attention to environmental issues and calling on the government to end state subsidies that are harmful to the environment. Police later removed those activists who did not comply with police demands. Total of 137 people were arrested.
On 12 June 2024, police personnel broke up a student protest encampment outside of the University of Helsinki in Helsinki. Around 30 people were removed from the site while no one was detained.

On 12 June 2024, police forces upon request of the President of the University of Warsaw forcibly removed students protesting at the premises and blocking entrances to the campus. The students were declaring solidarity with civilians in Gaza and demanding immediate suspension of cooperation with Israeli academic institutions due to the ongoing violence.

On 12 June 2024, people demonstrated in various parts of Reykjavik to show support and solidarity with Palestine. Later, a group of demonstrators prevented access to the prime minister's car, resulting in police dispersing the crowd and using pepper spray on the demonstrators.

On 12 June 2024, an unknown number of people occupied the Faculty of Letters of the RijksUniversiteit in Groningen (Groningen) to express their support to the Palestinian people and to demand that the university cut all ties with Israel. Outside the building, between 100 and 200 people were present, and many of them were trying to enter the premises to join the protesters. The police used truncheon and some protesters insulted and spat at the officers. Police evicted the protesters and arrested two people. The mayor then decided that the pro-Palestinian encampment set up on 13 May 2024 must end, and the protesters left before the police came.

On 12 June 2024, 16 people staged a protest and occupied lecture halls at the university in Bonn (Nordrhein-Westfalen) to protest against Israel's military campaign in the Gaza Strip. The police intervened physically, dissolved the protest, and recorded the personal details of several demonstrators. Simultaneously, around 20 to 40 people participated in a protest outside the building in solidarity with the squatters.

On 13 June 2024, law enforcers removed tents near the government's office in Prague, occupied by an anti-government oppositionist. During the eviction, a group of his supporters gathered nearby; two of them were detained for public disobedience.

On 13 June 2024, people conducted a series of single-person protests in front of the regional administration building in Samara (Samara) against a proposed bill that would allow to euthanize stray animals. The police detained three of the protesters.

On 13 June 2024, about 10 students and pro-Palestine activists chained themselves to the gates of the Polytechnic University in Torino (Piemonte) to demonstrate against the killing of Palestinian people and the University management's unwillingness to end cooperation with Israeli-based companies and Universities. Professor and No Tav activist Massimo Zucchetti joined the protest. Activists also attempted to enter the rector's office but were prevented by security guards who pushed the activists back. A demonstrator was injured. Demonstrators attempted again to enter the building in the afternoon but were prevented by police in riot gear and pushed back with batons.

On 14 June 2024, students set up a protest camp outside the Swedish parliament in Stockholm, calling on the government to impose sanctions on Israel. Police later intervened and removed the activists from the site.

On 14 June 2024, Last Generation activists staged a protest in Wien - Alsergrund (Wien) against politicians' inactivity regarding the climate crisis, to call for immediate climate protection measures, and to show solidarity with five fellow activists detained at a police detention center for protesting against the Austrian government's inaction regarding climate protection. Several of the participants glued themselves to the street, and 12 were arrested by the police.

On 14 June 2024, under the motto 'Siegen stands up for Gaza', around 150 people participated in a pro-Palestine protest in Siegen (Nordrhein-Westfalen) in solidarity with the civilians in Gaza, some using anti-Semitic slogans. The police intervened, cordoned off Markt Strasse, arrested one participant and intervened in five cases because of initial suspicion of a criminal offense, including punishable verbal and pictorial statements. Under the motto 'Vigil against all forms of anti-Semitism', up to 45 people staged a counter-demonstration.

On 15 June 2024, people protested in the Nikolaevka district of Krasnoyarsk (Krasnoyarsk) against the demolition of their houses and the changes in the city's building code that would take over green areas, stores and other locations for new construction. They were dispersed by the police.

On 15 June 2024, around 400 people, including PS affiliates and national deputy Michel Sala (LFI), demonstrated in Ales (Occitanie). The event was part of a nationwide wave of demonstrations against racism, far-right ideology, and in support of an open society called by CGT, CFDT, FSU, UNSA, and SUD. The event took place after the National Rally (RN) came first in the European elections in France and President Emmanuel Macron announced the dissolution of the National Assembly on 9 June, raising fears of a government led by the far-right party. The demonstrators demanded all parties from the left to unite in a 'Popular Front' (Front Populaire) ahead of the upcoming legislative elections. Police arrested 3 people.

On 15 June 2024, between 15,000 and 50,000 people, including students, demonstrated in Toulouse (Occitanie). The event was part of a nationwide wave of demonstrations against racism, far-right ideology, and in support of an open society called by CGT, CFDT, FSU, UNSA, and SUD. The event took place after the National Rally (RN) came first in the European elections in France and President Emmanuel Macron announced the dissolution of the National Assembly on 9 June, raising fears of a government led by the far-right party. The demonstrators demanded all parties from the left to unite in a 'Popular Front' (Front Populaire) ahead of the upcoming legislative elections. Police arrested 3 people.

On 15 June 2024, Last Generation and XR activists staged a protest in the Schanzenviertel area of Hamburg - Hamburg-Mitte (Hamburg) and blocked a road for environmental reasons, calling for an end to fossil fuels, more justice, and a speed limit on highways. The police intervened physically, carried protesters off the road and encircled other activists in front of a pharmacy.

On 17 June 2024, pro-Palestine students from University College Cork held a protest outside the Gluckman Gallery on the university campus in Cork (Cork) to oppose a visit by Ireland's Minister for Foreign Affairs. Protesters demanded 'No government politicians on campus until the Occupied Territories Bill is enacted'. Police forces arrested two demonstrators.

On 17 June 2024, activists from Palestine Action held a protest outside the Scotiabank building in the Bishopsgate area of London - City of London (England) against the bank's investments in Israel. Protesters spray-painted over the building and police forces arrested 10 participants.

On 17 June 2024, activists from the Emergency Break movement blocked a motorway exit in Herlev, Hovedstaden, calling for an end to motorway construction in the country due to environmental concerns. Police later removed the activists from the site after they failed to comply with police demands, five people were detained.

On 18 June 2024, activists from the Emergency Break movement blocked a motorway in Copenhagen to demand an end to motorway construction and to oppose the government's plan to build 15 more motorways in the country. Police later removed the activists from the site after they failed to comply with police demands, six people were detained.

On 19 June 2024, around 50 pro-Palestinian demonstrators blocked the entrance to the Danish Parliament in Copenhagen to oppose the Danish government's stance on the Palestinian-Israeli conflict and the export of Danish military aircraft components to Israel. Police later removed the activists from the site after they failed to comply with police demands, and around 27 people were detained.

On 19 June 2024, at the call of the local Antifa, people gathered in Toulouse (Occitanie). The event was part of a nationwide wave of demonstrations against racism, far-right ideology, and in support of an open society. The event took place after the National Rally (RN) came first in the European elections in France and President Emmanuel Macron announced the dissolution of the National Assembly on 9 June, raising fears of a government led by the far-right party. The demonstrators demanded all parties from the left to unite in a 'Popular Front' (Front Populaire) ahead of the upcoming legislative elections. As the demonstration was unauthorized, police intervened quickly to disperse the demonstrators and handed out fines to the participants.

On 19 June 2024, activists from Just Stop Oil sprayed orange paint on the prehistoric Stonehenge stones in Amesbury (England) to call on the new British government to agree to a plan to end the extraction and burning of oil, gas, and coal by 2030. The group said it used orange corn flour paint to spray onto the stones to prevent damage to the historic site. Police forces arrested two protesters.

On 19 June 2024, activists from the Emergency Break movement blocked a motorway exit in Kongens Lyngby, Hovedstaden, calling for an end to motorway construction due to environmental concerns. Police later removed the activists from the site after they failed to comply with police demands, five people were detained.

On 20 June 2024, activists from the Emergency Break movement blocked several major roads in Copenhagen, calling for an end to motorway construction due to environmental concerns. Police later removed the activists from the site after they failed to comply with police demands.

On 21 June 2024, around 40 pro-Palestinian demonstrators chained themselves and blocked the entrance to the Norwegian parliament in Oslo, demanding to stop all the economic relations with Israel and Israeli companies. Activists from the Action Group for Palestine took part in the event. Police later removed the activists from the site after they failed to comply with police demands, around 10 people were detained.

On 21 June 2024, people, called by several Argentinian and Spanish-Argentinian collectives like Argentinians in Movement (Argentinxs en Movimiento) and Sovereign Argentina Madrid (Argentina Soberana Madrid), held a protest in Alcala Street in Madrid - Centro (Madrid) against the visit of the Argentinian Prime Minister, Javier Milei, who received awards from the Region of Madrid and Instituto Juan de Mariana. Protesters were removed by the police amid some pushing and shoving, which caused the fall of one of them. Separately, members of Femen held a protest for the same reasons in the same district.

On 21 June 2024, activists from the Emergency Break movement blocked a major road in Copenhagen, calling for an end to motorway construction due to environmental concerns. Police later removed the activists from the site after they failed to comply with police demands, and five people were detained.

On 22 June 2024, Extinction Rebellion activists blocked traffic near Copenhagen Airport in Kastrup, Hovedstaden, calling for a ban on private jets and to oppose aviation industry. Police later removed the activists from the site after they failed to comply with police demands.
On 23 June 2024, as the memorial plaque for Kazys Skirpa was being removed in Vilnius, Lithuania, a few dozen protesters held an action. 3 protesters were detained.

On 23 June 2024, under the motto 'Away from fossil fuels, towards justice', up to 100 Last Generation activists protested at a roundabout in Witzenhausen (Hessen). The police cleared the assembly after about eight hours and carried away and temporarily detained 20 activists for not complying with an order to leave.

On 25 June 2024, dozens of people protested on the Jaarbeurs square in Utrecht (Utrecht) to express support for the Palestinian people and to demand that the University of Utrecht cut ties with Israel. Police arrested one person caught defacing a Utrecht University building during the demonstration.

On 25 June 2024, around 1200 environmental activists demonstrated in various locations of Helsinki as part of the 'Storm Warning' campaign, which aimed to draw attention to environmental issues and call on the government to end state subsidies that are harmful to the environment. Later, the activists blocked traffic and were removed from the site by police. Around 130 people were arrested in connection with the blockade and released the following day. The demonstration was organized by the Extinction Rebellion movement.

On 26 June 2024, activists, mostly students, chained themselves to the main entrance gate of the local university in Krakow, protesting against the ongoing violence in Palestine and demanding immediate suspension of cooperation with academic institutions in Israel. Law enforcers intervened and removed them from the location.

On 26 June 2024, at the call of the 'Let's set it all on fire' (Bruciamo Tutto) group, 6 activists poured red paint on the steps of Trinita dei Monti in Roma - City Center (Lazio) to protest against femicides and commemorate all women victim of violence since the beginning of the year. Activists also held up a banner and threw leaflets with the names of all women killed in Italy this year. The police removed the demonstrators. No incidents were reported, and nobody was injured.

On 26 June 2024, several dozen people, among which students from the Free University of Brussels (VUB), tried to occupy the Flemish Interuniversity Council (VLIR) building in Brussels - Ville de Bruxelles (Brussels) to demand the universities to end all collaborations with Israeli universities. They entered the building but the police immediately intervened to take them outside. There was pushing and shoving, and footage taken by students shows an officer using his pepper spray canister to knock a student's phone out of her hands. Some seated students were dragged down the stairs. The protesters were not allowed in the Ravenstein Gallery anymore and demonstrated in the street, where further confrontation occurred with the police.

On 27 June 2024, pro-Palestine activists from Palestine Action staged a protest and sprayed red paint over the Barclays bank branch on Albion Street in Leeds (England) over the bank's ties and investments in Israel. Shortly after the building was targeted, police forces arrested seven people involved in the action.

On 28 June 2024, around 80 people blocked the entrance of the Danish shipping company's office in Copenhagen calling on the management to cut all the economic ties with Israel. The activists were later removed from the road for failure to comply with police instructions and clear the entrance. Several activists were temporarily detained.

On 28 June 2024, about 50 XR activists blocked the road in Rotterdam (Zuid-Holland) to denounce that the Port of Rotterdam was failing to meet its climate goals and to demand the Port Authority and the city of Rotterdam to show more decisiveness to reach them. The demonstrators'' initial plan was to block the Botlek bridge but the police intervened to prevent it. One group of activists then sat on the Vondelingenweg, off Shell Pernis, near exit 17 of the A15 road and another part of the group was next to the Hoogvliet exit, near the McDonalds. As police directed demonstrators away from the bridge, a struggle ensued between officers and activists. One activist assaulted an officer and was subsequently arrested. A second arrest was made, for dangerous driving.

On 28 June 2024, environmental activists demonstrated in various locations of Helsinki as part of the 'Storm Warning' campaign, which aimed to draw attention to environmental issues and call on the government to end state subsidies that are harmful to the environment. Later, the activists blocked traffic and were removed from the site by police. At least several dozen of activists were arrested during the day. The demonstration was organized by Extinction Rebellion movement.

On 28 June 2024, approximately 15 Pro-Palestine activists gathered outside a lecture on antisemitism at the University of Hamburg in Hamburg - Eimsbuttel (Hamburg), disrupting the lecture by playing recordings through Bluetooth speakers and prompting police intervention, where the police escorted the protesters.

On 29 June 2024, at the fringes of the EuroPride 2024 parade in Thessaloniki police detained 15 far-right demonstrators, who were shouting obscenities and in one case attempted to approach the march to throw eggs at the protesters. Another 26 far-rightists attempted to rally in central Thessaloniki before they were dispersed by police, who detained 6 of their leaders. In the meantime, the leader of ultra-Orthodox party Niki visited in his detention cell, a man previously arrested for disobedience with discrimination characteristics, while inciting people to defy the ban on counter-demonstrating during EuroPride.
On 29 June 2024, people gathered at a detention center in Consett (England) to prevent the transport of van loads of women for deportation. Police at the scene arrested seven attendees.

On 29 June 2024, at the call of COBAS and USB, striking drivers and riders employed by supermarket chain Esselunga's subcontracting companies staged a picket in Campi Bisenzio (Toscana) to demonstrate against their working conditions and wage cuts. The police in anti-riot gear arrived on the site and forcefully removed the demonstrators and dismantled the picket. A demonstrator was reportedly blocked on the pavement by police and then kicked while on the floor as well.

On 30 June 2024, Deliverit Srl drivers staged a protest and refused to work in Campi Bisenzio (Toscana) against the lack of a porterage allowance. COBAS and USB Livorno participated in the event. The police intervened to clear out the garrison, and, according to protesters, they handcuffed a trade unionist who was released later.

On 30 June 2024, on the occasion of the second day of the passage of the Tour de France in Bologna (Emilia-Romagna), 6 Last Generation activists invaded the roadway, chained themselves to each other with padlocks, and threw a can of red paint on the road to demand more climate action and peace and freedom for Gaza. The police removed the demonstrators from the street and took them to the police headquarters.

On 30 June 2024, around 600 people gathered in Nantes (Pays de la Loire) to demonstrate. As the demonstration was unauthorized, police used tear gas to put an end to it. The event was part of a nationwide wave of demonstrations against far-right ideology and in support of an open society, and took place after the National Rally (RN) came first in the first round of the snap legislative elections in France on 30 June 2024 after Emmanuel Macron announced the dissolution of the National Assembly on 9 June 2024.

On 30 June 2024, about 35 people demonstrated inside and in front of the police headquarters in Den Haag (Zuid-Holland) against police violence. The demonstrators were asked to leave the station and were directed to a demonstration site near the Peace Palace. When they did not comply, the protesters were charged on a bus and dropped off near the ADO stadium, on the outskirts of the city. An activist threw an unknown liquid at a police officer and was arrested.
On 1 July 2024, about 15 Last Generation activists blocked a highway in Warsaw, demanding immediate climate action. Law enforces removed them from the spot.

On 2 July 2024, people including Extinction Rebellion members gathered outside of a crown court at English Grounds in London - Southwark (England) with signs that read 'jurors deserve to hear the whole truth'. Eleven attendees were arrested by police on suspicion of contempt of court under the directions of a judge. All individuals were released on bail until a contempt hearing proceeding to be held on 27 September.

On 2 July 2024, people blocked the entrance to the forest area in Gaustad, Oslo, to oppose the planned deforestation and construction works in the area. The activists were later removed from the site for failure to comply with police instructions.

On 2 July 2024, dozens of XR activists blocked the A12 highway in Den Haag (Zuid-Holland), walking and staging a sit-in inside a tunnel and attaching themselves with tubes to bikes, to demand more climate justice. The action took place on the day the new government was sworn in. The police evacuated the protesters, used concrete shears to cut the tubes loose and put the protesters in a bus. One man in a vehicle who opposed the protesters drove against a protester and a barrel to which several protesters were chained, and was charged for these actions in March 2025.

On 3 July 2024, more than 100 people including workers and union members gathered and blocked entrances to the Thales factory in Glasgow (Scotland) in support of Palestinians and calling for the company to end ties with Israel and the government to ban arms exports to Israel. Police used batons and pepper spray against attendees and arrested fourteen attendees including twelve at Govan Cross after they had left the picket line and two from outside the Thales factory building.

On 3 July 2024, people demonstrated at the Chisinau Buiucani courthouse, Chisinau - Buiucani, during a hearing of the Bashkan of Gagauzia. The participants refused to follow police orders to maintain a distance from the courthouse and the leader of the Chance party pushed the officers. He was detained at the protest for hooliganism.

On 3 July 2024, 17 XR activists protested in Bregenz (Vorarlberg), chaining themselves to a large Earth globe and birthday cake installation, opposing the 'Tunnelspinne' project in Feldkirch and Frastanz, demanding urgent action on the climate crisis. 14 activists were arrested after they refused to leave and chained themselves to the symbolic installations.

On 4 July 2024, farmers protested in Odzak against seizing their agricultural land for private company purposes. The police arrested several individuals, and during one arrest, broke the ribs and jaw of one farmer.

On 4 July 2024, around 40 pro-Palestinian demonstrators protested outside the University in Koln (Nordrhein-Westfalen), with about ten blocking the main entrance with a sit-in and chains. They demanded a public discussion with the university's rector regarding the situation in Gaza, but declined a private, limited-time meeting. The police intervened, clearing the entrance by removing the protesters and recording their details, while the university filed a criminal complaint for trespassing.
On 6 July 2024, gathered in Vasteras, Vastmanland, to promote the movement's national socialist values and to oppose migration. Later, police personnel intervened and arrested one person.

On 6 July 2024, several hundred XR activists blocked the A12 in Den Haag (Zuid-Holland) and various intersections leading to the A12, as well as the entrance to the Lower House, to demand the end of fossil fuel subsidies. When protesters did not comply with the police order to leave, the water canon was deployed. The activists who remained seated were eventually detained, among which was Swedish activist Greta Thunberg. About five hundred activists were detained under the Public Manifestations Act and one person was detained under the ID Act. Scientist Rebellion as well as healthcare professionals joined the protest.

On 7 July 2024, 2,000 NFP supporters demonstrated and chanted antifascist slogans in Lille (Hauts-de-France). Two police officers from the BAC unit hit a demonstrator in the face and testicles with a baton. The victim sustained serious injuries, requiring surgery, and PTSD. Investigations concluded that the use of force by the police officers was disproportionate. The event was part of a nationwide wave of demonstrations against far-right ideology and in support of an open society, and took place after the 'New Popular Front' (NFP) coalition came first and the RN coalition came third in the second round of the snap legislative elections in France on 7 July 2024.
On 7 July 2024, about 15 activists of the Last Generation movement blocked a street in Warsaw, demanding immediate climate action. Law enforcers removed them from the spot.

On 8 July 2024, tens of wives of Russian mobilized soldiers gathered in front of the Russian Ministry of Defense building in Moscow - Central (Tsentralnyy, Moscow). They demanded that the government immediately introduce a rotation scheme and return their husbands home. Some local journalists (who were supporting and covering the event) and the protesters were detained by the police.

On 9 July 2024, the police cleared the self-managed social center ex Lavatoio municipale in Torino (Piemonte). The occupied building was used by members of the social center and anarchists as a base for the organization of demonstrations, including demonstrations in support of the anarchist activist Alfredo Cospito. During the eviction, the police seized plexiglass shields, helmets, nautical signal flashlights, several batteries of flares, dozens of firecrackers and smoke bombs, slingshots, flammable liquid, sticks and gas masks.

On 9 July 2024, Extinction Rebellion activists staged a picket outside the municipality in Bologna (Emilia-Romagna) to demonstrate against the G7 meeting and demand more climate action. Activists exposed banners and showcased pieces of old computers and appliances covered in red paint. Some protesters lowered themselves with ropes from the battlements of the roof to display a banner, while other activists sat on the ground and chained themselves to block the entrance. The police cut away the chains and put an end to the picket. 21 activists were taken to the police headquarters to be identified and will be reported.

On 9 July 2024, up to 30 pro-Palestinian activists protested by occupying a lecture hall at the Free University in Berlin - Steglitz-Zehlendorf (Berlin), demanding the withdrawal of charges and an end to collaborations with Israeli universities. After the police intervened, clearing the building without significant resistance, and 27 individuals were reported for trespassing.

On 12 July 2024, people attempted to disrupt the vote in the Finnish Parliament in Helsinki on the proposed deportation law, which would allow border guards to turn away third-country migrants attempting to enter the country from Russia. The activists showed their strong opposition to the law. Security later removed the activists from the venue.

On 12 July 2024, people gathered in Saint-Denis (Ile-de-France) to demand Israel's exclusion from the 2024 Paris Olympics amid the Israel-Hamas war. The police physically removed the protesters from the area.

On 12 July 2024, 36 XR activists protested in KLM's lounge at the airport of Schiphol (Noord-Holland) against their frequent flyer program, which, according to the protesters, encourages a lot of CO2 emissions. Eleven protesters chained or glued themselves to a counter. The police told the protesters to leave and the protesters refused. Police then arrested all 36 protesters and took them away by bus.

On 12 July 2024, during the evening, at the call of Open-minded Steglitz-Zehlendorf (Weltoffen), between 600 and up to 1,000 people, including Grannies Against the Right members, The Left, The Greens, SPD, and Volt, demonstrated in Berlin - Lichtenberg (Berlin) against the presence of the Austrian right-wing extremist Martin Sellner. They were against all fascism, racism, and Nazis. Around 50 people pushed police officers to break through a police cordon at times to get to the venue. The police were able to prevent the attempt and one person was arrested. No physical violence or fights were reported. The protest was peaceful according to the police. Sellner was a guest at a lecture given by former AfD politician Andreas Wild and attended by AfD and Young Alternative for Germany affiliates.

On 12 July 2024, about ten Extinction Rebellion activists occupied an ING office in Nijmegen (Gelderland), demanding the bank stop financing the fossil fuel industry. Eight chained themselves inside, and refused to leave when confronted by the police, until their demands were met. Four activists were arrested for local peace violations but released shortly after.

On 13 July 2024, during the night, a group of about 20 activists, including many women, gathered and verbally insulted servicemen patrolling the border area between Poland and Belarus (coded to Bialystok). The activists criticized the physical barrier on the border and demanding its dismantlement. 17 of them were later detained or documented.

On 13 July 2024, 3 Last Generation activists rallied, threw orange paint, coated themselves in black paint, and blocked traffic by sitting on the ground in Prato della Valle in Padova (Veneto) to protest against the climate crisis and to ask for a climate change reparation fund and a meeting with the prefect. The police intervened and removed them physically.

On 13 July 2024, members of Last Generation, including students, demonstrated in front of the Parliament on Ringstrasse in Wien - Inner City (Wien) to call for more climate protection. They denounced climate disasters in Italy, Brazil, and Switzerland and called for climate protection to be enshrined in the Austrian constitution. Protesters set up a swimming pool to denounce global warming and glued themselves to the road. Police officers intervened physically to unglue them and remove them from the road as they peacefully refused to leave.

On 15 July 2024, pro-Palestine activists from the Youth Demand group staged a protest at the Cenotaph in London - Westminster (England) against the British government's policy toward Palestine, while holding signs saying 'Stop arming Israel' and 'Never again for anyone'. Protesters called for the suspension of licenses for arms sales to Israel. Protesters also spray-painted '180,000 killed' on the pavement in front of the memorial. Police forces arrested two protesters on suspicion of criminal damage on the spot.

On 17 July 2024, activists and Supporters of the Youth Demand group staged a protest in London - Westminster (England) against the Israeli military campaign in the Palestinian territories and in support of Palestine ahead of the State Opening of Parliament by King Charles. Police forces arrested 10 activists on suspicion of conspiracy to cause public nuisance at the event. On the same day, up to 25 Youth Demand activists staged a protest in Victoria Embankment Gardens in London - Westminster (England), holding up signs and banners that read 'Stop Israel's Gaza Genocide' and 'Free Palestine'. One of the participants was subsequently handcuffed and taken away by police forces.
On 17 July 2024, about a dozen activists affiliated with the Last Generation movement blocked a road in Warsaw, demanding immediate climate action. Law enforcers removed them from the spot.
On 18 July 2024, activists affiliated with the Last Generation movement blocked a road in Warsaw, demanding immediate climate action. Law enforcers intervened and removed them from crossing.

On 18 July 2024, 10 people rallied and collectively chalk-painted the Waalkade with Palestinian flags in Nijmegen (Gelderland) to express their support for the Palestinian people. Police officers arrived with several vehicles, detained the 10 participants, and brought them to the police headquarters.

On 19 July 2024, as several other protests against megabasins were taking place nearby, approximately 500 people gathered around a factory and a substitution reserve in Pamproux (Nouvelle Aquitaine). Police dispersed the protesters. The Niort public prosecutor said he opened an investigation 'for the organization of a prohibited demonstration and participation in an unarmed gathering after a summons to disperse by people deliberately concealing their faces so as to not be identified'.

On 19 July 2024, a group of protesters from the Solidarity Between Homeless Women (Solidarite Entre Femmes a la Rue) collective occupied an empty building in the 9th arrondissement of Lyon (Auvergne-Rhone-Alpes). Police arrested one of the protesters (who was released the next day). The protesters were requiring housing for 200 unhoused people.

On 19 July 2024, people, called by the Fed Up Neighborhoods Platform (Plataforma Barrios Hartos), held a protest outside Cerro-Amate district headquarters in Sevilla (Andalucia) against continuous power cuts in working-class neighborhoods, in particular during recent heatwaves, and to call for a meeting with the local government. Some participants peacefully broke into the building, though without the entity's consent, leading to the arrest of the spokesman of the platform, with police forces claiming he had displayed violent behavior and demonstrators arguing there had been no violence.

On 19 July 2024, between 3,800 and 6,500 protesters (including Italian activists) partook in an unauthorized protest against megabasins in Migne-Auxances (Nouvelle-Aquitaine), citing environmental concerns. Police and gendarmerie officers used tear gas to disperse the protest, leading to the fields where the protest was taking place in catching on fire. Nearly 6 hectares burned down. The protesters turned back. Basins No Thank You and SLT - Earth uprisings (Soulevements de la Terre) staged the protest. 3,000 policemen (including CRS) and gendarmerie officers were deployed. The government said the use of tear gas was justified due to the presence of '500 black blocks'.

On 19 July 2024, a protest against megabasins and their environmental impact was held in Saint-Sauvant (Nouvelle-Aquitaine). Police dispersed the protesters using tear gas at the beginning of the protest and left towards Migne-Auxances (coded separately).

On 20 July 2024, more than 200 local residents blocked one of the main roads in Krasnodar city, Krasnodar region. They demanded power and water supply be restored immediately chanting 'give us light'. Several protesters were detained by the National Guard units and Cossacks.

On 20 July 2024, around 300 Last Generation activists staged a protest in Bremen (Bremen), blocking several streets in the city center, including the main train station, causing traffic disruptions. The protest aimed to condemn the government's support of fossil fuel companies and to demand stronger climate action, which resulted in police intervention using water cannons to clear the demonstrators who refused to disperse.

On 21 July 2024, hundreds of people gathered outside the former St. Joseph's female orphanage and Industrial School and St. Malachy's Convent at Seatown in Dundalk (Louth) to protest against the decision to house 260 Ukrainian refugees in the facility. A large group of counter-demonstrators also gathered nearby and chanted 'Refugees are welcome here'. Dundalk Says No campaign group organized the protest. Members of the Irish Freedom Party and The Irish People also addressed the crowd. The protest remained peaceful. When the crowd was dispersing, the police arrested three people for public order offenses, but the report does not specify whether arrests were among protesters or counter-protesters.

On 24 July 2024, activists of Futuro Vegetal held a protest at the airport of Barcelona in El Prat de Llobregat (Cataluna) against the oil and meat industries as being major pollutants. Protesters entered peacefully into the building and tried to access the runways where they were arrested by the police for vandalism and damage to the public property. Activists denounced that during the protest the agents 'threw them to the ground, grabbed them by the neck, and handcuffed them even when they were not under arrest'.

On 24 July 2024, three Extinction Rebellion and Act Now! activists staged a blockade on the access road to Zurich-Kloten Airport in Zurich (Zurich) to demand action against climate change from the Swiss government. Some of the protesters taped their hands to the road. Police forces arrested the protesters.

On 24 July 2024, a group of climate activist attempted to disrupt traffic at Oslo Airport in Gardermoen, Viken, as part of the 'People versus Fossil Fuels' protest. The activists called to halt government approvals of all new fossil fuel projects and exports, emphasizing the need for immediate action to transition to renewable energy sources. The activists were later removed by the police personnel.
