On 24 July 2024, early in the morning, five Last Generation activists occupied a runway at traffic at Cologne Bonn Airport in Koln (Nordrhein-Westfalen), disrupting international air traffic for up to three hours, to demand immediate climate action as part of an international protest campaign calling for the exit from fossil fuels by 2030. Police officers physically removed them from the airport premises and the runaway, and traffic resumed at around 9 am.

On 25 July 2024, dozens of activists, called by Moratalaz Neighbors Union (Sindicato de Barrio de Moratalaz), held a protest in Madrid - Centro (Madrid) against the eviction of a vulnerable family. One activist hung from the top of the building as a measure to stop the eviction, leading to police intervention and the activist's arrest.

On 25 July 2024, 16 pro-Palestinian activists gathered at the Grand-Place and Bourse Square in Brussels - Ville de Bruxelles (Bruxelles-Capitale) to protest in solidarity with the Palestinian people. They were administratively detained by the police for public disorder and rebellion, as they refused to put away their Palestinian flags, and were accused of having staged a spontaneous demonstration and having disrupted an event of the Tomorrowland Festival on Grote Markt, during which some participants carried Israeli flags. Some protesters were handled forcefully and pushed against walls or tackled to the ground. Some local politicians condemned police violence displayed during the arrests.

On 27 July 2024, around 15,000 protesters led by far-right activist Tommy Robinson held a march from the Royal Courts of Justice to Trafalgar Square in London - Westminster (England) against refugees, migrants, and Muslims and chanting 'Rule Britannia' and 'We want our country back'. Protesters waved Union, English, Scottish, and Israeli flags. Around 5,000 anti-racism and anti-fascist activists joined a counter-protest organized by SUTR outside the Whitehall. Speakers of the counter-protest included Independent MP Jeremy Corbyn (Independent), and representatives from NEU, PSC, UCU, CWU, Unison, Unite, and PCS. Police forces had a heavy presence and arrested nine people from the right-wing protesters.

On 27 July 2024, activists from the Restore Wetlands movement demonstrated and attempted to disrupt peat extraction operations in Grimsas, Vastra Gotaland, due to its alleged negative environmental impact. During the demonstration, one of the activists was physically assaulted by an unknown individual. Later, police personnel detained four activists and removed them from the site.

On 29 July 2024, climate activists from Just Stop Oil staged a protest and blocked the departure gate at Gatwick Airport in Crawley (England) to demand a transition from fossil fuel energies. Police forces intervened to remove the protesters and arrested eight activists.

On 29 July 2024, around 20 members of Extinction Rebellion demonstrated on Waldeggstrasse in Linz (Oberosterreich) against the planned construction of the A26 road. They blocked traffic with a wooden scaffold. 3 people chained themselves to the scaffolding. Police officers intervened physically to remove the demonstrators from the street and one activist was arrested. Protesters denounced Austria's transport sector as the source of health risks and consequences of the climate crisis.

On 29 July 2024, activists from the Restore Wetlands movement demonstrated in Grimsas, Vastra Gotaland, to oppose peat extraction operations due to its alleged negative environmental impact. Later, two activists were detained by the police after they chained themselves to the working equipment in an attempt to disrupt harvesting works.
On 30 July 2024, in the morning, police carried out the eviction of the self-managed social center il Burrida, located in Genova (Liguria).

On 30 July 2024, at the call of AFPS, 3 people gathered and held up a Palestinian flag in La Chapelle-sur-Erdre (Pays de la Loire) to express solidarity with the Palestinian people and condemn what they deemed a 'genocide' of Gazans by the Israeli army. Police arrested all protesters. The event occurred before a football game between Israel and Japan during the 2024 Paris Summer Olympics.

On 30 July 2024, climate activists from Just Stop Oil staged a protest and sprayed orange paint on departure boards at Heathrow Airport in London - Hillingdon (England) to demand a transition from fossil fuel energies. Police forces intervened and arrested two protesters.

On 30 July 2024, activists from the Restore Wetlands movement demonstrated in Grimsas, Vastra Gotaland, to oppose peat extraction operations due to its alleged negative environmental impact. Later, several activists were detained by the police after they glued themselves to the working equipment in an attempt to disrupt harvesting works.

On 31 July 2024, more than 100 people, including Futuro Vegetal activists, held a protest outside the informal settlement of Can Rova in Ibiza (Islas Baleares), where around 1,000 people live in tents, against its eviction by the police that was taking place. 6 residents were arrested, citing resistance to the police during the eviction.

On 31 July 2024, animal rights activists threw bags containing excrement outside the headquarters of the Province of Trento in Roma - City Center (Lazio) to protest against the killing of the Kj1 bear in Trentino Alto-Adige, after the signing of the decree by President Maurizio Fugatti (Lega). The police prevented them from entering the building.

On 31 July 2024, environmental activists and local residents again gathered at the springs of the Una river (coded to Donja Suvaja), protesting against the current construction of a water power plant in the area and demanding preservation of the natural reservation. A deputy of the We can! party was also present. Law enforcers intervened and ended the gathering.

On 31 July 2024, activists from the Restore Wetlands movement demonstrated and attempted to disrupt peat extraction operations in Grimsas, Vastra Gotaland, due to its alleged negative environmental impact. Later, several activists were detained by the police.

On 1 August 2024, a crowd gathered outside Rethymno police Security offices in Livadia of Mylopotamos municipality protesting against police narcotics operations in the area, and in particular the arrest of 2 brothers, who were growing 20 cannabis plants in their home. Police dispersed the crowd using tear gas.

On 1 August 2024, shortly after midnight, at least 5 to 7 Last Generation activists staged a protest at Leipzig/Halle Airport in Schkeuditz (Sachsen), gluing themselves to the runway to halt cargo flights, demanding the signing of an international treaty to phase out fossil fuels. This protest is part of the 'Oil Kills' campaign, which aims for the elimination of oil, gas, and coal by 2030 and for the need for increased climate protection. The police intervened by removing the activists from the runway around 5 AM.

On 2 August 2024, for a second consecutive day, activists from Extinction Rebellion demonstrated in Jyvaskyla, Keski-Suomi, to oppose a world rally event that was taking place in the area, due to its alleged negative environmental impact. Four people were arrested in connection with the demonstration.

On 2 August 2024, Last Generation activists temporarily blocked a street in Warsaw before the upcoming concert of Taylor Swift, criticizing the high negative impact of celebrities on climate change. Law enforcers later removed them from the road.

On 3 August 2024, estimated 150 far-right demonstrators gathered outside Leeds Art Gallery in Leeds (England) for an anti-immigration demonstration. Demonstrators chanted slogans such as 'You're not English anymore' and 'Paedo Muslims off our street'. Around 250 anti-racism and pro-Palestine counter-demonstrators gathered at the same location and chanted 'Say it loud, say it clear, refugees are welcome here' and 'Nazi scum off our streets'. The number of counter protesters grew during the afternoon. Police forces arrested several far-right demonstrators after an unspecified incident on George Street. The event is part of mass anti-migration gatherings and riots occurring across the country after the mass stabbing of children in Southport on 29 July 2024 2024 and the disinformation campaign on social media about the suspect of the attack being a refugee..

On 3 August 2024, far-right demonstrators gathered in the city center of Leicester (England) for an anti-immigration demonstration. Anti-racism campaigners from SUTR also gathered for a counter-demonstration. The police arrested two men, but the report does not state whether it was a protester or counter-protester. The event is part of a wave of gatherings and violence that occurred across the country and was triggered by the stabbing of children in Southport on 29 July 2024 and the disinformation campaign on social media about the suspect of the attack being a refugee.

On 6 August 2024, at the call of DAL - Right to Housing (Droit au Logement), The Reverse of the Medal (Le Revers de la Medaille), and Utopia, around 200 undocumented and homeless migrants gathered and set up tents on Bastille Square in Paris (Ile-de-France) to demand decent housing for migrants and protest against the eviction of homeless people from Paris during of the 2024 Paris Summer Olympics. Police intervened, physically dispersing the encampment and seizing the tents. There was no report of arrests.

On 7 August 2024, far-right anti-immigration protesters gathered on Maidstone Road in Chatham (England). About 25 anti-racism protesters gathered for a counter-protest in the same location. The protest remained mostly peaceful but police forces arrested two far-right protesters after minor scuffles with the police occurred. The event is part of a wave of gatherings and violence that occurred across the country and was triggered by the stabbing of children in Southport on 29 July 2024 and the disinformation campaign on social media about the suspect of the attack being a refugee.

On 7 August 2024, an unknown number of people protested at Dam Square in Amsterdam (Noord-Holland) to support the Palestinian people. Due to a recent municipal protest ban in the area, the police intervened, dragged and loaded demonstrators onto buses, before moving them to the Beursplein. Several participants then proceeded to protest at the central station.

On 8 August 2024, far-right anti-migration protesters gathered in Barnsley (England) for an anti-migration protest. Anti-racism and anti-fascist protesters gathered in the same spot against the far-right and riots across England. The protest remained mostly peaceful but police forces arrested two far-right protesters. A total of around 110 people gathered. Despite minor scuffles, the police described the event as a largely peaceful gathering. The event is part of a wave of gatherings and violence that occurred across the country and was triggered by the stabbing of children in Southport on 29 July 2024 and the disinformation campaign on social media about the suspect of the attack being a refugee.

On 8 August 2024, people, including members of Ransacking 2024 (Saccage 2024), a collective of Seine-Saint-Denis residents, demonstrated around the Saint-Denis Canal in Saint-Denis (Ile-de-France) against the Paris 2024 Olympic and Paralympic Games being held in the department. Protesters denounced gentrification, eviction, surveillance policies, and police presence. Police officers stopped the march after 10 minutes and arrested 3 people.

On 8 August 2024, at the call of JxCat, between 2,500 (according to the police) and 15,000 people (organizers), including former Catalonia President Carles Puigdemont and Catalonian activists, held a protest near the Catalan Parliament in Barcelona - Ciutat Vella (Cataluna) in support of the visit of Puigdemont, who fled the country after the 2017 Catalan independence referendum attempt. Participants protested against ERC negotiations with PSOE to appoint Salvador Illa (PSOE) as the leader of the new regional government, claiming that a coalition pact with PSOE would imply 'treason' to the nation of Catalonia and its interests, and demanding unity of all pro-independence parties. Police used pepper spray to dissolve the protest and two people were arrested. During that day, dozens of people gathered near the Catalan Parliament at the call of Vox to oppose the visit of Carles Puigdemont and call for the unity of the Spanish nation.

On 8 August 2024, approximately twenty pro-Palestinian demonstrators demonstrated on Dam Square in Amsterdam (Noord-Holland), despite it being prohibited by the municipality at that location. Police intervened and directed demonstrators toward Central Station. A female protester spat at an officer and was arrested. Following her arrest, about twenty demonstrators sat on the ground outside the police station demanding her release, but the suspect remained detained.

On 9 August 2024, an unknown number of people protested at Dam Square in Amsterdam (Noord-Holland) to support the Palestinian people. Due to a recent municipal protest ban in the area, the police intervened and with buses, moved the protesters to the central station. One individual spat at a police officer and was detained in the process. A group of about 20 people then moved to the police station to demand her release. The police did not release the individual and the group lifted the protest rally in the evening.

On 9 August 2024, activists from the Restore Wetlands movement demonstrated and attempted to disrupt peat extraction operations in Grimsas, Vastra Gotaland, due to its alleged negative environmental impact. Later, three activists were detained by the police in connection with the demonstration.

On 9 August 2024, a group of students from UAntwerpForPalestine (UA4P) and LABO vzw held a pro-Palestinian demonstration during the Pride March in Antwerpen (Vlaanderen) to protest against 'genocide' and ongoing human rights violations in Palestine. Protest organizers emphasized intersectional solidarity between the LGBTQI+ community and Palestinian activists, but police arrested two students due to a ban of political flags during the event.

On 10 August 2024, 3 activists from the climate group Last Generation (Letzte Generation) staged a protest at the airport in Wenningstedt-Braderup (Sylt) (Schleswig-Holstein). One was arrested after cutting through a fence to access the runway and the other two managed to glue themselves next to a private jet, as part of the broader 'Oil Kills' campaign, which aims to highlight the environmental impact of private jets and call for a ban on fossil fuels by 2030. It did not interrupt flight operations but led to police intervention arresting all 3 protesters with charges for vandalism and trespassing.

On 10 August 2024, people called the police to a pro-Palestinian demonstration camp, registered and permitted from May 2024 until the end of August advocating for disarmament of Israel and criticizing Israel's policies, near the Dammtor train station in Hamburg - Eimsbuttel (Hamburg) , reporting altercation within the camp, which members of the demonstration camp did not confirm. One demonstrator slapped a police officer who was slightly injured. Two people had suffered a fainting spell during the police operation. Two ambulances and an emergency doctor were at the scene. According to the police, one of the injured people had left the scene in the meantime. Another police officer was slightly injured, and three demonstrators were taken into custody, what they were accused of was not specified.

On 11 August 2024, about 8 XR activists blocked a canal lock in Ijmuiden (Noord-Holland) by chaining or gluing themselves to the lock, to prevent a large cruise ship from entering Amsterdam's waterways. The protesters argued cruise ships exacerbated the climate crisis. The police intervened and physically removed the activists, though there was no report of arrests.

On 12 August 2024, demonstrators, including activists from the Action Group for Palestine, blocked the entrance to the Norwegian Central Bank in Oslo, calling for divestment from Israeli companies. Police later removed and arrested five activists after they failed to comply with police orders to free the entrance.

On 12 August 2024, around 20 people staged a pro-Palestinian demonstration during an opening ceremony for students at a university in Bergen, Vestland. The activists called for a free Palestine and a boycott of Israel. Police later removed several activists from the area after they failed to comply with police orders.

On 12 August 2024, about 30 participants of an unregistered protest, called a 'Monday demonstration' (Montagsdemo), following a registered protest of around 100 people before, in Aschersleben (Sachsen-Anhalt) faced intervention by police officers after attempting a march through the city following a previously permitted protest, when it became clear that no designated person to register the event was present, as required by local assembly law. There was physical violence between a protester and a police officer. The police applied physical force to end the disruption. There is no report of the protest's reasons and demands but they are often against the government and happen every Monday.

On 13 August 2024, people gathered outside Dundrum House Hotel in Tipperary (Tipperary) for a peaceful protest against the hosting of 80 asylum seekers (mostly of Ukrainian origin) at the venue. A male participant was arrested by the police during the demonstration but later released without charge.

On 15 August 2024, following days of power cuts in Northern Cyprus, employees at the Teknecik Power Plant (coded to Agios Epiktitos), all members of the Turkish Cypriot electricity union EL-SEN, blocked the entrance of the plant preventing the Prime Minister and strong police forces to enter insisting that this was the result of bad management and indifference. The PM claimed the workers had sabotaged the plant and brought spare parts and a team of workers from the private Turkish power company, Aksa. The leader of El-Sen was briefly arrested. Kibris newspaper (whose owner was also the owner of Aksa) reported that the leader of EL-Sen attacked the PM, but the union of journalists said this was a lie and that the PM ordered the arrest.

On 15 August 2024, environmental activists from Extinction Rebellion blocked the entrance to a construction site in Amager, Copenhagen, to protest the planned creation of an artificial island named Lynetteholmen that is supposed to house 35'000 residents. Activists claimed that the development project could harm both the marine and urban environment. Police later removed and detained four activists from the site after they failed to comply with police orders to free the entrance.

On 18 August 2024, an unknown number of XR activists blocked two river locks in Ijmuiden (Noord-Holland), chaining or gluing themselves to said locks, to prevent a cruise ship and an oil tanker from entering Amsterdam's fluvial network. The protesters condemned cruise ships for exacerbating the climate crisis. It was the third action on the lock that month. The police removed the activists and took 8 of them to the police station.

On 20 August 2024, activists from Extinction Rebellion staged a protest performance outside of the Royal Palace in Oslo calling on the royal family members to take action on climate change and environmental issues. Police later removed the activists from the site after they failed to comply with police demands, three people were arrested.

On 20 August 2024, between around 2,000 and 3,000 antifascist protesters, including members of the MLPD, the youth group REBELL, and other organizations, gathered in Jena (Thuringen) at the call of the 'Stop the Shift to the Right' ('Rechtsruck stoppen') alliance, to block a planned appearance by Bjorn Hocke, a prominent AfD politician, at a local community center and to protest against the AfD and Hocke's far-right ideologies. Despite attempts by the police to clear the way, the protesters prevented Bjorn Hocke from attending the event, leading to its cancellation. The event escalated when the police used pepper spray, batons, and physical force, including punches to the face, to break up the protesters' sit-in blockade. This resulted in several injuries among the demonstrators. No arrests were made.

On 20 August 2024, around 30 to 40 people gathered in the main hall of the Zoologischer Garten station in Berlin - Charlottenburg-Wilmersdorf (Berlin), chanting pro-Palestinian slogans. The protest was not registered, and the police dispersed the group, escorting them out of the station, and initiated several criminal investigations and one proceeding for violating weapons laws.

On 21 August 2024, around 140 people staged a pro-Palestinian protest at Karl Marx Square (Karl-Marx-Platz) in Berlin - Neukolln (Berlin), chanting various slogans, such as contested the slogan 'From the river to the sea, Palestine will be free.' The police initiated criminal investigations for incitement to hatred, property damage, and violations of the association law against six participants.

On 23 August 2024, a group of around 20 international group of activists from Fossil Free Adriatic, used kayaks to block a tanker importing liquefied natural gas (LNG), preventing it from connecting to the terminal in Omisalj. They also attempted to climb on the tanker. The activists protested against the fossil fuel industry and its impact on the ecosystem and environment around the island of Krk. Police on boats intervened, arresting 12 or 13 activists, and causing injuries that led to several of them being hospitalized. The police deny that their intervention caused the hospitalizations.

On 24 August 2024, in the evening, people gathered for a pro-Palestinian protest around Sonnenallee in Berlin - Neukolln (Berlin). Protesters set off pyrotechnics and chanted contested slogans. The police intervened multiple times to control the crowd, leading to arrests.

On 26 August 2024, around 100 climate activists blocked the road leading to the venue of the national energy conference in Stavanger, Rogaland. The protest was aimed at opposing the fossil fuel industry and accusing the event's organizers of greenwashing. Activists from Extinction Rebellion and Fridays For Future, including Greta Thunberg, participated in the blockade. Police later dispersed the crowd and removed activists from the area.

On 27 August 2024, the police interrupted a permanent picket against the cutting of some trees staged by residents and environmental activists in Gallarate (Lombardia) to seize some material from the demonstrators. Demonstrators held hands and created a human cordon to prevent the police from accessing the picket site. Pushing and pulling between the police and the demonstrators was reported. One activist was arrested on charges of resisting a public official.

On 28 August 2024, 6 Last Generation activists gathered on a bridge over the A27 highway near Achim (Niedersachsen), to protest for a traffic shift and climate issues, highlighting the need for a transition towards more sustainable and eco-friendly transportation systems, prompting a temporary closure of the highway in both directions. The police intervened to manage the situation, including removing the activists from the bridge and reopening the highway after the protest ended.

On 28 August 2024, around 60 to 100 pro-Palestinian demonstrators staged a sit-in at the main train station in Berlin - Mitte (Berlin), to protest against Israel's actions in Gaza while chanting anti-Israel slogans. The unauthorized demonstration was dispersed by a large police presence after about an hour. The police removed 79 pro-Palestinian demonstrators by physically escorting them out of the station and initiated 72 criminal proceedings for violations related to the use of banned symbols and assembly laws.

On 29 August 2024, Kosovo Serb protesters, including from Serbian Democracy, gathered in front of the new offices of the Kosovo post office in North Mitrovica to disrupt the official opening event. This comes as discontent continues to be high in northern Kosovo over the closing of the Serbian post office and the opening of Kosovo supermarket chains. Some of the protesters, who used whistles to stop the speeches from taking place, were physically pushed away by the police.

On 30 August 2024, in the morning, more than 200 gendarmes, including the specialized CNAMO team, intervened to evacuate the Cal'arbre ZAD protest encampment and arrested 10 people in Saix (Occitanie). Demonstrators had been opposing the A69 highway project between Toulouse and Castres, which they denounced as harmful to the environment. Activists denounced that several machines destroyed their huts, and tents, and that construction workers stole some of their equipment. Despite the intervention, environmental activists continued to occupy several trees near the former encampment.

On 31 August 2024, activists from the Nordic Resistance Movement demonstrated in Uppsala to promote the movement's national socialist values and oppose multiculturalism. Later, a minor scuffle occurred with passers-by, which led to the arrest of two Nordic Resistance Movement activists by the police.

On 31 August 2024, people gathered in Berlin - Tempelhof-Schoneberg (Berlin), to protest in solidarity with Palestine and against Israel. At the same time, people gathered for a counter-protest, in support of Israel. Due to the police presence, the event remained largely peaceful. A few protesters were arrested.

On 1 September 2024, under the motto 'For Democracy and Diversity', around 200 people gathered in Saarbrucken (Saarland), to protest against an AfD event happening simultaneously in the area. The protest was dissolved by police due to non-compliance with regulations and actions against police officers, involving physical confrontations and resistance against the police. Some demonstrators attempted to breach a police cordon and possessed items that could be used as weapons. One person was briefly detained.

On 2 September 2024, more than 100 protesters, including activists from the group 'Academics for Palestine' and students, demonstrated and set up a pro-Palestinian protest camp on the campus of Stockholm University in Stockholm, demanding that the university impose a total ban on academic cooperation with Israeli institutions. Subsequently, police broke up the camp and removed the tents from the area, several activists were detained.

On 2 September 2024, between 15 and 20 demonstrators, among which students and teachers, gathered for a rally, disrupting the opening of the academic year of the University of Groningen in Groningen (Groningen), by lying on the floor and making noise to show their support for the Palestinian people and demand that the university cut all ties with Israel. The police arrested two demonstrators: one for failing to provide identification and one for disruption of public order.

On 2 September 2024, activists from the Emergency Break movement staged a protest performance in Copenhagen, calling for an end to motorway construction due to environmental concerns. Police later removed the activists from the road.
On 2 September 2024, Last Generation activists blocked streets in Warsaw, demanding immediate climate action. Law enforcers intervened and removed them from the spots.

On 3 September 2024, pro-Palestine activists from Palestine Action staged a protest and sprayed red paint on the offices of APCO Worldwide in London - Westminster (England) against the firm's partnership with Israel's biggest weapons firm, Elbit Systems. Three protesters attached themselves to the entrance of the building and held a banner reading 'Stop lobbying for Genocide. APCO Drop Elbit'. Police forces arrived at the scene and removed the protesters from the building.

On 3 September 2024, around 400 demonstrators from Extinction Rebellion marched in Helsinki to demand stronger climate action from the Finnish government during budget negotiations. Later, activists attempted to block traffic on a major road and were dispersed by police. 57 people were arrested in connection with the blockade.
On 3 September 2024, Last Generation activists blocked streets in Warsaw, demanding immediate climate action. Law enforcers intervened and removed them from the spots.

On 4 September 2024, around 20 people, including activists from the Students Against the Occupation movement and Greta Thunberg, attempted to occupy the University of Copenhagen building in Copenhagen. The aim was to demand that the university impose a total ban on cooperation with Israeli institutions. The police later removed the activists from the venue, 6 people were arrested and released the same day.

On 5 September 2024, climate activists from Greenpeace locked themselves to all entrances at Unilever's Blackfriars headquarters in London - City of London (England) targeting the skincare brand Dove, over their role in plastic pollution. Protesters unfurled a huge banner that read 'Real beauty is not this toxic' and 'Dove, ditch plastic now'. Police forces came to the scene and tried to remove the protesters. In the process, police forces arrested 18 people.

On 5 September 2024, thirteen activists from the Emergency Break movement blocked a major road in Copenhagen, calling for an end to motorway construction due to environmental concerns. Police later removed the activists from the road and arrested them.
On 5 September 2024, Last Generation activists blocked a street traffic in Warsaw, demanding immediate climate action. Law enforcers removed them from the location.

On 5 September 2024, around 4,000 people, including members of groups such as 'Together against Right Essen,' gathered in Essen (Nordrhein-Westfalen) to protest an AfD 'citizens' dialogue' event at the Philharmonie, expressing their opposition to the AfD's policies, claiming they threaten democratic values and cultural diversity. The protest involved chants like 'Fascists out' and the use of noise devices to disrupt the event, which led to interruptions and a search of the venue. Some protesters who were using noise devices were removed by security.

On 6 September 2024, gendarme officers intervened in a ZAD (zone to defend) area in Saix (Occitanie) and arrested 20 activists who were occupying a piece of land to protest against the construction of the A69 highway between Toulouse and Castres, which they deemed damaging to the environment. Due to the intervention, two activists fell from trees they occupied and were hospitalized. One activist remained to occupy a tree.

On 7 September 2024, at the call of PSC, thousands of pro-Palestine protesters held a march from Piccadilly Circus to Kensington Road in London - Westminster (England) to call for a ceasefire in Gaza. Protesters waved Palestinian flags and held signs that read 'Starmer has blood on his hands'. A pro-Israel counter-protest also formed on Kensington High Street (same location), where participants protested, danced to music, and waved Israeli, British, and American flags, and were kept separate by police officers. Police forces arrested eight people on public order offenses.

On 7 September 2024, about 60 XR activists chained themselves to the fence at the entrance of the Rijksmuseum in Amsterdam (Noord-Holland) to demand the museum to break its sponsorship relationship with the bank ING, according to XR one of the biggest drivers of the climate crisis. Police arrested 33 activists after they refused to move.

On 7 September 2024, around 1,700 people gathered for a protest, among them the Grannies agains the Right (Germany), in Hofheim am Taunus (Hessen) against the state party congress of the AfD. The protest was organized around a 'Festival of Democracy,' where participants voiced opposition to the AfD's policies and their growing political influence. The day began with around 200 protersters blocking access roads to the town hall, where the congress was taking place, leading to police officers pushing back and hitting protesters to contain them and stop the demonstration. Protesters emphasized their discontent over the police presence, which included helicopters, drones, and mounted officers. There was an additional and connected vigil with around 1,500 participants organized by the group 'Main-Taunus-Kreis Against the Right' to highlight concerns about the AfD's nationalist rhetoric and its perceived threat to human rights.

On 7 September 2024, around 70 climate activists from Last Generation (Germany) occupied the intersection of Am Wall/Herdentorsteinweg in Bremen (Bremen) to highlight the impending consequences of climate change. The activists, who described their action as a 'disobedient assembly' and did not have official permission, blocked traffic and repeatedly ignored police requests to clear the intersection. Traffic was restored after 31 activists were forcibly removed and taken into custody. The protest aimed to raise awareness about future flood risks and climate change impacts to advocate for preventive measures.

On 8 September 2024, around 300 participants took part in a car convoy in solidarity with Palestine in Berlin - Charlottenburg-Wilmersdorf (Berlin), specifically around the intersection of Leipziger Strase and Markgrafenstrase, also causing traffic disruptions in the area of Tauentzienstrase. The protest involved approximately 125 vehicles and was halted due to violations of regulations, such as noise, speeding, and leaning out of windows. 21 people were arrested. The rally aimed to draw attention to issues including the blockade of Gaza, land grabs in the West Bank, and other grievances related to Palestine.

On 9 September 2024, former employees of the 'Kosuta' shoe factory protested once again by blocking the road from Cetinje to Podgorica near Krusevo zdrijelo (coded to Cetinje) due to their unpaid wages, despite a directive from the National Security Council to the police not to allow the blocking of road infrastructure. For this reason, police officers arrested three of the protesters and fined them 50 euros each.

On 9 September 2024, demonstrators, including Greta Thunberg, gathered and set up protest tents inside the University of Stockholm's library in Stockholm to show solidarity with Palestine in response to Israeli military actions in Gaza and Rafah, while calling for an academic boycott of Israel. Police later removed the activists from the venue after they failed to comply with police demands.

On 9 September 2024, striking Richemont employees working in Firenze (Italy) (nationality not specified) gathered outside their company's headquarters in Geneva (Geneve) to demand better working conditions. Police intervened to remove the protesters.

On 9 September 2024, about 30 people, including representatives of the self-managed social center Askatasuna and members of the committee 'Let's Save Meisino' (Salviano il Meisino), staged a protest outside the entrance of the former Meisino horse racing circuit in Torino (Piemonte) to demonstrate against a project for the construction of the Center for Sports and Environmental Education. Demonstrators prevented the entry of trucks and workers into the area. The police physically removed the demonstrators, allowing workers and vehicles to enter the construction site.

On 9 September 2024, ten activists from the Emergency Break movement staged a protest and blocked a major road in Copenhagen, calling for an end to motorway construction on environmental grounds. Police later physically removed the activists from the site. The activists then returned to the blockade and were subsequently arrested.

On 9 September 2024, around between 500 to 800 people, including members of Grannies Against the Right (Germany), gathered in front of the Citizens' House in Bilk in Dusseldorf (Nordrhein-Westfalen) to protest against an event featuring controversial AfD EU parliamentarian Maximilian Krah. The protest, organized by the anti-racist alliance DSSQ ('Dusseldorf takes a Stand'), was prompted by Krah's presence, given his controversial statements and recent internal conflicts within the AfD. Protesters voiced their opposition loudly with slogans such as 'Nazis out!' and displayed various signs criticizing the far-right. The police were present in significant numbers to prevent clashes and maintain order, resulting in a few minor altercations and temporary detentions.
On 10 September 2024, Last Generation activists blocked a local street in Warsaw, demanding immediate climate action. Law enforcers removed them from the spot.

On 10 September 2024, Kosovo Serbs staged a peaceful protest in North Mitrovica while prime minister Albin Kurti visited a newly opened restaurant in the northern part of the city. Police briefly arrested the leader and deputy leader of Serbian Democracy for blowing a whistle, then released them the same day.

On 11 September 2024, educators rallied outside the offices of the Education Authority of West Attica in Eleusis demanding permanent jobs for substitute teachers. 20 police officers and 4 patrol cars were blocking their way and prevented them from approaching the building. 1 substitute teacher was detained.

On 11 September 2024, about a dozen of Last Generation activists gathered for a rally near a local court in Warsaw, declaring solidarity with their peers during their trial over climate protests from this March. After the court hearing, they again blocked a local street, demanding immediate climate action. Law enforcers removed them from the spot.

On 12 September 2024, police dispersed a protest by locals in the village of Voskresenskiy (Anapa, Krasnodar). People protested against the illegal landfill in the area and blocked the road with their bodies.

On 14 September 2024, around 800 XR activists staged a protest and blocked the A12 highway in Den Haag (Zuid-Holland) to denounce governmental support for fossil fuels and related projects. The police used water cannons and physically removed most protesters from the highway portion, arresting a total of 370 - 350 for violating the Public Demonstrations Act, and 20 for 'vandalism', including spray-painting street furniture.

On 14 September 2024, around 2,500 people participated in the Christopher Street Day (CSD) parade in Dortmund (Nordrhein-Westfalen), to protest for LGBTQ+ rights and visibility. Around 50 right-wing individuals staged a counter-protest nearby, while at the call of Antifa, around 150 left-wing protesters demonstrated against the right-wing protest. The police effectively kept the groups apart. Two right-wing protesters were detained for making homophobic remarks and performing a Hitler salute. In addition, there were minor incidents, including children attempting to throw eggs at CSD participants.

On 15 September 2024, Extinction Rebellion activists demonstrated and entered the restricted area of Norrkoping Airport in Norrkoping, Ostergotland, demanding an end to subsidies for the aviation industry and a complete cut in municipal financial support for the airport. The activists were later removed by security.

On 15 September 2024, activists from the group 'Stop Fossil Subventions' (Stoppt Fossile Subventionen) and XR staged a protest by blocking the Elsenbridge between the districts of Berlin - Friedrichshain-Kreuzberg and Berlin - Treptow-Kopenick (Berlin), to protest against the expansion of the A100 freeway. The police intervened by carrying away the protesters, eventually clearing the blockade and arresting 20 activists after they failed to comply with repeated dispersal orders.

On 16 September 2024, around 170 pro-Palestinian demonstrators protested at the Technical University of Berlin in Berlin - Charlottenburg-Wilmersdorf (Berlin) during a lecture by former The Greens politician Volker Beck on antisemitism. They opposed Beck's support for Israel, accusing Israel of genocide and labeling Germany a racist state. Demonstrators confronted Volker Beck, shouting insults and accusing him of having 'blood on his hands.' The police intervened to control the situation and made two temporary arrests.

On 17 September 2024, four pro-Palestine activists held a protest and targeted a stall for the weapons firm Leonardo at the SPIE Security and Defense Conference at the Edinburgh International Conference Center in Edinburgh (Scotland) over the company's ties with Israel. The company manufactures components for F-35 fighter jets used by Israel in its airstrikes on Gaza. Protesters held a banner that read 'Leonardo kills kids'. Later police forces intervened and dragged away protesters but no one was arrested.

On 17 September 2024, 8 environmental activists (dubbed 'Squirrels') climbed onto trees in the ZAD protest camp in Verfeil (Occitanie) to protest and prevent the Atosca construction company from felling the last trees on the path of the future A69 highway project between Toulouse and Castres, citing environmental concerns. Police intervened on cranes to physically remove the protesters from the trees.

On 17 September 2024, environmental activists, including Extinction Rebellion, took part in the Democracy Street Walk in Stockholm to raise awareness about climate change and to protest against insufficient government action. Police later intervened and forced the activists to stop the demonstration.

On 19 September 2024, in the evening, people gathered in Lyon (Auvergne-Rhone-Alpes), a day before the participation of a former FEMEN and feminist activist (Marguerite Stern) in a conference entitled 'How transgender ideology destroys lives' at the ISSEP school (founded by far-right politician Marion Marechal in 2018), to demonstrate against what they perceive as her transphobic views, citing her critique of transgender identities and the language associated with them. The police arrested three participants due to a prefectural decree temporarily banning demonstration activity around the school.

On 19 September 2024, anti-immigration protesters held a march in the city center toward the Irish Parliament in Dublin (Dublin) against the housing of international protection applicants (IPAs) in communities in Dublin and Wicklow. Protesters waved Irish flags and chanted 'Whose streets? Our streets'. Local councilors addressed the crowd. Anti-racism campaigners, called by United Against Racism, gathered for a counter-demonstration at the bottom of Grafton Street chanting 'Refugees welcome, racists not', and 'When migrant rights are under attack, stand up, fight back'. Participants included PBP representatives and other left-wing groups. The two groups exchanged insults and slurs but no violent incident happened as the police kept the two groups separated. Police forces made 19 arrests among anti-immigration protesters when clearing the gathering that disrupted traffic.

On 21 September 2024, female relatives of the mobilized were detained by the police during a protest next to the main building of the Ministry of Defense in Moscow - Central (Tsentralnyy, Moscow). The wives and mothers of the mobilized came to the Ministry of Defense demanding demobilization. 10 of them were detained and released at night with an obligation to appear at the police station again. In addition to the protesters, 2 journalists covering the event were detained too, and later released with 'warnings' that protests of relatives of the mobilized 'should not be covered'. Centre for Combating Extremism police also participated in the intervention against protesters. Provocateurs insulting the protesters were also reported.

On 23 September 2024, fifty people demonstrated in Bilbao (Pais Vasco) to stop the eviction of migrants from a flat. There were scuffles between the police and demonstrators, and the police arrested one person and denounced several others.

On 25 September 2024, around 10 activists from Extinction Rebellion and the Restore Wetlands Movement (Sweden) staged a protest performance by spraying red paint on the pillars of the Parliament building in Helsinki. The activists called for a ban on peat extraction due to its alleged negative impact on the environment. Ten activists were arrested in connection with the demonstration.

On 25 September 2024, over 60 Last Generation activists staged a protest in Kassel (Hessen), blocking traffic on a major road, to demand an end to the public subsidization of Kassel-Calden Airport. The activists criticized the airport for being a financial burden, accumulating millions in losses since its opening, and aimed to raise awareness about the environmental impact of maintaining such an underutilized facility. The police intervened by physically carrying the protesters away from the road.

On 26 September 2024, police officers from the CNAMO unit intervened in a ZAD (zone to defend) area in Verfeil (Occitanie) and arrested all four activists who were sitting on a roof to protest against the construction of the A69 highway between Toulouse and Castres, which they deemed damaging to the environment.

On 26 September 2024, at the call of PSC, dozens of people gathered on Downing Street from 6 pm until 8 pm in London - Westminster (England) in an 'emergency' protest in solidarity with Lebanon and Palestine following Israeli airstrikes on the former. Protesters called on the British government to end its complicity with Israel's 'genocidal assault' on Palestine and Lebanon. Five people were arrested for refusing to disperse after 8 pm.

On 26 September 2024, in the morning, around 50 Ende Gelaende activists gathered and blocked the construction site of the LNG terminal in Brunsbuttel (Schleswig-Holstein) to protest against liquefied natural gas (LNG) imports, aiming to draw attention to environmental concerns related to the terminal's construction. The police took two protesters into custody and identified seven others, after some protesters resisted and failed to comply with orders to leave the construction site.

On 26 September 2024, around 250 people gathered at Potsdamer Square in Berlin - Mitte (Berlin) to protest against Israeli actions in Gaza and Lebanon. The demonstration was drawn to a close by police intervention following escalating verbal tensions. The police made 14 arrests for offenses such as 'chanting illegal slogans' and 'showing banned symbols'.

On 27 September 2024, during a speech by the Infrastructure and Public Transport minister at an event marking European Researchers' Night at the National Technical University of Athens, Athens - Central Athens, a group of researchers, mostly postgraduate students, protested holding a banner behind the podium, scattering fliers and chanting slogans. They demanded to be paid for their research work and also shouted slogans in solidarity with Palestine.

On 27 September 2024, three activists from Just Stop Oil gathered and poured soup over two Vincent Van Gogh paintings at the National Gallery in London - Westminster (England) just hours after other members of the group were sentenced to jail for a similar action, while demanding more climate action. Police forces arrested all of the protesters.

On 27 September 2024, Extinction Rebellion activists marched in Helsinki as part of the 'Boiling Point' campaign aimed to stop what they saw as environmentally harmful subsidies and to take responsibility for environmental issues. Later, the activists blocked a major road and were dispersed by the police after refusing orders to clear the area. At least 78 activists were arrested.

On 28 September 2024, fifteen XR activists protested, seven of them climbing on the grounds of the Amercentrale power plant near Geertruidenberg (Noord-Brabant). The protest, organized by XR, Quit with Coal, 'WISE Netherlands' (WISE Nederland), and Committee Clean Air (Comite Schone Lucht), called for an end to emissions and the removal of emission rights, opposing the shift to biomass, which they considered greenwashing. The police physically removed the protesters at 16:00.

On 28 September 2024, in the afternoon, during a march for Palestine in the center of Eindhoven (Noord-Brabant), a participant was arrested by the police after acting aggressively toward a PowNed camera crew. The march began on 18 September Square and made its way through the city center. Tensions rose between the demonstrators and the crew, with demonstrators claiming the journalists were provocatively pushing the camera in participants' faces. The altercation resulted in a police report being filed, as the cameraman sustained a black eye and a scratch on his nose.

On 28 September 2024, around 200 Last Generation activists blocked a traffic intersection in downtown Kassel (Hessen), to protest against the multimillion-euro subsidy of Kassel-Calden Airport funded with taxpayer money. The police intervened by carrying away a large portion of the protesters after they failed to respond to requests to allow traffic to flow.

On 29 September 2024, animal rights activists from the Vegan Strike Group and Animal Rebellion Noord disrupted a dolphin show at the Dolfinarium in Harderwijk (Gelderland), demanding its closure due to inadequate living conditions for dolphins and other marine mammals. During the demonstration, two activists entered the water, leading to their arrest.

On 29 September 2024, under the motto 'Lebanese resistance', members of the Arab community and leftist groups gathered for a pro-Palestine demonstration in Berlin - Mitte (Berlin). The demonstration was marked by anti-Israel sentiment and involved aggressive behavior. The police arrested several demonstrators.

On 30 September 2024, at the call of the far-right group Chouan Movement (Mouvement Chouan) and far-right student group RED - Rally of Right-Wing Students (Rassemblement Etudiant de Droite), around 150 people gathered in Angers (Pays de la Loire). The event took place after the death of Philippine, a 19-year student who was found dead in the Bois de Boulogne on 21 September. The main suspect is a Moroccan man who had already been found guilty of rape in the past and was under the obligation to leave French territory (OQTF) at the time of Philippine's death. The protesters condemned 'mass migration', which they considered responsible for the increase in crime, and what they deemed the French justice's leniency towards foreign criminals. A few streets away from the demonstration, around 70 Antifa affiliates gathered to denounce what they considered the far-right's 'weaponization' of Philippine's death. Police used tear gas to disperse the Antifa demonstrators.

On 30 September 2024, around 20 to 30 pro-Palestinian activists staged a protest in Berlin - Mitte (Berlin) by attempting to disrupt an event hosted by the CDU-affiliated Konrad Adenauer Foundation, opposing Israel's actions in Gaza and expressing solidarity with the Palestinian cause. The demonstration included activists wearing Palestinian scarves and chanting slogans against Israel, resulting in police intervention to clear the blockade, by carrying the protesters away.

On 1 October 2024, during the Cyprus Independence Day parade in Nicosia, 4 protesters raised a banner reading 'Republic of Cyprus: the only solution' opposite the dignitaries' stage. Police removed the protesters and when 2 of them, a Greek Cypriot journalist and a Turkish Cypriot political activist, confronted them verbally, police arrested them.

On 1 October 2024, activists from the Emergency Break movement demonstrated in Copenhagen, in connection with the opening of the new parliamentary session and called for an end to motorway construction due to environmental concerns. The activists attempted to prevent the Danish Prime Minister Mette Frederiksen from entering parliament and were arrested at the spot.

On 3 October 2024, a group of pro-Palestinian activists interrupted a debate in the Swedish Parliament in Stockholm and threw a bag of tomatoes at the Minister of Foreign Affairs, Maria Malmer Stenergard. Three activists were later removed from the premises.

On 4 October 2024, between hundreds and 2,000 students held a protest outside the Department of Education in Murcia (Murcia) to denounce the lack of transparency of the newly implemented college entrance exam and demanded more information. Protesters threw lemons and eggs at the police who charged them. One person was physically by the police.

On 4 October 2024, police removed four squatters from the former cafe De Drie Snoekjes in Gouda (Zuid-Holland), which had been vacant for four years. The squatters were protesting against long-term property vacancy and called for the abolition of the anti-squatting law.

On 4 October 2024, around 60 people gathered for a pro-Palestinian demonstration called 'Vigil for Gaza' in Berlin - Mitte (Berlin). The police intervened due to actions, such as tearing Israeli paper flags. Police reported that the protest included speeches by minors, leading to an investigation against a mother for alleged failure of care. A total of ten individuals were temporarily detained.

On 5 October 2024, hundreds of people, including students, antifascists, and pro-Palestine activists, took to the streets of Cagliari (Sardegna) to protest against the war in Gaza, the Israeli government, and the Security Decree, a law proposal that they believe would significantly hinder people's freedom to protest and demonstrate publicly. The demonstration had not been authorized. When protesters tried to break through the police lines, the police pushed and reportedly beat them with truncheons.

On 5 October 2024, squatters returned to the vacant cafe De Drie Snoekjes in Gouda (Zuid-Holland), leading to the arrest by the police of five individuals who did not provide identification. The protestors urged the government to take stricter measures against prolonged property vacancy and highlighted the growing homelessness issue in the country.

On 5 October 2024, at the call of PSC, 300,000 pro-Palestine protesters marched from Russell Square to Trafalgar Square and Downing Street in London - Westminster (England) ahead of the anniversary of the October 7 attacks as part of a national demonstration to call for ending the 'genocide' in Gaza and stop arming Israel. Protesters carried Palestinian flags and chanted 'Free, free Palestine', while others held banners stating 'We do not stand with genocide'. Protesters also chanted against companies and institutions complicit in Israel's crimes throughout the march. A group of pro-Israeli protesters also gathered in Covent Garden for a counter-demonstration. The protests remained peaceful but police forces arrested 15 people on suspicion of public order offences and assaults. The report does not specify whether the police arrested protesters or counter protesters.

On 5 October 2024, hundreds of people held a march in Brussels - Ville de Bruxelles (Brussels) to demand an end to all government support for the fossil fuel industry in the European Union (EU). Over 150 activists, including Greta Thunberg, organized a blockade in the city center. Extinction Rebellion (XR) and United for Climate Justice (UCJ), a coalition of climate groups, organized the rally. Police arrested more than 100 protesters due to traffic blocking.

On 5 October 2024, 400 people gathered for a solidarity rally in Aichach (Bayern), organized for an imprisoned soldier from Ingolstadt, who was incarcerated for refusing vaccination and not paying a fine. The participants marched from the city square to the local correctional facility (JVA), expressing their support for the soldier and protest against his imprisonment. One individual was briefly arrested at the event.

On 6 October 2024, at the call of the Galician Committee for Solidarity with Palestine (Coordenadora Galega de Solidariedade con Palestina), around 4,000 people took to the streets in Santiago de Compostela (Galicia) to demonstrate in solidarity with the Palestinian people and against Israeli military operations in Palestine and Lebanon, with some demonstrators spray-painting the facades of buildings during the demonstration march. UIP unit police officers arrested at least five participants after about 20 of them entered a Burger King restaurant and shouted slogans denouncing the company's operations in Israel. A police cordon was subsequently assembled outside the restaurant. The police said that some officers were injured during the demonstration.

On 6 October 2024, police arrested 4 participants of the food distribution campaign for the homeless in Yekaterinburg (Ekaterinburg, Sverdlovsk). The event was not only humanitarian in nature. The organizers, associated with the Confederation of Anarchists of Yekaterinburg, hung posters in support of political measures to help the homeless.

On 7 October 2024, pro-Palestine protesters gathered outside the BAE Systems site in Blackburn (England) to protest against the sale of arms to Israel by BAE Systems. Police forces arrested two protesters.

On 7 October 2024, police officers intervened in a ZAD (zone to defend) area in Verfeil (Occitanie) and arrested all 16 activists who were sitting on a roof to protest against the construction of the A69 highway between Toulouse and Castres, which they deemed damaging to the environment.

On 7 October 2024, thousands of pro-Israeli protesters held a rally at Dam Square in Amsterdam (Noord-Holland) to mark the first anniversary of the Israel-Hamas war and to show their support for Israel. Pro-Palestinian counter-protesters rallied on Damrak Avenue to express solidarity with the Palestinian people and to condemn Israel's military operations on Gaza. The tensions escalated when some pro-Palestinian protesters allegedly sought confrontation as pro-Israel demonstrators walked by. Riot police intervened several times, and some minor physical altercations occurred. The riot police prevented the counter-demonstrators from reaching Dam Square. Eventually, 26 arrests were made at the pro-Israel demonstration, and 328 counter-demonstrators were detained after relocating to Nieuwezijds Voorburgwal. The counter-demonstrators later staged a sit-in at Central Station, which proceeded peacefully without further arrests. These demonstrations occurred amid the ongoing Israel-Hamas war, which began in October 2023.

On 7 October 2024, around 200 people gathered for a pro-Palestine protest, marching from Schlossplatz to Rotebuhlplatz, in Stuttgart (Baden-Wurttemberg) under the theme 'Against the Ongoing War in Gaza and for Solidarity with Palestine.' During the event, police arrested a 45-year-old individual for being masked, which is a violation of assembly laws. Simultaneously, there was a pro-Israel rally nearby at Marktplatz with around 350 participants.

On 8 October 2024, police pushed protesters away from the administration building in Chulman (Neryungrinskiy, Republic of Sakha). People came to the administration building, demanding a solution to the problem of homeless animals in the village. The specific reason for the gathering was an attack by a pack of stray dogs on a child.

On 8 October 2024, about 25 pro-Palestinian protesters held a rally and blocked access to the OIP company in Oudenaarde (Vlaanderen) to mark the first anniversary of the Israel-Hamas war, to express solidarity with the Palestinian people and to condemn Israel's military operations on Gaza. They demanded halting what they saw as OIP's involvement in supplying military equipment to Israel. OIP produces thermal cameras, night vision devices, and other military equipment and is part of Elbit, an Israeli military technology company. Police cleared the entrance and arrested twelve people. This demonstration occurred amid the ongoing Israel-Hamas war, which began in October 2023.

On 8 October 2024, three pro-Palestine activists from Palestine Action staged a protest at Allianz Insurance offices in Guildford (England) over the company's investments and ties to Israeli-based weapon manufacturer Elbit Systems. Protesters climbed onto a glass canopy above the entrance to the building. Police forces intervened and removed the protesters and arrested all three.

On 9 October 2024, around 100 students blocked access to the main Sciences Po Paris campus in Paris (Ile-de-France) to express solidarity with the Palestinian and Lebanese people and condemn what they deemed a 'massacre' of Palestinian and Lebanese civilians by the Israeli army. Police physically removed all protesters from the entrance.

On 9 October 2024, 7 Last Generation activists staged a protest at Kassel Airport in Calden (Hessen). They entered the airport grounds, planted small trees on the runway, and protested against the airport's environmental impact, calling for its 'renaturation'. The police arrested all seven of them, and charged them with offenses including dangerous interference with air traffic and trespassing.

On 9 October 2024, 3 activists from the group 'Stop Tesla' staged a protest near the Tesla factory in Grunheide (Mark) (Brandenburg), by occupying a construction digger for over 20 hours to block earthworks for a new freight station, preventing construction work in the area. Around 25 to 30 additional protesters supported them in the nearby forest, playing loud music and chanting slogans. After initials attempts to remove the activists failed, the police used tear gas when some protesters tried to breach the fence.

On 10 October 2024, people organized a human chain around the Buchholz bookstore in Lisboa (Lisboa) to protest against the presence of four activists of the Habeas Corpus far-right association, after Habeas Corpus called on its affiliates to attend and disrupt a book presentation organized by the Association of Mothers and Fathers for the Freedom of Sexual Orientation and Gender Identity (Associacao de Maes e Pais pela Liberdade de Orientacao Sexual e Identidade de Genero - AMPLOS) at the venue to 'aim to help families have better relationships with LGBT children.' The police intervened, with some officers dragging AMPLOS supporters away to put an end to the human chain.

On 11 October 2024, at the call of SLT and LGV, No Thank You (LGV, Non Merci), 11 people drove (in 3 cars and 1 tractor) from Saint-Jorys to Grisolles (Occitanie) to protest against the construction of a high-speed train line between Bordeaux and Toulouse, which they deemed damaging to local biodiversity. The protesters were originally planning to reach a climate protest camp in Lerm-et-Musset. As five of them refused to comply with a gendarmerie check in Grisolles, they were arrested and the convoy stopped.

On 12 October 2024, at the call of Shannonwatch, Cairde Palestine Belfast, and Mothers Against Genocide, thousands of pro-Palestine protesters gathered outside Shannon Airport in Shannon (Clare) against the use of the airport by US military planes, notably transporting weapons to Israel. Independent MEP Luke 'Ming' Flanagan and PBP TD Richard Boyd Barrett also attended the protest. Demonstrators carried Palestinian and Lebanese flags. The protest was peaceful but police forces arrested two people concerning public order incidents.

On 12 October 2024, at the call of LGV, No Thank You (LGV, Non Merci) and SLT, around 100 people cycled from various localities to the Saint-Jean train station in Bordeaux (Nouvelle-Aquitaine) to demonstrate against the construction of a high-speed train line between Bordeaux and Toulouse, which they deemed damaging to local biodiversity. Police (CRS unit) intervened to remove the demonstrators from the scene.

On 12 October 2024, at the call of the Gaza Genocide Emergency Committee, pro-Palestine protesters gathered outside a Barclays bank in Argyle Street in Glasgow (Scotland) calling for a boycott due to Barclays' alleged financial investments in Israel. Social media posts showed protestors inside the bank holding banners, with one dressed as the Grim Reaper. The demonstrators claimed to have successfully closed the branch. Police forces arrested one of the protesters, Mike Napier, a prominent leader of the Scottish Palestine Solidarity Campaign.

On 12 October 2024, police physically intervened in a squatting attempt and demonstration. Demonstrators trying to squat a building were protesting against the housing crisis and the vacancy of a building in Korte Groenendaal, Gouda (Zuid-Holland). They displayed Palestinian flags and banners. The protest escalated when some demonstrators, dressed in black and wearing face coverings, confronted the police, shouting and making aggressive gestures toward the officers. This confrontation prompted the police to use force to disperse the crowd, resulting in five arrests. According to the spokesperson of the squatters, the police hit some of them on the head.

On 12 October 2024, the police physically ended a demonstration by several dozen protesters of Extinction Rebellion (XR) and Quit with Coal in Haarlem (Noord-Holland), where protesters blocked Paviljoenslaan near the North Holland provincial house. The activists protested against Tata Steel, calling it a major polluter, and demanded the closure of two outdated coke gas plants. The demonstrators were removed by bus.

On 13 October 2024, in the evening, NO TAV activists gathered in San Giuliano (Piemonte) to protest against the expropriation procedures related to the construction of the Turin-Lyon high-speed railway line. Protesters struck the fences of the construction site to create noise. The police used water cannons and tear gas to disperse the crowd, an intervention which was described as 'disproportionate' by the activists.

On 13 October 2024, approximately 25 squatters occupied an old chocolate and sugar factory in Gouda (Zuid-Holland) to protest against vacant buildings and the squatting ban. The police, including riot units and dogs, intervened and surrounded the group. Several arrests were made, though the exact number is unclear. One protester was bitten in the leg by a police dog.

On 13 October 2024, gendarmes searched a climate camp and dismantled it in Lerm-et-Musset (Nouvelle-Aquitaine), while arresting an unspecified number of activists. The camp had been set up by environmental activists on 11 October at the call of SLT and LGV, No Thank You (LGV, Non Merci) to demonstrate against the construction of a high-speed train line between Bordeaux and Toulouse, which they deemed damaging to local biodiversity. Between 800 (according to authorities) and 1,500 demonstrators were present.

On 14 October 2024, a protest against the eviction of a squatted building took place at Lage Gouwe, Gouda (Zuid-Holland), where individuals opposing the eviction claimed the property had been vacant for a long time. The police was evicting for more than 5 hours, during which some squatters resisted, leading to the intervention of the riot unit. 23 individuals were arrested, including six who had to be removed from the roof, for reasons such as lack of identification and trespassing.

On 14 October 2024, protesters gathered in North Mitrovica to protest a visit by a Self-Determination party politician, using whistles to disrupt their visit. Police briefly arrested one of the protesters and a local politician from the Serbian Democracy party.

On 15 October 2024, around 100 people took part in a pro-Palestinian demonstration in Stockholm. Police later used pepper spray after demonstrators attempted to break through the police blockade. One person is suspected of violence against an officer.

On 15 October 2024, up to around 15 activists gathered in Wiener Neustadt (Niederosterreich) to protest against the construction of the eastern ring road in Wiener Neustadt. The protesters climbed onto construction machinery and displayed banners. The police intervened, leading to the preliminary arrest of three individuals who were uncooperative. The EKO Cobra police unit was deployed to assist in their removal from the machinery.

On 15 October 2024, residents in Bogetici blocked the road in protest, attempting to prevent the burial of the cows that had died of cow fever at the location of Ljeskovi doli situated near their houses. Three residents were arrested during the protest, after which the trucks carrying the dead livestock were able to pass.

On 18 October 2024, around 1,600 people gathered for a pro-Palestine protest, titled 'For a just peace in Palestine and Israel: Protect civilians, stop arms exports,' on Washingtonplatz in Berlin - Mitte (Berlin). The protest was called for by close to 40 organizations, including well-known human rights organizations such as Amnesty International Germany and Medico, Palestinian and Israeli groups, and left-wing organizations such as IL. The police reported a total of twelve preliminary arrests, indicating that participants were taken into custody for various offenses, including 'insult', 'incitement to hatred', and the 'use of symbols associated with unconstitutional organizations.'

On 18 October 2024, at 5 pm, around 500 people gathered for a pro-Palestine demonstration titled 'Joe Biden Is Not Welcome', at Alexanderplatz in Berlin - Mitte (Berlin), opposing both the war in the Middle East and criticizing US President Joe Biden's support for Israel, as he was visiting Berlin. The march, which was planned to proceed from Dircksenstrase to Alexanderufer, was interrupted multiple times by the police due to the chanting of slogans considered unconstitutional by authorities. Simultaneously, a small counter-protest of around 20 pro-Israel supporters took place near the Museumsinsel subway station nearby. Police intervened to keep both groups apart, and several arrests were made throughout the evening.

On 19 October 2024, around twenty activists from XR staged a protest at the Naturalis museum in Leiden (Zuid-Holland), holding a 'death march' for biodiversity while carrying a coffin labeled 'biodiversity.' The protest continued past the museum's closing time of 17:30, leading to police intervention when the demonstrators refused to leave. Some activists were forcibly removed by police, though no arrests were made. Naturalis has filed a complaint for trespassing against the protesters. This protest follows previous actions by XR in the museum.

On 20 October 2024, around 130 people gathered for a pro-Palestinian protest aimed to advocate for 'Freedom for Palestine and Lebanon' in Munster (Nordrhein-Westfalen), where the police intervened and dissolved the event after taking a speaker into custody. The 27-year-old speaker, who was arrested, had previously been banned from speaking at events due to past offenses, refused to stop his address, leading to his removal. Some attendees reacted by resisting police actions, prompting the authorities to disband the gathering for safety reasons. Participants had also been reported for chanting prohibited slogans.

On 21 October 2024, police officers from the CRS unit removed around 80 members of the CLAP Petanque Club occupying their petanque field in Paris (Ile-de-France) to protest against their planned expulsion, which was ordered by a French court. The occupation was going on since 22 April 2024.

On 21 October 2024, XR activists blocked the Zeesluis in IJmuiden (Noord-Holland) to prevent the MSC Virtuosa cruise ship from passing, citing the cruise industry's harmful impact on the climate, resulting in the ship experiencing a two-hour delay. Around sixty counter-demonstrators protested against XR's actions, displaying banners with slogans and booing the climate activists, arguing that the locks and ships are essential for their livelihoods. The police maintained a distance between the two groups to prevent confrontations. Approximately ten XR activists chained themselves to the lock gates, and police physically pulled them away as they refused to leave voluntarily. The activists were taken away by bus to the nearby station Santpoort-Zuid, where they were subsequently released.

On 22 October 2024, around ten activists were arrested by the police while protesting against coal trains at the Westelijk Havengebied in Amsterdam (Noord-Holland), demanding the closure of all coal power plants in the Netherlands. The demonstration was initiated by Quit with Coal, and aimed for an immediate end to the importation of coal from Colombia. The protest was disbanded by Mayor Halsema after the activists did not comply with an order to move away from the tracks, leading to the arrests.

On 22 October 2024, four activists gathered for a protest against the expansion of the Tesla factory in Grunheide (Mark) (Brandenburg). The police intervened by removing the activists from two excavators near the factory and detaining them for identification, with no reported injuries. The protest aimed to oppose ongoing construction works related to the factory's expansion, which involves the creation of a construction road for the German Railway and the development of new storage facilities.

On 23 October 2024, activists from the Emergency Break movement staged a protest and blocked a major road in Copenhagen, calling for an end to motorway construction due to environmental concerns. During the demonstration, a protester was run over by a car, with no injuries reported at the time. Police personnel later removed activists from the demonstration site.

On 23 October 2024, around 22 activists from the Green Youth Movement entered the Danish Ministry for the Green Tripartite in Copenhagen to show their opposition to the recently developed Tripartite Agreement that is aimed to transform Denmark's agricultural practices towards sustainability by reducing greenhouse gas emissions and protecting biodiversity. The activists protested against what they perceived as insufficient commitments, arguing that the agreement lacked the actions necessary to achieve real climate justice and environmental protection. The activists were later dispersed and removed from the site by police.

On 24 October 2024, 5 to 10 protesters gathered at the construction site of the east bypass road in Wiener Neustadt (Niederosterreich), to oppose tree-clearing activities. The police intervened, dispersing the unauthorized assembly and briefly detaining one demonstrator who had attached themselves to a tree.

On 25 October 2024, approximately 20 protesters gathered in Geffen (Noord-Brabant) near the dog training company Four Winds K9, blocking access to the company until around 3:45 PM. The protest was organized by Justice Now, with participation from Extinction Rebellion and the director of Landschap Overijssel. The demonstration opposed the suspected training of attack dogs for use by Israel against Palestinians. No damage occurred, but twelve demonstrators were arrested by the police.

On 25 October 2024, people demonstrated outside of the Cabinet of Iceland in Reykjavik urging the Icelandic government to take swift action regarding the Palestine-Israel war and Israeli attacks on Lebanon. During the demonstration, a minor was arrested.

On 25 October 2024, people marched in Gothenburg (Goteborg), Vastra Gotaland, to show support and solidarity with Palestine amid the Israeli offensive in Gaza. Activists also paid tribute to the late chairman of the Hamas Political Bureau, Yahya Sinwar, who was eliminated by the Israeli Defense Forces in Gaza on October 2024. Several activists were detained or removed from the demonstration site after they failed to comply with police demands. The demonstration was later reported for its perceived anti-Semitic sentiments.

On 25 October 2024, activists from the Emergency Break movement blocked a major road in Copenhagen, calling for an end to motorway construction due to environmental concerns. Police later removed the activists from the site after they failed to comply with police demands, and move them to a sidewalk.

On 26 October 2024, thousands of supporters of far-right activist Tommy Robinson marched from Victoria Station to Parliament Square in London - Westminster (England) for a 'pro-UK' rally endorsed by Robinson. Demonstrators held Union flags and signs reading 'Bring back Rwanda' and 'Stop the Boats.' Robinson did not attend the rally, as he was in police custody following charges linked to a film screening in July 2024. In response, a counter-demonstration organized by SUTR also gathered nearby, with participation from various unions, independent politicians, and student groups, who marched from Regent Street to the northern end of Whitehall and spoke against the far-right, fascism, and racism. Both demonstrations remained largely peaceful, though there were reported instances of pushes and shoves, and police arrested four individuals from both sides for breaches of public order, including racially aggravated offenses.

On 26 October 2024, between 150 and 200 people, including LFI affiliates, gathered in Vertou (Pays de la Loire) to protest the visit of RN Vice-President Sebastien Chenu. The demonstration was unauthorized due to concerns over public order, and gendarmerie forces used tear gas to disperse protesters attempting to reach the city center. Three demonstrators sustained minor injuries to the ear, head, and leg. The protest reflected opposition to the RN's policies, with demonstrators criticizing the party's stance as contradictory to the interests of ordinary citizens.

On 26 October 2024, around 350 gathered in Berlin - Tempelhof-Schoneberg (Berlin), to protest in support of Palestine, calling for an end to the Gaza genocide and arms sales to Israel. The protesters carried Palestinian, Lebanese, and Iranian flags, and chanted slogans such as 'Free Gaza' and 'Free Lebanon.' The police arrested some demonstrators who shouted the controversial slogan 'From the river to the sea, Palestine will be free,' A small counter-protest with up to 25 participants took place nearby.

On 26 October 2024, under the motto 'Solidarity with Palestine: Stop the Gaza Genocide, No Weapons for Israel, Stop the War in Lebanon', around 400 people gathered on Wittenberg Square in Berlin - Mitte (Berlin). The event featured anti-police chants, with demonstrators facing several restrictions from the police due to violations of assembly laws, resulting in multiple detentions and investigations. Under the motto 'Counter-Protest to the Pro-Palestine Demonstration: Solidarity with Israel and the IDF, Stop the Terror for the Freedom of the Hostages', around 25 people gathered for a counter-protest.

On 26 October 2024, under the motto 'Stop the Genocide in Gaza and Lebanon', around 380 people gathered in Berlin - Neukolln (Berlin), to protest against Israel's military action in Gaza and Lebanon. Police enforced participation bans on two individuals, responded to attempts to disrupt the identification of another participant, and arrested several demonstrators for illegal slogans, including 'From the River to the Sea.' At the same time, 9 people gathered for a pro-Israel counter-protest under the motto 'Solidarity with Israel and the IDF for the Release of the Hostages.'

On 26 October 2024, under the motto 'Against Attacks by the Turkish State in Rojava', around 120 people gathered in Berlin - Friedrichshain-Kreuzberg (Berlin), to protest against the actions of the Turkish state in Rojava, specifically addressing the bombings conducted by Turkey in that region. The event included slogans and messages opposing the Turkish government's military actions and saw heightened tension when a participant displayed the 'Wolfsgrus,' leading to police intervention, a dispersal order, and an arrest following an attempted assault by another protester.
