On 26 October 2024, around 80 Last Generation activists staged a protest in Oldenburg (Niedersachsen), by blocking a major intersection in the city center, aiming to draw attention to climate issues. The police detained around 20 participants.

On 26 October 2024, about 1,000 Code Rood activists blocked access to the Noordkasteel Bridge at the port of Antwerpen (Vlaanderen) to protest against TotalEnergies' activities, and against the war in Gaza. They also blocked the Boomsesteenweg in Wilrijk and protested on the Scheldelaan. These events were part of a number of coordinated actions by Code Rood that occurred on the same weekend. The police arrested at least 270 demonstrators, including two journalists and seven lawyers, redirected traffic and eventually dismantled the protests around 16:00. Three legal observers from the LDH who were present, arrested and detained without cause, resulting in the LDH taking the Belgian state to court as of 24 June 2025.

On 27 October 2024, Extinction Rebellion associated group blocked a road outside of the Copenhagen Kastrup Airport in Kastrup, Hovedstaden, calling for a ban on private jets and opposing the aviation industry. Police later removed the activists from the site after they failed to comply with police demands.

On 28 October 2024, around 40 Greenpeace activists gathered inside and around the Gravelines nuclear power plant (Hauts-de-France) to protest the planned expansion of the facility, which they argued was increasingly dangerous due to rising sea levels. Activists used paint to mark the plant's walls, displayed banners on zodiac boats, and released blue smoke to symbolize encroaching water. The protest, part of Greenpeace's ongoing campaign against the addition of two new reactors, highlighted the risks of nuclear accidents due to climate-related flooding. Police arrested 25 activists during the demonstration.

On 28 October 2024, seven activists from the Emergency Break movement blocked a motorway exit in Roedovre, Hovedstaden, calling for an end to motorway construction due to environmental concerns. Police later removed several activists from the site after they failed to comply with police demands.

On 28 October 2024, at the call of 'Young Struggle' and 'Palestine at the forefront', around 30 to 50 people gathered outside the Criminal Court in Berlin - Mitte (Berlin), to protest against the trial of a 20-year-old student. The protesters aimed to show support for the student, who was facing charges of approving criminal acts and attacking law enforcement after distributing anti-Israel flyers and participating in a pro-Palestinian gathering in Berlin - Neukolln on 21 October 2024. The police intervened by arresting two participants for unclear reasons and filing charges against the rally organizer for playing a banned song.

On 29 October 2024, a group of protesters occupied a supermarket in Lisieux (Normandie) to demand decent housing for homeless families who had been evicted from a squat owned by the Inolya company in Caen (Normandie). Police later physically removed the protesters from the supermarket. The protest action, claimed on the website Attaque, followed the eviction of around forty people who had occupied the property since June 2023.

On 29 October 2024, hundreds of XR activists marched through the insurance district in London - City of London (England) as part of their 'Insure Our Survival' campaign, demanding that the insurance industry stop underwriting new fossil fuel projects. Activists gathered outside SwissRe's headquarters, where some entered the lobby and unfurled banners calling for an end to support for fossil fuel projects like the East Africa Crude Oil Pipeline, while some also lined up with a symbolic wheelbarrow carrying a giant potato and bowls with single peas to draw attention to the impending food shortages linked to climate change. Throughout the day, protesters targeted various insurance firms, accusing them of perpetuating the climate crisis. Police forces arrested six activists, including an 80-year-old retired healthcare worker, for their involvement in non-violent direct actions such as covering premises with posters and chalk spray paint.

On 29 October 2024, approximately seventy pro-Palestinian students occupied the I-building at the Vrije Universiteit Brussel (VUB) campus in Brussels - Etterbeek (Brussels), to protest VUB's academic ties with Israeli institutions and in solidarity with a hospital in Jabalia, Gaza. The university did not support this protest, and police intervened around 17:00, forcibly removing students and their belongings without making arrests. According to activists, the police encircled and 'brutally' removed them, though the university maintains the intervention was 'calm but firm.'

On 30 October 2024, protesters occupied the headquarters of real estate company Inolya and a media library in Lisieux (Normandie) to demand housing for homeless families evicted the previous day from their long-term squat in Caen (Normandie). The squat, owned by Inolya and housing approximately forty people since June 2023, was cleared by police despite the upcoming winter truce. Police later removed the demonstrators from both the Inolya headquarters and the media library.

On 30 October 2024, several supporters of the Victory Bloc (associated with the SOR party) protested in Chisinau - Centru by rolling a large balloon bearing the image of President Maia Sandu, calling for her removal from office. The police intervened and stopped the protest, detaining one participant.

On 1 November 2024, around 30 people, called by Animaslistak, held a protest at the Aquarium of San Sebastian (Pais Vasco). Protesters broke peacefully into the building and blocked the entrance. 3 people were arrested.

On 1 November 2024, No TAV activists gathered at the High-Speed Turin-Lyon railway (TAV) work site in San Didero (Piemonte), where they held a loud protest by striking the site's fences to demonstrate against the project. The protest followed an aperitif and toast at the San Didero Presidio in celebration of past No TAV 'resistance efforts'. Police stationed at the site responded with water cannons, but the activists continued to march around the site to protest.

On 2 November 2024, at the call of PSC and on the occasion of Balfour Day, tens of thousands of pro-Palestine protesters, including independent politician and MP Jeremy Corbyn, held a march from Whitehall in London - Westminster to the US Embassy in London - Wandsworth (England) to protest US support for Israel amid ongoing conflicts in Palestine and Lebanon. Protesters carried Palestinian and Lebanese flags, with signs reading 'Free Palestine' and 'End Israeli apartheid.' Meanwhile, a small pro-Israel counter-protest took place nearby, with demonstrators holding British and Israeli flags and calling for the release of Israeli hostages held in Gaza. The Metropolitan Police reported arrests related to 'suspected support for proscribed organizations' among pro-Palestinian demonstrators.

On 4 November 2024, more than 40 people gathered inside the French Football Federation (FFF) headquarters in Paris (Ile-de-France) to demand the cancellation of the France-Israel match, scheduled for 14 November 2024. The protesters condemned what they considered a 'genocide' of Gazans by the Israeli army and expressed solidarity with the Palestinian people. After a few hours, police removed the protesters from the scene and arrested some of them.

On 4 November 2024, the police intervened and ended a protest in the Golzheim neighborhood in Dusseldorf (Nordrhein-Westfalen) and took away the activists who occupied an apartment the previous days at the end of a protest against property owners' tactics to evict tenants.

On 5 November 2024, around 60 people gathered to disrupt a lecture at the University of Leipzig (Sachsen) about prostitution. The protest was organized by various groups, including the Queerfeminist Group Leipzig, the Open Anarchist Network Leipzig, and the Left.SDS, in response to transphobic statements made by the speaker, Inge Kleine, associated with the Sisters E.V. organization. The protest led to a large police presence, which, after being called by the university, detained and identified the participants for several hours before issuing charges for trespassing. The student body criticized the police's actions, describing the measures as overly repressive.

On 6 November 2024, seasonal firefighters rallied at the ministry for Civil Protection in Athens - North Athens to protest for year-round contracts and permanent positions, while their representatives were meeting the minister. OPKE and security police detained 3 youths, who participated in the protest in solidarity with the firefighters, after they searched them and found a banner in one of their bags. They also detained a seasonal firefighter, who defended them asking the police officers to release them.

On 6 November 2024, construction workers rallied in Patras during a strike-protest for collective labor agreements and a pay rise. According to the Labor Center of Patras, while their leader was making a speech, MAT riot police attacked the construction workers without provocation, pushing and beating them and using tear gas and stun grenades.

On 7 November 2024, pro-Palestinian demonstrators gathered at the Anton de Komplein in Amsterdam (Noord-Holland), as part of a planned protest related to the football match between Ajax and Maccabi Tel Aviv. Activists attempted twice to march toward the arena, but police successfully blocked their path and drove them back. In the run-up to the match, 57 people were arrested.

On 8 November 2024, activists from Quit With Coal and XR Zeeland protested at the OVET coal handling facility in Vlissingen-Oost (Zeeland) by climbing over the perimeter fence and occupying part of the site. The group aimed to disrupt coal operations, calling for an immediate cessation of coal use due to its environmental impact. After nearly two hours, the police intervened, arresting seven of the nine protesters, who were later released after identity checks.

On 9 November 2024, a group of 12 environmental activists from Quit with Coal and Extinction Rebellion Zeeland, protested at Ovet's facility in Terneuzen (Zeeland), demanding an immediate halt to coal use. Nine of the activists were arrested after minor vandalism was carried out at the property.

On 9 November 2024, around 1,300 people gathered in Karlsruhe (Baden-Wurttemberg), to protest against a far-right commemoration march organized by the party The Right. Protesters opposed the gathering held on a historically significant date in Germany, with the event remaining mostly peaceful aside from minor police interventions involving a person from the left-wing spectrum who was temporarily arrested for striking a police horse, and some individuals were issued dispersal orders.

On 10 November 2024, 'ecureuils' (activists occupying trees in protest of the construction of the Bordeaux-Toulouse high-speed rail line) were forcibly removed by police forces in Saint-Jory (Occitanie).

On 10 November 2024, a pro-Palestinian demonstration occurred on the Dam and in Nieuwendijk in Amsterdam (Noord-Holland), despite a city-wide demonstration ban. The police, after repeated warnings, used force to disperse the crowd, including baton charges against demonstrators. Approximately 340 demonstrators were arrested or relocated, with many transported by buses to other areas. One woman sustained an injury to her head, initially attributed to a fall, but later investigations revealed it was likely caused by a baton strike by a Mobile Unit police officer. The police are investigating the incidents of potential excessive use of force by their Mobile Units, as social media videos and eyewitness reports raised concerns about excessive use of force.

On 11 November 2024, about 1000 activists gathered for a patriotic march through Wroclaw, praising Polish sovereignty and independence. At least part of them criticized the European Union for what they see as challenging the Polish sovereignty and critically referred to alleged 'Banderism' in the contemporary Ukraine. One man was detained.

On 11 November 2024, around 60 pro-Palestinian demonstrators gathered at the Esplanade Solidarnosc near the European Parliament in Brussels - Ville de Bruxelles (Brussels), protesting EU complicity in the Israel-Palestine conflict, demanding a weapons embargo against Israel and the suspension of the EU-Israel association agreement. The police intervened around 12:30 pm, arresting 28 protesters, including six Palestinian undocumented migrants.

On 11 November 2024, 18 demonstrators occupied the Greek Embassy in Berlin - Mitte (Berlin), attempting to send an email from the embassy's computer. The email demanded the release of individuals who were imprisoned, but the embassy staff successfully prevented it from being sent in connection with a recent explosion in Athens. Embassy staff allowed them entry initially, but as the situation escalated, the police were called and cleared the building peacefully, with demonstrators now facing charges of violating assembly laws. Outside the embassy, 20 people staged a protest related to an explosion in Athens in late October, which had claimed the life of an anarchist, Kyriakos Xymitiris. The police intervened by removing 18 individuals from the embassy premises, issuing them orders to leave, and the embassy filed a report for trespassing.

On 12 November 2024, police arrested six demonstrators during a protest at the Stopera in Amsterdam (Noord-Holland) in support of Gaza and against the demonstration itself being banned. The demonstration was protesting the demonstration ban. The arrests were made peacefully.

On 12 November 2024, four activists from XR's branch XR Justice Now! smeared the KPN headquarters in Rotterdam (Zuid-Holland) with red paint for the second consecutive day, using fake blood to protest against KPN's sponsorship of the NEDS arms fair in Ahoy Rotterdam on 21 November. Three of the activists were arrested by the police.

On 13 November 2024, around 300 pro-Palestinian demonstrators gathered on the Dam in Amsterdam (Noord-Holland), despite the municipal ban that was put in place after the riots a few days earlier. The gathering was organized by six pro-Palestinian groups, and although the authorities designated Westergasterrein as the approved location, the 300 demonstrators assembled on the Dam. The police, in large numbers, attempted to disperse the group. The remaining demonstrators were surrounded, arrested, and placed on buses. Three buses were used to transport protesters to various locations, including the Westelijk Havengebied, where video footage released shows members of the Mobile Unit of the police using batons against demonstrators, leading to injuries, including one individual who was hospitalized with severe bruises. An investigation into this use of force has been launched by the police and the Amsterdam municipality. Police arrested 281 individuals.

On 14 November 2024, three activists from Extinction Rebellion were arrested for vandalizing KPN's headquarters on the Wilhelminapier in Rotterdam (Zuid-Holland). The building was defaced with fake blood, and slogans accusing KPN of sponsoring 'genocide' were written on the windows. This protest was part of a campaign against KPN's support for the upcoming arms fair at Ahoy, Rotterdam. The activists demand that KPN stop supporting events that promote the profit of companies involved in war and violence.

On 14 November 2024, activists from Internationalist Youth Communities climbed the 'Molecule Man' statue in Berlin - Friedrichshain-Kreuzberg (Berlin), unfurling a banner against Germany's military policies, including missile deployments and fighter jet sales to Turkey. The protest lasted hours, and police removed the banner and briefly detained three activists.

On 15 November 2024, in the morning, 24 students occupied a university building at the Drift 13 in Utrecht (Utrecht). The action was organized by a pro-Palestinian group named UU Encampment, and their demands included the severance of ties between Utrecht University and Israel. The police physically removed 24 demonstrators from the premises after they refused to leave. The police arrested three individuals for allegedly insulting officers, while the other 21 activists were transported away in a city bus.

On 16 November 2024, dozens of Kick Out Zwarte Piet (KOZP) activists, including leader Jerry Afriyie, protested during the Sinterklaas arrival in Middelharnis (Zuid-Holland), against the use of traditional Zwarte Piet costumes. Dozens of opposing demonstrators shouted insults, threw eggs, apples, and fireworks, and displayed blackface in support of Zwarte Piet. Police heavily guarded the protest area, used a drone, and escorted KOZP members to their buses for safety. Five people were arrested, two of them because of fireworks charges, and the other three because they threw apples and eggs at the KOZP protesters.

On 16 November 2024, around 20 activists from Kick Out Zwarte Piet (KOZP), XR Zeeland, and Zeeland Can Do It (Zeeland Kan Het) protested in Yerseke (Zeeland) against fully black-painted blackfaces ('pieten') at the Sinterklaas parade. Around 100 counter-protesters, including some fully black-painted individuals, disrupted the demonstration by throwing eggs, stones, and fireworks. The police intervened, made four arrests for throwing projectiles and incitement, and declared an emergency order requiring people to leave the area.

On 16 November 2024, about 500 people joined a pro-Palestine protest in Berlin - Charlottenburg-Wilmersdorf (Berlin), organized by pro-Palestinian groups with support from Mera25 and the Youth Organization of the Left (Germany) Berlin-Wedding, under the slogan 'Solidarity with Palestine. Stop the Gaza Genocide.' Demonstrators used fireworks, flares, and banned slogans. Police arrested 111 people for offenses, including incitement. A small pro-Israel counterprotest also occurred.

On 17 November 2024, about 300 activists gathered in front of the National Museum in Prague, protesting against the ongoing support of Czechia to Ukraine and hoisting Ukrainian flags od official state buildings. At least some of them supported the Russian and anti-western positions. Later they embarked on a march through the city. Five of them were detained.

On 17 November 2024, pro-Palestine protesters, including Dublin for Gaza activists and other groups, staged a protest at Shannon Airport in Shannon (Clare) against 'the Irish Government's failure to enact its own rules and stop the transportation of weapons bound for Israel through Shannon airport and surrounding Irish airspace'. Police forces arrested eight protesters for 'offenses contrary to the Criminal Justice'.

On 18 November 2024, XR Justice Now!, the pro-Palestinian branch of XR, protested at Rotterdam Ahoy (Zuid-Holland), by covering the venue with fake blood in opposition to the upcoming NEDS arms fair scheduled for 21 November. Two activists were arrested during the protest, which marks the eighth consecutive day of action by the group, which has also targeted KPN, a sponsor of the event. XR Justice Now! demanded that Ahoy cancel the arms fair and that KPN stop funding such events, calling for more responsible event hosting. Central to the controversy in the protest series is that one of the companies exposing at the arms fair is Israeli.

On 20 November 2024, around 70 farmers with 25 tractors and 30 vehicles, who left as a convoy from Agen through Montauban (Nouvelle-Aquitaine) in the morning, blocked the Grand Sud Logistique zone in Montbartier (Occitanie). They dumped manure and waste on the RD 820 roundabout and Graves Street, where they also lit a rapidly growing 'anger fire,' requiring firefighters' intervention. In the evening, 60 CRS police officers forcibly dispersed the protesters. The event was part of a nationwide demonstration movement by French farmers opposing the EU-Mercosur trade deal and condemning delays in agricultural reforms promised by the previous government following the winter 2023-2024 farmers' demonstrations.

On 20 November 2024, around 100 activists, including those from the Green Youth Movement blocked the Danish Ministry for the Green Tripartite in Copenhagen to show their opposition to the recently developed Tripartite Agreement that is aimed to transform Denmark's agricultural practices towards sustainability by reducing greenhouse gas emissions and protecting biodiversity. The activists protested against what they perceived as insufficient commitments, arguing that the agreement lacked the actions necessary to achieve real climate justice and environmental protection. The police later moved the activists from the site to clear the entrance.

On 20 November 2024, less than 50 activists from the group 'Stop Tesla!' gathered in Grunheide (Mark) (Brandenburg), near Tesla's factory, to protest against the clearing of a protest camp by the police. The activists opposed the environmental impact of the factory. Police cleared the protest camp, removing 11 activists from trees using a cherry picker, dismantling barricades, and securing the area to prevent further occupation.

On 21 November 2024, members of Rouvikonas protested outside the Ministry for Citizen Protection in Athens - Central Athens, scattering flyers demanding the release of a Kurdish prisoner. There were detentions.

On 21 November 2024, about two hundred pro-Palestinian activists, climate activists, members of the coalition Resistance Against War (Verzet Tegen Oorlog), and Extinction Rebellion (XR Justice Now!) protested at the Ahoy complex in Rotterdam (Zuid-Holland) against the NEDS arms fair, accusing Israel of committing genocide in Gaza. Demonstrators defaced the building with fake blood, blocked access roads, and shouted slogans at attendees. Police intervened by pushing back demonstrators and using physical force, removing them forcefully, and with members of the mobile unit striking protesters. Police made fifteen arrests throughout the day for vandalism, defying protest zones, and insulting an officer, while demonstrators reported being pushed back and struck by police.

On 22 November 2024, about 100 XR activists dumped manure on the sidewalk in front of the Ministry of the Interior in Roma - City Center (Lazio) and set up approximately 30 tents as part of a demonstration calling for action on climate security. The police intervened to disperse the protest, pulling demonstrators out of tents, dismantling and seizing the tents, and stopping individuals attempting to climb trees to display banners. Some activists, who practiced passive resistance, were taken to the police station for identification.

On 22 November 2024, members of the 'Let's Burn Everything' committee (Bruciamo Tutto) threw balloons filled with tempera paint at the facade of the Ministry of Education and Merit in Roma - City Center (Lazio). After the action, protesters sat on the ground with a banner displaying the group's name. Carabinieri intervened promptly, physically removing the demonstrators from the site. The motives behind the demonstration were not specified.

On 22 November 2024, student organizations marched towards the Faculty of Economics of the University of Rome in Roma - Tiburtino (Lazio), intending to reach and denounce a picket held by the right-wing student union AU, to denounce the climate of 'tension and hate' at the university. Between Castro Laurenziano Street and Ippocrate Street, DIGOS police officers resorted to light charges to disperse the demonstrators taking part in the march.

On 22 November 2024, police forces began to dismantle a pro-Palestinian encampment outside the University of Gothenburg building in Gothenburg (Goteborg), Vastra Gotaland, due to a planned demonstration in the area. Several activists refused to leave the area and chained themselves. The police later removed the activists from the area and several people were forcibly carried away. Total of around 100 activists were present at the demonstration site.

On 25 November 2024, women rallied outside a police station in Chalandri, Athens - North Athens, in solidarity with a woman refusing to hand over her child to the father who had custody. They were joined by a Course of Freedom MP and a journalist, who was briefly detained.

On 25 November 2024, about 15 activists from Christian Collective (Christelijk Collectief) and the pro-Palestinian XR: Justice Now protested in front of the building of Christenen voor Israel in Nijkerk (Gelderland) with slogans like 'stop child murder' and 'baby killers' to protest against what they viewed as the organization's complicity in actions in Gaza, the West Bank, and Lebanon. They painted the building with slogans, and four activists were arrested for vandalism.
On 25 November 2024, Last Generation activists gathered and blocked a main highway in Warsaw, demanding immediate climate action. Later they were removed from the spot by law enforcers.

On 26 November 2024, around 35,000 members and supporters of the main Albanian opposition party, the Democratic Party of Albania, protested in central Tirana as a continuation of their protests for months demanding the resignation of the current government and mayor of Tirana. Police used water spray cannons, tear gas, and force on them. 63 protesters were arrested.

On 26 November 2024, about 500 activists gathered in Celje in front of a local court, declaring their support for Janez Jansa, a politician and former MP, who organizes frequent protests of pensioners, over his unclear real estate business deals. One person was detained over verbal assaults against present journalists. Members of the SDS party actively participated too.

On 26 November 2024, around 70 demonstrators, including activists from Extinction Rebellion, blocked the entrance to an energy conference in Oslo attended by Equinor, a Norwegian state-owned energy company, the Norwegian Ministry of Petroleum and Energy, and the International Energy Agency (IEA), among others. Activists called on Equinor to halt development of the controversial Rosebank oil field in the United Kingdom, citing environmental concerns. Police later removed around 10 to 15 activists who refused to comply with the police orders to leave the site.
On 26 November 2024, Last Generation activists gathered and blocked a main highway in Warsaw, demanding immediate climate action. Later they were removed from the spot by law enforcers.

On 27 November 2024, Wageningen University had the police dismantle a pro-Palestinian encampment on its campus in Wageningen (Gelderland), citing safety concerns due to storm Cornall. The police intervened when demonstrators arrived to protest the sudden removal. The activists from Wageningen Encampment, who had been occupying the site since May to protest the university's ties with Israeli institutions, claimed they were not informed beforehand and felt caught off guard. The police used batons to keep demonstrators at bay and pushed them to remove them.

On 27 November 2024, members of the Kurdish community held a protest outside the Kurdish Community Centre in London - Haringey (England), following the arrest of six individuals during dawn raids as part of a counter-terrorism investigation. The arrests were linked to alleged activities connected to the Kurdistan Workers' Party (PKK), which was classified as a terrorist organization in the UK at the time of reporting. Protesters gathered peacefully to voice their concerns over the arrests and the closure of the community center for up to two weeks as part of the investigation. The Metropolitan Police maintained a presence at the protest and arrested four participants, though arrest motives were not specified.
On 27 November 2024, Last Generation activists gathered and blocked a main highway in Warsaw, demanding immediate climate action. At least 16 of them were removed from the spot by law enforcers.

On 28 November 2024, the police dismantled the pro-Palestinian protest camp set up at the campus of Wageningen University in Wageningen (Gelderland). The occupation had been ongoing since 15 May 2024.

On 29 November 2024, about 40 activists from Extinction Rebellion conducted a blockade at the Chemours factory in Dordrecht (Zuid-Holland). They demanded that Chemours cease PFAS emissions due to their harmfulness to the environment and health, and demanded them to conduct a comprehensive health study on the impact of the emissions on local residents. Some protesters had chained themselves to the factory's entrance gates. The police removed them and arrested 17 protesters.

On 30 November 2024, between 500 and 1,000 pro-Palestinian demonstrators, organized by the International Socialists and supported by Medics for Gaza (Artsen voor Gaza), gathered at the Stopera in Amsterdam (Noord-Holland) for a peaceful protest march to Museumplein to show support for Palestine and promote unity while condemning antisemitism and genocide. Six people were arrested, including Pegida leader Edwin Wagensveld, for attempting an unauthorized counter-demonstration and for other public order offenses.

On 30 November 2024, over 1,000 participants, some affiliated with or supporting the FPOE, including individuals displaying Austrian and Russian flags, gathered at the Heldenplatz in Wien - Inner City (Wien) for a protest initially planned as a march but later restricted to a stationary demonstration due to police concerns. The protestors voiced discontent against the exclusion of the FPOE from government negotiations and policies related to 'Sky Shield' and Ukraine. Spontaneous marches from Heldenplatz to locations like the Ring near the Parliament were dissolved by police, who also confiscated knives and a blank-firing gun. Despite tensions and attempts to breach restricted areas, no arrests or assaults occurred.

On 30 November 2024, Extinction Rebellion (XR) activists carried out a protest at the Primark store at Spui in Den Haag (Zuid-Holland). Nude activists smeared the storefront with fake oil to draw attention to the environmental and ethical issues of the fast fashion industry. The protestors, under the slogan 'we'd rather be naked than wear fast fashion,' intended to convey that companies like Primark are not welcome in the city. The activists were physically carried away by the police.
On 1 December 2024, Last Generation activists blocked the main highway in Warsaw, demanding immediate climate action. Law enforcers removed them from the spot.

On 2 December 2024, around 100 taxi drivers blocked access to the A7 highway toll barrier in Reventin-Vaugris (Auvergne-Rhone-Alpes) to protest against new regulations on the transport of people in need of medical assistance, as well as decreasing fares. In the evening, CRS police and other law enforcement officers intervened to clear the highway blockade, physically removing some demonstrators. There was no report of arrests.

On 2 December 2024, pro-Palestinian activists, mostly students, marched on the campus of Stockholm University in Stockholm to call on the university to implement an academic boycott of Israeli institutions and to end all forms of academic cooperation with the country. Activists later entered one of the buildings and were dispersed by police, with several activists temporarily detained.

On 3 December 2024, around 12 environmental activists held a climate-related demonstration in Amager, Copenhagen. Later, police officers arrested the activists on suspicion of violating restricted airspace at the Copenhagen's Kastrup Airport due to the activists' use of a drone. Airspace over the airport was temporarily closed due to the potential security threat.

On 4 December 2024, around 100 people, including homeless people, undocumented migrants, and members of Right to Housing (Droit Au Logement), gathered outside the Prefecture in Lyon (Auvergne-Rhone-Alpes) to demand sustainable housing solutions and emergency accommodations after a fire destroyed a squat in Caluire-et-Cuire and left one dead and two injured on the night of 2 December 2024. During the protest, police intervened and conducted immigration checks, leading to the arrest of at least three undocumented individuals. Many demonstrators rejected the prefecture's offer of temporary hotel accommodations, calling for long-term solutions instead.

On 4 December 2024, XR activists protested at the UK headquarters of A&O Shearman in London - City of London (England), targeting the law firm's ties to the fossil fuel industry. Protesters occupied the offices, sprayed windows with fake oil, and demanded the firm sever its connections with fossil fuel clients. Five activists were arrested by the police, with footage showing one protester being dragged from the lobby and carried to a police van. Demonstrators also displayed signs, banged drums, and used flares to amplify their message, accusing the firm of facilitating over GBP285 billion in fossil fuel transactions.

On 4 December 2024, environmental activists from Extinction Rebellion blocked the entrance to a construction site in Amager, Copenhagen, to protest the planned creation of an artificial island named Lynetteholmen that is supposed to house 35,000 residents. Activists claimed that the development project could harm both the marine and urban environment. Police later removed and detained four activists from the site after they failed to comply with police orders to free the entrance.
On 4 December 2024, Last Generation activists blocked the main highway in Warsaw, demanding immediate climate action. Law enforcers removed them from the spot.

On 4 December 2024, Extinction Rebellion (XR) blocked the A12 highway in Den Haag (Zuid-Holland), protesting against fossil fuel subsidies. The police arrested 24 protesters for not following their instructions and transported them to the police station; 128 others were taken by bus to the ADO stadium. The protest, which started at 12:00 and ended around 19:15, disrupted traffic, preventing vehicles from leaving The Hague but allowing entry.

On 5 December 2024, at the call of the CP, nearly 200 farmers gathered outside the Grand Palais in Paris (Ile-de-France) during a European grain trade meeting involving major agribusiness corporations such as Bunge, ADM, Dreyfus, and Cargill. The protesters demanded structural reforms, including price controls on imports, market regulation mechanisms, and opposition to free trade agreements like the EU-Mercosur deal. The BRAV-M intervened 20 minutes into the protest, blocking participants for over an hour and arresting five individuals (four farmers and one supporter) on charges of 'violence' and 'attempted intrusion,' which the arrested individuals denied. The event was part of a nationwide demonstration movement by French farmers opposing the EU-Mercosur trade deal and condemning delays in agricultural reforms promised by the previous government following the winter 2023-2024 farmers' protests.

On 6 December 2024, around 1000 to 1500 people took part in the 'Helsinki without Nazis' demonstration at Toolontori, Helsinki, to oppose the ongoing 612 Torch Parade. Later, riot police ordered the demonstration to be ended and began arresting people, at least 41 activists were arrested in connection with the demonstration. Activists from the A-group and Varis Verkosto took part in the event, among others.
On 8 December 2024, Last Generation activists again blocked a street in Warsaw, demanding immediate climate action. Law enforcers removed them from the spot.

On 8 December 2024, under the motto 'Solidarity with the Syrian Revolution', around 5,000 people from the Syrian community gathered at Oranienplatz in Berlin - Friedrichshain-Kreuzberg (Berlin) to celebrate the fall of Bashar al-Assad's regime. The event which included drumming, fireworks and chants, began as a rally for solidarity with the Syrian revolution and later transformed into a procession. There were also car processions and street gatherings. While the police tried to control the situation by halting car convoys and blocking roads, there was at least one arrest. The event was part of wider celebrations following the overthrow of Assad in Syria.

On 9 December 2024, people gathered in Paris (Ile-de-France) to protest against what the demonstrators referred to as the 'Bollore Empire', a reference to Vincent Bollore, a prominent billionaire from Brittany. Demonstrators expressed their opposition to his influence and alleged role in promoting far-right ideologies in France. The protests coincided with Vivendi's extraordinary shareholder meeting, where the company approved a breakup plan to split into separate entities. Activists criticized this move as consolidating Bollore's control over key media and publishing assets. The police intervened to remove a group of anti-Bollore activists who were attempting to disrupt Vivendi's General Assembly.
On 9 December 2024, Last Generation activists joined by the ORP movement again blocked a street in Warsaw, demanding immediate climate action. Law enforcers removed them from the spot.

On 9 December 2024, around 500 people participated in the 200th Monday protest in Bautzen (Sachsen). The event included an auto rally with several tractors and trucks, and some attendees sang the first and second verses of the national anthem of Germany. The protest featured right-wing symbols and rhetoric, including chants like 'Our rules, our city' and calls for 'remigration.' Members of the Free Saxony party participated. As the demonstration crossed the Friedensbrucke, unknown persons lit fireworks and pyrotechnics at St. Michael's Church. The police arrested several suspects nearby and the remains of the fireworks were collected.

On 10 December 2024, following a call on social media, hundreds of solidarity protesters rallied outside the home of a single mother in Ano Patissia, Athens - Central Athens, to prevent the foreclosure of her home for a debt of 880 euros. MAT riot police forces pushed and dispersed the crowd.

On 13 December 2024, police intervened to remove striking bus drivers blocking access to the bus depot in Saint-Ouen-l'Aumone (Ile-de-France). The strike had been going on for 36 days. The protesters demanded a pay rise.

On 13 December 2024, around 30 to 40 activists from the Emergency Break movement blocked major roads in different locations of Copenhagen calling for an end to motorway construction due to environmental concerns. Police later detained activists from the demonstration sites after they failed to comply with police demands. At least 30 to 40 activists were detained in connection with the blockades.

On 13 December 2024, activists affiliated with various movements, including Last Generation, ORP or Women's Strike, blocked the main highway in Warsaw, demanding immediate climate action. Law enforcers quickly removed them from the spot.

On 14 December 2024, 120 XR activists protested inside Schiphol Airport's departure hall (Noord-Holland) against KLM's Frequent Flyer program, pouring 200 liters of brown water to symbolize Valencia's October floods and chaining themselves to luggage carts. Approximately 99 demonstrators were arrested by the Royal Marechaussee for defying a protest ban, while others were removed from the area, many of them having to be physically dragged away. Simultaneously, a peaceful and authorized XR and Greenpeace protest with several dozen protesters occurred at Schiphol Plaza, focusing on frequent flyer programs.

On 14 December 2024, around 50 pro-Palestinian activists gathered outside the State Office of Criminal Investigation in Berlin - Tempelhof-Schoneberg (Berlin), awaiting the release of a fellow activist. After her release, some activists entered the building, chanting a banned pro-Palestinian slogan. Police intervened and the activists were pushed outside.

On 14 December 2024, several activists occupied the roof of the former Turkish consulate in Frankfurt am Main (Hessen), demanding an end to arms deliveries to Turkey. Furthermore, activists staged a subsequent spontaneous gathering of around 30 participants in front of the consulate to show solidarity with Kurdish self-administration regions in Syria. The gathering led to some pushing and shoving with the police, resulting in four temporary arrests.

On 15 December 2024, around four Last Generation climate activists staged an action against climate change, hanging orange warning vests on Greifen statues at Steintor in Rostock (Mecklenburg-Vorpommern). The police quickly intervened, detaining the activists at Ziegenmarkt.

On 16 December 2024, at the call of Platform for the Burial of the Railway in Valladolid (Plataforma por el Soterramiento del Ferrocarril en Valladolid), people protested in Valladolid (Castilla y Leon) to denounce high-speed railway construction works in the area, demanding the railway to be underground so that not communities will be divided and segregated. National Police officers dispersed the demonstration.

On 16 December 2024, four activists from the initiative 'RiseUp4Rojava' climbed the Brandenburg Gate in Berlin - Mitte (Berlin) and unfurled a 30-meter banner reading 'For Democracy in Syria - Defend Rojava' to show solidarity with the Kurdish areas in Syria. The police intervened and brought the activists down without injuries.

On 18 December 2024, at the call of the student organization Luna and ADL Cobas, around 30 students gathered in front of the entrance of the Camplus Alma Mater student residence in Bologna (Emilia-Romagna) to protest against problems inside the apartments, including mold and water infiltration and to ask for a meeting with the management. The police intervened with force to disperse them.

On 18 December 2024, 12 activists from the youth organization 'Young Struggle' briefly occupied the television broadcasting company ZDF capital studio in Berlin - Mitte (Berlin), demanding recognition of Rojava's democratic self-administration. Police intervened using pain compliance techniques, recorded the identities of 13 individuals, and issued dispersal orders after the activists refused to leave voluntarily.

On 20 December 2024, members of the Christian Collective (Christelijk Collectief) staged a demonstration at the Israelcentrum in Nijkerk (Gelderland), during which they removed the center's flag, defaced the building with slogans such as 'Stop genocide' and 'Stop child murder,' and hung posters. Some demonstrators climbed onto the roof, necessitating the use of a fire department's high ladder to remove them. Police arrested four people: three for vandalism and one for failing to provide identification.

On 21 December 2024, several hundred demonstrators from XR, including children, protested at the Rijksmuseum in Amsterdam (Noord-Holland) against ING's sponsorship of the museum, because of alleged environmental destruction and human rights violations of ING. Nine XR activists had to be removed from the Eregalerij by police after gluing themselves together.

On 26 December 2024, anti-hunting campaigners protested against the annual Boxing Day hunt parade in Lewes (England), organized by the Southdown and Eridge Hunt. Protesters carried signs reading 'Make hunts history' and 'Trail hunting is a lie,' highlighting their opposition to trail hunting, which they claimed disguises illegal fox hunting. Police were present at the event and arrested eight demonstrators. Details about the arrestees were not provided in the report.

On 28 December 2024, women held a protest near the 'pro-choice' clinic Dator in Madrid - Tetuan (Madrid) against a group of 'pro-life' activists who were praying and protesting outside the clinic. Police intervened and physically removed both groups from the area. A pro-life doctor was subsequently arrested for resisting authority.

On 30 December 2024, several members of the National Union of Police and Contractual Personnel protested in front of the Government building in Bucharest against salary reductions and the non-indexation of pensions for 2025. Protesters opposed measures in the proposed 'train ordinance,' which included cuts to weekend and holiday bonuses, reductions in travel reimbursements, salary freezes, and non-adjustment of pensions for inflation. During the protest, a policeman used tear gas and injured a protester.

On 3 January 2025, thousands of fans held a protest outside Mestalla stadium before the Valencia-Real Madrid match in Valencia (Valencia) against Valencia's club management, demanding the resignation of its manager, leading to police charges to push the crowd back to the safety police cordon.

On 3 January 2025, five Last Generation activists blocked the Frauenstrasse in Munchen (Bayern) to protest the perceived disproportionate five-month prison sentence of fellow activist Karl Braig. The group, dressed in stylized prisoner outfits, aimed to show solidarity with Braig, who had been sentenced for briefly gluing himself to streets in 2023. During the protest, some onlookers became verbally violent and the situation tense, prompting some police officers to physically remove the activists from the street.

On 5 January 2025, 5 activists of Animal Rebellion (Ribellione Animale) smeared with manure the display case of Pablo Picasso's painting inside the Te Palace in Mantova (Lombardia) to protest against the presence of a livestock company, which produces cured meats, among the members of the Foundation Te Palace. The police brought the activists to the police station.

On 6 January 2025, four activists from Quit with Coal demonstrated at the Ministry of Climate and Green Growth in Den Haag (Zuid-Holland), displaying banners and urging the minister to halt negotiations with Tata Steel until the company reduces its CO2 and harmful emissions. Three were arrested after refusing to leave.

On 6 January 2025, around 80 students gathered for a protest in front of the Alice Salomon University of Applied Sciences in Berlin - Marzahn-Hellersdorf (Berlin), organized in solidarity with the occupation of the Audimax in the university building by pro-Palestine activists on the same day. Police were present with approximately 180 officers and temporarily detained six individuals during the protest.

On 7 January 2025, around 200 people gathered in Strasbourg (Grand Est) to celebrate the death of Jean-Marie Le Pen, the founder of the far-right party FN/RN, and denounce far-right ideology. As the protest was not authorized by authorities, police physically intervened to disperse the demonstrators. There was no report of arrests.

On 9 January 2025, people, including students, representatives of CUA Torino, pro-Kurdistan activists, members of the association Defend Kurdistan Torino, women, and members of Non Una di Meno gathered outside the check-in desk of the Turkish Airline at the Terminal 1 of the Malpensa Airport in Ferno (Lombardia) to demonstrate against the Turkish government and in support of the Kurdish people. Demonstrators exposed banners highlighting the Turkish government's repression policies against Kurdish people. The demonstration was not authorized. The police surrounded the demonstrators, and pushed and pulled some of them to the side, forcibly separating them from the group to identify them. Nobody was injured, and nobody was arrested.

On 11 January 2025, more than 1,500 protesters from XR, supported by groups such as Christian Climate Action NL and 'Christian Collective' (Christelijk Collectief), and including international protesters, blocked the A12 Utrechtsebaan in Den Haag (Zuid-Holland) and nearby intersections, including the Koningskade and Zuid Hollandlaan, demanding an end to fossil fuel subsidies. Police cleared the area using water cannons and stretchers, with some protesters chained to objects. The demonstration caused traffic disruptions, including rerouted ambulances and two vehicle collisions on the A12. The protest resulted in 700 arrests, with 12 individuals detained for offenses such as incitement and assault.

On 12 January 2025, six pro-Palestinian demonstrators disrupted Gent's official New Year's reception by displaying a banner reading 'No Happy New Year in Palestine' and entering the city hall. Six individuals were detained for disturbing public order.

On 13 January 2025, CGT affiliates gathered outside the town hall in Livry-Gargan (Ile-de-France) to demand increased public funding for the local hospital. During the protest, Kamel Brahmi, head of the departmental CGT section, was arrested while attempting to enter the town hall, leading protesters to relocate to the police station to demand his release and denounce what they viewed as repression of union activism. Brahmi was released later that evening.

On 13 January 2025, Extinction Rebellion and pro-Palestine activists gathered outside the seat of Leonardo SPA in Brescia (Lombardia) to protest against the company's usage of fossil fuels and its support of the Israeli government. Demonstrators also protested the war in Gaza and the killing of Palestinian civilians. Activists chained themselves to the company's gates to block the entrance. The police intervened and physically removed the activists, several of whom were then taken into custody pending charges.

On 14 January 2025, Extinction Rebellion Nederland and Quit with Coal, demonstrated at the HES Bulk terminal in Amsterdam (Noord-Holland) to demand the cessation of coal trade, particularly from Colombia, because of the human rights abuses and the environmental damage. They also blocked a coal train on tracks not used for passenger transport. All demonstrators were arrested but later released.

On 18 January 2025, at the call of PSC, thousands of pro-Palestine protesters gathered for a static rally in Whitehall in London - Westminster (England) to show solidarity with Palestine and to call for an end to British complicity in Israel's 'genocide and apartheid'. The protest, originally planned as a march past the BBC and near a synagogue, was restricted to a static rally in Whitehall following a heavily policed presence. After the rally, some protesters broke through the police line marching toward Trafalgar Square to lay flowers in memory of the children of Gaza. Police forces arrested 77 protesters including Chris Nineham, Chief Steward of the protest. Independent MPs Jeremy Corbyn and John McDonnel also attended the protest.

On 18 January 2025, people gathered in Berlin - Neukolln (Berlin) to demonstrate at a pro-Palestinian assembly and to celebrate the ceasefire in Gaza, but the demonstration was cut short by the police after antisemitic slogans were shouted and pyrotechnics were set off, leading to 12 arrests, and media representatives reported harassment against them during the protest. The protestors voiced opposition to the Gaza conflict and called for solidarity with Palestinians.

On 19 January 2025, at the call of Strike WEF, several hundred people blocked access to the town center in Davos (Graubunden) to protest against the Davos World Economic Forum (WEF), accusing its participants of driving climate change and economic inequality. Protesters ignored repeated police warnings to clear the road, leading authorities to deploy an anti-riot vehicle to disperse them. The event was part of a broader march that started the previous day in Kublis.

On 19 January 2025, following the police killing of a young Pakistani in Potamia on 6 January, about 300 demonstrators, Cypriots and migrants, participated in an anti-racist march in Nicosia, demanding justice with the slogan 'Stop the war on migrants'. They protested against the government's migration policies, institutional racism and the normalization of violence against migrants, and expressed their lack of trust towards the police, 'who were investigating themselves, covering up their actions'. Police dispersed the peaceful demonstration and made 3 arrests.

On 19 January 2025, in the morning, pro-Palestinian activists blocked the entrance of the VicenzaOro exhibition in Vicenza (Veneto) to protest against the presence of Israeli companies which, according to protesters, by trading diamonds, finance the Israeli army and to ask for the liberation for the Palestinian people. The occupation was cleared by the police after two hours, who physically removed protesters engaging in passive resistance.

On 20 January 2025, 8 Extinction Rebellion and Quit with Coal activists staged a protest on a dangerous part of the Tata Steel site in IJmuiden (Noord-Holland), aiming to disrupt coal deliveries, which they see as causing large environmental damage. The protest led to the halting of operations involving transport belts and large excavators. The activists were relocated to another location by the police but were not arrested.

On 20 January 2025, eleven activists from the Emergency Break movement blocked a major road in Copenhagen, calling for an end to motorway construction due to environmental concerns. Later, Police later removed and detained four activists from the site after they failed to comply with police orders to free the intersection.

On 21 January 2025, at the call of PAH, around 50 people protested inside and outside a building in Vallecas (Madrid) to prevent the eviction of a vulnerable resident who had lived in the apartment for over 50 years. Protesters, including housing activists and neighbors, attempted to block the eviction by occupying the premises and hanging banners from the facade. Police intervened early in the morning, arresting several activists who had tried to stop the eviction by chaining themselves and hanging from windows.

On 21 January 2025, four high school students, armed with a knife and equipped with a megaphone, banners, and smoke flares, attempted to block access to the Bonaparte school in Toulon (Provence-Alpes-Cote d'Azur) to protest against the Parcoursup university admission system. They repositioned barriers to obstruct the entrance. Police intervened, arresting all four students, including one adult who was later released, while the three minors were handed over to their parents.

On 22 January 2025, police dismantled the ZAD (Zone to Defend) 'La Guinguette Vaillante,' which had been established by environmental activists on 30 August 2024 near Saint-Jory (Occitanie) to oppose the Bordeaux-Toulouse high-speed railway (LGV) project, citing environmental concerns. During the operation, 12 activists were arrested by the police, while two remained in tree cabins before being removed later in the day.

On 23 January 2025, students in Sulejowek gathered with pickets for a rally, protesting against what they see as unjust dismissal of the current school principal by a local mayor. Law enforcers intervened; tear gas was sprayed by an unspecified person.

On 24 January 2025, at the call of CP, about 30 people gathered near the gendarmerie in Saint-Pons-de-Thomieres (Occitanie) to express ongoing concerns about justice and policy issues affecting farmers. The demonstration, described by participants as passive and peaceful, concluded with five arrests, though motives for the arrests were not specified.

On 24 January 2025, a group of around 25 demonstrators protested in front of the Abdijplein in Middelburg (Zeeland), against the potential awarding of bus transport to Israeli company EBS. The protest was aimed at EBS due to its involvement in transporting settlers to occupied territories in Israel, while forbidden to transport Palestinians, which the protesters equate to apartheid. One protester was arrested near the station in Middelburg for refusing to move off the road and not showing an ID.

On 25 January 2025, supporters of the UKIP party held a march in Southampton (England) to express their concerns over immigration, Islam, and labor. At the call of SUTR and Southampton Tenants Union people also marched for a counter-demonstration rejecting racism and division 'promoted by UKIP'. Several signs, including one reading 'Fascists belong in the dustbin of history,' were displayed at the counter-demonstration. A heavy police presence ensured both groups remained separated after some minor scuffles broke out on Bargate Street where a bottled drink was thrown at a bus driving towards Westquay stops and a separate arrest was made. The demonstrations ended without major incidents.

On 25 January 2025, at the call of Extinction Rebellion (XR), a few hundred protesters attempted to block the A10 highway in Amsterdam (Noord-Holland), protesting the fossil fuel financing of ING. Demonstrators gathered at the S109 on- and off-ramp near the former ING headquarters, but they did not reach the highway itself. Police arrested 187 people, of whom 40 were suspected of attempting to obstruct traffic, while others were transported and later released in Amsterdam-Noord. The city had previously banned the demonstration.

On 27 January 2025, in the afternoon, at the call of a coalition of civil groups including XR and Last Generation, under the motto 'The rich eat? We eat with them', several hundred people participated in a demonstration at the Springer headquarters in Berlin - Friedrichshain-Kreuzberg (Berlin) against the 'Welt' newspaper's economic summit, voicing their discontent with the secretive nature of the summit, which invited prominent figures like Olaf Scholz (SPD), Friedrich Merz (CDU), Robert Habeck (The Greens), Sahra Wagenknecht (BSW) und Alice Weidel (AfD). The demonstration turned tense as police forcibly dismantled a sit-in, by using physical force, including dragging protesters away and arresting one person.

On 28 January 2025, at the call of the association 'Bergamo for Palestine' (Bergamo per la Palestina), about 30 people, including pro-Palestine activists, interrupted the city council in Bergamo (Lombardia) to protest against the Israeli government and the killing of Palestinian civilians. Protesters also criticized the administration for refusing to take a stance on the topic. Demonstrators were asked to leave repeatedly but failed to comply. Therefore, the police physically pushed them outside of the building.

On 29 January 2025, five individuals who called themselves 'squirrels' climbed up trees in Compiegne (Hauts-de-France) to protest against the construction of the Seine-Nord Canal, which they considered damaging to local biodiversity and too expensive. Two members of the 'Mega channel resistance Collective' (Collectif Mega canal resistance) were subsequently taken to the police station by officers.

On 29 January 2025, at 12:00 pm, about 50 students, faculty members, doctoral candidates, and professors gathered in front of the Flemish Interuniversity Council (VLIR) headquarters in the Ravensteingallery, central Brussels (Brussels). The demonstrators, many dressed as judges, chanted 'Free Palestine' and called for a boycott of academic institutions in Israel, accusing them of complicity in genocide and violations of international law. This protest was part of ongoing efforts to encourage Belgian universities to sever ties with Israeli institutions, following a public letter signed by 7,000 academics. The protest lasted for about an hour before being broken up by the police.

On 29 January 2025, six activists from the Emergency Break movement blocked a motorway exit in Kongens Lyngby, Hovedstaden, calling for an end to motorway construction due to environmental concerns. Police later removed several activists from the site after they failed to comply with police demands.

On 29 January 2025, for the second day, workers staged a protest in front of the entrances to the GLS warehouses in the Gianturco area in Napoli (Campania), blocking the delivery of packages, against the dismissal of 58 workers and demanded better working conditions. The police, after several attempts at mediation, physically removed the demonstrators from the area.

On 30 January 2025, police intervened and removed 80 students from the Palestine Commitee (Comite Palestine) blocking access to Sciences Po Strasbourg (Grand Est) to protest against Sciences Po's partnership with the Reichman University in Israel. The students expressed solidarity with the Palestinian people in Gaza and condemned Israel's military offensive on Palestine. Their protest action started on 27 January.

On 30 January 2025, police intervened and removed a few climate activists who called themselves 'squirrels' from trees in Compiegne (Hauts-de-France). The protesters had climbed up the trees the day before to protest against the construction of the Seine-Nord Canal, which they considered damaging to local biodiversity and too expensive.

On 30 January 2025, police removed 30 pro-Palestinian activists from the student collective Palestine Solidarity Tilburg (PST) who were occupying the corridor of the Cobbenhagen building at Tilburg University in Tilburg (Noord-Holland). The activists had occupied the corridor to protest the university's decision not to boycott Israeli universities.

On 31 January 2025, environmental activists from the French movement Ode Aux Ratsss, which opposes the fast fashion industry, with the involvement of XR, threw ampoules containing a foul-smelling substance inside an H&M store in shopping center De Tuinen in Naaldwijk (Zuid-Holland). Several people became unwell, including one store employee. A note left behind referenced a 'stench sabotage campaign' opposing the fast fashion industry. Police arrested two suspects and confirmed the substance was not harmful. Extinction Rebellion acknowledged involvement and apologized.

On 31 January 2025, people gathered in Trento (Trentino-Alto Adige) to demonstrate against police violence and commemorate Ramy Elgaml, a 19-year-old Egyptian man who died on 24 November 2024 following a police chase. The police intervened to prevent traffic blockages, pushing the protesters to the side of the road. According to reports, some fireworks were set off in response.

On 31 January 2025, the police evicted the building hosting the self-managed social center Bocciodromo in Vicenza (Veneto). The building had housed associations and Bocciodromo activities for 15 years, and its ownership was transferred from the municipality to Iricav Due, the company responsible for the construction of the high-speed railway (TAV), which plans to demolish the structure.

On 31 January 2025, around noon, a small group of pro-Palestinian activists, including university students and members of activist groups, demonstrated at Broerplein near the Academiegebouw at the Rijksuniversiteit Groningen (RUG) (Groningen), during the latter's Open Day. Some of the demonstrators had to physically be removed by police and security from the stairs. The demonstration demanded that the university sever ties with Israeli organizations due to the ongoing conflict in Gaza, accusing RUG of indirect involvement in companies contributing to the destruction of Gaza.

On 31 January 2025, nine activists from the Emergency Break movement staged a protest and blocked a major road in Copenhagen, calling for an end to motorway construction on environmental grounds. Police later physically removed the activists from the site.

On 1 February 2025, in the afternoon, thousands of supporters of the 'Stop the Isolation' movement marched from Waterloo Station to Parliament Square in London - Westminster (England) in support of far-right activist Tommy Robinson, who was serving an 18-month prison sentence at the time of reporting. The march, during which participants carried banners with slogans such as 'Free Tommy Robinson' and 'Stop the Boats,' crossed Westminster Bridge and concluded at Whitehall. At the call of SUTR, over 5,000 anti-fascist campaigners and trade unionists from Unison, NEU, UCU, PCS, CWU, and Unite organized a counter-demonstration, marching from Piccadilly to Whitehall in London - Westminster (England) and counter-demonstrators highlighting concerns about the rise of far-right movements both in the UK and globally. Police arrested six people from both sides for incidents such as setting off flares, breaching police lines, and spitting on an officer.

On 1 February 2025, activists, mostly students, gathered in Split for a rally and demonstrative silence, declaring their solidarity with protesting students in Serbia. Seven young men gathered in Split near them, verbally assaulting them and disrupting the gathering with noise. Law enforcers detained all of them.

On 3 February 2025, around 600 people gathered in Kiel (Schleswig-Holstein) to demonstrate against an event organized by the AfD at their office in Walkerdamm. Demonstrators split into two groups, attempting to prevent participants from reaching the event's venue. One group went from Hopfenstrase to Walkerdamm and positioned themselves in front of the AfD office. The second group came from Schulper Baum and positioned themselves at the junction with Backergang. Eventually, the police used physical force and pepper spray to break the blockade in the Walkerdamm area.

On 4 February 2025, in the morning, around 60 gendarmes and police conducted an operation in Saint-Jory (Occitanie) to evacuate an ecologist camp opposing the construction of the Bordeaux-Toulouse high-speed rail line (LGV) over environmental concerns. Approximately 10 activists remained perched in the trees while law enforcement dismantled unoccupied platforms and ground-level structures. The police restored access to a road blocked by debris and tree branches before beginning the operation. Three protesters were arrested during the intervention.

On 4 February 2025, several hundred people gathered to protest against Germany's CDU leader Friedrich Merz's visit at the University Hospital in Koln (Nordrhein-Westfalen). The protesters blocked exits and greeted Merz with boos, demanding political changes. After the police asked protesters to move spontaneously, they intervened and pushed demonstrators aside to clear the road and allow cars to leave the venue. The event was part of a wider protest movement against far-right politics in response to the CDU's proposed migration plan, which was supported by the AfD.

On 5 February 2025, members of Rouvikonas entered the Senate Hall in parliament, Athens - Central Athens, during a public event, and raised a banner reading 'Cover-up' in protest over the Tempe railway disaster. Police officers from the Parliament's security service removed the banner and escorted the protesters out of the building without making any arrests.

On 6 February 2025, health workers held a protest at the University Hospital in A Coruna (Galicia) to demand better safety measures after a nurse and a security guard were stabbed by a patient. Protesters denounced that during the protest, a police officer charged at the crowd, resulting in a worker being injured and requiring urgent medical attention.
On 6 February 2025, residents protested in Copanca in an attempt to interrupt the work connecting the village to Moldova's power grid. The protesters were dispersed by the police.

On 7 February 2025, at the call of No Tav activists, people, including anarchist activists, students, members of self-managed social centers such as Askatasuna, and pro-Palestine activists, took to the streets in Torino (Piemonte) to demonstrate against the high-speed Turin-Lyon railway project, the government, repression, and police brutality, among several other things. Demonstrators were prevented from accessing a conference concerning infrastructures held at the Royal Park. Demonstrators also defaced buildings and shop windows and the windows of a cafe's outdoor area. A representative of the self-managed social center Askatasuna tried to force the police block and was placed under arrest. However, no other incident was reported and no clashes between police and demonstrators took place.

On 7 February 2025, protesters gathered in central North Mitrovica to voice their opposition to the visit by Kosovo Prime Minister Albin Kurti ahead of the Kosovo parliamentary elections. Kurti is unpopular in Serb-majority northern Kosovo due to his policies which are perceived to be against the local Serb population. One member of Serbian Democracy of the protest was detained for blowing into a whistle and released after the event.

On 8 February 2025, more than 1,000 people, including members of the Chinese, Tibetan, and Uyghur communities, gathered outside the historic former site of the Royal Mint in Tower Hill, London - Tower Hamlets (England), to protest against the proposed Chinese 'mega-embassy' in the city. Demonstrators waved flags and carried placards denouncing the project, citing concerns over security threats and transnational oppression by the Chinese Communist Party. There were scuffles - shoves and pushes - between demonstrators and the police, after which two individuals were arrested for breaching public order conditions.

On 8 February 2025, in the evening, at the call of XR, people gathered at the Amsterdam Passenger's Terminal in Amsterdam (Noord-Holland) to protest the polluting impact of cruise ships. Two people, about whom it is unclear if they belonged to XR, reached a cruise ship at Piet Heinkade in Amsterdam by boat and sprayed 'Fuck cruises' on it to protest the cruise industry's environmental impact. Police and the Harbor Service arrested both, seizing spray cans, and were investigating possible further involvement at the time of reporting.

On 8 February 2025, under the motto 'Stop the Aggression in West Bank! No Arms Supplies to Israel,' around 300 people gathered in Berlin - Tempelhof-Schoneberg (Berlin) to protest in solidarity with the Palestinian population and against arms delivery to Israel. The event was prematurely ended due to repeated violations of restrictions set by the police which included speeches and chants in Arabic. 40 to 50 people remained and were carried away by police, resulting in several temporary arrests.

On 8 February 2025, in the afternoon, at the call of Grannies Against the Right, between 20,000 to 24,000 people gathered in Hannover (Niedersachsen) to demonstrate against the far-right shift in politics, racism and exclusion, carrying Antifa flags. Demonstrators pressed close to an AfD stand nearby, with some pushing against police lines and one individual stealing a flag from the stand. The police responded by using physical force, including pushing demonstrators to the ground, and making seven arrests for assault and resistance. The event was part of a nationwide movement focused on defending democracy ahead of the elections.

On 8 February 2025, at 11:30 am, around 100 people gathered in front of an AfD stand on Bismarck Square in Heidelberg (Baden-Wurttemberg) to protest against the AfD in response to AfD supporters distributing 'deportation tickets' at the same location a week earlier. Police intervened by pushing protesters to the other side of the square after issuing dispersal orders and the protesters remained. Authorities are investigating whether any legal action will be taken against participants. The event was part of a nationwide protest movement focused on defending democracy ahead of the elections.

On 8 February 2025, at midday, at the call of the Action Network 'Leipzig Takes a Stand', around 1,000 people gathered in Leipzig (Sachsen) to protest against an AfD campaign event featuring Tino Chrupalla (AfD). The police secured the venue with construction fences and vehicles. There were isolated attempts to block access. One of them was prevented by pushing people away and using pepper spray. The event was part of a nationwide protest movement focused on defending democracy ahead of the elections.

On 9 February 2025, people dressed in black and wearing hoods staged an unauthorized demonstration in solidarity with prisoners outside the prison in Como (Lombardia). Demonstrators lit up smoke bombs and shouted slogans against prisoners' living situation. Demonstrators fled the scene at the arrival of the police. Following a chase, the police were able to apprehend six demonstrators, one of whom, a 34-year-old man, former candidate for mayor of Como in the last elections, was then arrested on charges of resisting arrest.

On 10 February 2025, before noon, at the call of ACV-CSC, CNE, and ABVV-FGTB, around 100 subcontracted workers from Audi Brussels gathered at the Albertinaplein in Brussels - Ville de Bruxelles (Brussels) to demand a reform of the Renault Law on collective dismissals so they could benefit from Audi's social plan. The workers, employed by subcontractors such as Imperial Logistics and Rhenus Automotive, were excluded from the severance package offered to Audi's direct employees, prompting calls for equal treatment and legal changes to make main contractors accountable for subcontracted workers. After the demonstration, about 30 protesters moved to the factory in Brussels - Forest (Brussels), where at around 1:30 pm they tried to enter the site by climbing over fences. Police intervened and physically stopped them, though no injuries were reported.

On 10 February 2025, at the call of the 'Alliance to Resist Freiburg' (Bundnis Widersetzen Freiburg), around 10,000 people gathered in Freiburg im Breisgau (Baden-Wurttemberg) to protest against an election campaign event organized by the AfD and against the AfD and CDU forming the next government. There were some disturbances and isolated physical altercations between individuals of opposing political views, leading to 8 criminal offenses and 6 arrests, although the exact nature of the disturbances or altercations and on which side arrests occurred isn't detailed in the report. The event was part of a nationwide protest movement focused on defending democracy ahead of the elections.

On 11 February 2025, environmental activists, including members of Extinction Rebellion, attempted to block the entrance to an energy conference venue in Oslo to oppose perceived political inaction on addressing climate crisis and to advocate for fossil fuel phase out. The activists were dispersed by police, several were arrested.

On 12 February 2025, at the call of UNEF, around 60 students blocked access to the Pont-de-Bois faculty in Villeneuve-d'Ascq (Hauts-de-France) to protest against state-imposed funding cuts to universities and research. Police intervened at 6:30 am, using tear gas to disperse protesters and dismantling their installations. Students denounced the intervention as a disproportionate use of force. Later in the morning, UNEF and NPA mobilized around 90 students, who marched through campus buildings, chanting slogans against the cuts. Police reported that some protesters attempted to block access by taking materials from a nearby construction site.

On 12 February 2025, at the call of six activist groups, around 150 protesters staged a protest outside the House of Culture and Education (HKB) in Neubrandenburg (Mecklenburg-Vorpommern), where CDU chancellor candidate Friedrich Merz was speaking to invited guests, to protest against the CDU and far-right ideologies. During the protest, a man threw a beeping object into the HKB and was arrested by the police.

On 14 February 2025, around 2,500 people gathered in Saarbrucken (Saarland) to demonstrate against the AfD, racism, fascism, and the far-right. Some demonstrators threw tomatoes and potatoes at AfD members and verbally confronted them. A few attempted to climb over police barriers, prompting officers to use pepper spray. The event was part of a nationwide movement focused on defending democracy ahead of the elections.

On 15 February 2025, at the call of PSC, tens of thousands of pro-Palestine protesters held a march from Whitehall to the US Embassy in London - Wandsworth (England) to protest the proposal by President Donald Trump for the United States to consider taking ownership of the Gaza Strip and redevelop the territory into the 'Riviera of the Middle East'. Protesters carried banners and signs that read 'Hands off Gaza', 'Stand up to Trump', and 'Mr. Trump, Canada is not your 51st state. Gaza is not your 52nd'. Various campaign groups, including the Campaign for Nuclear Disarmament, Stop the War Coalition, and a Jewish community also attended the march. Independent MP Jeremy Corbyn also attended the march and spoke to the crowd. A pro-Israeli counter-protest by Stop the Hate group also took place along the route of the march at the junction of Grosvenor Road and Vauxhall Bridge. The two groups were separated, and the protests remained peaceful. However, police forces arrested eight individuals, but it is unclear from what side.

On 15 February 2025, in the afternoon, at the call of XR, between 30 to 40 demonstrators protested outside an ING banking office on Kerkstraat in Den Bosch (Noord-Brabant), calling on ING to stop financing the fossil fuel industry. The activists had been inside for several hours before being asked to leave around 5 pm. Some had chained or glued themselves to the building and the police had to physically remove them, arresting around 30 for trespassing.

On 15 February 2025, between 2,300 and 2,500 far-right actors and Neonazis, including members of groups like 'The Right,' 'Free Saxony,' and 'Young Nationalists,' gathered in Dresden (Sachsen) for a so-called 'Mourning March' to commemorate the 80th anniversary of the bombing of the city during World War II and to propagate revisionist narratives. In response, over 4,000 counter-protesters, mobilized by the 'Alliance Dresden Resists' and 'Antifa Against Antisemitism,' attempted to block the march with sit-ins and protests. The police intervened as a response to the counter-protesters' sit-in, using pain grips and pepper spray, until it dissolved.

On 17 February 2025, people demonstrated outside a hospital in Lindekollen, Oslo, to oppose plans to build new hospitals in the area and the planned closure of Ulleval Hospital. Police later removed several activists from the protest site after they failed to comply with police demands.

On 18 February 2025, in the evening, at the call of pro-Palestinian activists, around 10 people gathered near the Viage casino in Brussels - Ville de Bruxelles (Brussels) to protest the lecture of Israeli comedian Yohay Sponder. The protestors shouted 'Free Palestine,' and the police intervened forcefully, using tear gas to disperse the group, but conducting no arrests.

On 18 February 2025, pro-Palestine activists from Palestine Action staged a protest outside the Armstrong Works, a defense engineering factory owned by the Israeli government on Scotswood Road in Newcastle upon Tyne (England) against the use of force by Israel in Gaza. During the protest, two women climbed onto the roof of the security building at the entrance, where they hung a Palestinian flag. Police forces arrested six individuals and ended the protest.

On 18 February 2025, in the afternoon, at the call of End Fossil Occupy Delft and 'Delft Student Intifada,' students and pro-Palestinian activists gathered outside the congress building of TU Delft in Delft (Zuid-Holland), blocking the entrance by chaining themselves, to protest the presence of companies from the arms and fossil fuel industries at the university's career fair. The protesters were specifically opposing companies like Shell and Allseas, accusing them of contributing to climate change and human rights violations by Israel in Gaza through the university's contracts with military companies. During the action, the police made 11 arrests.
