On 19 February 2025, ahead of the Tsiknopempti celebrations, traditionally a day for eating meat, animal rights activists Nemesis and the Panhellenic Federation for the Environment, Animals and against hunting, participated in a peaceful action at Syntagma square, Athens - Central Athens, to protest against the killing of animals. They were arrested by police.

On 19 February 2025, between 5,000 to 5,300 people from the Network Migrantifa gathered in Berlin - Neukolln (Berlin) to commemorate the fifth anniversary of the attack in Hanau, where a far-right attacker killed nine people, with some participants waving Palestinian flags. Protesters criticized the political system and the police for their actions during the attack a year prior. Police pulled a protester out of the crowd, who had been previously prohibited from attending the demonstration, which triggered a reaction from other demonstrators, who began chanting 'Where were you in Hanau?' and 'Viva, Viva Palastina'. 100 masked individuals then attempted to push the police, to which the police responded with physical force by pushing and shoving back, leading to 11 arrests.

On 22 February 2025, in the afternoon, at the call of Quit with Coal, 60 activists, including XR affiliates, gathered at the coal railway in Westelijk Havengebied in Amsterdam (Noord-Holland), blocking the tracks, to protest the import of Colombian coal, which they claimed involved human rights violations. After the mayor ordered the protest to disperse and demonstrators refused, police arrested 13 activists.

On 22 February 2025, in the afternoon, at the call of 'Harburg Against the Right' (Harburg gegen Rechts), and the Alliance 'Together Against the Right' (Einig gegen Rechts), the SPD, and left-wing affiliates, and under the motto 'Hargurg together against the right', between 950 to 1,300 people gathered in the Heimfeld district of Hamburg - Harburg (Hamburg) to participate in several demonstrations against the AfD's campaign closing event. During the event, demonstrators confronted a man who was filming them and in response, police used pepper spray against the demonstrators and arrested a dozen of them. A demonstrator also hit a police officer on the head with a cardboard sign. The event was part of a nationwide movement focused on defending democracy ahead of the 2025 federal elections.

On 22 February 2025, between around 200 and 250 people, including members of the Alliance Against the Right, gathered outside the Swiss home of AfD chancellor candidate Alice Weidel and her family in Einsiedeln (Schwyz) to protest against far-right ideology and for diversity. Protesters held banners reading 'Weidel out'. Between dozens and several hundred counter-demonstrators affiliated with MassVoll gathered, unauthorized, and expressed their support for AfD, waving Swiss flags. Although short scuffles between protesters and counter-demonstrations broke out, the police intervened to avoid clashes between the two groups. Five people were temporarily arrested.

On 22 February 2025, thousands of Calin Georgescu supporters protested in Constitution Square in Bucharest, demanding the resumption of the presidential elections and calling for Georgescu to become president. AUR members were also present at the event. A television reporter was harassed by two participants, which were taken to the police station. A POT MP and an AUR MP participated.

On 23 February 2025, around 80 people gathered in front of the AfD federal headquarters in Berlin - Mitte (Berlin) to protest against the party's election results. As part of the demonstration, the Center for Political Beauty (Zentrum fur Politische Schonheit) set up a bus emitting a loud siren, intended as a symbolic warning against fascism. The police forcibly broke into the bus after receiving multiple noise complaints from residents and emergency calls. Officers recorded the identities of three protesters involved in setting up or operating the siren. The demonstration was part of a broader nationwide protest movement in defense of democracy ahead of the elections.

On 24 February 2025, activists affiliated with the Kaputin movement gathered in Prague in front of the Russian Centre for Science and Culture, occupied the entrance area, replaced Russian flags with Czech ones and demanded closure of the facility. Law enforcers briefly detained them. The event was held to mark the third anniversary of Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine and the ongoing war that followed.

On 24 February 2025, pro-Palestinian activists blocked the entrance to the headquarters of the Danish shipping company in Copenhagen, demanding that management cut all economic ties with Israel. The activists demanded, among other things, that the company stop transporting military cargo that is complicit in the genocide of the Palestinian people, and suspend the company's alleged contracts with the US Department of Defense and the Israeli Ministry of Defence. Riot police later dispersed the demonstration, using tear gas and batons. Twenty activists were detained, several of whom were arrested.

On 24 February 2025, antifascist campaigners from the Cornwall Resists group held a protest outside the Reform UK Party conference at Carn Brea Leisure Center in Redruth (England) against the party's far-right policies and Nigel Farage's visit. Protesters blocked the entrance and chanted 'Shame on you', 'Nazis', 'refugees are welcome here' and 'Cornwallis anti-fascist' during Nigel Farage speech at the conference. Police forces intervened and pushed back protesters from the entrance. Other groups supporting the protest include the Bakers Food and Allied Workers Union, Radical Pride, Falmouth and Penryn Acorn, All Under One Banner Kernow, Youth Demand Falmouth and the Kernow Antifascist Network.

On 24 February 2025, around 150 protesters, including members of Ukrainian community in Ireland, gathered outside the Russian Embassy in Dublin (Dublin) to mark the third anniversary of the Russian invasion of Ukraine and calling for Russia's troops to withdraw from Ukraine. Protesters held Ukrainian flags and banners, as well as placards condemning the invasion and Russian President Vladimir Putin. There was a small number of counter-protesters that led to a minor scuffle, but police forces intervened and separated protesters. No injuries were reported, and no arrests were made.

On 27 February 2025, members of the republican group Saoradh gathered at the entrance of Craigavon Civic Center in Craigavon (Northern Ireland) to protest against the Policing and Community Safety Partnership meeting taking place inside. After initially being allowed entry, the protesters were physically removed by police when one participant attempted to make a speech. The demonstration was part of a broader campaign by Saoradh to disrupt community policing events. Local officials condemned the protest as an attempt to intimidate residents and the police.

On 28 February 2025, around 100 people demonstrated outside a construction site in Aalborg, Nordjylland, to accuse the contractor of severe labor rights violations. The protest followed a report from the Danish Construction Association stating that over 200 workers were potentially exposed to asbestos at the site. Later, police personnel dispersed the protesters after they started setting off fireworks and cannon blasts at the site.

On 28 February 2025, a man was arrested on a protest demonstration in Polevskoy (Sverdlovsk). According to the detainee, the police decided to arrest him when he was already leaving a demonstration against the liquidation of a local bus station. The man was charged with 'violation of the rules of the demonstration by the participant'.

On 28 February 2025, on the 2nd anniversary of the Tempe rail disaster, 25 members of Rouvikonas managed to enter in the headquarters of Hellenic Train in Athens - Central Athens and unfurled a banner from the rooftop reading '(Justice) To The End' and 'Murderers'. They were shouting slogans and people below were applauding. Police forces broke down the doors of the building and reached the rooftop, where they detained the protesters. On 22 May, an Athens court acquitted all 25 Rouvikonas members of the main charges and handed six-month suspended sentences to 18 of them for refusing to submit their fingerprints during their arrest.

On 2 March 2025, around 50 activists gathered near Roma Square in Venezia (Veneto) in support of Palestine, opposing what they referred to as 'imperialist war' and 'apartheid' policies. Demonstrators attempted to march toward the Calatrava Bridge but were blocked by police forces, leading to physical confrontations, including pushing and shoving. At least one activist was taken into custody.

On 2 March 2025, more than 150 locals protested on a rally organized by the local branch of the Communist Party of Russia in Perm (Perm). Residents protested the development on the territory of a local sports center. Members of the National Bolshevik Party tried to join the protesters, but the police prevented them from joining.

On 5 March 2025, around 50 gendarmes intervened to remove climate activists from their climate camp against the construction of the high-speed train line (LGV) between Bordeaux and Toulouse in Saint-Jory (Occitanie). The protesters considered the project damaging to local biodiversity. 4 protesters climbed on trees as the gendarmerie arrived but were then taken down. One individual was arrested.

On 5 March 2025, around 140 people, including DGB Youth, Grannies Against the Right, and Initiative Niederbayern Nazifree (Initiative Niederbayern Nazifrei) gathered in Osterhofen (Bayern) to protest against the AfD's Political Ash Wednesday event and against far-right ideologies. 60 other demonstrators blocked access roads by gluing themselves to the pavement, and the police physically removed the protesters after repeated warnings. Additionally, 10 protesters chained themselves to a gate at another entrance but complied with police orders and joined the authorized demonstrations.

On 6 March 2025, from 7 am to 8.30 am, between 70 and around 100 police officers from the CRS unit intervened at the humanities faculty in Brest (Bretagne) to remove around 30 students occupying the university since 4 March 2025 to protest against cuts in funding for public universities [coded as a separate event]. 4 individuals were arrested. According to the president of the University of Western Brittany, the protesters sprayed multiple graffiti on the walls, damaged equipment, and forced entry into rooms.

On 7 March 2025, several activists of France Nature Environment (France Nature Environnement - FNE) and climate activist Thomas Brail staged a protest, entering the construction site of the bypass road to stop the machinery from operating, in Montauban (Occitanie). The protesters condemned what they considered the project's detrimental effect on local biodiversity, such as the destruction of protected species. The police arrested 7 individuals.

On 7 March 2025, in the morning, more than 3,000 students and teachers marched to parliament in Athens - Central Athens, in demonstrations of the education sector at the call of university student associations, the Athens high school students' coordinating committee, DOE and OLME, demanding political accountability and justice for the victims of the 2023 Tempe rail disaster. At noon, they held a minute of silence and a sit-in protest. Students carrying placards formed the message 'their profits or our lives'. Earlier, they held speeches. Police detained 23 demonstrators, 5 of which were arrested for possession of drugs, a pocket knife and smoke bombs. Public transportation and traffic were disrupted.

On 7 March 2025, police arrested 7 recently expelled Turkmen students that were protesting in front of a university in Stavropol (Stavropol). 30-40 students were speaking out against their expulsion that happened suspectedly because they refused to transfer to the universities located in border regions of Belgorod, Kursk and Bryansk.

On 7 March 2025, at around 5 pm, at the call of OGR, under the motto 'Fire and Flame Against Patriarchy: Fight Sexism in Hofburg and State', hundreds of people gathered at the University of Wien, and proceeded through Wipplinger Street to Stephans Square in Wien - Inner City (Wien) to protest against the Academic Ball organized by the FPOE and in opposition to the presence of far-right figures and the FPOE's stance on women's rights. Several arrests were made when protesters attempted to continue the march beyond the designated route and despite police orders.

On 7 March 2025, at the call of Extinction Rebellion, people, including environmental activists, occupied the Tesla dealership in Milano - Municipio 9 (Lombardia) to denounce Elon Musk's power and political influence, demonstrate against fascism, and demand more climate action. Some activists chained themselves to the cars on display inside the store while others remained outside displaying a banner reading 'Ecology for all, no to green fascism'. Security guards and police officers intervened on the scene and dragged the protesters outside.

On 8 March 2025, police detained 5 female activists of Ural Maoists Union and by doing that dispersed a protest in Yekaterinburg (Sverdlovsk). 5 women were staging a demonstration for women's economic and reproductive rights and against domestic violence in Russia, timed to the International Women Day. The demonstration took place in Hyde Park, where events are permitted to be held without notifying the authorities.

On 8 March 2025, under the motto 'March for Life', people, including members of the Christian community, gathered in Innsbruck (Tirol) to protest against abortion. At the same time, people gathered for a counter-protest in support of abortion rights, aiming to oppose the anti-abortion demonstrators. As the anti-abortion march moved through Innsbruck, the counter-protesters formed a sit-in blockade at the bus terminal, preventing the protesters from proceeding. The police dissolved most of the blockade by telling them to leave, but when some protesters refused to leave, the police resorted to making 20 arrests to disperse the counter-protesters and end the blockade.

On 8 March 2025, at 3 pm, at the call of the alliance '8 March' (Bundnis 8 Marz), under the motto 'We fight, we strike, we live!', thousands of people, including queer, and anti-fascist groups, 'Critical Pride Alliance', Antifa and trade unions like Ver.di gathered in Stuttgart (Baden-Wurttemberg) to protest for women's rights, gender equality, demand and end to the gender wage gap and violence against women, and denounce the current political climate. The protest also supported the ongoing tariff negotiations in the public sector, emphasizing equality in labor conditions, carrying signs with slogans like 'Women's rights are human rights'. According to the demonstrators, the police intervened using force, violently pulling protesters out of the crowd, after a purple smoke flare was ignited, and a banner reading 'Stop Femicide, We Want to Stay Alive!' was displayed along the protest route. Five individuals were arrested and temporarily detained. This event was part of a broader mobilization on the occasion of International Women's Day.

On 8 March 2025, over 10,000 participants, including feminist and anti-capitalist groups such as the World Women's March Belgium and feminist collective Furia, as well as members of political parties, gathered in Brussels (Brussels) to mark International Women's Day. Protesters opposed austerity measures, called for the decriminalization of voluntary abortion, and demanded stronger social security. During the march, tensions escalated when an MR elected official was surrounded by activists, pushed to the ground, and had their protest materials taken and trampled. Police intervened to disperse the crowd and assist the individual. Later, Hadja Lahbib, the European Commissioner for Equality (MR), was booed and pelted with water by demonstrators, prompting police to escort her out of the march for her safety.

On 8 March 2025, in the afternoon, at the call of XR, at least 37 demonstrators gathered at Schiphol Airport in Schiphol (Noord-Holland) to protest against KLM's frequent flyer program, Flying Blue, arguing it incentivized excessive air travel and worsened climate change. In solidarity with women disproportionately affected by climate change on International Women's Day, protesters also disrupted airport walkways. Authorities arrested 38 demonstrators in Departure Hall 2 for refusing to leave the area, with the total number of arrests rising to 67 by around 3 pm. The group was later condemned to a 5 to 10 year access ban imposed by airport authorities on 37 participating demonstrators.

On 10 March 2025, at around 8:30 pm, between 12 and 15 climate activists from the 'Turbo Climate Battle Group' (TurboKlimaKampfGruppe Kiel - TKKG) occupied construction vehicles on a construction site along Highway 404 near Kiel (Schleswig-Holstein) to protest against its planned conversion into the A21 motorway, citing environmental concerns. 4 of them abseiled from a bridge, displaying a banner reading 'Public transport for all & free'. Police cleared the blockade between 9 and 10 am, detaining 12 activists for identification.

On 11 March 2025, in the afternoon, at the call of Nijmegen Student Encampment, around 40 people, including students and university staff, gathered inside and outside the Spinoza building at Radboud University in Nijmegen (Gelderland), interrupting a lecture by pro-Israel activist Rawan Osman by shouting pro-Palestinian slogans and later blocking her car as she left. Security and police intervened multiple times, physically removing demonstrators from the lecture and clearing the way for Osman's car to depart. No arrests were reported.

On 13 March 2025, student associations organized education sector rallies with the participation of teachers. At noon, students rallied and then marched to Syntagma square demanding political accountability and justice for the victims of the 2023 Tempe rail disaster. Police detained 6 people during security checks before the march. The protest continued in the evening, when a large crowd rallied at Syntagma square, Athens - Central Athens, for a concert. Security measures, such as street closures and the temporary suspension of service at key stations on the metro, were put in place.

On 13 March 2025, in the morning, dozens of XR activists gathered and blocked access to the MECC congress center in Maastricht (Limburg), despite a ban by the mayor, to protest the use of private jets during the international art fair TEFAF. The protesters denounced the environmental impact of about 200 private flights linked to the event. After refusing police orders to relocate, twenty demonstrators were arrested. The protest was part of Operation Storm, a three-day campaign targeting companies receiving fossil fuel subsidies.

On 14 March 2025, at the call of XR, 25 activists gathered at the RWE Eemshavencentrale in Eemshaven (Groningen) to demand its closure, citing its environmental impact and the fossil fuel subsidies it received. The protest was part of Operation Storm, a three-day campaign targeting companies benefiting from such subsidies. When ordered to leave by police, seven activists refused, were arrested, interrogated, and later released.

On 14 March 2025, in the morning, at the call of XR, including XR Agriculture (XR Landbouw), and XR Healthcare (XR Zorg), about 30 demonstrators gathered at the Yara fertilizer plant in Sluiskil (Zeeland), blocking the access road, to protest Yara's fossil subsidies and their production of artificial fertilizer. The protest ended at around 17:00, after 10 demonstrators were arrested and briefly detained by the police. The action was part of Operation Storm, involving multiple actions over three days targeting companies receiving fossil fuel subsidies.

On 15 March 2025, in the afternoon, at the call of the group 'Tools in Solidarity Against Police Violence' (Outils Solidaires contre les Violences Policieres - OSVP), around 900 people marched from Luxembourg Square in Brussels - Ixelles (Brussels) through several streets and ended near Central Station in Brussels - Ville de Bruxelles (Brussels) to denounce police violence on the International Day Against Police Brutality. The demonstrators demanded an end to police repression, justice for victims, and changes to policing practices. Some masked participants defaced police vehicles, buses, private cars, and buildings - including the statue of King Leopold II - with anti-police, anti-colonial, and pro-Palestinian graffiti. Police intervened, seized crude incendiary devices carried by some demonstrators, and made 11 arrests (9 administrative and 2 judicial).

On 15 March 2025, people took to the streets to protest alleged illegal activities of a residential development company and film a video addressed to Vladimir Putin in front of the Moscow Oblast administration building in Krasnogorsk. Police arrested 9 defrauded shared equity holders, and by doing that dispersed a protest and video message filming. The 9 detainees were charged with coronavirus social gathering restrictions violations.

On 17 March 2025, at the call of Granada Student Movement (Movimiento Estudiantil de Granada), people demonstrated at the Granada Law School in Granada (Andalucia) against the public university from serving as a platform for far-right and ultraconservative ideas, as a former Vox MP, Macarena Olona, was participating in a colloquium at the university. Around thirty people tried to prevent her from accessing the auditorium where the event was being held. In an attempt to enter the auditorium, Olona, assisted by two of her companions, physically climbed onto the group. The demonstrators reacted by pushing her and getting her hair pulled. Police officers intervened and forcibly removed the demonstrators by shoving and dragging them. Police arrested two people that committed a crime against law enforcement officers.

On 18 March 2025, in the early morning, police forces evacuated up to 450 unaccompanied migrant minors who had been occupying the Gaite Lyrique theater in Paris (Ile-de-France) since 10 December 2024 to demand regularization, the right to education, and dignified living conditions. Several dozen demonstrators, including National Deputy Danielle Simonnet (The Aftermath/NFP), gathered outside the venue to express solidarity. Police used tear gas to disperse the demonstrators, and some participants reported that officers beat migrants with batons. A total of 46 people were arrested, and nine were injured, including migrants, a police officer, and a journalist.

On 18 March 2025, students blocked access to the main Sciences Po campus in Paris (Ile-de-France) to express solidarity with the Palestinian people and condemn the Israeli airstrikes on Gaza that killed over 400 civilians the previous night. The protest included speeches, debates, and artistic workshops. Around 11 pm, police intervened at the request of the school's administration and forcibly removed protesting students from the campus.

On 18 March 2025, several dozen activists gathered in front of the Israeli embassy in Warsaw, declaring solidarity with civilians in Gaza and criticizing Israel for ongoing military actions. Two people were detained for pouring red color on the building's walls.

On 19 March 2025, at 6:20 am, police intervened to lift the student blockade at the Villejean campus of Rennes 2 University in Rennes (Bretagne), forcibly evicting students protesting against budget cuts in higher education. The intervention was requested by the university administration. The university announced that the campus would remain closed until at least 21 March 2025.

On 19 March 2025, 5 Last Generation activists staged a protest at a Michelin restaurant owned by renowned chef Carlo Cracco in Milano - Municipio 1 (Lombardia) as part of the initiative 'The Right Price', a campaign against luxury, excess, and extreme inequality. Protesters demanded concrete actions in support of the less fortunate and highlighted the necessity of sharing equitably and promoting social justice. The police dragged the protesters outside and reported them.

On 19 March 2025, police officers dispersed an ongoing occupation of a house in Lillehammer, Innlandet, in protest against the planned construction of a new motorway in the area. The police expelled 5 to 10 activists from the site.

On 20 March 2025, activists from an Extinction Rebellion affiliated group demonstrated and entered the venue of a major Scandinavian bank's annual meeting in Helsinki, calling for an end to investments in new fossil fuel extraction projects and urging stronger climate action from financial institutions. Later, several activists were detained and removed from the venue by police personnel.

On 21 March 2025, 5 activists gathered and abseiled from a bridge on the A49 highway near Dannenrod (Hessen) to protest against the highway extension due to deforestation concerns, blocking traffic on the newly opened section, displaying a banner reading 'All forests remain! Our dreams cannot be evicted!'. Police intervened by deploying height rescue specialists to remove the two activists who had abseiled from the bridge, with five individuals taken into custody.

On 22 March 2025, around 50 activists from Animal Rebellion and Extinction Rebellion demonstrated and blocked a slaughterhouse and food processing facility in the Nurmo area of Seinajoki, Etela-Pohjanmaa, to demand a controlled phase-out of broiler production in Finland and to promote a transition toward plant-based food systems. Police later detained and removed around 26 activists from the site after they failed to comply with police demands and unblock the property.

On 22 March 2025, XR activists protested in 't Zand in Brugge (Vlaanderen), distributing flyers and briefly occupying a CashPoint branch in the Geldmuntstraat to denounce BNP Paribas for its investments in fossil fuels and the arms industry, such as the Israeli arms producer Elbit Systems, which XR accused of complicity in 'genocide' against the Palestinians. After the peaceful protest, three protesters were arrested and said to have been subjected to a 'degrading' strip search, prompting the group to file complaints with the police, accusing the Bruges police of disproportionate and humiliating treatment.

On 22 March 2025, under the motto 'Together for Germany', between 600 and 620 people, including Querdenken movement affiliates and other far-right activists, staged a protest on Opern Square in Hannover (Niedersachsen) to demand border controls, an end to military support for Ukraine, and the protection of free speech, with participants waving German and Russian flags. Counter-demonstrators, including Left Youth Solid affiliates, gathered and tried to interrupt the speeches of the main demonstration at Steintor Square, uttering loud chants and calls. The police intervened by pushing the group into Lange Laube Street to separate them from the Querdenken demonstrators. This event was part of a broader far-right mobilization against immigration, government policies, and support for Ukraine.

On 22 March 2025, under the motto 'Together for Germany', around 550 people staged a protest in Munchen (Bayern) demanding border controls and an end to military support for Ukraine. Between 100 and 200 counter-protesters, including leftist groups, Grune Jugend and Grannies Against the Right, gathered under the motto 'Together against the Right' to protest far-right ideologies. Minor scuffles occurred near Bayer- and Herrmann-Lingg Street during a blockade attempt by counter-demonstrators who pushed against police cordons in an effort to approach the far-right march. Police physically blocked their path and shoved them away. The event was part of a broader far-right mobilization against immigration, government policies, and support for Ukraine.

On 23 March 2025, at the call of the Federation of Alawite Unions of the Netherlands (Federatie van Alevitische Verenigingen Nederland - HABF), between several dozen to 100 demonstrators gathered on Malieveld in Den Haag (Zuid-Holland) to demonstrate against the recent mass killings of Alawites in Syria, calling for an end to the violence. The demonstration escalated when a physical altercation occured between one supporter and three opponents of the demonstration, leading to four arrests by the police. It is unclear who the arrested individuals were.

On 25 March 2025, police officers dispersed an ongoing blockade of a logging site near Ramsele, Vasternorrland, aimed to stop the logging operations within the traditional reindeer grazing areas, demanding that the logging company halt all activities until a fair and respectful agreement is made with the local Indigenous community.

On 26 March 2025, 27 activists from the Emergency Break movement blocked traffic in various locations of Copenhagen calling for an end to motorway construction due to environmental concerns. Police later removed and detained several activists from the site after they failed to comply with police demands.

On 27 March 2025, several youngsters held a protest in Bilbao (Pais Vasco) during the municipal plenary session to oppose the eviction of the self-managed occupied social center, as it is a community space. The police peacefully removed the protesters.

On 27 March 2025, around 30 to 40 pro-Palestinian activists gathered outside of the Central Bank of Norway in Oslo to protest against the Norwegian oil fund's alleged investments in Israel-related companies, demanding that the fund divest from these entities. Later, police personnel physically removed protesters who refused to follow police orders and leave the premises.

On 27 March 2025, several hundred activists, including supporters of PiS and Confederation and affiliates of far-right groups, gathered for a rally in Radom in front of a local municipal house, protesting against the proposed opening of a new refugee center in their neighbourhood. Law enforcers intervened several times, as some of the activists attempted to enter the building and disrupt a meeting taking place inside.

On 28 March 2025, in the morning, around 20 workers, including ABVV union members, struck at the AB Inbev depot in Hasselt (Vlaanderen), with an ABVV delegation blocking the factory entrance with flags and banners. The management called the police, and the police detained a union representative.

On 28 March 2025, politicians and activists of the Momentum movement protested in front of the MTVA headquarters, Budapest - III, against Viktor Orban during his radio interview. Protesters sat down at the entrance of the building and linked arms, while the police tried to disrupt the protest by removing the participants.

On 30 March 2025, at the call of Mothers Against Genocide group, pro-Palestine protesters gathered for an overnight vigil and blocked the entrance to the Irish Parliament in Dublin (Dublin) to mark Mother's Day and to commemorate the children and mothers killed in Gaza by Israeli forces. Protesters called on the Government to pass the Occupied Territories Bill and to prevent the use of Irish airspace to carry weapons to Israel. Police forces intervened and forcefully removed the protesters, and a total of 14 people were arrested.
